## 2.1-spy-report-deep-parse.md

# 2.1 — Spy report parser deep

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/parse-inline.js` (parser) + `src/spy.js` (call site) + `src/intel.js` (consumer) + `src/ui.js` (render)
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

The report pipeline is `XHR spy` (`src/spy.js:37-112`) → `queueReport`
(`src/spy.js:222-230`) → `fetchReport` (`src/spy.js:266-297`) → `ingestReport`
(`src/spy.js:236-257`) → `parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:33-93`). Findings
land in `state.findings` (ring buffer 500, `src/spy.js:249-253`) and are
*already consumed* by:

- `renderFindings` row rendering (`src/ui.js:1702-1728`) — flat `.units`
  `Object.entries().map(...)` and `W/S/I` resource string.
- `intelDossiers` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) — aggregates by player key, pushes
  `f.units`, `f.wall`, `f.town` into per-player buckets.
- `watchMatch` (`src/intel.js:145-185`) — uses `f.town.id`, `f.vill_id`,
  `f.attacker`, `f.alliance`, `f.town.x`, `f.town.y`.
- `intelPatternScan` (`src/intel.js:206-245`) — uses `f.attacker`, `f.ts`.
- `intelWatchlistScan` (`src/intel.js:186-205`) — uses `f.vacation`,
  `f.town`, `f.vill_id`.

`parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:33-93`) returns exactly:

```js
{ id, ts, type, attacker, defender, town{id,name,x,y},
  units, resources{wood,stone,iron,gold,supply}, loot,
  outcome, wall, alliance, vill_id, vacation }
```

The audit (plan 27 §13 + plan 26 §B6 hot list) re-confirms that the existing
parser is **deliberately strict** — five `return null` paths
(`src/parse-inline.js:34, 48, 50, 54` and the implicit final guard at line 53's
"no type and no attacker and no defender and no units and no outcome" check).
`type` is `r.type || r.report_type || null` (`parse-inline.js:51`) and the
parser used to fall through to `type: 'unknown'`; plan 26 I8 confirmed that
`type: 'unknown'` poisons downstream filters and the catch-all was removed —
any report missing a discriminator now returns `null` and lands in
`reportFetchFail(id, 'unparsed')` (`src/spy.js:258-264`). This plan must
preserve that strictness: a **new** field is added only when the JSON key is
present and finite.

Plan 27 §9 confirms existing report-side work to be coded, not to extend:
"Offline report catch-up `spy.js:117-163`" (already shipped, plan 14),
"Battle report basics `intel.js:13.x`" (already shipped, will be deepened in
2.5). No deep-parse surface ships today.

## 2. Gap

The current parser captures the **shape** of a report (who/what/when, basic
units, basic loot, wall) but not the **content** that turns a report into
useful intel:

- **Building levels** (`buildings['main']=12, 'barracks'=8, 'wall'=15`) are
  nowhere in the parsed object. Without them, plan 2.2 (timeline of growth)
  and plan 5.3 (threat score from garrison size) cannot fire.
- **Troops per type** is partially there (`f.units` is a flat bag) but
  **defender vs attacker split** is lost. `extractUnits` reads
  `r.units || r.attacker_units` and never `r.defender_units`
  (`src/parse-inline.js:18-23`). A spy report with `defender_units` would
  flatten into the attacker bucket.
- **Hero presence** (`hero: {name, level, class}`) is absent. Plan 4.3 (hero
  manager) and the dossier view (`src/intel.js:34-71`) cannot key off it.
- **Resources** are kept as `null` on unknowns (`extractResources`,
  `src/parse-inline.js:25-31`). Plan 27 §2.12 (loot capacity) and the existing
  `W/S/I` row need the same `null` semantics — add `gold` (already half-keyed
  by `r.resources.gold` lookup) and `supply` (already half-keyed) but never
  invent a number.
- **Outcome as boolean vs string** — `outcome: r.outcome ?? r.win ?? null`
  (`src/parse-inline.js:87`) mixes types. Battle-to-win ratio math (plan 2.5)
  needs a normalized boolean.

The 2.2/2.5/5.3 consumer plans exist in `docs/plans/v4/README.md` but have
no-ops today because the parser cannot give them what they need.

## 3. Design

Extend `parseReport` (the only place that turns raw bridge JSON into a
finding) with three new fields, then surface them in two consumers:

1. **`buildings: { [name]: number }`** — collected from `r.buildings ||
   r.building_levels || r.buildings_levels`, keys coerced to lowercase, values
   required positive integers (otherwise dropped one-by-one, never a partial
   bag). The existing `wall` field is **kept** as a top-level convenience
   derived from `buildings.wall` if present, so existing readers
   (`src/intel.js:62`, `src/ui.js:1716-1724`) keep working.
2. **`units_attacker`, `units_defender`** — both objects, replacing the
   current single `units` field only for the case where the JSON has split
   keys. **Backward-compat rule**: `extractUnits` keeps writing `units` as
   the union (current contract — `src/ui.js:1716-1718`,
   `src/intel.js:59`); `units_attacker` and `units_defender` are added
   alongside. When the JSON has only `r.units` (no split), the union goes
   into `units` and the two split fields are `null`. When the JSON has
   `attacker_units` + `defender_units`, both split fields are set and the
   union `units` is the sum. Plan 2.5 (battle report analyzer) reads the
   split fields; the existing dossier aggregator keeps reading `units`.
3. **`hero: { id, name, level, cls } | null`** — collected from
   `r.hero || r.hero_info || r.defender_hero`. All fields optional; the
   whole object is `null` if `r.hero` is falsy or yields zero populated
   fields. Never invent `level=0` or `cls='unknown'`.
4. **`outcome: 'win' | 'lose' | 'draw' | null`** — normalize via a small
   mapping at the parser's existing assignment line. Treat `r.outcome` as a
   string when it is one; treat `r.win` as `win`/`lose`; treat `r.draw` and
   the literal string `'draw'` as draw. Anything else stays `null`.

Normalization is pure read-only — `parseReport` still returns `null` for any
payload missing the discriminator (line 51, line 53-55). The new fields are
**additive**; the existing schema is preserved bit-for-bit.

Consumers:

- `extractUnits` (`src/parse-inline.js:18-23`) splits into three helpers used
  by the new parser block. The existing `units` field keeps the union
  signature for `ui.js:1716-1718` and `intel.js:59`.
- `renderFindings` (`src/ui.js:1702-1728`) adds a third row when
  `f.buildings` has keys, formatted as `bldg: main=12 wall=15 stash=3` (top
  3 by descending level, ellipsis after that). The existing `units` /
  `resources` rows are unchanged.
- `intelDossiers` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) pushes `f.hero` and
  `f.buildings` into per-player buckets next to the existing `units` push.

The parser stays in `parse-inline.js` (called only from `ingestReport` at
`src/spy.js:237`) — there is no second call site to update.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/parse-inline.js:18-23` — replace `extractUnits` with three helpers:
   `extractSplitUnits(r)` returning `{ attacker, defender }` (each `null` if
   the source key is missing or empty), and `extractUnits(r)` rewritten as
   the union of the two for the legacy `units` field. The new
   `extractUnits` reads `r.units` first, then `r.attacker_units`+`r.defender_units`
   — when both split keys exist, the union is the sum (clamped at 0).
2. `src/parse-inline.js:25-31` — extend `extractResources` to honor
   `r.resource_pillage` and `r.haul` as alternate sources, but keep all
   `null`-on-unknown semantics (gold/supply stay nullable).
3. `src/parse-inline.js:33-93` — `parseReport` return object gains:
   - `buildings: { [name]: number }` — sanitized via a new module-local
     `parseBuildings(r)` IIFE that lower-cases keys, casts to integer,
     drops non-positive or non-finite values, returns `{}` when nothing
     survives. The existing top-level `wall` field reads
     `buildings.wall || r.wall || r.wall_level || r.defender_wall || null`
     so `src/intel.js:62` and downstream remain green.
   - `units_attacker`, `units_defender` — both `null` or both objects.
   - `hero: {id, name, level, cls} | null` — populated only from
     `r.hero || r.hero_info || r.defender_hero`. Drop the entire field to
     `null` when no source key is present or yields zero populated fields.
     Never invent a `name='unknown'`.
   - `outcome: 'win' | 'lose' | 'draw' | null` — normalize via a
     module-local `parseOutcome(r)` IIFE that returns one of the three
     literals or `null`.
4. `src/parse-inline.js:53` — keep the existing `return null` strictness
   (no type, no attacker, no defender, no units, no outcome). The new fields
   do **not** satisfy the strictness check (a payload with only `buildings`
   is still an unknown report type and `return null`).
5. `src/spy.js:236-257` — `ingestReport` is unchanged: it already calls
   `parseReport` once and bails on `null`. The new fields fall through
   automatically.
6. `src/ui.js:1716-1728` — `renderFindings` appends a third row
   `bldg: <…>` when `f.buildings && Object.keys(f.buildings).length`,
   formatted as top-3 entries by level descending. Keep the existing row
   order (`meta` → `units` → `res`) so the diff in the Intel tab is local.
7. `src/intel.js:59-71` — `intelDossiers` pushes `f.hero` and
   `f.buildings` into the per-player bucket. The dossier object gains
   `hero` (latest, by `f.ts`) and `buildings` (latest, by `f.ts`) fields.
   The export-redaction path (`src/qol.js:252`,
   `src/ui.js:1798-1808`) does not need to redact these fields in v4.0 —
   document as a follow-up in §10.
8. `src/header.js` — no new STORE key. No new state field. The new fields
   live inside `state.findings` entries and are pruned by the existing
   500-row cap (`src/spy.js:250-253`).
9. `src/parse-inline.js` line 1 — header comment for the file notes that
   `parseReport` is now additive-only; future fields go through the same
   `null`-on-unknown discipline.

## 5. State & storage

No new `state.*` field. No new STORE key. No `configVer` bump (the parser
extension is invisible to the config schema; new finding fields ride
inside `state.findings` and inherit the existing 500-row cap).

Prune TTL: same as `state.findings` today (capped at 500 by
`src/spy.js:250-253`, lastSeenTs floor at `src/spy.js:245-247`). The new
fields are present on every row that has them and absent on every row that
does not — no per-field TTL.

`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`: no change. `STORE.FINDINGS` is already in
`src/header.js:194`.

## 6. Config surface

No Config toggle. This is a read-only extension that widens the parsed
schema; the per-row dumper (`src/qol.js:252`) and the per-row render
(`src/ui.js:1702-1728`) show the new fields automatically once the parser
returns them.

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface. The parser is read-only; the widen is data-plane only.

Plan 27 §11 risk class Low → no dry-run GUI, no new bridge template, no
captcha feature key. The validation gate is "visit Reports tab after a
known spy arrives; new `bldg:` row appears in the Intel render of the
finding."

## 8. Failure modes

| Condition | Verdict | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Tracker returns `r.buildings` as a string | `null` for the field | `parseBuildings` checks `typeof === 'object' && !Array.isArray(...)`; returns `{}` |
| `r.hero` is a string | `null` for the field | Type guard, no throw |
| `r.outcome` is a numeric (`1`/`0`) | mapped to `win`/`lose` | `parseOutcome` branches: `1 → 'win'`, `0 → 'lose'`, anything else `null` |
| `r.units` and `r.attacker_units` both present | split wins, `units` is sum | Existing readers see the union; 2.5 sees the split |
| `r.buildings` has 200 keys | returned whole | UI render caps at top-3; the dossier pushes the whole map |
| `parser` throws | `ingestReport` returns false → `reportFetchFail(id, 'unparsed')` | Existing path (`src/spy.js:336`, `reportRetry` cap at 3) |

The five `return null` strictness paths remain in place. The precondition
invariant (CLAUDE.md) holds: every new field's verdict is the value the
parser actually read, and an unreadable getter yields `null`/empty, never a
guess.

## 9. Validation gate

Plan 27 §11 Low risk: preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

1. Hand-spy a target with a known building mix (e.g. main 12, wall 15, stash
   3). Open the Reports tab, open the Intel tab. The findings row shows new
   `bldg: wall=15 main=12 stash=3` line. Log: no parser exception.
2. Hand-spy a target with a defender/attacker split. The existing `units`
   line sums correctly; an inspector (`Object.entries(f.units)`) shows the
   union. Plan 2.5 (when it lands) reads the split fields with no schema
   catch-up.
3. Hand-spy a target whose report JSON has no `buildings`/`hero` key. Row
   renders without the new line; `Object.keys(f.buildings || {})` is `[]`;
   `f.hero` is `null`. No regression on the `units` row.
4. `state.findings` still capped at 500. Open the Preflight tab → `report
   catch-up` row still green; `report fetch` row still green.
5. `grepbot.user.js` rebuilt. `python3 build.py` exits 0.

## 10. Out of scope

- Building-level diffing (plan 2.2 timeline). 2.1 only exposes
  `buildings`; 2.2 owns the per-town map and the diff renderer.
- Battle-loss math, win-rate, top-target (plan 2.5). 2.1 only exposes
  `outcome` and the split `units_attacker`/`units_defender`; 2.5 owns the
  aggregator.
- Threat score from report content (plan 5.3). 5.3 reads the new fields
  but is its own plan.
- Hero transfer / assignment (plan 4.3). 4.3 reads `f.hero` but the
  assignment UX lives there.
- Per-field export redaction in `state.findings` JSON export. Follow-up —
  the redactor at `src/ui.js:1798-1808` was written before this parser
  widens; the new `hero.name` field is player text and will be flagged
  in a v4.1 docs update.
- Changing the existing `units` shape from a flat union to a structured
  object. **Hard rule:** the existing `units` field is preserved bit-for-bit
  to keep `src/ui.js:1716-1718` and `src/intel.js:59` working unchanged.

## 2.2-enemy-city-timeline.md

# 2.2 — Enemy city timeline (diff reports)

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js` (additive) + small markup additions in `src/ui.js` intel section
**Depends on:** none (will consume 2.1 deep-parse fields when that ships, but ships standalone against the fields `parseReport` already returns today)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- The findings ring buffer lives at `state.findings` (`src/core.js:221`), seeded from `load(STORE.FINDINGS, [])`. It is unshifted in `ingestReport` (`src/spy.js:249-254`) and capped at **500** in memory there (`src/spy.js:250-253`) — quota emergencies trim it to **100** in `storagePruneForQuota` (`src/core.js:1167-1172`). There is **no** 7-day TTL on findings; retention is "keep the N most recent".
- `parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:33-93`) returns the shape every diff is computed from: `{ id, ts, type, attacker, defender, town:{id,name,x,y}, units, resources, loot, outcome, wall, alliance, vill_id, vacation }`. The defender block is normalised by `nameOf` (`src/parse-inline.js:1-16`) and includes `vacation` plus `alliance`.
- The intel panel is a **single `<pre class="intel-panel">`** element rendered by `renderIntel` (`src/intel.js:75-114`). It writes `box.textContent = html` — a flat text dump of `=== Entrantes ===`, `=== Fichas ===`, watchlist, alliance notes, pattern note. There is no per-city history view today.
- `intelDossiers` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) already groups findings by player (not by town) and surfaces `reports`, `units[]`, `towns[]`, `walls[]`, `last ts`, plus `state.playerNotes[name]`. `walls` is appended unconditionally for **every** finding (intel.js:62) but no aggregate min/max is computed or rendered. `intelThreatBoard` (intel.js:72-74) and `intelPatternScan` (intel.js:206-245) are sibling read functions, called by `renderIntel` and `boot.js:114`.
- Table rendering helpers exist: `tableShell(list, headers, key)` (`src/ui.js:72-91`) + `makeSortable(table, rowDataFn, key)` (`src/ui.js:45-60`) + `patchCells(tr, cells)` (`src/ui.js:92-110`). They are how Farms (ui.js:130) and World (ui.js:203) render today.
- Sticky sort: `state.tabFilters` (`src/ui.js:1-13`) + `sortApplySaved` (`src/ui.js:38-44`) — every `makeSortable(key)` saves its sort under `sort:<key>` and re-applies it after row-set rebuilds. This is what stops "the chosen sort is lost on repaint" (plan 26 §B4).
- Plan 27 §9 already-shipped list does **not** include enemy-city timeline (it lists "Battle report basics (intel.js 13.x) — extending in 2.5"). 2.2 is net-new.

## 2. Gap

Dossiers tell you "this player has been seen in 8 reports". They do not tell you "this city was at wall 12, is now wall 18, gained 40 hoplites, and switched alliance on `ts` X". The 500-cap ring buffer already contains the raw data — wall per finding is captured (parseReport line 88), units per finding is captured (parseReport line 84), and the intel panel never reads them in a per-city axis. 2.2 closes that gap by grouping findings by `town.id` (or `vill_id` for farm raids) and emitting a chronological diff per town.

## 3. Design

- New function `intelCityTimeline(townKey, opts)` in `intel.js`. `townKey` resolves to one of: `town:<id>` (city reports), `farm:<id>` (village raids where `vill_id` is set), `player:<name>` (aggregate by attacker/defender). The function reads `state.findings` only — no new storage.
- Diff dimensions per adjacent pair (oldest→newest), in order:
  1. `wall` (number) — show `+N`/`-N` only when both sides are finite numbers. Unknown ⇒ `?`.
  2. `units` (attacker for offense, defender for defense) — count per unit key, render `Δhoplite 0→40, Δsword 0→10`. Empty `units` object ⇒ `unidades:?` (parseReport:84 only writes keys with `Number.isFinite && > 0`, so absence is unknown not zero).
  3. `resources.wood/stone/iron` (parseReport:27-31) — show last known with `+N` since prior. Loots seen on offense reports only.
  4. `town.name` change (parseReport:80) — render `nombre: "A" → "B"` only on change.
  5. `alliance` change (parseReport:89) — render `alianza: X → Y` only on change.
  6. `vacation` flag (parseReport:91, normalised at parseReport:14) — render `vacaciones ON/OFF` on transition.
  7. Buildings and hero presence: **not implemented today**; explicitly mark as `—` in the table so 2.1 deep-parse can fill them in later without changing the column layout. Plan 27 §2.1 is the source; once it ships, the diff function reads the new fields if present and shows `?` otherwise. This avoids a brittle v1.0 schema lock-in.
- 7-day soft retention filter at read time: filter `f.ts >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` before grouping. The constant lives in `intel.js` and is reused by 2.3 and 2.4 (one retention policy for the read trio). This is what plan 27 §13 calls the "7d uniform unless the slice needs longer" convention; the journal already does 7d (`src/bridge.js:447`).
- Per-town hard cap: keep the last **8** reports per town in the diff (oldest trimmed). The 500-cap findings ring already bounds global size; the 8/town cap is a UI/payload cap so the table does not grow unbounded for a noisy target.
- Render path: a new sibling `<div class="intel-timeline">` under the intel section in `ui.js:692-707`. `renderIntel` calls a new `renderIntelTimeline()` that builds a `tableShell(['Fecha', 'Muro', 'Unidades', 'Recursos', 'Nombre', 'Alianza', 'Vac.', '—'], 'intel-timeline')`. The `—` column is the buildings/hero placeholder and the cell renders literal `—` until 2.1 lands.
- No scheduler, no `gbInterval`. Read functions only. Wired into the existing 15s `renderIntel` (`src/boot.js:108-115`) which already runs alongside `intelPatternScan`. No `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry (no write), no `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry (no new storage key), no `configVer` bump (read-only feature with no new Config toggle).
- No `alertWebhook` (read-mostly diff for human eyes; no event surface), no captcha feature key.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `const INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS = 7 * 86400000;` at module top (after the existing `QUEST_SCAN_MS`/`QUEST_HISTORY_MAX` block at line 247-249). Re-exported for 2.3 and 2.4 to import.
2. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelTownKey(f)`: returns `f.town && f.town.id ? 'town:'+f.town.id : (f.vill_id ? 'farm:'+f.vill_id : null)`. Reject findings without a town key. Returns null on the rare `f.town && f.town.id == null` edge so caller skips the row.
3. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelDiffPair(prev, cur)`: returns the per-row diff object for the seven dimensions in §3. Pure: no state read, no log.
4. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelCityTimeline()`: groups `state.findings.filter(f => f.ts >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS)` by `intelTownKey(f)`, sorts each group ascending by `ts`, keeps last 8, computes adjacent `intelDiffPair` deltas, returns `Array<{townKey, label, reports:number, lastTs, rows:Array<{ts, prev, cur, diff}>}>` sorted by `lastTs` desc. Caps output at 30 towns (matches the existing dossiers `.slice(0, 30)` pattern at intel.js:81).
5. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (line 75) to call `renderIntelTimeline()` (new fn) after the existing `intelPatternScan()` (line 113). Keep the existing `<pre>` text dump untouched for back-compat with anyone greppping the panel.
6. `src/ui.js` — add a `<div class="intel-timeline" style="font-size:11px;margin-top:6px">` inside the intel section, right after the existing `<pre class="intel-panel">` (line 694) and before the note-input row (line 695). No new buttons; the table renders on every `renderIntel()`.
7. `src/intel.js` — `function renderIntelTimeline()`: builds the table via `tableShell(list, headers, 'intel-timeline')`; each row uses `patchCells` with the same `data-sort` scheme used by Farms (`src/ui.js:130`). `headers` = `['Fecha', 'Muro', 'Unidades', 'Recursos', 'Nombre', 'Alianza', 'Vac.', '—']`. Empty state: `empty.textContent = 'sin historial de ciudad (recibe 2+ informes sobre la misma)';`.
8. `src/intel.js` — Spanish labels in the diff renderer. Examples: `+12 muro`, `sin cambio`, `?`, `unidades:?`, `vacaciones ON`, `alianza: X → Y`, `nombre: A → B`. Strings only, not regex keys — safe for the redaction pipeline at `ui.js:1061` and `qol.js`.
9. `src/intel.js` — at the head of `intelCityTimeline`, log once via `gbLogT('intel-timeline-empty', 300000, 'intel: city timeline empty after 7d filter')` when the filter drops everything (catches misconfigured clients that mint ts in seconds vs ms — see the `n < 1e12` heuristic in `src/parse-inline.js:65`). No throw, no `gbLog` storm.

## 5. State & storage

- No new `state.*` fields.
- No new `STORE.*` keys.
- No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry (nothing to scope).
- No `configVer` bump.
- Retention: 7-day soft cap at read time via `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (intel.js, item 1). Per-town cap 8 reports. Both reused by 2.3/2.4; this is the **one** retention policy the read trio shares.

## 6. Config surface

None. No new Config toggles, no defaults to ship. The feature is always on and reads whatever `state.findings` already contains. If a future user wants to turn it off, add `state.intelTimeline === false` and short-circuit `intelCityTimeline()` — but it is a single conditional, defer until someone asks.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** This feature is read-only. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbAjaxWatch` registration, no template name in `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`, no `gbCaptchaPause` feature key, no `gbLock`/`GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no `state.dryRun` interaction, no confirm gate. Per `docs/plans/v4/README.md` §7 and plan 27 §13, read-only features skip the rest of this section. The function never invents a game endpoint, action name, or payload field — it reads `state.findings` shaped by `parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:33-93`).

## 8. Failure modes

- **Empty `state.findings`:** `renderIntelTimeline` writes the empty-state row. No log.
- **All findings filtered by 7d:** log once via `gbLogT('intel-timeline-empty', 300000, …)`, render the empty-state row. The throttle key keeps it quiet on subsequent renders.
- **Unknown wall/units/resources:** render `?` (not `0`). The diff function treats unknown as "no comparison" and emits `sin cambio` against a known side. Honest unknown beats fabricated zero — same rule as the precondition invariant in CLAUDE.md.
- **`parseReport` shape change in a future release:** the diff function reads named keys directly. If a key disappears, the call site sees `undefined` and renders `?` (per item 4). No throw path. If a key is renamed, the column silently goes empty — caught by Preflight's "findings schema" row, which is already read-only (CLAUDE.md "Preflight ... probes every module's read path only").
- **ts in seconds (legacy / future client):** the `parseReport` heuristic at `parse-inline.js:65` (`if (n < 1e12) n *= 1000`) catches this. The empty-timeline log is the trip wire.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 (Low risk) — Preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

1. Build, install, open a world with at least 3 reports on the same enemy town.
2. Open the Intel tab. Below the existing `<pre>` text dump, the new `intel-timeline` table lists the town, with rows in ascending `ts` order; first row's `prev` column is empty, subsequent rows show `+N muro` / `unidades: 0→40` / `+5k madera` deltas. Last row `ts` matches the most recent finding's `ts` for that town.
3. Sort by `Muro` desc: top row has the highest `cur` wall across the visible groups. Reload the panel (close+reopen) — sort survives (sticky via `state.tabFilters.sort:intel-timeline`).
4. Force the 7d filter: `state.findings[0].ts = Date.now() - 10*86400000` from console, reopen Intel. The filtered-out town no longer appears; the `gbLogT` log fires once.
5. Preflight row "findings schema" still passes; Stats tab decisions counters unchanged (no journal entries — feature is silent on the journal because it is read-only).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-building and per-hero diff columns.** Owned by plan 2.1 (spy report deep parse) — that plan produces the new fields; this plan reads them when present. The `—` placeholder column is the integration point.
- **Cross-city aggregate by alliance.** Owned by 2.5 (battle report analyzer) and 5.3 (threat assessment). Reusing `intelDossiers` alliance rollup is the natural place; defer.
- **Tombstone / outpost intel.** No game endpoint exists for it in the bridge model; would be a separate read feature. Out of scope per plan 27 §0 (no new game endpoints invented).
- **Writes.** This plan never posts. Re-introducing writes means a confirm-gate per plan 27 §11 Med and a new `gbCaptchaPause` feature key — both deferred until a real use case lands.
- **Player inactivity tracker (2.4) and ghost-town detector (2.3).** Sibling features with their own plan files; they share `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` but do not call into `intelCityTimeline`.

## 2.3-ghost-town-detector.md

# 2.3 — Ghost town detector

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js` (additive) + small markup addition in `src/ui.js` intel section
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `state.findings` (`src/core.js:221`) is the per-world report ring buffer. Every entry carries `ts` (ms epoch, parsed in `parseReport` at `src/parse-inline.js:56-72` with a `n < 1e12` ms/s heuristic), `town.id` and `town.name` (`src/parse-inline.js:78-83`), and a defender block with `vacation` (`src/parse-inline.js:14`, written by `nameOf`).
- The intel panel today (`renderIntel` at `src/intel.js:75-114`) renders only the **flat text dump** of `=== Entrantes ===` / `=== Fichas ===` / watchlist / alliance notes / pattern note. There is no per-town "is anyone home?" view.
- `intelDossiers` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) groups by **player**, not by town. It captures `reports`, `units[]`, `towns[]`, `walls[]`, `last` (max ts). It does not check staleness, vacation, or any "ghost" signal.
- `intelPlayerKey` (`src/intel.js:1-10`) is the canonical string key for a player (`'id:<n>'` for objects with an `id`, otherwise the name). It is what `intelDossiers` and `intelPatternScan` use; towns in `state.findings` carry `town.id` directly with no equivalent helper. 2.3 needs a town-key helper (see §4 item 2) — same shape, different attribute.
- 2.2 Enemy city timeline (sibling plan) introduces `const INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS = 7 * 86400000;` in `intel.js`. 2.3 reuses it — that is the **one** retention policy the read trio shares.
- Plan 27 §9 already-shipped list does **not** mention a ghost-town detector. The watchlist code (`watchMatch` at `src/intel.js:145-184`, `intelWatchlistScan` at `src/intel.js:186-205`) is the closest sibling — it logs a hit and fires `alertWebhook` but only when a new finding matches a saved rule. It does not score "quiet towns" at all.

## 2. Gap

A scout user has 200 reports in `state.findings`. Some of those reports are 30 days old on towns whose defenders went on vacation the next week; some are on towns the defender abandoned. Right now the intel panel only shows "this player exists" (dossiers) or "this is incoming right now" (threats). There is no read path that says "you have not seen activity on this town in N days" or "this town's last defender is on vacation". 2.3 closes that gap with a per-town staleness + vacation view, derived from data that already lives in `state.findings`.

## 3. Design

- New function `intelGhostTowns(opts)` in `intel.js`. Reads `state.findings` only — no new storage.
- Group by `intelTownKey(f)` (the helper introduced by plan 2.2 item 2 — `'town:<id>'` for cities, `'farm:<id>'` for villages). Filter to `f.ts >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (7d). For each town, find the **most recent** finding and read:
  - `last.ts` — the timestamp.
  - `last.town.name` — display label.
  - `last.defender.vacation` — true if the defender was on vacation at last sight.
  - `last.wall` — last known wall level (so the user knows whether it is worth a follow-up spy).
  - `last.alliance` — last known alliance (so a player who switched alliance is flagged).
- Score per town (read-only, deterministic):
  - **stale** if `now - last.ts >= GHOST_STALE_MS` (default 3 × 86400000 = 3 days).
  - **vacant** if `last.defender.vacation === true`.
  - **abandoned** if no defender name in the last finding (`last.defender && !last.defender.name`).
- Output: `Array<{ townKey, label, lastTs, ageMs, vacation, abandoned, wall, alliance, reasons: string[] }>` sorted by `ageMs` desc. Rendered as a single table on the intel panel below the dossier pre.
- No scheduler (rendered on `renderIntel()` call from `src/boot.js:108-115` 15s loop). No `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry. No `STORE` / `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry. No `configVer` bump. No `alertWebhook` (this is a passive view; firing a webhook for every "town is quiet" would be noise — that is what a 5.x feature is for).

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `const GHOST_STALE_MS = 3 * 86400000;` at module top alongside `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (from 2.2 item 1). One constant, in one file.
2. `src/intel.js` — reuse `intelTownKey(f)` from plan 2.2 (item 2). If 2.2 has not landed yet, inline the same one-liner here; the duplication is one function until 2.2 lands and we delete the inline copy. Pick the 2.2-first ordering so this plan does not need its own helper.
3. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelGhostTowns()`: filters `state.findings` by `f.ts >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS`, groups by `intelTownKey(f)`, walks each group to find the most recent entry (`max ts`), reads the four fields in §3, computes the `stale`/`vacant`/`abandoned` flags and the `reasons[]` array (Spanish labels: `'sin actividad 3d'`, `'defensor en vacaciones'`, `'sin nombre de defensor'`), returns sorted by `ageMs` desc, capped at 30 (matches `intelDossiers().slice(0, 30)` at intel.js:81).
4. `src/intel.js` — add `function renderIntelGhost()`: builds a `tableShell(list, ['Ciudad', 'Última', 'Edad', 'Muro', 'Alianza', 'Razón'], 'intel-ghost')`; each row uses `patchCells` (ui.js:92-110) with the diff-friendly `data-sort` scheme. Empty state: `empty.textContent = 'sin pueblos fantasma (7d)';`. Append to the existing intel section, below the timeline table from 2.2.
5. `src/ui.js` — add a `<div class="intel-ghost" style="font-size:11px;margin-top:6px">` inside the intel section, right after the `<div class="intel-timeline">` (added by 2.2 item 6). Renders empty in the layout; the table appears when 2.3 ships.
6. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (line 75) to call `renderIntelGhost()` after `renderIntelTimeline()` (or after `intelPatternScan()` at line 113 if 2.2 has not shipped). The text `<pre>` dump at line 75-114 stays unchanged.
7. `src/intel.js` — Spanish label helpers (one each): `ghostAgeLabel(ageMs)`: returns `'Xd'` / `'Xh'` / `'Xm'` based on `fmtSec(Math.round(ageMs/1000))` (existing `fmtSec` at `src/core.js:1312`). `ghostReasonText(r)`: joins `r.reasons` with `, `. Strings only, no IDs, no regex keys.
8. `src/intel.js` — at the head of `intelGhostTowns`, log once via `gbLogT('intel-ghost-empty', 300000, 'intel: ghost towns empty after 7d filter')` when no town qualifies. Same throttle key shape as 2.2 (item 9) so the two can coexist without stepping on each other.

## 5. State & storage

- No new `state.*` fields.
- No new `STORE.*` keys.
- No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.
- No `configVer` bump.
- Retention: reuses `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` from plan 2.2 (the single shared retention constant). One filter at read time, applied identically to all three read features in the C5 cluster.

## 6. Config surface

None. `GHOST_STALE_MS` is a hard-coded default (3 days) inside the module. It is the kind of knob that does not earn its own Config row until someone asks; if a user wants to tune it, they change the constant in `src/intel.js` and rebuild. Document in code comment that this is the "3d default per Grepolis vacation cap norm" — players who go on vacation usually take at least 3-7 days off, so anything silent for longer is the actionable signal.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** Read-only. Skips the rest of §7 per `docs/plans/v4/README.md` and plan 27 §13. Never invents a game endpoint. Reads `state.findings` only.

## 8. Failure modes

- **No findings at all:** empty-state row, no log. `intelGhostTowns` returns `[]`.
- **All findings filtered by 7d:** `gbLogT('intel-ghost-empty', 300000, …)` fires once; empty-state row renders. The trip wire is the same one that catches a ts-in-seconds client.
- **Town seen only in outgoing farm raids (no `defender`):** the `last` finding for that town has `defender = null` and `town.id` set (the raid was on a known city id via `parseReport:79`). `abandoned` flag is **not** set (we have an attacker on record, just not a defender), so the row reads `sin nombre de defensor` only when a defenderless finding is the most recent. Honest unknown — the precondition invariant in CLAUDE.md.
- **`last.wall` unknown:** render `?`, not `0`. Same rule as 2.2.
- **User deletes the intel tab section markup:** `panel.querySelector('.intel-ghost')` returns null; `renderIntelGhost` early-returns. The function never throws on missing DOM (matches `renderIntel` line 76-79 pattern).

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 (Low risk) — Preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

1. Build, install, open a world with at least 5 reports covering a mix: one town last seen today, one town last seen 4 days ago, one town whose last defender was on vacation, one farm village with no defender in the most recent raid.
2. Open the Intel tab. The new ghost-towns table appears below the (eventual) timeline table. The 4-days-ago town shows `Xd` age and `sin actividad 3d` reason. The vacation town shows `defensor en vacaciones`. The defenderless village shows `sin nombre de defensor`. The today town is **absent** (it is not stale — `< GHOST_STALE_MS`).
3. Force a vacation flag in console: `state.findings[0].defender.vacation = true`; reopen Intel. The row reappears with `defensor en vacaciones` reason. (The redaction pipeline at `ui.js:1061` does not touch `vacation`.)
4. Sort by `Edad` desc; close+reopen the panel — sort survives via `state.tabFilters.sort:intel-ghost`.
5. Preflight row "findings schema" still passes; journal still silent (no entries).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-building and per-hero "what changed while you were away".** Owned by 2.1 + 2.2. 2.3 only reports the *fact* of staleness; the diff lives in 2.2.
- **Auto-fire a follow-up spy on a stale town.** That is plan 4.1 (auto-spy scheduler) with a per-target cadence. Out of scope here — 2.3 is read-mostly.
- **Webhooks / alerts for ghost detection.** No event surface; would add noise. If a future user wants it, add `alertWebhook('ghost', payload)` behind a `state.intelGhostAlert === true` toggle. Defer until asked.
- **Player-level inactivity.** Plan 2.4 owns that axis (group by `intelPlayerKey`, not by town). Different table, different sort.
- **Tombstone / outpost intel.** No game endpoint exists in the bridge model. Plan 27 §0 — do not invent endpoints.

## 2.4-player-inactivity-tracker.md

# 2.4 — Player inactivity tracker

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js` (additive) + small markup addition in `src/ui.js` intel section
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `intelPlayerKey` (`src/intel.js:1-10`) is the canonical string key for a player. Object-with-id ⇒ `'id:<n>'`; bare string ⇒ trimmed; object with name only ⇒ `String(name)`. Used by `intelDossiers` (line 34-71) and `intelPatternScan` (line 206-245).
- `intelDossiers` (intel.js:34-71) already aggregates findings by player and surfaces `last` (max ts) per player, plus `reports`, `units[]`, `towns[]`, `walls[]`, and the player note from `state.playerNotes[name]` (line 65). It does **not** score inactivity — a player last seen 30 days ago and a player last seen 30 minutes ago are both rendered with the same flat `reports: N` line.
- `intelPatternScan` (intel.js:206-245) groups findings by attacker in a 24h window, fires a webhook at `hits >= 3`, and writes `state.attackPatternNote`. It is the **opposite** signal (active recently) and uses a different window (24h, hard-coded at line 208).
- `watchMatch` (intel.js:145-184) + `intelWatchlistScan` (intel.js:186-205) tracks a saved list of players/towns and fires `alertWebhook('attack', …)` when a new finding matches. Bookkeeping: `state.watchHits[m.rule] = Date.now()` (line 199), persisted via `STORE.WATCH_HITS` (header.js:170, in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` line 211). This is a "still active" signal, not an inactivity one.
- 2.2 Enemy city timeline introduces `const INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS = 7 * 86400000;` in `intel.js`. 2.4 reuses it.
- Plan 27 §9 already-shipped list does **not** mention a player inactivity tracker. The closest is the `attackPatternNote` (intel.js:109-110) which is the active-player signal. 2.4 is net-new and the inverse view.

## 2. Gap

`intelDossiers` answers "who do we know?" and `intelPatternScan` answers "who is hitting us right now?". Neither answers "who has gone quiet?" — the player we used to see every day, who stopped two weeks ago, who is worth a re-spy because they may have gone on vacation or been replaced. A scout who farms 20 nearby players needs that signal: prioritise re-spy on the inactive, leave the active ones alone. 2.4 closes the gap with a per-player last-seen view, grouped by both attacker and defender axes so the user can see "incoming is quiet" *and* "outgoing scouts are quiet" independently.

## 3. Design

- New function `intelPlayerInactivity(opts)` in `intel.js`. Reads `state.findings` only — no new storage.
- For each finding, contribute to **two** player-keyed maps:
  - `attackerMap[key]` — bumped when `intelPlayerKey(f.attacker)` is not null. Captures "this player attacked".
  - `defenderMap[key]` — bumped when `intelPlayerKey(f.defender)` is not null. Captures "this player was attacked".
  - Skip the `me`-self signal: `intelActorIsMe(actor, me)` (`src/intel.js:28-33`) — if either side resolves to `intelMyIdentity()` (intel.js:17-27), do not count it as "other-player activity". The same self-discard rule `intelDossiers` uses at intel.js:40-44.
- Filter both maps to entries with `lastTs >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (7d), so a player who vanished two months ago does not pollute the list. 2.2/2.3 set this constant; this is the third consumer.
- Score per player per axis:
  - **inactive** if `now - lastTs >= PLAYER_INACTIVE_MS` (default 5 × 86400000 = 5 days). The 5d default sits between the 3d ghost-town window (2.3) and the 7d retention ceiling — players who go on vacation usually take 5-14 days off; 5d is the actionable threshold for "re-spy them".
  - **disappeared** if `now - lastTs >= PLAYER_DISAPPEARED_MS` (default 14 × 86400000 = 14 days). Hard cutoff above which re-spying is wasteful — the player is most likely gone for good.
- Output: two tables.
  - `Attackers` (offense axis): rows = sorted by `(inactive-desc, lastTs-asc)`. Capped at 30.
  - `Defenders` (defense axis): same shape, capped at 30.
  - Each row carries `player` (from `intelPlayerLabel`, intel.js:11-16), `lastTs`, `ageMs`, `n` (report count), `inactive` flag, `disappeared` flag, and the `intelPlayerLabel`-derived `note` if `state.playerNotes[noteKey]` is set (matches `intelDossiers` line 65).
- Render: a single sibling `<div class="intel-inactive">` containing two sub-tables (`intel-inactive-atk` and `intel-inactive-def`), each built via `tableShell` + `makeSortable` with the sticky-sort `state.tabFilters` key already wired (`src/ui.js:1-13`).
- No scheduler. No `gbInterval`. No `GB_LOCK_TTL`. No `STORE` / `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry. No `configVer` bump. No `alertWebhook` (passive view; the user is the consumer).

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `const PLAYER_INACTIVE_MS = 5 * 86400000;` and `const PLAYER_DISAPPEARED_MS = 14 * 86400000;` at module top alongside `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (2.2 item 1) and `GHOST_STALE_MS` (2.3 item 1). One block of constants, in one file.
2. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelPlayerInactivity()`: walks `state.findings.filter(f => f.ts >= now - INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS)`, drops self per `intelActorIsMe` (line 28-33), populates two maps keyed by `intelPlayerKey` (line 1-10), records `{ lastTs, n }` per entry, sorts, computes `inactive`/`disappeared` flags, returns `{ attackers: [...], defenders: [...] }`. Cap each at 30 entries.
3. `src/intel.js` — add `function renderIntelInactive()`: builds two sub-tables via `tableShell`, headers `['Jugador', 'Última', 'Edad', 'Informes', 'Nota']`, keys `'intel-inactive-atk'` and `'intel-inactive-def'`. Each row uses `patchCells` (`src/ui.js:92-110`). Empty state per table: `'sin atacantes inactivos (5d)'` / `'sin defensores inactivos (5d)'`.
4. `src/ui.js` — add `<div class="intel-inactive" style="font-size:11px;margin-top:6px">` inside the intel section, right after the `<div class="intel-ghost">` (added by 2.3 item 5). Contains the two sub-tables; renders empty in the layout until 2.4 ships.
5. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (line 75) to call `renderIntelInactive()` after `renderIntelGhost()`. The text `<pre>` dump at line 75-114 stays unchanged.
6. `src/intel.js` — Spanish label helpers: `inactiveAgeLabel(ageMs)` reuses `ghostAgeLabel` shape from 2.3 (or inlines the same `fmtSec` reduction if 2.3 has not shipped yet). `inactiveStatusLabel(row)` returns `'inactivo'` / `'desaparecido'` / `''` based on the two flags. Strings only.
7. `src/intel.js` — at the head of `intelPlayerInactivity`, log once via `gbLogT('intel-inactive-empty', 300000, 'intel: player inactivity empty after 7d filter')` when both maps are empty. Independent throttle key from 2.2/2.3 so the three coexist without bundling.

## 5. State & storage

- No new `state.*` fields.
- No new `STORE.*` keys.
- No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.
- No `configVer` bump.
- Retention: reuses `INTEL_HISTORY_TTL_MS` (7d) from plan 2.2. **One** retention policy for the read trio. The `PLAYER_INACTIVE_MS` (5d) and `PLAYER_DISAPPEARED_MS` (14d) are *score* thresholds, not retention TTLs — a player who vanished 20 days ago is still represented in the source data (up to 7d) but excluded from the inactive output by the retention filter, which is the correct behaviour.

## 6. Config surface

None. The two score thresholds are hard-coded defaults in `intel.js`. If a user wants a stricter "inactive" definition, they edit the constant. Same rationale as 2.3: knobs that nobody has asked for do not earn Config rows. Comment each constant with the heuristic ("5d = typical Grepolis vacation cap floor; 14d = likely abandoned").

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** Read-only. Skips the rest of §7 per `docs/plans/v4/README.md` and plan 27 §13. Never invents a game endpoint. Reads `state.findings` only.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Self-pollution:** if `intelMyIdentity()` is unreadable (the `try { … } catch { return { id: null, name: null } }` at `src/intel.js:18-26`), `intelActorIsMe` returns `false` for everything and the user's own attacks/incidents show up in the tables. Acceptable: the rule degrades to "show everything" when the identity is blind, not "silently drop". The precondition invariant in CLAUDE.md says exactly that — never silently dead.
- **Empty `state.findings`:** empty-state rows, no log.
- **All findings filtered by 7d:** `gbLogT('intel-inactive-empty', 300000, …)` fires once; empty-state rows render.
- **Player name collision across worlds:** not a concern here because the function reads `state.findings` which is **already** world-scoped via `STORE.FINDINGS` in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:194`). No additional scoping needed.
- **`intelPlayerKey` returns null** (no id, no name — `nameOf` saw a player block with neither): finding is dropped from the map. The active-player `intelPatternScan` has the same drop at intel.js:214 (`if (!key || key === 'unknown') return;`). Consistent.
- **No `note` in `state.playerNotes`:** render the empty cell, do not fabricate a placeholder. Same as `intelDossiers` (line 65: `if (state.playerNotes && state.playerNotes[noteKey]) d.note = …`).

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 (Low risk) — Preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

1. Build, install, open a world with a mix: a player who attacked you yesterday, a player who attacked you 6 days ago, a player you attacked 20 days ago, the `me` player (self).
2. Open the Intel tab. The new "Atacantes" sub-table shows the 6-day-ago attacker as `inactivo`, the yesterday attacker absent (`< 5d`). "Defensores" sub-table shows the 20-day-ago defender absent (filtered by 7d retention). Self is absent from both.
3. Click a row in "Atacantes" — no nav, no post. The note column reads the existing `state.playerNotes[name]` if set; empty otherwise.
4. Sort by `Edad` desc; close+reopen the panel — sort survives via `state.tabFilters.sort:intel-inactive-atk` and `sort:intel-inactive-def`.
5. Force self-pollution: from console, `state.findings[0].attacker.name = '<my name>'`; reopen. The row now shows up — confirms the self-discard rule works (and degrades cleanly when identity is blind).
6. Preflight row "findings schema" still passes; journal still silent (no entries).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-building and per-hero "what this player has changed".** Owned by 2.1 + 2.2. 2.4 is a presence signal, not a diff.
- **Auto-fire a re-spy on inactive players.** Plan 4.1 (auto-spy scheduler) with per-target cadence. Out of scope — 2.4 is read-mostly.
- **Webhooks / alerts on inactivity transitions.** No event surface. If a user wants it, add `alertWebhook('inactive', payload)` behind a `state.intelInactiveAlert === true` toggle. Defer.
- **Alliance-level inactivity aggregation.** Owned by 7.5 (NAP / war tracking) and 7.6 (alliance member activity). Different grouping axis, different view.
- **Activity heatmap by hour-of-day.** The data shape is there (`f.ts`), but the visualisation is owned by 6.12 (city growth timeline chart) and 6.13 (alliance intel heatmap). Reusing a chart widget belongs in those plans.
- **Player notes setter.** Already coded at `intelSetNote` (`src/intel.js:115-120`) and wired at `ui.js:997-1001`. 2.4 only reads `state.playerNotes`; never writes.

## 2.5-battle-report-analyzer.md

# 2.5 — Battle report analyzer

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js`
**Depends on:** none (data source `state.findings` is already populated; 2.1 will widen what is parseable but is not a prerequisite)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `parseReport(id, data)` (`src/parse-inline.js:33-93`) returns the canonical
  finding shape: `{id, ts, type, attacker, defender, town:{id,name,x,y}, units,
  resources, loot, outcome, wall, alliance, vill_id, vacation}`. Both
  `attacker` and `defender` go through `nameOf()` (`src/parse-inline.js:1-16`)
  and carry `{id, name, town_id, town_name, alliance, vacation}`.
- `state.findings[]` is the sole ingester target. `spy.js:249`
  (`state.findings.unshift(parsed)`) is the writer; `spy.js:250-253` caps it at
  500 rows; `spy.js:254` saves to `STORE.FINDINGS`. `core.js:1167-1171` does
  the same prune offline.
- `intelDossiers()` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) already aggregates findings into
  per-player dossiers and is the Intel-tab section "Fichas"
  (`src/intel.js:92-97`). It counts reports and the last-seen timestamp but
  does **not** compute loss/win ratios or per-village profitability — that is
  exactly the gap 2.5 fills.
- `intelPatternScan()` (`src/intel.js:206-245`) already counts ≥3 findings per
  attacker in a 24h window and emits a `pattern` webhook — that is the
  "attack pattern" feature shipped per plan 27 §9 and is not duplicated here.
- `findingsFilter` (`src/core.js:280`, persisted via `STORE.FINDINGS_FILTER`,
  key already in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`) is honoured by the Findings tab
  (`src/ui.js:1688-1693`). The Intel tab does **not** honour it (it is a
  summary view by design); 2.5 keeps that line.
- `unitMeta(id)` (`src/attack.js:31-...`) returns per-unit metadata including
  `population` and `attack`/`defense`/`hp`/`is_naval` — the natural weighting
  for loss ratio. `defenseLocalStrength` (`src/wonder.js:142`) already uses
  `unit population` as the weight when scoring a town's defensive power,
  so this codebase precedent is settled.
- Plan 27 §9 already lists "Battle report basics" as shipped at `intel.js
  (13.x)`. 2.5 is the **delta over** what plans 12 + 13 already shipped:
  support ETA + attack-pattern alert. Per plan 26 §B2 quality bar, treat
  that §9 row as confirmed but not as a synonym for 2.5.

## 2. Gap

The Intel tab shows a count of reports per player but no per-player **outcome
profile** (how much loot you extracted, how many losses you took, how often
you won), and no per-farm-village **profitability** ranking. Without these,
the "top farms" question is answered by inspection of every Findings row.

## 3. Design

Two derivations over `state.findings`, both pure read-mostly, both fire once
per Intel-tab render:

- **`intelLossRatio()`** — for each player in the dossier set, sum attacker-loss
  and defender-loss pop separately (where the player IS the attacker, count
  their losses; where they ARE the defender, count the losses they inflicted
  on the attacker). Use `unitMeta(id).population` for weight; unknown units
  are skipped, not estimated. Output: `{attacker, wins, losses, popLost,
  popKilled, ratio}`. Stored on the dossier object as `d.loss = {...}`,
  independent of the existing `reports`/`last` fields.
- **`intelFarmProfitability()`** — derive from `state.findings` rows where
  `vill_id` is set (farm-village raids) and `state.playerNotes[attacker]` or
  dossier shows the player was the attacker. Aggregate per `vill_id`: raid
  count, sum of `loot.wood+stone+iron` (or `resources` — same shape, see
  `parse-inline.js:25-31`), ratio of raids that returned loot > 0. Output:
  `[{vill_id, name, raids, haul, successRate}]` sorted by `(haul / max(raids,
  1)) desc`. Cut at top 20 for the panel; full list goes in the export.

Both depend only on `parseReport` output already captured. Nothing is fetched.
Both re-use `intelPlayerKey`/`intelPlayerLabel`/`intelActorIsMe`
(`src/intel.js:1-33`) — no new identity helpers.

The aggregate is computed when `renderIntel()` (`src/intel.js:75-114`) runs
(15s loop, `boot.js:108-115`) and stamped into the session snapshot
`state.intelSnapshot = { computedAt, lossByPlayer, topFarms }`. The snapshot
is **not** persisted — derived cheaply on demand, and any historical view
over `state.findings` already trims to 500 rows. Stats tab (`src/stats.js:480`
already reads `state.findings.length`) does not change.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/intel.js`** — add `intelLossRatio(findings)` taking the (already
   pre-filtered by `intelDossiers`) dossier set + raw findings, returning a
   `Map<playerKey, lossStats>`. Pure function, no side effects.
2. **`src/intel.js`** — extend `intelDossiers()` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) to
   accept the loss map and attach `d.loss` to each entry. Keep the existing
   shape additive; the Intel tab text render at `src/intel.js:92-97` stays
   compatible.
3. **`src/intel.js`** — add `intelFarmProfitability(findings, me)` returning
   `[{vill_id, name, raids, haul, successRate}]` sorted by haul-per-raid,
   capped at 20. Uses `parseReport.vill_id` (`src/parse-inline.js:90`) as the
   farm town id and `loot/resources.wood/stone/iron` (same shape, `parse-inline.js:86`)
   for the haul. When `me` is unknown the function still returns the
   unsorted set (so Export works); sorting by "yours" only happens when
   `intelActorIsMe(attacker, intelMyIdentity())` is true.
4. **`src/intel.js`** — extend `renderIntel()` (`src/intel.js:75-114`) with
   two new sections after the existing `Fichas` block: `=== Pérdidas ===`
   shows the top 5 by `losses/popLost desc`, `=== Granjas top ===` shows the
   top farms. Sections are appended to the same `<pre class="intel-panel">`.
5. **`src/ui.js`** — add a Config checkbox `[data-cfg=intel-battle-stats]`
   (default ON) bound through the existing `bindToggle` pattern
   (`src/ui.js:1364-1370`). When OFF the Intel tab still renders the dossier
   list and the threat board but skips the two new sections. Default ON
   because the computation is O(N) over 500 rows.
6. **`src/ui.js`** — extend the panel markup at `src/ui.js:692-705` (Intel
   tab) only if a manual refresh button is wanted; otherwise the 15s
   renderIntel cadence (`boot.js:108-115`) is sufficient. Skipped by default.

## 5. State & storage

- **No new `state.*` field, no new STORE key.** Output is recomputed per
  render from existing `state.findings`. Plan 27 §9 already credits the
  surface to intel.js, and plan 26 §B6 warned us not to ship "Config-shaped
  boolean that does nothing" — same logic for state.
- `STORE.FINDINGS` (`src/header.js:25`) is already in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
  (`src/header.js:194`); 2.5 inherits that.
- `STORE.FINDINGS_FILTER` is already loaded into `state.findingsFilter`
  (`src/core.js:280`). 2.5 does **not** consult it (the Intel summary is not
  the filtered Findings tab) and explicitly says so in §3 to avoid surprising
  the user.
- Bumping `configVer` is unnecessary: 2.5 adds a feature-toggle field but
  defaults it ON, with the absence behaving like a missing toggle being read
  as `true` (consistent with how `state.csAlert !== false` is treated at
  `src/intel.js:191`, `src/core.js:335`, `src/ui.js:1333`).
- No prune TTL — derived, not stored.

## 6. Config surface

- One toggle: `[data-cfg=intel-battle-stats]` default ON. Persisted to
  `STORE.FINDINGS_FILTER` would be wrong (semantically unrelated); instead
  co-store as a sub-key on the existing toggle pattern, but since the
  feature is **derived not stored**, the toggle is a UI switch bound through
  `bindToggle(sel, 'intelBattleStats', STORE.INTEL_BATTLE_STATS)` only if
  step 5 is implemented with persistence. If persistence is deferred (it is
  for this plan), the toggle is a per-session checkbox read at render time
  with no save call — that is honest and matches `csAlert`'s read-time
  default without a setter in scope.
- **HIGH-RISK?** No — read-only aggregation.

## 7. Post surface & safety

None. Read-only. Plan 27 §0 and §1 reinforce this; no `bridgePost`, no
`gameAjaxPost`, no `gbAjaxWatch`. Nothing routes through the captcha breaker.
Nothing in §7 (post surface) applies — by plan 26 §B2 and README §7: "Skip
the rest" is the right move.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`parseReport` returns null** (`src/parse-inline.js:48-54`) — silently
  dropped at intake (`src/spy.js:237-241`); no impact on the aggregation.
- **Unit metadata missing for an attacker unit id** — `unitMeta(id)`
  (called via `wonder.js` style with `Object.entries`) returns `null` or
  `undefined`. The aggregator must `if (!m || m.is_naval) skip` (navel units
  do not appear in farm raids; the existing precedent is
  `wonder.js:defenseLocalStrength` which filters `m.is_naval`). Per CLAUDE.md
  "Precondition invariant": unreadable == unknown == skip, never estimate.
- **Identity loss** — `intelMyIdentity()` (`src/intel.js:17-27`) returns
  `{id:null, name:null}` on read failure; `intelActorIsMe()` (`src/intel.js:28-33`)
  then returns `false`, so "yours" filtering falls back to the unsorted
  export. Do not log a warning on every render — throttle via
  `gbLogT('intel-identity-blind', 300000, ...)`.
- **`state.findings` > 500** — already capped at intake (`src/spy.js:250-253`
  and `src/core.js:1167-1171`). Aggregation re-runs cleanly after the cap.
- **`vill_id` field absent** in older report shapes — `parseReport`
  (`src/parse-inline.js:90`) defensively falls back through `r.vill_id ???
  r.farm_town_id ?? null`; absent rows contribute zero raids to that farm.

## 9. Validation gate

Plan 27 §11 risk class Low: preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

- Preflight row `intel: battle stats`: pass when `state.findings.length`
  reads; warn (not fail) when `<5` findings (sample size too small to be
  meaningful).
- Manual: let one farm-cycle run with `intel-battle-stats=ON`, then visit
  the Intel tab. Expected: `=== Pérdidas ===` shows the player whose
  attacker appears most often, ranked by losses desc; `=== Granjas top ===`
  shows the farm villages sorted by haul-per-raid. Log shows no new entries
  (read-only).
- After a known-loss battle (loss to a CS or to a stronger player), the
  player's row in `Pérdidas` should reflect it within the next 15s render
  tick (`boot.js:108-115`).
- Export (Actions → Copy config): the snapshot must round-trip through
  `qolExportConfig`'s redaction contract (`qol.js:251-256`, `redact:true` in
  `src/core.js:347`). The aggregator's output is *not* part of the export;
  only the toggle state is, when persisted.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Spy report deep parse** (plan 27 §2.1, "buildings + hero + res"): 2.5
  only consumes what `parseReport` already returns. When 2.1 lands and adds
  building levels / hero roster, 2.5's `intelFarmProfitability` will get
  richer without a re-write — by reading `f.buildings` / `f.hero` from the
  same `parsed` shape it already walks.
- **Attack pattern alerts** (plan 13, `intel.js:206-245`): already shipped.
  2.5 adds losses + farms, not duplicate pattern emission.
- **Spy report timeline** (plan 27 §2.2): own plan, separate call site.
- **Counter-intel** (plan 27 §4.2 = this plan's sibling 4.2): entirely
  different signal — who is **spying you**, not who is attacking. 4.2 owns it.
- **Threat assessment engine** (plan 27 §5.3 = this cluster's 5.3): writes a
  score; 2.5 reads no risk field and emits none.
- **Persist the snapshot** — recomputing on every render (500 rows × 2
  passes) is well below the 250ms renderLog threshold
  (`src/intel.js:renderLog` flush, set in CLAUDE.md).

## 2.6-farm-profitability-ranking.md

# 2.6 — Farm profitability ranking (res/min + travel)

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/farms.js`
**Depends on:** none (one of the §2 data-plane items; 5.2 will consume the rank)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/farms.js`, `src/bridge.js`, `src/core.js`.

- **Per-village stock is NOT in the bridge model.** Plan 26 §A1 proved
  `fetchFarmResources` (`farms.js:722-815`) is dead — `ACTION_GUESSES`
  (`farms.js:694`) never resolves on this world, the circuit breaker
  (`farms.js:651-692`) keeps `state.farmScrapeState.dead = true` after two
  0-ok sweeps, and plan 26 closes with: "Farm-village stock is not in the
  bridge model". `parseResourceJson` (`src/parse-inline.js:143-166`) reads
  the response when the ladder happens to land, but the response comes from
  the HTTP endpoint, not from `MM`/`ITowns`. The only in-bridge village
  attributes are listed in `farmsFromGame()` `farms.js:226-238`:
  `vill_id`, `relation_id`, `x`/`y` (island coords, `f.island_x`/`f.island_y`),
  `lootable_at`, `name`, `_rel`, `_attrs`. **There is no field that reports
  current village stock.** That is the honesty ceiling on this feature.
- **Claim payload returns no amount.** `state.claimTpl` (`farms.js:10-15`,
  `core.js:250`) only carries `model_url`/`action_name`/`arguments`/
  `town_id`; the bridge callback for `FarmTownPlayerRelation/claim` carries
  `err` (or nothing) but no loot totals. `verifyClaims`
  (`farms.js:633-643`) proves a claim landed by re-reading `lootable_at`,
  not by measuring the haul. So **historical yield per village is also not
  in the bridge model today.**
- **Per-village x,y and per-town x,y ARE in the bridge model.** `farms.js:230-231`
  stores `f.island_x`/`f.island_y` from the `FarmTown` collection; `farms.js:280-281`
  reads `getIslandCoordinateX()`/`getIslandCoordinateY()` from `ITowns.towns[tid]`.
  Same-island town resolution already runs in `townIdForFarm` (`farms.js:291-299`)
  via `islandTownMap()` (`farms.js:270-290`), which keys on `x + ',' + y`. Same
  island ⇒ same numeric coordinate frame ⇒ distance is computable.
- **Durations and loyalty are known.** `farmOptionMap` (`farms.js:325-329`)
  maps duration → option index for whatever the player has hand-taught
  (`farmSnapDuration` snaps to `FARM_DURATIONS` `farms.js:320`). Loyalty
  status per town is `farmLoyaltyResearched(townId)` (`farms.js:379-409`)
  with a 60s cache at `farms.js:382`.
- **Best-duration picker already exists.** `farmDurationPick(townId)`
  (`farms.js:426-445`) walks `FARM_PICK_LADDER = [600, 1200, 2400, 5400, 10800, 14400]`
  and returns the longest learned option that fits warehouse headroom, using
  `ROOM_PER_HOUR = 8000` (`farms.js:435`) and `SAFE_FILL_PCT = 0.6` as a
  very rough expected-haul estimate.
- **No travel-time helper for farms.** `Movement`/`getTravelTime` are
  referenced only in `recruit.js`, `bandit.js`, `favor.js`, `planner.js:163`,
  `attack.js`, `native-ui.js:614` — never for farm-village → own-town path.
  Distance in island-coordinate units has to be computed manually
  (Euclidean `sqrt(dx² + dy²)`).
- **No ranking column.** `renderFarms` (`src/ui.js:122-170`) shows id, name,
  W, S, I, pop, seen + a THR button; sort key is `tr.dataset.sort`
  (`ui.js:165`). User-saved sort applies via `sortApplySaved` (`ui.js:169`).
  `tableShell` (`ui.js:35-49`) adds click-to-sort. There is **no**
  res/min or profitability column.
- **Plan 27 §9 lists 15 already-shipped ideas.** None covers farm
  profitability ranking; closest is "Battle report basics" (`intel.js`,
  extends in 2.5). 2.6 is genuinely new.

## 2. Gap

`renderFarms` is a flat, alphabetical-by-id table with the columns the
bridge scrape used to feed. With the scrape dead (plan 26 §A1), every
row but id/name is `-` most of the time, and the player has no way to see
which of their villages actually pays back the slot against the option
they taught the bot. The data we DO have (x/y, learned durations, loyalty,
town warehouse headroom) is enough to estimate `res/min` per village and
rank by it; we just do not compute or render it today.

## 3. Design

Compute a per-village **expected resource rate** from signals that are
actually in the bridge model, then surface it in `renderFarms` as a
sortable column. The rank is intentionally an *estimate* (the actual
haul per village is unknowable — see §1). The function lives in
`farms.js` as a pure helper; nothing posts.

Inputs (all read-only):

- `farmOptionMap` (`farms.js:325-329`) — longest *learned* duration the
  player has hand-taught (the seed `{300:1}` (`core.js:255`) means 300s is
  always known). This is the longest claim the bot is allowed to fire
  here, capped by `farmDurationPick(townId)` against warehouse headroom.
- `island_x`, `island_y` (`farms.js:230-231`) — village coordinates.
- `islandTownMap()` (`farms.js:270-290`) → `townIdForFarm(f)`
  (`farms.js:291-299`) — owning town id (already used by `claimFarm`).
- `townResState(townId)` (`src/bridge.js:235-273`) — town warehouse
  headroom; used by `farmDurationPick`. **Unreadable ⇒ `null` ⇒ the
  village is excluded from the rank with `score: null`** (precondition
  invariant: do not block on an unreadable value).
- `farmLoyaltyResearched(townId)` (`farms.js:379-409`) — bool with 60s
  cache. Cached lookup, no new I/O.

Formula (single helper `farmProfitScore(farm) → { score, duration, distance, loyalty, headroom }`):

```
const learned  = longest learned option in farmOptionMap (>= 300, <= farmDurationPick cap);
const duration = learned;                            // seconds
const loyalty  = farmLoyaltyResearched(tid) ? 1.0 : 0.5;  // 50% penalty mirrors the in-game multiplier
const headroom = townResState(tid)?.cap - max(wood, stone, iron);  // null ⇒ blind
const expected = (duration / 3600) * ROOM_PER_HOUR * loyalty;      // 8000/h baseline
const distance = euclideanIslandDist(farm, tid);                   // > 0 only if cross-island? same island only.
const travel   = distance * TRAVEL_SEC_PER_UNIT;                   // const, pin in Config
const cycleSec = duration + travel;
const score    = expected / cycleSec;                              // res/sec; higher = better
```

`TRAVEL_SEC_PER_UNIT` defaults to **0.0** and is exposed in Config — the
in-game march formula is client-side and not in the bridge model, so a
*guess* here is the only honest choice; defaulting to 0 makes rank
distance-agnostic (the column says `dist=N/A` until the user pins a
value). On worlds without a pinned travel time the rank reduces to
**expected haul per cycle-second**, which is still useful.

Output is written to `state.farmProfit[farm.vill_id] = { score, duration,
distance, loyalty, ts }` (key in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`, `header.js:193-214`).
Pruned alongside `state.farmResources` at `core.js:1177-1182`.

`renderFarms` (`ui.js:122-170`) gets a new `res/min` column between
`pop` and `seen`, computed via `farmProfitScore` lazily inside the row
build (no pre-pass; same loop). Sort key adds the score at the end
(`ui.js:165`) so `sortApplySaved` keeps working.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/farms.js`: add module-local `ROOM_PER_HOUR` (move the 8000 from
   `farmDurationPick:435` to module scope) and `TRAVEL_SEC_PER_UNIT`
   (default 0). Add `farmProfitScore(farm)` per §3. Memoize per village id
   for 5min via a `farmProfitCache` map (consistent with the
   `farmLoyaltyCache` pattern at `farms.js:369-372`).
2. `src/farms.js`: write `state.farmProfit[vill_id] = { score, duration,
   distance, loyalty, ts }`. Add prune in `refreshFarmsParsed`
   (`farms.js:255-268`) using the same `pruneMapsToIds` pattern as
   `state.farmResources` (`farms.js:265`).
3. `src/core.js`: add `state.farmTravelSecPerUnit: load(STORE.FARM_TRAVEL, 0)`
   near the existing farm state block at `core.js:256-261`. Add
   `STORE.FARM_TRAVEL: 'grepbot:farm-travel-sec-per-unit'` to
   `src/header.js` and to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:193-214`).
4. `src/core.js`: register `state.farmProfit: load(STORE.FARM_PROFIT, {})`
   so it survives reloads (this is the id-bearing key — `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`).
5. `src/ui.js:130`: extend `tableShell` header from
   `['id', 'name', 'W', 'S', 'I', 'pop', 'seen', '']` to
   `['id', 'name', 'W', 'S', 'I', 'pop', 'res/min', 'seen', '']`. Add a
   `farmCells(f)` cell (`ui.js:109-121`) for the rank: `'-'` if
   `state.farmProfit[id]?.score == null`, else `Math.round(score * 60)`
   followed by a `±` flag if the village was excluded for blind
   headroom.
6. `src/ui.js:165`: append the score (or `-Infinity` for null) to the
   `tr.dataset.sort` so the existing `sortApplySaved` (`ui.js:169`)
   handles default-rank sort without a code path change.
7. `src/ui.js` Config tab: add a numeric input labelled
   `Segundos de marcha por unidad de isla` (placeholder `0`), bound to
   `state.farmTravelSecPerUnit`, save via `save(wkey(STORE.FARM_TRAVEL), …)`.
   Default 0 (rank is distance-agnostic). `configVer` bump per
   `qol.js qolExportConfig`.
8. `src/stats.js`: add a `farm profit` row to the Preflight output that
   reports `(scored, blind)` over `state.farmParsed` so a 0-scored world
   is visible without re-deriving.

## 5. State & storage

- New: `state.farmProfit` (object keyed by `vill_id`; per-row
  `{score, duration, distance, loyalty, ts}`).
- New: `state.farmTravelSecPerUnit` (number, default 0, Config-editable).
- New: `STORE.FARM_PROFIT: 'grepbot:farm-profit'` and
  `STORE.FARM_TRAVEL: 'grepbot:farm-travel-sec-per-unit'` in
  `src/header.js`. Both go in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
  (`header.js:193-214`).
- `configVer` bump in `qol.js qolExportConfig` for the new Config field
  (re-export round-trips through redaction per `qol.js:230`).
- Prune: `state.farmProfit` pruned in `refreshFarmsParsed` alongside
  `state.farmResources` (`farms.js:265`). 5min in-memory memo for the
  score (loosely mirrors `farmLoyaltyCache` at `farms.js:369`).

## 6. Config surface

- Toggle: none. Feature is always-on and read-only.
- Numeric field: `Segundos de marcha por unidad de isla` (default 0).
  Lives in the Farms Config group. Re-ranks all rows on change (memo TTL
  is 5min; force-recompute on input change).

No HIGH-RISK toggle (no post surface, plan 27 marks Low).

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** This feature is purely a derivation + render change.
It reads `farmOptionMap`, `islandTownMap`, `townResState`, and
`farmLoyaltyResearched`, all already in use by `claimFarm` /
`farmDurationPick`. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbXhr`.

Therefore: no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry, no
`gbCaptchaPause` key, no `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no dry-run
gate.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`townResState(townId)` returns null.** Precondition invariant: the
  rank for that village is `null`, the `res/min` column shows `-`, and
  the row drops to the bottom on default sort. `gbLogT('farm-profit-blind-' + villId, 600000, …)`
  fires once per village per 10min (mirroring `wh-unknown-` at
  `farms.js:307`). The bot never blocks a claim on this signal
  (`farmDurationPick` already handles a null headroom by falling back to
  300s at `farms.js:442`).
- **`farmLoyaltyResearched` cache miss / not researched.** Default
  multiplier is 0.5 (matches the in-game "no loyalty" penalty). On a
  world where the research id is `villagers_loyalty` and the bot's
  `FARM_LOYALTY_RE` (`farms.js:368`) does not match, the bot stays at
  0.5 forever; that is a known failure of the existing detector, not a
  regression of this plan.
- **`farmOptionMap` empty for the village.** Seed `{300:1}` (`core.js:255`)
  guarantees a 5min option is always known. Rank uses 300s in that
  case; res/min is necessarily low.
- **`f.x`/`f.y` null.** `farms.js:292` already drops these in
  `townIdForFarm` (no same-island town). Profit row is excluded
  (`score: null`, log once).
- **Bridge model renames a getter.** `farmLoyaltyResearched` is wrapped
  in `try/catch` (`farms.js:406`); `townResState` does the same
  (`bridge.js:244,250`). Renames surface as `null` and the village
  ranks to bottom; the rank never silently invents a value.
- **`state.farmProfit` bloat.** Capped by `pruneMapsToIds` to the live
  farm id set; one row per village, payload <100 bytes.

## 9. Validation gate

Low-risk (plan 27 §11: Preflight + one in-game session).

- Open a world with ≥3 villages. Verify the Farms tab now has a `res/min`
  column; numbers are stable across reload (memo + persisted). On a
  world with the dead HTTP scrape, the W/S/I columns stay `-` and
  `res/min` is still populated from x/y + durations + loyalty.
- Pin a non-zero `Segundos de marcha por unidad de isla` (e.g. 4). Rows
  reorder; the rank falls as distance grows. Re-pin to 0; rank returns
  to duration-only.
- Hand-teach a 20min option (per plan 26 §C1). Verify a town with
  headroom ≥ ~1.6k re-ranks higher; a near-full town keeps a shorter
  option (`farmDurationPick` already clips it at `farms.js:441`).
- Preflight row `farm profit`: pass when `state.farmParsed.length > 0`
  and at least one row has a numeric score; warn when 0/0; fail never
  (read-only).
- Decisions view must show **no** new feature key (no posts).

## 10. Out of scope

- Per-village current stock (cannot be read; plan 26 §A1).
- Per-village historical yield (claim payload does not return amount).
- Per-village building bonus / hero presence (not in the bridge model
  for `FarmTown`).
- Auto-sorting the claim queue. That is plan **5.2** (adaptive farming)
  which consumes `state.farmProfit` and rotates targets under captcha /
  budget pressure. 2.6 only computes and displays.
- Per-village option index selection (which `option` index the player
  hand-taught for which duration) — that lives in `farmOptionMap`
  (`farms.js:325-329`) and is unchanged.
