## 5. State & storage

- `state.autoDump: boolean` — `STORE.AUTO_DUMP`, default **false**
  (HIGH-RISK OFF per CLAUDE.md). No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.
- `state.dumpThreshold: {wood, stone, iron}` —
  `STORE.DUMP_THRESHOLD`, defaults `{95, 95, 90}`, each clamped
  50..100.
- `state.dumpKeep: {wood, stone, iron}` — `STORE.DUMP_KEEP`,
  defaults `{50, 50, 50}`, each clamped 0..95.
- `state.dumpSinks: string[]` — `STORE.DUMP_SINKS`, default `[]`.
  Town ids are strings. The list is **not** world-scoped because
  the user's own-town ids are stable across logins on the same
  world (the world-scoped id invariant is "id means something on
  this world", which holds for own-town ids — but `dumpSinks` is
  a config-object pointer, not a foreign-world reference; the
  world-scope rule for `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` is for **data**
  carrying world-specific meaning, which `dumpSinks` does not).
  Cite plan 26 §B6 audit (`tradeMaxHops` deletion note): the
  precedent is that config-pointers to user town ids are
  world-scope by inheritance when the parent state is world-scoped.
  `dumpSinks` is therefore left out of `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
  (matches `STORE.TOWN_GROUPS` at `header.js:106`, which is in
  the world-scoped set via `header.js:202`; we leave the
  explicit registration to the migration commit if the
  parent state becomes world-scoped later).
- `configVer` bump 11 → **12** (work item 8).
- Prune TTL: not applicable.

## 6. Config surface

| Toggle / field | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `state.autoDump` | `false` | `STORE.AUTO_DUMP` |
| `state.dumpThreshold` | `{95, 95, 90}` | `STORE.DUMP_THRESHOLD` |
| `state.dumpKeep` | `{50, 50, 50}` | `STORE.DUMP_KEEP` |
| `state.dumpSinks` | `[]` | `STORE.DUMP_SINKS` |

- HIGH-RISK OFF default. The post is irreversible.
- Per-resource threshold (separate wood / stone / iron) so the user
  can keep iron at 90 % (above the cave reserve) while dumping wood
  at 95 %.
- `dumpSinks` is the explicit "dump into these own towns" knob; empty
  means "fall back to profile + transport".

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Post path is unchanged.** Every dump job runs through
  `tradeSend` (`src/trade.js:37-46`) which posts
  `gameAjaxPost('trade', 'town_info', 'trade', {id, wood, stone,
  iron, town_id, nl_init:true})`. The endpoint is in
  `TX_WRITE_FEATURES` (`src/planner.js:212-216`) and routes through
  `txRun` → `gameAjaxRaw` (`src/bridge.js:149-189`).
- **No `gbAjaxWatch` registration.** Same as 1.3 — trade is server-
  rendered.
- **No `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry.** Same as 1.3.
- **Captcha breaker.** `'trade'` (existing), shared with global
  `tradeScan` + 1.3 `transportBalanceJobs` + 5.1 `transportAiJobs` +
  sibling plan 3.1 routes. Captcha on the trade queue pauses
  everything, including the dump loop, for the ladder window.
- **Lock name.** `'trade'` (existing), TTL 180000ms
  (`src/core.js:153`). Acquired once per `tradeScan` at `trade.js:381`.
- **Dry-run.** `txActionGate` (`tx.js:522-534`) returns `'dryrun'`
  when `state.dryRun` is set. `txRun:554-562` logs
  `DRY-RUN trade: …`. Every dump send inherits this — verified by
  tracing through `gameAjaxPost → txRun → gameAjaxRaw`.
- **`ironReservedForCave` interaction.** When the source town has
  `state.autoCave` on AND `caveTownInfo(townId)` shows the hide
  building has headroom AND the ETA to cave target is within
  CAVE_SOON_MS (15 min, `core.js:683`), the dump loop **skips iron**
  on that town. Same gate as `trade.js:217-223`. A blind
  `ironReservedForCave` returns `{reserved: false}` (per
  `core.js:717` "unknown, not 'no'"), so the dump loop proceeds
  without the reservation.
- **`caveHasHeadroom` guard.** When the destination is itself a
  cave town with `state.autoCave` on, the dump only fires into
  that destination if the hide building has free space (mirrors
  the existing `cave.js:181-184` skip logic).
- **Confirm ladder for manual-trigger mode.** Optional Config
  toggle `dumpRequireConfirm` (default OFF) — when ON, a manual
  "Dump now" panel button opens a confirm modal listing the
  planned jobs and only proceeds on OK. Same pattern as the
  attack planner v0.6.0 confirm gate (`CLAUDE.md` "Attack
  planner v2"). **No effect on the orchestrator loop** — the
  confirm gate is for manual fires only; the auto loop has its
  own dry-run + decision-memory discipline.
- **No new scheduler.** No `gbInterval`. Cadence is `'trade'`
  120000ms (`qol.js:393`), jittered ±20 %.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`townResState(from)` blind.** Skip that source; log once via
  `gbLogT('dump-blind-' + from, …)`. Per scan, per town.
- **`tradeLedger` returns null (`tradeIncomingByTown()` unknown).**
  `tradeScan` fails closed (`trade.js:357`) — dump loop never runs.
- **`caveHasHeadroom(from)` blind** (cave reads return null). Skip
  iron-send on that source; log once via
  `gbLogT('dump-cave-blind-' + from, …)`. Per scan.
- **`ironReservedForCave(from) === reserved:true` and resource is
  iron.** Skip that triple. Same path as `tradeGoalJobs:301`.
- **`pickDumpDestination` returns null** (no sinks, no profile
  match, no transport fallback). Skip the source for this
  resource; no log spam (per-scan, per-resource, gbLogT-keyed).
- **`dumpThreshold[r] <= dumpKeep[r]`.** Skip that resource on
  every town; amount would be ≤ 0. Preflight warns
  (`stats.js:171` work item 9).
- **`dumpSinks` contains a town id that is not in `state.towns`.**
  Filtered out by `pickDumpDestination` before the post; logged
  once via `gbLogT('dump-sink-unknown-' + id, …)` at the
  validation gate, not per-tick.
- **Two dump picks in the same scan target the same destination.**
  `tradeApplyJob` mutates `L` after each pick, so the second pick
  sees the first's deduction and clamps itself. The 6-job ceiling
  (`tradeFillStorageJobs:168` analogue) keeps the scan bounded.
- **Captcha during a dump send.** `tradeScan` releases the trade
  lock on `'captcha'` callback (`trade.js:399`). Dump inherits.
- **Decision-memory trip.** `trade` is a write feature in
  `TX_WRITE_FEATURES` (`planner.js:212-216`); three hard errors
  open a 5/15/60min skip window. The dump loop is the latest
  sub-planner to recover after a bad window — that's the right
  behaviour for an irreversible high-stakes action.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 (Med risk + HIGH-RISK OFF): **dry-run + one
hand-triggered firing + one full orchestrator tick + payload
verification.**

1. **Dry-run smoke.** Toggle `state.dryRun` on; toggle
   `state.autoDump` on; set `dumpThreshold = {wood:50, stone:50,
   iron:50}` (force every town above threshold). Wait one trade
   tick. Expect one `DRY-RUN trade: A→B w…/s…/i…` line per
   planned dump job (max 6); zero real posts.
2. **Live, single tick.** Disable dry-run, force one scan on a
   world with one town fill > 95 % wood. Expect one
   `trade: A→B w<amount>/s0/i0` log line; verify the
   destination is `dumpSinks[0]` (when sinks are configured) or
   the transport-fallback destination otherwise.
3. **Cave guard.** On a town with `state.autoCave` on AND
   `caveThreshPct = 90`, force iron fill to 96 %. The dump loop
   **must skip iron** because the cave reserve beats the dump
   threshold. Verify via `gbLogT('dump-cave-skip-' + from, …)`.
4. **Iron-reserve-for-cave interaction.** With cave ON and iron
   fill > 95 %, force a dump. Expect iron skip; wood/stone
   dumps proceed if their thresholds are met.
5. **`dumpSinks` priority.** Set `dumpSinks = ['townB']`, force
   wood fill on town A > 95 %, wood fill on town C < 30 %. The
   destination must be **townB** (not C — the sink wins over
   the profile match). Verify in journal `decision` rows.
6. **Six-job ceiling.** Disable other sub-planners; force a
   scan with 8 valid (from, to, resource) triples via direct
   state mutation. Expect 6 picked; the next 2 wait for the
   following tick.
7. **Manual confirm gate.** Set `dumpRequireConfirm = true`;
   click "Dump now" from the panel. Expect the confirm modal
   to list the planned jobs; click Cancel → no posts; click OK
   → posts fire.
8. **Preflight row.** Stats → Preflight shows `dump: ok` when
   `autoDump === false`. Toggling on with valid thresholds flips
   to `ok`; setting `dumpThreshold.wood = 40` flips to `warn`;
   setting `autoDump === true` with empty `dumpSinks` AND no
   cave-eligible town flips to `fail`.
9. **Export round-trip.** Export config; the four new fields
   (`autoDump`, `dumpThreshold`, `dumpKeep`, `dumpSinks`) ship
   in the dump. Re-import restores them; no redact warning (no
   player data).
10. **No new scheduler.** `rg -n 'gbInterval' src/dump.js`
    returns zero hits; `rg -n 'InFlight' src/dump.js` returns zero
    hits; no new top-level `function` (IIFE only).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Auto-route discovery** ("GrepBot noticed you dump iron A→B
  every cycle…"). Plan-27 §0 out-of-scope (anti-pattern detection).
- **Inter-player dump (alliance treasury).** Grepolis does not
  expose a treasury transfer endpoint. The dump loop targets
  **own** towns only. If a future client exposes an alliance
  treasury post, 3.4 v2 widens `pickDumpDestination` with a
  fourth tier; the public surface (`dumpJobs(towns, ledger)`)
  stays the same.
- **Cave-bypass dump.** A user who wants to dump iron WITHOUT
  the cave reserve gate can set `state.autoCave = false` for that
  town via `state.caveTowns` (`src/core.js:289`). 3.4 does not
  add a per-town dump override; that is a `caveTowns` extension
  for a future plan.
- **Adaptive cadence per planner.** `orchAdaptive`
  (`orchestrate.js:107-114`) keys on the whole `'trade'` feature
  via `ORCH_JRN['trade']` (`qol.js:412`). Per-sub-planner adaptive
  cadence is a future optimisation.
- **Per-resource dump batching.** Same as 5.1 — Grepolis ships one
  resource per trade post; multi-resource dump batches are a
  future optimisation.
- **Sniffing `transportTpl`.** Plan 27 §1.3 hint; does not exist
  in the tree. The dump loop uses the existing `tradeSend`
  payload verbatim (see plan 1.3 §7 explicit unknown).

## 3.5-emergency-cave-mode.md

# 3.5 — Emergency cave mode

**Bucket:** v4.5 · **Risk:** High · **Size:** L
**Module:** new `src/emergency.js` (slot after `culture.js`, before `trade.js` in `build.py:31-72`)
**Depends on:** 5.3 threat assessment engine (a no-op when eta is null reads as 0, plan 27 §5), `cave.js` `caveTownInfo`, `cave.js` `caveStoreIron`
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `cave.js:166 caveScan(reason)` fires from `orchTick` (`orchestrate.js:4`,
  via `ORCH_HANDLERS`) and stashes iron when `state.autoCave` is on AND
  iron ≥ `state.caveThreshPct` (default 90, `core.js:288`). Toggle default
  OFF per HIGH-RISK convention (`core.js:287`). Cadence is the orchestrator
  cadence — `ORCH_CADENCE.cave` plus ±20% jitter (`orchestrate.js:115-119`).
- `cave.js:133-140 caveStoreIron(townId, amount, onDone)` posts
  `{model_url: 'BuildingHide', action_name: 'storeIron', arguments:{iron_to_store:+amount}, town_id:+townId}`
  via `bridgePost('cave', ...)`. The payload is **hardcoded** — no learned
  template, no `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` slot. Path-sniff is unnecessary here; the
  schema is set by us.
- `cave.js:26 caveTownInfo(townId)` returns `{hideLvl, iron, cap, hideCap,
  stored, unlimited}` and the `BuildingHide` model probe (`cave.js:62-68`).
  `cave.js:114 caveExcessAmount(info)` returns the iron that's currently
  past the threshold and still fits the hide, or `0` for `unreadable`.
- `dodge.js:53 dodgeIncomingMovements()` is the trusted hostile-source
  funnel — every incoming must pass `dodgeIsHostileMovement` (dodge.js:41,
  the v1.5.3 audit fix). It yields `{id, dest, origin, type, hasCs, arrival,
  units, model}` per movement. `dodge.js:181 DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC =
  15*60` is the parallel "ETA < 15min means imminent" anchor for militia;
  same constant should gate emergency cave auto.
- Per-town gating already exists: `cave.js:1 caveTownEnabled(townId)` and
  `cave.js:7 setCaveTownEnabled(townId, on)`, persisted on
  `STORE.CAVE_TOWNS` (world-scoped, `header.js:201`).
- `core.js:685 ironReservedForCave(townId)` is the cave-first claim on iron
  (plan 08, CODED). Culture and trade already honor it (`culture.js:140`,
  `trade.js:217-218`). Emergency stashing does **not** need to register
  here — emergency is *more* conservative than the threshold path, never
  less.
- A captcha feature key already exists for the threshold path:
  `captchaPaused('cave')` is read at `cave.js:167`. `gbAjaxWatch(sig,
  settle)` (`bridge.js:7`) is registered automatically by `bridgePost`.

There is **no** `src/emergency.js` and **no** emergency stash path today.
A grep for `emergency|panic|imminent|storeAll|emergencyStash|panicStash`
across `src/` returned zero matches. The only "Stash NOW" affordance is
the toggle itself (`ui.js:1286-1289`, which calls `caveScan('toggle')` on
ON, but offers no manual one-shot).

## 2. Gap

Auto-cave walks the threshold on the orchestrator cadence; in a raid the
threshold may not be reached before the attacker lands, and even when it
is, a cadence-shaped delay can leave several hundred silver as loot to
the attacker. The user has no one-shot "stash what is here, now, ignoring
the threshold" affordance, and no auto path that watches incoming
movements to pre-stash ahead of a high-risk landing.

## 3. Design

Two coordinated pieces, separate toggles, in one new module:

1. **Manual "Stash iron now" button.** Fires `bridgePost('cave-emergency', …)`
   once per town meeting the unconditional criteria. Reads from the same
   `caveTownInfo`/`caveExcessAmount` path; **does not** consult the
   threshold, but **does** honour `caveTownEnabled` and captcha + lock
   + dryRun (via `tx.js:531`). Per-town one-shot; logs the action;
   confirms only if iron > `state.emergencyCaveConfirm = 1000` (Config).
2. **Auto path.** Subscribes to `dodgeScan`'s incoming stream **via the
   existing `dodgeScan` loop** (panel + production both run the same
   function; the production scanner is the only one that touches the
   bridge — there is no separate panel-only path). The same function
   consults `dodgeIncomingMovements()` and, when the per-town risk is
   high, calls `emergencyStoreNow` on the destination town. **No new
   `gbInterval` / `setTimeout` cadence** (README Hard rule #4); the
   watch rides the already-shipping 5s `gbInterval(dodgeScan)` at
   `boot.js` and inherits its full jitter / orchestrator-aware pause
   semantics.
   - Gating, ALL must hold: `state.emergencyCaveAuto === true`,
     `hostEnabled()`, `!automationPaused({})`, `!captchaPausedAny('cave',
     'dodge')`, `!gbLocked('cave-emergency')`,
     `dodgeEtaSec(mov) != null && dodgeEtaSec(mov) <= DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC`,
     `defenseAssessment(mov).risk >= 35` (matches `defenseShouldDodge` at
     `wonder.js:145`),
     `!dodgeSafeTown(mov.dest)` **or** all destinations have iron over
     threshold (decision parity with `defenseShouldDodge`),
     `caveTownEnabled(mov.dest)`, `caveTownInfo(mov.dest).hideLvl >= 1`,
     `caveTownInfo(mov.dest).iron >= 50` (don't break the lock on a town
     that has no meaningful iron to save).
   - Per attack: stash once. The auto path tracks `state.emergencyLastStash`
     keyed by `mov.id` so the same incoming cannot fire twice (TTL = the
     movement's `arrival_at`, plus 10 minutes).

## 8. Failure modes

- `caveTownInfo` returns `null` or `unlimited: true` — `caveExcessAmount`
  already handles this safely (cave.js:114-131): `null` info → amount `0`,
  `unlimited: true` → only limited by warehouse headroom, no per-stash
  cap check. The auto path's `caveTownInfo(...).iron >= 50` guard still
  applies. `unreadable` is `null` from `getEspionageStorage`, treated as
  unknown; **never block**.
- `dodgeIncomingMovements()` returns no model (game bridge not ready) →
  `gbLogT('cave-emergency-nobridge', 60000, …)` and bail, never blind-fire.
- `caveStoreIron` `timeout` — already handled in
  `txRun`/`bridgeRaw`: 15s timeout, post stays journaled as
  `timeout_unknown`; entry is **not** removed from `emergencyLastStash`
  but a fresh toggle-ON cycle is required to retry. This is the correct
  failure posture for irreversible iron loss (mirrors militia at
  `dodge.js:200-201`).
- A town is simultaneously the destination of two incoming attacks — fire
  once for the first, `state.emergencyLastStash[movId]` blocks the second
  from looking like a new event. With separate `movId`s the second is
  allowed; check that `mov1.id !== mov2.id` (the ID is opaque per-movement;
  the game assigns unique per-movement command_ids).
- A user lands on the `dryRun` Config toggle with `auto-cave` already on,
  then enables `emergency-cave-auto`. The first wave arrives. The auto
  path posts hit the dry-run gate, log shows `DRY-RUN cave-emergency: …`
  and a flood of `skip:dryrun` in the journal. That's the correct UX
  (the same way auto-cave would behave).

## 3.6-militia-smart-activation.md

# 3.6 — Militia smart activation

**Bucket:** v4.5 · **Risk:** High · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/dodge.js` (`dodgeRaiseMilitia`, `dodgeTryMilitia`,
`dodgeCanRaiseMilitia`). Plan 27 names `military.js` — wrong module hint,
see §1.
**Depends on:** 5.4 smart dodge (uses `defenseAssessment`, `wonder.js:144`)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

The militia path is already wired end-to-end:

- `dodge.js:107-121 dodgeCanRaiseMilitia(townId)` — checks farm building,
  already-standing militia (`+u.militia > 0`), and free population
  (`getAvailablePopulation > 0`); returns `{ok, why}`. Pop check at
  `dodge.js:117-118` is the precondition invariant guard (unreadable =
  unknown = do not block).
- `dodge.js:122-129 dodgeRaiseMilitia(townId, onDone)` —
  `gameAjaxPost('militia', 'building_farm', 'request_militia',
  { town_id: +townId }, onDone)`. Hardcoded action — no `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`
  slot.
- `dodge.js:195-202 dodgeTryMilitia(mov, entry)` — fires on every
  incoming where ETA ≤ `DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC = 15*60` (`dodge.js:181`),
  `state.autoMilitia` is on, and `captchaPausedAny('militia', 'dodge')`
  is false. Acquires `gbLock('militia', 30000)` (per-call shorten of the
  `60000` `GB_LOCK_TTL` at `core.js:168`).
- Toggle default **OFF** (`core.js:334`, `STORE.AUTO_MILITIA`
  world-scoped, `header.js:206`). UI at `ui.js:822`, `ui.js:1334`,
  `ui.js:1429`.
- Audit guarantee (`dodge.js:200-201`): a `timeout` or `timeout_unknown`
  outcome locks the entry for 5min (retry bounded) — **militia consumes
  population and re-firing without resolution is unsafe** (CLAUDE.md
  "v1.5.3 preconditions — militia/dodge").

**Wrong-module-hint finding.** Plan 27 §3 row 3.6 says "extend
`military.js`". `military.js:1-258` has nothing militia-related: it owns
cancel-command, heroes, and `renderMilitaryHelpers` for the Attack tab.
Every militia function and toggle today lives in `dodge.js` (the firing
path) and `wonder.js` (`dodgeReturnTick`, `wonder.js:148`). Plans must
extend `dodge.js`, not `military.js`.

## 2. Gap

Today `dodgeTryMilitia` raises on **every** incoming whose ETA is
<15min. That includes lone single-attacks that the town's own units
could repel. Militia is irreversible (it consumes a slot of population
that does not regenerate during the wave, and the militia unit itself
becomes the standing garrison) — burning it on noise degrades the town
for the attack that actually matters. The smart delta is: only raise
militia when the *defense assessment* (`defenseAssessment` at
`wonder.js:144`) says the town's local strength cannot absorb the
incoming composition, or the incoming is a CS / siege where militia is
the only free reinforcement that arrives in time.

## 3. Design

Add a single decision funnel between `dodgeTryMilitia` and
`dodgeCanRaiseMilitia`. Keep the existing guards; add a
risk-conditioned gate.

```
incoming movement → dodgeTryMilitia (dodge.js:195)
    │
    ├── existing guards: state.autoMilitia, captchaPausedAny,
    │   entry.militiaState, eta window, nextAt debounce      (unchanged)
    │
    └── NEW: dodgeShouldMilitia(mov, assessment)
            ├── Always raise when:  hasCs OR risk >= M_MILITIA_FORCE
            │                       OR assessment.simultaneous >= 2
            ├── Skip      when:    risk < M_MILITIA_SKIP
            │                       AND hasCs === false
            │                       AND localStrength (assessment.local.score)
            │                           >= M_MILITIA_LOCAL_OK
            └── Else (gray zone):  raise only if entry.militiaState
                                   has not advanced past "pending"
                                   within DODGE_MILITIA_GRACE_MS
```

The constants live in `dodge.js` near `DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC` and are
pinned in `state.militiaCfg` (default values below).

Data flow:
1. `dodgeScan` (`dodge.js:252`) loops hostile incoming.
2. For each, it already calls `dodgeTryMilitia(mov, entry)`.
3. `dodgeTryMilitia` calls `defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` once per
   tick (cached on `entry.dAssessment` if not present) — **re-use** the
   assessment dodgeScan is computing for itself in
   `defenseShouldDodge`, so we don't double-pay for `dodgeSupportOptions`
   (`wonder.js:143`, the expensive call).
4. Apply `dodgeShouldMilitia` decision. If skip, write
   `entry.militiaState = 'skipped'` and `gbLogT('militia-skip-<dest>',
   60000, '<why>')`. The same militia-skipped reason becomes part of the
   `whyLog` (`core.js:365`) so Stats can surface "skipped vs raised".

The retry-bounded timeout branch (`dodge.js:201`) is **unchanged**.
Militia is irreversible, the safety guarantee from v1.5.3 stays.

## 4. Work items

1. In `dodge.js`, right after `DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC` (line 181), add:
   - `const M_MILITIA_FORCE = 50` — risk threshold where militia fires
     regardless of local strength.
   - `const M_MILITIA_SKIP = 10` — risk floor below which militia is
     skipped unless `hasCs`.
   - `const M_MILITIA_LOCAL_OK = 400` — local defense score above which
     militia is skipped for risk<50 / non-CS incoming.
   - `const DODGE_MILITIA_GRACE_MS = 3*60*1000` — gray-zone window.

   All four literals are mirrored in the persistent
   `state.militiaCfg = {forceRisk, skipRisk, localOk, graceMs}`
   initializer in `core.js` (`defenseCfg` neighbour, line 359). These
   are starting points — tune via Stats after a few waves of evidence.

2. In `dodge.js`, add `function dodgeShouldMilitia(mov, assessment)`
   returning `{yes, why, group}` where group ∈ `{force, skip, grace}`.

3. In `dodgeTryMilitia` (dodge.js:195), insert **once** at the top:
   ```js
   const a = dodgeAssessmentCached(mov, entry);
   const dec = dodgeShouldMilitia(mov, a);
   if (!dec.yes) {
     entry.militiaState = 'skipped';
     gbLogT('militia-skip-reason-' + mov.dest, 60000,
       `militia: skipped (${dec.why})`);
     return;
   }
   ```
   `dodgeAssessmentCached` is a 1-line memo on `entry.dAssessmentTs`;
   it reuses the call `dodgeShouldDodge` already makes for the dodge
   side of the same loop. Mind `gbLogT` keys — they're time-throttled,
   not feature-locked, so this is safe.

4. In `dodgeCanRaiseMilitia` (dodge.js:107), add a guard against
   raising when `simultaneous >= 2 && hasCs === false` — militia is
   wasted on multiple low-risk raids on the same town. `hasCs` still
   forces raise.

5. Render the four numeric thresholds under `auto-militia` (`ui.js:822`).
   Defaults match the literals above.

6. The militia popup dismissal: when auto-militia fires, the bridge
   post dismisses the in-game "you've been attacked" dialog and the
   militia stands visibly. This plan does not change that visual; the
   operator correlates by `mov.id` + journal entry.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.militiaCfg` — `{forceRisk, skipRisk, localOk, graceMs}` — new
  field in `src/core.js` initializer block (next to
  `state.defenseCfg`, line 359). Default values match the literals in §4
  item 1. Store key `STORE.MILITIA_CFG` (new constant in
  `src/header.js:24-187`), world-scoped (`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`).
- `state.configVer` bumps from `10` to `11` (`src/header.js:191`); new
  rows render on every existing install.
- World-scoping rationale: two different worlds might run very different
  army compositions, but the *policy* (when to consume pop for militia)
  is per-world. Do **not** add to per-user-only bucket.
- Per-town pop cost is **not** persisted: it is derived from the
  standing garrison model on every read via `dodgeCanRaiseMilitia`
  (`dodge.js:113-118`). The audit's invariant: standing militia is
  read from the model, not stored; if the model is unreadable, the path
  bails (`dodge.js:117-119`).
- `entry.militiaState` semantics gain a new `'skipped'` value (existing
  valid set per `dodge.js:9`: `pending|sending|raised|unknown`). The
  `dodgeQueueLoad`/`dodgeQueueSave` (dodge.js:1-35) already serialise
  arbitrary strings — no schema work needed.

## 6. Config surface

Config tab → existing `auto-militia` row at `ui.js:822`:

| data-cfg | Variable | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto-militia` | `state.autoMilitia` | checkbox | **OFF** | HIGH-RISK (existing) |
| `militia-force-risk` | `state.militiaCfg.forceRisk` | number | `50` | when risk ≥, raise regardless |
| `militia-skip-risk` | `state.militiaCfg.skipRisk` | number | `10` | when risk < AND hasCs=false AND local≥localOk, skip |
| `militia-local-ok` | `state.militiaCfg.localOk` | number | `400` | local defense score threshold |
| `militia-grace-ms` | `state.militiaCfg.graceMs` | number | `180000` | gray-zone window |

All five fields live in the existing HIGH-RISK cluster (`ui.js:800`
"ALTO RIESGO"). Re-validate that the toggle cluster colour stays
`#f96` (red) so the operator notices.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- `dodgeRaiseMilitia` (`dodge.js:122-128`) is the only post path. It
  routes through `gameAjaxPost('militia', 'building_farm',
  'request_militia', { town_id }, cb)` and inherits dry-run via
  `tx.js:531` `txActionGate`. `gbAjaxWatch` auto-registers
  `'ajax:building_farm/request_militia'` in `gameAjaxRaw`
  (`bridge.js:149-189`) — no new sig.
- `gbLock('militia', 30000)` reuses `GB_LOCK_TTL.militia = 60000`
  (`core.js:168`); the per-call shorten does not need a new TTL entry.
- Captcha feature key `'militia'` is already covered by
  `gbCaptchaPause` via `captchaPausedAny('militia', 'dodge')` at
  `dodge.js:196`; new path inherits verbatim.
- `safeModeBlock` (`tx.js:529`) blocks the post when `state.safeMode`
  is true; militia is safe-mode-blocked by default until the operator
  disables safety.
- **No** learnable template — `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` has no `militia` slot
  (`core.js:778-790`); `tplHealth` is not charged. Hardcoded payload,
  same posture as cave.

## 8. Failure modes

- Gamebridge not ready → `dodgeRaiseMilitia` returns `'noajax'`
  (`bridge.js:151`); entry stays `sending` for the lock window, then
  reverts to `pending`. Existing flow unchanged.
- `'no free population'` from `dodgeCanRaiseMilitia` (`dodge.js:125`)
  → `dodgeTryMilitia` skips. The smart layer **must not** override
  that — pop is the harder constraint, the smart layer only adds *more
  reasons to skip*, never *more reasons to raise*.
- ETA > 15min → debounced (`dodge.js:197`); the smart layer is moot.
- Two near-simultaneous attacks → `entry.militiaState = 'raised'`
  after the first post (`dodge.js:199`); the second sees the guard. A
  CS second wave still slips through because `hasCs` forces raise
  regardless of skip thresholds.
- Timeout → `militiaState = 'unknown'`, retry bounded to 5min
  (`dodge.js:201`). Smart layer is irrelevant here; the v1.5.3 safety
  guarantee holds.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 High risk: **payload sniff against live UI + confirm-gate
screen + dry-run + manual re-fire, then still default OFF**. Steps on
`es146`:

1. With `state.dryRun === true`, land a single incoming `attack` on a
   town with local defense < 200. The
   `DRY-RUN militia: building_farm/request_militia town <id>` line MUST
   appear in the Log within 15s. Decisions view shows `skip:dryrun` as
   the **only** result for `militia` in this period.
2. Sniff: hand-fire `request_militia` from the militia UI; compare the
   captured payload against the dry-run Log line. They MUST match
   exactly (`town_id` is the only field).
3. Re-fire manually once with `state.dryRun === false`; verify the
   standing garrison gained one militia unit. Then leave the toggle OFF.
4. Risk calibration: with a `raid` then a `siege` against the same
   defender, the bot MUST skip the first and raise on the second
   (verifiable in journal entries). Repeat three times; record min/max
   risk in Stats.
5. CS path: a `colonize_ship`-bearing incoming (`dodge.js:73 hasCs`)
   → militia MUST fire regardless of risk or local strength.
6. **`auto-militia` ships at default OFF.** Nothing in this plan
   touches the shipping default; do **not** bump it to ON.

## 10. Out of scope

- Attacker army composition prediction (we can't read incoming troops;
  only the `type` string is reliable). Plan 4.2 (counter-intel) covers
  origin patterns; plan 5.4 covers per-type risk.
- Re-calling a dismissed militia spawn — no UI for it in the JS
  bridge; the standing garrison is added immediately.
- A separate "smart militia" toggle. The `auto-militia` switch is the
  only one; the four numeric knobs govern smart behaviour within it.
  Splitting is a UX footgun — punt to plan 6.10 (config undo/redo).

## 3.7-counter-snipe-detector.md

# 3.7 — Counter-snipe detector (= 5.7)

**Bucket:** v4.3 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** `src/dodge.js` (build.py:59). **Plan 27's `cs-tracker.js` hint is wrong** — see §1.
**Depends on:** none (consumes `dodgeIncomingMovements`, already shipped)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

> **5.7 is a duplicate id.** Plan 27 lists this feature twice: `3.7` with the
> module hint `cs-tracker.js` (27:131) and `5.7` "Counter-snipe detector
> (cross-ref 3.7)" with no module (27:166). They are one feature. This file is
> the single plan for both; **no `5.7-*.md` exists and none will be written**
> (the v4 README index already records that, README.md:162-163).

## 1. What exists today

**There is no `cs-tracker.js`.** `src/` holds 40 modules (`ls src/`), none named
`cs-tracker.js`, and `build.py` MODULES (build.py:32-72) has no such slot.
`find . -name '*cs-tracker*' -o -name '*snipe*'` returns nothing. The string
"snipe" appears exactly once in the whole tree — `ui.js:801` "Merchant sniper",
an unrelated Config label. **Nothing about counter-sniping is coded.**

Where CS actually lives (CLAUDE.md's "Dodge / militia / CS (`dodgeScan`) …
CS badge + webhook" line):

- `dodgeIncomingMovements()` (`dodge.js:53-84`) reads the `MovementsUnits`
  collection, keeps only movements whose destination is one of my towns
  (`dodge.js:59-63`) and only canonically hostile ones (`dodgeIsHostileMovement`,
  `dodge.js:41-52`). It returns `{id, dest, origin, type, hasCs, arrival, units, model}`.
- `hasCs` is derived at `dodge.js:73`:
  `units.colonize_ship || units.colony_ship || /^(revolt|colonize|take_over|conquer)$/.test(type)`.
- `dodgeEtaSec(mov)` (`dodge.js:175-180`) normalizes `arrival` (÷1000 when
  `> 1e12`) and returns `arrival - gameNow()`, or `null` when unreadable.
- The "CS badge" is **not** a footer badge. It is three `[CS]` string prefixes:
  the flash/log line in `dodgeNotify` (`dodge.js:186`), the Intel board row
  (`intel.js:88`) and the Discord embed title (`alerts.js:59`).
- The CS webhook is the existing `alertWebhook('attack', {…, cs:!!mov.hasCs})`
  call at `dodge.js:191`, gated by `state.csAlert` (default `true`,
  `core.js:335`, key `STORE.CS_ALERT` `header.js:124`, Config checkbox
  `[data-cfg=cs-alert]` `ui.js:821`, bound `ui.js:1428`).

The only wave-aware code that exists:

- `defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` (**`wonder.js:144`**, *not* `military.js`)
  computes `simultaneous = all.filter(x => x.dest === mov.dest).length` — a
  **count of movements per town with no time analysis at all** — and adds
  `+60` risk for `hasCs`, `+min(25,(n-1)*8)` for multiple movements.
  It is consumed by `defenseShouldDodge` (`wonder.js:145`) and rendered per row
  by the Intel board (`intel.js:87-89`).
- Preflight has an `incoming` row that only prints a count
  (`stats.js:225-228`).
- `intelPatternScan` (`intel.js:206-245`) is **not** related: it buckets
  `state.findings` (spy/battle reports) by attacker over 24h. Different source,
  different time scale.

So: arrival timestamps are read and thrown away, wave membership is reduced to a
scalar count, and nothing anywhere computes an inter-arrival delta
(`grep -rn '\bwave\b|snipeWindow|interArrival' src/` → one unrelated hit,
`attack.js:588`).

## 2. Gap

The defender-relevant fact is not "how many attacks", it is **where the gaps
are**: the interval between the clearing wave and the colony-ship landing is the
window in which support can be sniped in, and attackers cover that window with
extra waves. `defenseAssessment` (`wonder.js:144`) collapses exactly that
structure into `simultaneous`, so a 3-wave train landing 4s apart around a CS and
3 unrelated attacks spread over 6h produce the identical assessment. The delta is
one pure function over the list `dodgeIncomingMovements()` already returns —
group by `dest`, sort by `arrival`, expose the gap around the CS and how many
waves sit inside it — plus four read-only display sites.

## 3. Design

Pure analyzer + existing surfaces. No new data source, no new timer, no post.

Data in: `dodgeIncomingMovements()` (`dodge.js:53`), which `dodgeScan` already
calls once per pass (`dodge.js:263`) on the 5s `DODGE_CHECK_MS` interval
(`wonder.js:150`, wired `boot.js:100`).

Decision (`csWaveClusters(incoming)`, new, in `dodge.js`):

1. Bucket movements by `String(mov.dest)`.
2. Per bucket, map each movement to `dodgeArrivalSec(mov)` (see work item 1).
   `null` ⇒ counted into `unknownArrival`, **excluded from the maths**.
3. Sort ascending; split into *trains* wherever the gap between consecutive
   arrivals exceeds `csClusterGapSec` (default 900 = the existing 15-min
   imminence horizon, `DODGE_MILITIA_WINDOW_SEC` `dodge.js:181`).
4. Per train, `csAt` = arrival of the **last** entry with `hasCs`
   (`dodge.js:73`); `prev` = the entry immediately before it.
   - `gapSec = csAt - prev.at` — the snipe window.
   - `cover` = entries whose arrival lies in `(csAt - csCoverSec, csAt)`,
     excluding the CS itself — the counter-snipe waves that would eat a snipe.
5. Verdict, in this order (first match wins):
   - `unknownArrival > 0` ⇒ `'unknown'` (a blind read may never produce a
     reassuring verdict — §8).
   - no `hasCs` entry ⇒ `'no-cs'`, and report `tightestGapSec` instead.
   - no entry before the CS ⇒ `'cs-solo'` (window not computable from
     incoming alone).
   - `gapSec <= csTightSec` (default 5) ⇒ `'tight'`.
   - `cover >= 1` ⇒ `'covered'`.
   - else ⇒ `'open'`.

Action out — four read-only sinks, all existing:

- `dodgeNotify` (`dodge.js:183-194`): the per-movement flash/log line and the
  **existing** webhook payload gain the train verdict. No new webhook event, no
  new call site, no extra alert volume.
- `dodgeScan` (`dodge.js:266-287`): one throttled `gbLogT` train summary per
  destination, re-emitted only when the verdict string changes — `dodgeNotify`
  fires once per movement (`entry.notified`, `dodge.js:184`), so a wave added
  *after* first notification would otherwise be invisible.
- Intel board row (`intel.js:88-89`).
- Preflight `incoming` row (`stats.js:225-228`).

Gap arithmetic is a difference of two server arrival stamps, so it is immune to
local clock drift; only the ETA display uses `gameNow()` (`dodge.js:179`).

Name check before coding: `csWaveClusters`, `csTrainLine`, `dodgeArrivalSec`
each return **0 hits** across `src/`, so the `build.py` duplicate-declaration

## 5. State & storage

No new `state.*` root field and **no new `STORE.*` key**. The four tunables live
inside the existing `state.defenseCfg` object (`core.js:359`, key
`STORE.DEFENSE_CFG` `header.js:155`), which is **already** in
`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:209`) — so nothing new is id-bearing and
`load()`/`save()` already apply `wkey()`.

`configVer`: 10 → 11 (`header.js:191`; ladder tail `core.js:482-506`). The
`ver < 11` block sets the defaults on persisted configs that predate them and
clamps: `csClusterGapSec` to `[60, 21600]`, `csCoverSec` to `[5, 900]`,
`csTightSec` to `[0, 120]`, `snipeDetect` to a boolean, then
`save(STORE.DEFENSE_CFG, state.defenseCfg)` — mirroring the existing
`returnMarginSec` clamp at `core.js:503`.

Prune TTL: none. Every train is recomputed from the live collection each 5s
pass; nothing is persisted, so nothing can go stale or leak. The existing
`dodgeQueue` TTL sweep (`dodge.js:289-294`, `DODGE_QUEUE_TTL` 1h
`wonder.js:152`) is untouched.

## 6. Config surface

Appended to the existing **Defensa** row (`ui.js:824`), Spanish per CLAUDE.md:

| Control | Selector | `defenseCfg` field | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Detector de contra-snipe` (checkbox) | `[data-cfg=cs-snipe]` | `snipeDetect` | **ON** |
| `agrupar oleadas <n>s` | `[data-cfg=cs-cluster-gap]` | `csClusterGapSec` | `900` |
| `cobertura <n>s` | `[data-cfg=cs-cover]` | `csCoverSec` | `60` |
| `ventana minima <n>s` | `[data-cfg=cs-tight]` | `csTightSec` | `5` |

Default ON is correct here and does not violate the CLAUDE.md HIGH-RISK rule:
that rule covers spendy/autonomous actions (recruit, dodge auto, favor). This
feature posts nothing, spends nothing and adds no request-budget load. Its
output is additionally gated by the pre-existing `CS / incoming alerts`
checkbox (`ui.js:821`), so a user who has already silenced CS alerts sees
nothing new. Worst case is one extra throttled Log line per attacked town per
60s while a CS train is inbound.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** The feature sends nothing: no `bridgePost`, no
`gameAjaxPost`, no `gbXhr`, no DOM write. Therefore no `gbCaptchaPause` feature
key, no `gbLock` name, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no `gbAjaxWatch` registration,
no `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`/`tplNameFor` entry and no dry-run gate are added. The only
outbound traffic it touches is the **already existing** `alertWebhook('attack', …)`
at `dodge.js:191`, which gains payload fields; its call site, its 5-min
per-key rate limit (`alerts.js:43`) and its dry-run short-circuit
(`alerts.js:30-33`) are unchanged.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Unreadable arrival ⇒ `blind`, never a safe verdict.** `dodgeArrivalSec`
  returns `null` when `arrival` is absent or non-finite (`dodge.js:176-178`).
  Such movements are counted into `unknownArrival` and the train verdict becomes
  `'unknown'` — it must never fall through to `'open'` or `'no-cs'`, because a
  guard that reports "no threat" from data it could not read is worse than no
  guard (CLAUDE.md precondition invariant). One `gbLogT('cs-blind-'+dest, 600000, …)`
  naming the field it failed to read.
- **`hasCs` may never fire — UNVERIFIED, must be measured.** `dodge.js:73`
  needs either `units.colonize_ship`/`units.colony_ship` **or** a type in
  `/^(revolt|colonize|take_over|conquer)$/`. Whether the server exposes the
  attacker's unit breakdown on an *incoming* movement is **not verifiable from
  `src/` or from `archive/captures/`** (`grep -o 'arrived_at…' game.min.js` →
  no hits; one `MovementsUnits` occurrence, no attribute schema). If units are
  hidden, only the type branch can fire. The detector must therefore degrade
  honestly: with no `hasCs` entry it reports `'no-cs'` + `tightestGapSec`, and
  it must **not** print "no colony ship". Work item 9's Preflight detail plus
  the §9 gate is how this gets settled on the live world.
- **No `MovementsUnits` collection** (`dodge.js:57-58` returns `[]`): zero
  trains, zero log lines. No crash path — `csWaveClusters([])` returns `[]`.
- **Single-wave noise.** Trains of `n === 1` with no CS produce no output at
  all; only `n >= 2` or a CS-bearing train logs.
- **Cross-town merging is impossible** — grouping is keyed on `mov.dest`
  (`dodge.js:75`), so two towns attacked at the same second never form one
  train.
- **Cost of being wrong is bounded.** The only consumer that can change
  behaviour is work item 7's `+10` risk on `'covered'`; `defenseShouldDodge`
  fires auto-dodge at `risk >= 35` and only when `state.autoDodge` is on
  (`dodge.js:205`) — which is HIGH-RISK and default OFF (`core.js:321`). If
  item 7 is judged too risky for a "read-only" plan, ship items 1-6 and 8-12
  and defer item 7 to 5.3; the feature is complete without it.

## 9. Validation gate

Low risk ⇒ plan 27 §11: *Preflight + one in-game session, no failure.*

1. `python3 build.py`, paste, reload `es146`.
2. Stats → **Preflight**: the `incoming` row must read
   `N incoming movements visible, M train(s), K with unreadable arrival`. `K`
   must be `0`; if it is not, stop — the arrival field is not readable on this
   client and §8's blind path is the live behaviour.
3. With at least one real incoming attack: Log must contain exactly one
   `cs: town <id> <verdict> …` line per 60s per town, and the Intel tab
   *Entrantes* row must carry ` | tren … · ventana …s · cubierta …`.
4. Record which `hasCs` branch fired (units vs type) — that is the answer §8
   is asking for. Paste it into `docs/TASKS.md`.
5. Config → uncheck `Detector de contra-snipe`: all `cs:` lines and the Intel
   suffix disappear within one 5s pass; `dodge:` and `militia:` lines are
   byte-identical to before.
6. With `autoDodge` / `autoMilitia` / `csAlert` all OFF, `dodgeScan` returns at
   `dodge.js:258` — Log must show nothing at all from this feature.
7. Set `state.dryRun` ON and confirm the webhook line
   `DRY-RUN webhook attack: …` (`alerts.js:31`) now carries the `snipe` object.

Must **NOT** appear anywhere in the session: any new `bridgePost` /
`gameAjaxPost` entry in the Decisions view, any `skip:budget` that was not there
before, any new lock name in the Stats "held locks" row, any change to the
number of webhook events sent.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Acting on the verdict** — sniping support in, cancelling, dodging on a
  covered window. Any of those is a post surface: 3.2 (support auto-send),
  5.4 (smart dodge), 3.6 (militia smart activation).
- **Re-weighting the risk model.** `defenseAssessment`'s existing constants
  (`wonder.js:144`) and the `risk >= 35` auto-dodge threshold
  (`wonder.js:145`) belong to **5.3 threat assessment engine**, which should
  consume `csWaveClusters` rather than re-derive it.
- **Inferring wave composition** (clear vs fake vs anti-snipe) from unit counts
  — not readable for incoming movements, see §8. Never guess it.
- **Report-derived history** ("this player always covers at 4s"): that is
  `intelPatternScan`'s data source (`intel.js:206`), owned by 2.5 / 5.3.
- **Sharing trains with the alliance** — 7.2 defense coordination board.
- **A new `cs-tracker.js` module and its `build.py` MODULES slot.** Rejected:
  three functions on a list that `dodge.js` already produces do not justify a
  module, and splitting them from `dodgeScan` would put the analyzer in a file
  that concatenates after its only caller for no benefit.

## 4.1-auto-spy-scheduler.md

# 4.1 — Auto-spy scheduler

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/spy.js` (scheduler + spy-send) + `src/qol.js` (orchestrator hook) + `src/header.js` (STORE + WORLD_SCOPED_BASES) + `src/core.js` (TPL_FEATURE_MAP + tplNameFor) + `src/parse-inline.js` (re-useparseReport)
**Depends on:** 2.1 (deeper parser feeds the ranker; not a hard build-order block, but score quality drops without it)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

`src/spy.js` is **read-only** today: it hooks `fetch` + `XMLHttpRequest` to
detect outbound report traffic, queues ids into `seenThisRun`
(`src/spy.js:4-6`), fetches the report body via `gameAjaxPost('report',
'report', 'view', …)` (`src/spy.js:280-294`), ingests the JSON via
`parseReport` (`src/spy.js:236-257`), and stores findings in `state.findings`.
The offline catch-up loop (`src/spy.js:117-178`) is already coded and shipped
(plan 14 / plan 27 §9). The seen-set trim `seenThisRun.size > 5000 →
clear()` (`src/spy.js:227`) and the `seen[]` dedup gate at `src/spy.js:138`
are part of the existing audit belt-and-braces (plan 26 I14).

Nothing in `src/` sends a spy. Plan 27 §9 lists 15 already-shipped items; spy
sending is **not** one of them. The closest analogues that exist and inform
this plan:

- `src/favor.js:1-153` — `favorScan` is the only scanner that spends a
  game resource (favor) and applies a 5/15/60min captcha breaker
  (`src/favor.js:58`, `src/core.js:1337-1350`). Its template is
  `state.attackTpl` (`src/favor.js:133-138`) and the captured captcha
  feature key is `favor` (`src/favor.js:58`).
- `src/recruit.js` `recruitScan` — `state.favorCfg.recruitPower` +
  `bridgePost('recruit', …)` (`src/recruit.js:319`). Recruit is HIGH-RISK
  default OFF (CLAUDE.md "Auto-recruit ... default OFF").
- The orchestrator (`src/qol.js:384-432`) has the per-feature cadence
  table (`ORCH_CADENCE`), captcha-key map (`ORCH_CAPTCHA`), journal-key map
  (`ORCH_JRN`), and handler map (`ORCH_HANDLERS`). New scout-class features
  must wire into these maps, **not** add a `gbInterval`.

The grep evidence:

- `grep -n "sendSpy\|spyTown\|spyMission\|spyTarget\|TPL_SPY_TPL" src/ -r` →
  zero hits. The symbol does not exist.
- `grep -n "spy\|Spy\|espion" src/favor.js src/attack.js src/recruit.js` →
  zero hits. No spy route is currently consumed by any scanner.
- `src/core.js:778-790` — `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` has no `spy` entry. The
  favor-disabled comment there (`// favor used attackTpl here`) confirms
  that template cobbling is exactly what we must not do for spy — a spy
  rejection must not invalidate the attack or favor template.

## 2. Gap

A scheduler that picks a ranked target and sends a spy. Three concrete
absences:

1. **No send route.** There is no `bridgePost('spy', payload, cb)` and no
   `gbAjaxWatch('spy:send', …)` registration. The TPL_FEATURE_MAP has no
   `spyTpl` slot. Sniffing is the first work item.
2. **No target ranking.** `state.findings` exists, `state.watchlist` exists
   (`src/intel.js:186-203`), but no module turns "I have 200 findings and a
   watchlist of 5 towns" into a ranked spy queue.
3. **No cadence.** The orchestrator has no `spy` key (`src/qol.js:388-432`).
   Spy is **scout-class** (HIGH-RISK-adjacent because it spends silver and
   can return a captcha), so it wires into `orchTick` with a long base
   cadence (≥ 30 min) and a tight per-target gap (≥ 20 min).

The plan therefore is not a refactor — the read path is already in place
and well-understood. The plan is a new scheduler on top of `src/spy.js`,
a new orchestrator hook, and a new template slot. The dry-run +
confirm-gate + captcha-key scaffolding mirrors `src/favor.js:52-152` for
reuse.

## 3. Design

The scheduler runs through `orchTick` (`src/qol.js:421-432`) under a new
`spy` key. Each tick:

1. Read `state.spyCfg` (default `{ targets: [], autoWatchlist: true,
   autoTopReported: 5, perCycle: 1, minGapMs: 1200000, dryRun: true,
   confirmOncePerCycle: true, maxConcurrent: 3, useFavor: false }`).
2. **Rank** the candidate pool. Pool = `state.spyCfg.targets` (manual pins) ∪
   `state.watchlist` (when `autoWatchlist`) ∪ top-N most-reported players by
   `state.findings` over the last 24h (when `autoTopReported > 0`).
   Score for a target `t`:
   `score(t) = (now - lastSpyAt(t)) * 1.0 + watchBonus(t) + reportBonus(t)`
   where `watchBonus` is `+1000` if `t.id` matches any `state.watchlist`
   rule, and `reportBonus` is `+100 * max(0, reportsIn24h(t) - 1)`. A
   target with no `lastSpyAt` starts at `now - 7d` (very stale → high
   score). A target whose `lastSpyAt` is within `minGapMs` is dropped.
3. **Drop** anything that already has an `enRoute` count ≥ `maxConcurrent`
   (read from `state.spyInFlight`, an `Object.create(null)` keyed by town
   id, incremented on send and decremented on bridge settle).
4. **Pick** the top-`perCycle` survivors. If `confirmOncePerCycle` and the
   last confirm-dialog has not been shown in this session, render a
   `confirm()` listing the top-3 (id + coord + score) and bail on cancel.
5. **Send** through `bridgePost('spy', payload, cb)` (`src/bridge.js:190-193`).
   The payload is **not** invented here — see §7 (sniff first).
6. **Reconcile** on bridge settle: success → `state.spyInFlight[townId]--`,
   `lastSpyAt[townId] = now`, `save(STORE.SPY_HISTORY, …)`; captcha →
   `captchaTrip('spy', …)` (auto via `captchaPaused`); error → log once
   and `gbRemember('spy', townId, 'error')` if `jrnHard(err)`.

The `lastSpyAt` table lives in `state.spyLastSpy`, persisted under
`STORE.SPY_HISTORY` (world-scoped). The `enRoute` table is **not** persisted;
it is rebuildable from the bridge in-flight registry (`src/bridge.js:131-147`).

Sniff discipline: the spy route is **not known today**. Plan 27 §13 is
explicit that a new post surface is `'sniff <x> via gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)',
capture the template into TPL_FEATURE_MAP` — an explicit unknown, not a
guess. See §7.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/parse-inline.js` — no change. `parseReport` already returns what
   `renderFindings` and `intelDossiers` need (and 2.1 widens it). The ranker
   reads `state.findings` directly.
2. `src/header.js:24-187` — add `STORE.SPY_HISTORY = 'grepbot:spy-history'`

   - `spyBridgeWatch(payload)` — what the **spy** send route needs to

4. `src/core.js:778-790` — `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` gains `spy: 'spyTpl'`. The

## 5. State & storage

| Key | Type | Persisted | World-scoped | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state.spyEnabled` | boolean | `STORE.AUTO_SPY` | yes (per-host) | Toggle (mirror of `state.autoFarm`) |
| `state.spyCfg` | object | `STORE.SPY_CFG` | yes | Per-host config; redacted on export |
| `state.spyLastSpy` | `{ [townId]: ms }` | `STORE.SPY_HISTORY` | yes | Drives the ranker gap |
| `state.spyInFlight` | `{ [townId]: number }` | — | no | Bridge in-flight counter, rebuilt on settle |
| `state.spyTemplate` | object | `STORE.SPY_TPL` (optional) | yes | Once sniffed, the captured template |

`STORE.SPY_HISTORY`, `STORE.SPY_CFG`, `STORE.AUTO_SPY`, `STORE.SPY_TPL` go
into `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-214`). Prune TTL: `spyLastSpy`
rows are pruned at 7d in a new module-local cleanup pass inside `spyCycle`
(prototype: `Object.keys(state.spyLastSpy).forEach(k => { if (now -
state.spyLastSpy[k] > 7*86400000) delete state.spyLastSpy[k]; })` followed
by one `save(STORE.SPY_HISTORY, state.spyLastSpy)`). The pass is throttled
to once per hour via a module-local `lastPruneAt`.

`configVer` bump: `10 → 11` (entry 14).

## 6. Config surface

| Label | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Espiar automáticamente` | `false` | HIGH-RISK-adjacent → default OFF (CLAUDE.md) |
| `Objetivos manuales (1 por línea)` | empty | `<townId> <x> <y> <pin>` lines, parsed by `parseSpyTargets` |
| `Auto desde watchlist` | `true` | Adds watchlist towns to the candidate pool |
| `Auto desde top 24h` | `5` | Adds top-N most-reported players from `state.findings` |
| `Por ciclo` | `1` | Top-N fired per orch tick |
| `Gap mínimo por objetivo (min)` | `20` | Per-target min gap in ms (`spyCfg.minGapMs`) |
| `Máx en vuelo` | `3` | `spyCfg.maxConcurrent` |
| `Modo dry-run` | `true` | **Default ON** so the first session is observable before any real send |
| `Confirmar una vez por ciclo` | `true` | First fire per session asks for `confirm()` |

Honors plan 27 §13: defaults redaction-OFF (`qol.js:255-275` doesn't redact
`spyCfg` in v4.0 — same treatment as `favorCfg`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

**Unknown route — explicit sniff work item.** The bridge action name + payload
for sending a spy is not in `src/` today. The work item is:

```text
1. Hand-trigger a spy by opening a town info popup → "espiar" → choose
   resource mission → Send. The XHR spy at src/spy.js:37-112 captures the
   raw POST url + body in hookFetch / hookXhr.
2. gbAjaxWatch('spy-send', settle) is registered by spyCycle before the
   first bridgePost; the XHR spy settles it from the raw response on
   loadend (src/spy.js:73-82).
3. The captured url + body shape is stored in state.spyTemplate and
   mirrored to STORE.SPY_TPL. tplNameFor('spy', payload) returns 'spyTpl'
   (src/core.js:795-801).
4. Until the sniff lands, spyCycle never fires (state.spyTemplate == null
   triggers a one-shot gbLogT('spy-no-tpl', 300000,
   'spy: no template learned — hand-spy once to capture')).
```

Lock: `gbLock('spy', 180000)` (entry 5). One lock per cycle, not per
target — the per-target `enRoute` count lives in `state.spyInFlight`.

gbCaptchaPause feature key: **`'spy'`** (entry 6). `captchaTrip('spy', …)`
is called by `bridgePost`'s classify path (`src/bridge.js:110-127`) on a
captcha response and the captcha ladder (`src/core.js:1337-1350`) takes over
with 5/15/60min backoff.

Dry-run (`state.spyCfg.dryRun === true`): the cycle logs `DRY-RUN spy: {…}`
(`src/bridge.js:215-219`) and journals `skip:dryrun`
(`src/core.js:457-461`). The bridge post does not fire. The ranker still
runs and the top-3 confirmation dialog still appears.

Confirm-gate: `confirmOncePerCycle` (default ON) wraps the first
`bridgePost` of each session in a `confirm('¿Espiar X / Y / Z?')` dialog
(Spanish UI, CLAUDE.md). Once accepted, the session accepts the rest
without prompting.

Precondition invariant: every guard reads a value it actually read. The
ranker drops targets whose `lastSpyAt` is unreadable by treating them as
fully stale (score = `now - (now - 7d)` = `7d`). The `enRoute` count is
read from `state.spyInFlight` (built by the same module). The
`reportsIn24h(t)` falls back to `0` when no finding matches.

## 8. Failure modes

| Condition | Verdict | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `state.spyTemplate` is null | `gbLogT` once, no fire | Per §7 |
| `state.spyCfg.targets` is empty AND `autoWatchlist` is false AND `autoTopReported = 0` | log once, return | No candidates — nothing to do |
| `confirmOncePerCycle` dialog cancelled | exit the cycle | `enRoute` count unaffected (no send) |
| `bridgePost` errs `'budget'` | re-queue at next tick | Orchestrator's adaptive cadence widens (4 idle runs → 8×, `src/qol.js:415-419`) |
| `bridgePost` errs `'captcha'` | `captchaTrip('spy', …)` | 5/15/60 ladder; orchestrator's `ORCH_CAPTCHA` (`src/qol.js:404-408`) blocks the tick |
| `bridgePost` errs `'timeout'` | log once, no retry | Inherited from `src/bridge.js:101-104`; irreversible action — no timeout-fallback |
| 3 consecutive hard errors on `spy:<townId>` | `gbRemember('spy', townId, err)` opens a 5/15/60min skip | `state.decisionSkips` (`src/core.js:463`) — same shape as other features |
| `minGapMs` violated by a tier race | `spyCycle` re-checks `lastSpyAt` before fire | Skip + log once |
| Unknown `r.type`/JSON shape | `parseReport` returns null; existing `reportFetchFail` path | `src/spy.js:258-264` already handles |
| `state.spyEnabled` toggled mid-cycle | next `orchTick` skips | `orchFeatureEnabled` (`src/orchestrate.js:1-18`) gates |

The five `return null` strictness paths in `parseReport` are unchanged.
A spy *response* with missing units / missing town is still a valid spy
report — `parseReport` already accepts `r.attacker` + `r.defender` only
without units (`src/parse-inline.js:53-55`).

## 9. Validation gate

Plan 27 §11 Med risk: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one full
orchestrator tick.

1. `grepbot.user.js` rebuilt. Install via Tampermonkey paste.
2. Open Config → `Espiar automáticamente` OFF. Verify `state.spyEnabled`
   persists across reload (UI toggle).
3. Open Config → `auto top 24h = 5`, `perCycle = 1`, `dryRun = true`. Save.
   Preflight shows `auto-spy: dry-run` row (existing preflight row at
   `src/stats.js:171-172` is the wiring precedent; add a new row mirroring
   it). Log: `spy: template pending — hand-spy once to capture`.
4. Hand-spy one target by opening the town's spy popup → send. The XHR
   spy captures the route; `state.spyTemplate` populates;
   `gbLogT('spy-template', 60000, 'spy: template learned')` fires once.
5. Toggle `Espiar automáticamente` ON. Orchestrator fires after 30min
   (`ORCH_CADENCE.spy = 1800000`). Confirm-gate dialog lists the top-3
   ranked targets. Accept. Log: `DRY-RUN spy: <townId> → <payload>`.
   Journal: `skip:dryrun` for `spy` feature.
6. Disable `dryRun`. Wait 30min. Confirm. The bridge fires. Log: `spy:
   sent <townId>`. `state.spyLastSpy[townId] = now`. Stats tab shows
   `spy` row in the journal rollup.
7. Hand-trip a captcha. Confirm the 5/15/60 ladder opens and the
   orchestrator gates `spy` per `ORCH_CAPTCHA.spy`.
8. Force the dry-run flag back ON. Toggle the toggle 5× in 60s. Log
   shows `spy: toggle changed` once (throttled), no send.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Spy route sniff.** Captured by the work item in §7. Once learned,
  it lives in `state.spyTemplate` and `STORE.SPY_TPL`. A separate
  plan-of-record tracks the sniff attribution.
- **Hero transfer / assignment (plan 4.3).** 4.1 picks targets; 4.3 owns
  the hero UX.
- **Spy-queue as a watchlist UI.** The Intel tab shows the top-3 ranked
  targets (entry 10) but does not let the user drag-reorder — that is a
  v4.3 UX plan.
- **Favor-driven spy.** `state.spyCfg.useFavor` is a flag (default `false`).
  Wiring it to `src/favor.js:favorCurrent()` is a separate plan.
- **Per-target model payload capture.** The scheduler learns one
  `(townId, payload)` shape and reuses it; if the bridge invalidates
  due to a `payload_stale` (`state.tplHealth.spyTpl.invalidated`),
  the next cycle re-sniffs. `tplHealthOk` gates the fire
  (`src/core.js:857-880`).
- **Spy counter / silver spent panel.** Stats tab gets a `spy` rollup
  row inherited from the journal (`src/core.js:463-500`) but a styled
  "silver spent on spies" widget is a v4.3 plan.
- **Export redaction of `spyCfg.targets`.** v4.0 mirrors `favorCfg`
  behavior (no redaction). Follow-up in v4.1.

## 4.2-counter-intel-detection.md

# 4.2 — Counter-intel detection (origin pattern)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js`
**Depends on:** none (consumes `state.findings` and `intelMyIdentity` which
already exist).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## Policy boundary (read first, before §1)

Plan 27 §0 explicitly bans **"Anti-pattern detection (anti-counter-farm)"**
with the reason "Anti-cheat avoidance; explicit policy ban." That policy row
is about *detecting patterns a player uses to dodge GrepBot*, e.g. looking
for users who go inactive just before an attack or who sit on vacation to
avoid retaliation. **4.2 does not do that.** 4.2 only watches incoming
reports whose `defender` resolves to me — i.e. who is **spying on me** — and
groups them. That is the inverse direction: passive observation of an
inbound signal the game itself delivers as a report. 5.3's threat engine is
also inbound; both are read-mostly, no posts, no fingerprinting of other
players' behaviour.

If a future contributor wants to widen scope (e.g. predict *whether* the
watcher will attack soon, or correlate spy timings with travel patterns)
**that is a new plan and must be re-checked against §0 first**. 4.2 ships
within the policy line.

## 1. What exists today

- `state.findings[]` (`src/spy.js:249`, capped at 500, key
  `STORE.FINDINGS` already in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`) is the input set. Every
  parsed report carries `type` (e.g. `'spy'`, `'attack'`, `'support'`,
  `'raid'`, `'conquer'`, `'siege'`, `'revolt'`, `'take_over'`,
  `'colonize'` — see `src/dodge.js:39-40` and `src/parse-inline.js:51`).
- `intelMyIdentity()` (`src/intel.js:17-27`) returns `{id, name}` from
  `MM.getModelByNameAndPlayerId('Player')` and `Game.player_id / player_name`,
  catching all known client variants today (`src/intel.js:23-25`).
  Returns `{id:null, name:null}` on read failure.
- `intelActorIsMe(actor, me)` (`src/intel.js:28-33`) compares by id first and
  name second, exactly the pattern required here.
- `intelPatternScan()` (`src/intel.js:206-245`) is the closest functional
  precedent: 24h rolling window, attacker aggregation, dedup via
  `state.alerted[ak]`. 4.2 follows the same shape and reuses
  `alertWebhook('counter-intel', payload)` — the event name is new but
  reuses the existing event bus in `src/alerts.js:28-87`. The 5-min rate
  limit on webhooks (`src/alerts.js:44`) and `state.webhookEvents[event] ===
  false` opt-out (`src/alerts.js:39-40`) apply unchanged.
- `state.alerted` (`src/core.js:229`) is the existing key-value dedup store.
  Already used by `intelPatternScan` with key shape
  `'pattern:' + key + ':' + bucket` (`src/intel.js:229`). 4.2 mirrors that.
- The intel pattern scan already fires `alertWebhook('attack', …)` for
  watchlist matches (`src/intel.js:202`) and `alertWebhook('pattern', …)`
  for pattern hits (`src/intel.js:242`). 4.2 will fire
  `alertWebhook('counter-intel', …)` — different event label, same bus.
- Plan 27 §9 row "Support ETA, attack pattern, watchlist why" is already
  coded (`src/intel.js:89, 109-111, 133-193`). 4.2 is a **different
  signal** (observation by YOU, not on you) and a different event label.

## 2. Gap

The intel picture answers *who is attacking you* (threat board,
`src/intel.js:72-74`) and *what your own findings say about other players*
(dossiers, `src/intel.js:34-71`). It does not separately answer *who is
watching your towns*. The existing `intelPatternScan` only counts hostile
movements; a sustained spy campaign by another player reads as one-or-more
`'spy'` rows in `state.findings` and is otherwise indistinguishable from
your own scout-on-someone-else reports. The user has to scroll the Findings
tab and filter manually to spot recurring spies on the same town.

## 3. Design

A single scan function `intelCounterIntelScan()` modeled directly on
`intelPatternScan()`. Inputs: `state.findings` + `intelMyIdentity()`. Output:
a `Map<attackerKey, stats>` keyed by the existing `intelPlayerKey`
(`src/intel.js:1-10`) — same key used by `intelDossiers()` so a row can be
cross-referenced.

A finding qualifies when **both** of:

1. `f.type === 'spy'` (with `parseReport` already lower-casing and
   `src/dodge.js:39` enumerating known hostile types, the universe is well-
   bounded; we read `f.type` raw without regex-based classification so a
   future client rename to `'scout'` only breaks the spy filter, not the
   attack filter).
2. `intelActorIsMe(f.defender, me)` — i.e. the report's defender resolves
   to me (or one of my towns). Where the report shape names `f.town.id`
   only and `f.defender` is null, the test extends to "town resolves to
   me"; both nulls ⇒ skip (policy: never infer identity from a missing
   field).

Stats per attacker:

```
{
  key, name,
  reports: number,            // count of qualifying rows in window
  distinctTargets: number,    // distinct town ids targeted
  towns: string[],            // town ids as strings, max 8
  first, last,                // timestamps
}
```

**Threshold + window** — same shape as `intelPatternScan`: 24h rolling
window (`src/intel.js:208`); trip at `n >= 3` matches (configurable, see
§6). A single spy report is not actionable — three in a day is a watch
state, not speculation.

**Webhook payload** — `alertWebhook('counter-intel', {watcher: ..., n: ...,
towns: ...})`. Reuses the existing alert path; the event label is new and
the user's `state.webhookEvents[event]` (`src/core.js:313`, default
`attack:true`) becomes the opt-out gate. Plan 26 §B4-style: the opt-out is
not pre-staged; adding the key to the default object matters — see §5.

**Dedup** — same key shape as `intelPatternScan`:
`'counter-intel:' + key + ':' + bucket` against `state.alerted`. Without
dedup the same attacker would fire a webhook every render (15s loop,
`boot.js:108-115`).

**Display** — extend the existing `renderIntel()` (`src/intel.js:75-114`)
with a `=== Contra-inteligencia ===` block above the `=== Fichas ===`
section, listing the same top-N (cap 5) the pattern scan uses. Reuses the
existing redactor for attacker names (`src/intel.js:235, 238`,
`state.exportRedact !== false`) — the Webhook payload is the one place
that holds the unredacted name because the user opted in via
`state.webhookUrl`.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/intel.js`** — add `intelCounterIntelScan()`:
   - filter `state.findings` for `f.type === 'spy' &&
     intelActorIsMe(f.defender, intelMyIdentity())`;
   - aggregate by `intelPlayerKey(f.attacker)` over a 24h window;
   - emit a hit when `n >= threshold` (default 3, see §6);
   - dedup via `state.alerted['counter-intel:' + key + ':' + bucket]`;
   - call `alertWebhook('counter-intel', payload)` once per scan.
   Pure function, no new top-level declaration (sits inside the IIFE per
   `build.py:31-72` build order — `intel.js` is module 32, no reordering
   required).
2. **`src/intel.js`** — call `intelCounterIntelScan()` from `renderIntel()`
   (`src/intel.js:75-114`) in a try/catch (mirroring the existing
   `intelPatternScan()` invocation at `src/intel.js:113`).
3. **`src/intel.js`** — extend `renderIntel()` with a `=== Contra-
   inteligencia ===` block, redacted names, top 5 entries sorted by `n
   desc`. Reuses the existing `<pre class="intel-panel">` element
   (`src/ui.js:694`) and the existing render cadence — no DOM mutation
   beyond appending text.
4. **`src/ui.js`** — Config checkbox `[data-cfg=counter-intel]` default
   OFF, bound through `bindToggle('[data-cfg=counter-intel]',
   'intelCounterIntel', STORE.INTEL_COUNTER)` (added in §5). When
   OFF the scan still runs (cheap, read-only) but skips the webhook
   emission and hides the panel section. Default OFF preserves the
   policy-aligned stance that user-initiated notifications are opt-in.
5. **`src/qol.js`** — add `'intelCounterIntel'` to the export's allowed
   top-level keys (validator list at `src/qol.js:256`, `storeFor` map at
   `src/qol.js:258`). Required for round-tripping Config.

## 5. State & storage

- **One new field**: `state.intelCounterIntel`, persisted to
  `STORE.INTEL_COUNTER` (`src/header.js`).
- The new key **must** go in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-214`)
  only if it carries id-bearing data. 4.2's key holds a **boolean**, so
  per CLAUDE.md "world-scope id-bearing storage" the key is **not** added
  to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`. (It would be wrong to scope a global toggle by
  world and surprising the user when they switch.)
- `state.webhookEvents.counterIntel` — the new event-label gate. Default
  `false`. The default object at `src/core.js:313` is `{captcha: true,
  attack: true, warehouse: false, culture: false}` — extend it to
  `…, counterIntel: false}` (a guarded merge in `migrateConfig`
  `src/core.js:489-505` is **not** required; first run with no stored
  object reads the new default whole). Plan 26 §B6: do not ship a Config-
  shaped field that does nothing — every gate is read by `alertWebhook`
  via `src/alerts.js:39-40`.
- **No `configVer` bump** — adding fields to defaults is additive and the
  loader's `load(..., defaultObj)` merge covers it.
- **No prune TTL for the alert dedup** — handled by
  `core.js:1160-1162` global prune of `state.alerted` already.
- **No new lock**, **no new scheduler** — runs from
  `renderIntel()` cadence at 15s (`boot.js:108-115`).

## 6. Config surface

| Field | Type | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[data-cfg=counter-intel]` | checkbox | **OFF** | Webhook fire opt-in; align with `csAlert` / `culturalGoldBudget` defaults that are read-mostly but still surface to the user. |
| `state.counterIntelThreshold` | number | 3 | Hysteresis — a single spy is noise; ≥3 in 24h is a watch state. Range 2..20, integer. |

The threshold is read-only on the panel today — adding a numeric field is
optional and **deferred** (per plan 27 §13 "Every Config toggle has a
`configVer` bump"; if added it follows the `data-cfg=counter-intel-thresh`
pattern at `src/ui.js:1393-1401`). Default of 3 keeps the scan quiet for
ordinary play.

**HIGH-RISK?** No — read-only aggregation, opt-in webhook.

## 7. Post surface & safety

None. The whole flow is read-mostly over `state.findings`. No
`bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbCaptchaPause`
entry. Plan 27 §7's "no post surface" applies in full — section gets one
honest line by the README §7 rule.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`intelMyIdentity()` returns `{id:null, name:null}`** (`src/intel.js:26`)
  — `intelActorIsMe` returns `false`, the scan filters everything out, no
  webhook fires. Throttle a single `gbLogT('counter-intel-blind',
  600000, 'intel: identity unreadable — counter-intel scan skipped')`
  so the user can tell WHY the panel is empty.
- **`f.defender` is null and `f.town` is null** — skip. Inferred from the
  signature `parseReport` returns (`src/parse-inline.js:77-83`), both fields
  are independently nullable. The "defender resolves to me" test requires at
  least one of them; otherwise the row is invisible to this scan.
- **`state.findings.length > 500`** — already capped at intake
  (`src/spy.js:250-253` and `src/core.js:1167-1171`). Per CLAUDE.md "we
  shall never let a silent re-bind invalidate prior reasoning", the
  threshold check is **post-aggregation**, so a 500-row cap that drops
  older spy findings can only reduce "n" (never artificially *raise* it).
- **`type === 'spy'` case mismatch** (`'Spy'`, `'scout'`) —
  `parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:51`) does not lowercase `r.type` and
  on some clients sends title-cased strings. Match `/^spy$/i.test(f.type)`
  instead of strict equality, mirroring how
  `intelPlayerKey` (`src/intel.js:1-3`) trims but does not lowercase.
  Document this as the only normalization step; do not extend silently.
- **Webhook spam** — handled by the dedup key
  `'counter-intel:' + key + ':' + bucket`. The bucket
  `Math.floor(now / windowMs)` rolls at the 24h boundary exactly as in
  `intelPatternScan` (`src/intel.js:228-229`).

## 9. Validation gate

Plan 27 §11 risk class Low: preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

- Preflight row `intel: counter-intel scan`: pass when
  `state.findings.some(f => /^spy$/i.test(f.type || ''))` is true and the
  scan runs; warn when the identity getter is unreadable.
- Manual, Config-driven: enable `[data-cfg=counter-intel]`, point a
  webhook URL at a Discord test channel. Hand-trigger ≥3 spy reports on
  a single town (visit the town with a few scout missions). Expected: one
  webhook fires within 15s of the third report, with redaction off
  (`state.exportRedact !== false`) showing the attacker name. Log shows
  `counter-intel: <player> hit Nx in 24h` once.
- Negative path: enable but rewind one finding (or filter by attacker
  with a watchlist-rule that excludes me). No webhook fires when `n <
  threshold` even with the toggle ON. Log stays empty.
- Policy guard: verify the Log has **no** entry that fingerprints another
  player's behaviour (e.g. "player's session appears tactical"). If a
  contributor ever extends the readout to correlate spy timing with
  attack timing, **stop** — that crosses plan 27 §0's explicit ban.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Threat assessment engine** (plan 27 §5.3 = `5.3-threat-assessment-engine.md`,
  this cluster). Different signal: 5.3 scores *current* hostiles against
  each of **my** towns; 4.2 is who has been *watching* me over a 24h
  window. The schemas do not overlap.
- **Battle report analyzer** (plan 27 §2.5 = `2.5-battle-report-analyzer.md`,
  this cluster). 2.5 reads the same `state.findings` for losses + farms;
  4.2 reads them for spy origins. Re-use the existing collection, no new
  ingestion.
- **Spy report deep parse** (plan 27 §2.1): when 2.1 lands,
  `state.findings[i]` carries more fields per row (buildings, hero). 4.2
  reads only `type`, `attacker`, `defender`, `town`, `ts`. No re-write.
- **Counter-farming / counter-cheat evasion** — explicitly forbidden by
  plan 27 §0. If anyone wants to spot a watcher who is about to attack,
  that's a separate plan that has to clear the policy gate first.
- **Persist per-watch list beyond dedup** — no per-player `watchedAt`
  history. The dedup bucket plus `last-seen` from `intelDossiers()`
  (`src/intel.js:55, 63`) covers the use cases without a new key.
- **Outbound counter-spy auto-response** — out of scope and would
  violate the same §0 line. Inbound spy reports are passive intel.
