## 4.3-hero-manager.md

# 4.3 — Hero manager (stamina / equipment / notifications / auto-assign)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** L
**Module:** extend `src/military.js` (NOT a new `hero.js`) + minor edits to
`src/header.js`, `src/core.js`, `src/qol.js`, `src/orchestrate.js`, `src/stats.js`,
`src/boot.js`. Attack-tab render call site is `renderMilitaryHelpers(sec, plan)`
at `src/military.js:166`, invoked from `renderAttack` at `src/attack.js:957`.
No `build.py` MODULES slot change.
**Depends on:** none (foundation only; auto-assign reuses the `confirmed` opt
pattern from `heroAssignToTown` at `src/military.js:143`).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0

> **Plan 27 hints are partly wrong.** §4 says "new `hero.js` (extends Attack
> tab 11.2)"; §9 says "Hero transfer ... Coded". The Coded part is true; the
> new-module hint is wrong. All existing hero code lives in `src/military.js`
> (zero `[Hh]ero|[Tt]ransfer` hits in `src/attack.js`). A new `hero.js` would
> duplicate `state.heroTpl`, `gbLock('hero')`, the
> `MM.getModels().PlayerHero` read, and the Attack-tab render. Plan extends
> `src/military.js`.

---

## 1. What exists today

- **Hero model read** — `playerHeroesList()` at `src/military.js:90-107`
  returns `{type, name, home, origin, arrival, traveling, injured, attacking,
  assigned, status, level}`. Does **not** read stamina, mana, inventory, or
  equipment. Only derived predicate: `heroTownOccupied` (`src/military.js:108-111`).
- **Transfer (manual, confirm-gated)** — `heroAssignToTown`
  `src/military.js:142-151`, `heroUnassign` `src/military.js:152-158`,
  `heroCancelTravel` `src/military.js:159-165`. Each short-circuits on
  `!opts.confirmed` (`src/military.js:143,153,160`) — the **confirm gate**
  plan 27 §4 mandates for auto-assignment is already wired by hand.
- **Template learning** — `src/farms.js:101-110`. The `hookXhr` arm detects
  `PlayerHero` URLs containing `assignToTown|unassignFromTown|cancelTownTravel`
  and stores `{model_url, action_name, arguments}` into `state.heroTpl[action]`.
  Persisted at `STORE.HERO_TPL` (`src/header.js:57`), world-scoped
  (`src/header.js:200`).
- **Bridge post** — `heroBridgePost(action, heroType, targetTownId, onDone)`
  at `src/military.js:112-141`. Acquires `gbLock('hero')`, asks
  `captchaPausedAny('hero', 'attack')` (`src/military.js:115`), builds the
  payload by copying string/number/boolean fields from the captured template
  and injecting the hero type + town id under whichever key the template
  carries (`src/military.js:126-132`). **No payload field is invented.**
- **Reconciliation** — `txHeroStatus` at `src/tx.js:171-181`;
  `txReconcileNow` for `kind === 'hero'` at `src/tx.js:441-453` matches
  `assignToTown` / `unassignFromTown` / `cancelTownTravel` by regex. Stamina
  / equipment changes are not in `s.before` and are therefore not reconciled.
- **Stats probe** — `src/stats.js:219-223` reports learned actions from
  `Object.keys(state.heroTpl)`. No stamina, no equipment count.
- **Attack-tab render** — `.atk-heroes` container at `src/ui.js:641-644`,
  populated by `renderMilitaryHelpers` at `src/military.js:184-201`. Per hero:
  `name LvX | status @town` and **exactly one** action button (Cancel /
  Unassign / Assign), all `confirm()` gated at `src/military.js:196-198`.
- **Lock TTL** — `hero: 180000` at `src/core.js:165`. Captcha-breaker key
  `'hero'` already wired (`src/military.js:115` + lazy register at
  `src/core.js:1359-1365`).
- **State** — `state.heroTpl` at `src/core.js:275`, migrated in `ver < 4`
  (`src/core.js:430-444`).
- **Exports** — `heroAssignToTown` / `heroUnassign` / `heroCancelTravel` /
  `txHeroStatus` / `playerHeroesList` wired at `src/boot.js:231-236`.

## 2. Gap

Plan 27 §4 row: *assign / stamina / equipment / notifications*. The `assign`
column is **done by hand** (transfer coded; see §1). The other three columns
are absent — verified by ripgrep over `src/`: `stamina|heroMana|energy`,
`equipment|inventory|items|gear|slot`, and `autoHero|heroTick|heroScan` all
return zero hits. There is also no `alertWebhook('hero', …)` call anywhere
(`state.webhookEvents` at `src/core.js:313` has `{captcha, attack, warehouse,
culture}`; no `hero` key). The Med-risk surface this plan ships: (a) a read-
only **stamina / mana / equipment panel** in the Attack-tab hero row, (b) an
**equipment swap heuristic** that only proposes moves (never discards), (c) a
**low-stamina notification** wired through `alertWebhook('hero', …)`, and
(d) an **auto-assign loop** behind `state.autoHero` (default OFF) that
requires a per-tick user confirm via the existing `opts.confirmed` opt — same
shape as `dodgeScan` smart-auto (`src/dodge.js:196,261`).

## 3. Design

- **Read: stamina + mana + equipment** — extend `playerHeroesList` to also
  read each model's stamina/mana/equipment. The model's getter names are
  **unknown** until a hand-click is sniffed; §4 item 1 captures the sniff.
  Every field returns `null` when its source getter is `undefined` or a non-
  finite number — precondition invariant, never a block.
- **Read: equipment slots** — same source. Slot ids and item ids are
  **unknown**. Store the raw snapshot per world as
  `state.heroEquip[heroType] = {slots: {…}, items: […]}` for diffing.
- **Decision (heuristic)**: when a hero carries a low-tier item in a slot
  whose **known** upgrade is held by another (free) hero in the same world,
  propose a swap. **Never discard**: the heuristic never moves an item to a
  vault / sale / unknown destination. The proposal lives in
  `state.heroEquipSuggest` and surfaces as a row in the Attack-tab panel.
- **Decision (auto-assign)**: behind `state.autoHero` (default OFF). On every
  `orchTick` (5min cadence), `heroScan()` picks the lowest-fill owned town
  for each free hero and calls `heroAssignToTown(type, tid, {confirmed:
  false}, …)`. The handler short-circuits at `src/military.js:143` and the
  panel surfaces the proposal as a click-to-confirm button; the next tick
  posts via `{confirmed: true}`.
- **Notification**: when stamina ≤ `state.heroLowStaminaPct`% of max,
  `alertWebhook('hero', …)` fires + Log-tab one-liner. Throttled by
  `alertWebhookKey` (`src/alerts.js:19-27`); 5min/webhook rate-limit at
  `src/alerts.js:44`. Captcha-pause key `'hero'` already exists, no new key.
- **Cadence**: `ORCH_HANDLERS.hero` at 5min, no `gbInterval`. Add `'hero'`
  to `PRIORITY_ORDER_DEFAULT` (`src/header.js:189-190`).
- **Dry-run**: `bridgePost` honours `state.dryRun`. `heroScan` posts only via
  `heroBridgePost`, so dry-run coverage is automatic.

## 4. Work items

1. **Sniff PlayerHero attribute names** for stamina / mana / equipment. Watch
   `hookXhr` (`src/farms.js:101-110` arm) on one hand-clicked hero panel
   and capture into `archive/captures/hero-attrs.json`. Must include at least
   one integer field distinct from `level`, one stamina-like pair
   (current+max), and one item-bag field. **Do not guess attribute names.**
   Until the capture exists, the read path returns nulls and the heuristic
   never proposes a swap. Add a Preflight row `hero stamina readable`
   (`src/stats.js:219`-area).

2. **Extend `playerHeroesList`** (`src/military.js:90-107`) to also return
   `{stamina: {current, max, ts}, mana: {current, max, ts}, equipment:
   {slots: {…}, items: […]}}`. Add a 60s memo `playerHeroesListCached` (like
   `townResState` at `src/core.js`) so the orchestrator tick does not re-read
   `MM.getModels().PlayerHero` 3×/s.

3. **Add `state.heroEquipSuggest`** (world-scoped, see §5) and the heuristic
   `heroEquipmentSuggest()` at `src/military.js:<new>`. Rule: propose a
   slot swap **only** when both heroes' slot maps are readable AND the
   source slot's tier is lower than the destination's. Never proposes
   removal.

4. **Add `state.autoHero`** (`src/core.js` defaults; load
   `STORE.AUTO_HERO`, default `false`). HIGH-RISK toggle — default OFF per
   `CLAUDE.md`. The confirm-gate opt (`opts.confirmed`) already exists at
   `src/military.js:143`; no change to the post path.

5. **Add `state.heroLowStaminaPct`** (load `STORE.HERO_LOW_STAMINA_PCT`,
   default `20`). Notification only — never a precondition.

6. **Wire `heroScan` into `orchTick`** — `ORCH_HANDLERS.hero`,
   `ORCH_CAPTCHA.hero = 'hero'`, `ORCH_CADENCE.hero = 300000` at
   `src/orchestrate.js:<new>`. Do **not** add a `gbInterval`. Add `'hero'`
   to `PRIORITY_ORDER_DEFAULT` (`src/header.js:189-190`). `state.autoHero`
   gates dispatch.

7. **Notification path** — new `heroNotify(event, hero, extra)` at
   `src/military.js:<new>` calling `alertWebhook('hero', alertWebhookKey
   ('hero', {id: hero.type, …}))` (`src/alerts.js:19`). Events emitted:
   `low-stamina` (≤ `heroLowStaminaPct`%), `injured`, `auto-assign-proposed`.

8. **Attack-tab panel extension** — extend `renderMilitaryHelpers` at
   `src/military.js:184-201` so each hero row also shows `stamina cur/max`,
   `mana cur/max`, and (if readable) a one-line equipment summary. Below
   the rows: an "Auto-asignar" toggle bound to `state.autoHero`, and a
   "Alerta stamina baja %" toggle bound to `state.heroLowStaminaPct`. Reuse
   the existing `.atk-heroes` container.

9. **Config surface** — `src/qol.js` adds two Spanish rows: `Auto-asignar
   heroes` (checkbox, default OFF) and `Alerta stamina baja %` (number
   0–100, default 20). Bump `state.configVer` to **11**
   (`src/header.js:191`) and `@version` to `3.10.0` (`src/header.js:4`).

10. **Preflight** — add a probe at `src/stats.js:219`-area asserting
    `stamina.current !== null && stamina.max > 0` on at least one hero.
    **warn** (not fail) when no hero exposes stamina; **fail** only when
    the capture exists AND the live model disagrees with the capture.

## 5. State & storage

| Field | Default | STORE key | WORLD_SCOPED_BASES |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state.autoHero` | `false` | `STORE.AUTO_HERO` = `'grepbot:auto-hero'` (new) | no (boolean) |
| `state.heroLowStaminaPct` | `20` | `STORE.HERO_LOW_STAMINA_PCT` = `'grepbot:hero-low-stamina-pct'` (new) | no (number) |
| `state.heroEquipSuggest` | `{}` | `STORE.HERO_EQUIP_SUGGEST` = `'grepbot:hero-equip-suggest'` (new) | **yes** — keyed by `heroType`. Add to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-215`). |
| `state.heroStaminaCache` | `{}` | in-memory only, no STORE | n/a — 60s memo |

`configVer` → **11** (`src/header.js:191`). No `GB_LOCK_TTL` change —
`'hero'` already `180000` (`src/core.js:165`). Prune TTL 7d uniform.

## 6. Config surface

| Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Auto-asignar heroes` | checkbox | OFF | HIGH-RISK per `CLAUDE.md`. ON → `heroScan` runs in `orchTick`; per-tick confirm still required via the Attack-tab button. |
| `Alerta stamina baja %` | number (0–100) | 20 | Threshold for `low-stamina` notification. 0 disables. |

Both rows added to the Config tab in `src/qol.js` (Spanish UI). Hidden from
the JSON export by default (`exportRedact` at `src/core.js:347`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Auto-assign post** — goes through `heroBridgePost`
  (`src/military.js:112-141`), which already calls `gbLock('hero')`,
  `captchaPausedAny('hero','attack')`, `bridgePost('hero', …)` with
  `gbAjaxWatch` settlement via `TPL_FEATURE_MAP.hero = 'heroTpl'`
  (`src/core.js:781`). **No new post route.**
- **Equipment swap** — **no post**. The heuristic populates
  `state.heroEquipSuggest` and the panel renders the proposal. The
  equipment-swap payload is **unknown**; §10 keeps it out of scope.
- **Notification** — `alertWebhook('hero', …)` (`src/alerts.js:28`).
  `state.dryRun` short-circuits at `src/alerts.js:31-34`; dry-run logs
  `DRY-RUN webhook hero:` in the Log tab.
- **Captcha pause** — key `'hero'` already registered (`src/military.js:115`).
- **Lock** — `gbLock('hero')` already in `GB_LOCK_TTL` (`src/core.js:165`).
- **Dry-run gate** — inherited from `bridgePost`; §9 step 1 proves coverage.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Stamina / mana getter returns `undefined`** — surface `null`, never
  block. Panel renders `stamina -/-`; notification path treats the field as
  missing (no `low-stamina` event). Precondition invariant: a check may only
  block on a value it actually read. (CLAUDE.md "Precondition readers".)
- **Equipment slot ids change between client builds** — heuristic returns
  empty proposal list. Preflight `hero stamina readable` emits `warn` when
  no hero exposes stamina; `fail` only when the capture exists AND the live
  model disagrees.
- **Captcha response on auto-assign** — `captchaTrip('hero', …)` from
  `bridge.js` classify path; `heroBridgePost` rejects for the ladder
  duration. `heroScan` short-circuits via
  `captchaPausedAny('hero','attack')` at the top of its handler.
- **`state.dryRun` true + an auto-assign tick** — handler emits
  `skip:dryrun` via `bridgePost` and `gbLog('DRY-RUN hero: …')`. No payload.
- **Bfcache / mobile exit mid-transfer** — `gbLock('hero')` carries TTL +
  `pagehide`/`beforeunload` call `gbUnlockAll()` (CLAUDE.md "Lock registry").
  A stranded `heroTpl` entry is read-only and never posted — the resolver at
  `src/military.js:117` matches `tpl.action_name === action` and aborts on
  mismatch.
- **World switch** — `state.heroEquipSuggest` and `state.heroTpl` are both
  world-scoped (`src/header.js:200` + §5); previous-world proposals do not
  leak.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Med-risk class.

1. **Dry-run parity** — `state.dryRun = true`, `state.autoHero = true`, one
   free hero + one town selected. Trigger an `orchTick` (or wait 5min).
   Log shows `hero: auto-assign proposed <name> -> <town>` once; the per-
   tick confirm button reads `Asignar (dry-run)`; `bridgePost` never fires.
   Stats budget does not move.
2. **Live single transfer** — `state.dryRun = false`, one free hero. Click
   `Asignar`; `confirm()` fires, `heroBridgePost` logs
   `hero: assignToTown <type> -> <town> OK`, `txReconcileNow` returns
   `'applied'` once the model's `assigned` flips. Stats probe
   (`src/stats.js:219-223`) still lists `assignToTown`.
3. **Auto-assign with confirm gate** — `state.autoHero = true`. Log shows
   `hero: auto-assign proposed …` every 5min; clicking the proposal posts
   once, then `state.autoHero` does **not** fire again until the hero is
   unassigned. No double-post. `gbSkip('hero', 'auto-need-confirm')` row
   exists for each skipped tick.
4. **Stamina notification** — `state.heroLowStaminaPct = 80`. Wait for a
   hero's stamina to drop below 80% (or hand-edit `state.heroStaminaCache`
   in DevTools for one tick). Log shows `hero: low-stamina <name> <pct>%`.
   Webhook fires once per `(hero, reason)` per 5min
   (`alertLastSent` throttle at `src/alerts.js:44`).
5. **Equipment heuristic** — `state.heroEquipSuggest` populates only when
   two heroes' slot maps are both readable AND a tier difference exists.
   Preflight `hero equipment readable` returns `warn` until
   `archive/captures/hero-attrs.json` exists. With the capture present, two
   free heroes whose slot maps differ produce exactly one
   `state.heroEquipSuggest` row.
6. **HIGH-RISK OFF default** — fresh install (or after `qolResetConfig`):
   `state.autoHero === false`. Config row unchecked.
   `state.dryRun` covers the feature even when ON.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Equipment discard / sale / vault** — explicit plan 27 §4 policy: "swap
  heuristic only, NEVER discard". A future "vacate slot" plan would need a
  separate endpoint sniff.
- **Skill / spell selection** — hero ability automation is a different
  surface; belongs with divine-spell automation (4.4) or a future
  hero-skills plan.
- **Auto-recruit while traveling** — not part of hero manager; auto-recruit
  lives in `src/recruit.js` behind its own toggle.
- **Auto-assign while injured** — `playerHeroesList` returns
  `injured: true` (`src/military.js:101`) and `heroAssignToTown` rejects
  with `'injured'` (`src/military.js:147`). Reused as-is; no new code.
- **Hero XP / level-up notifications** — `level` already read
  (`src/military.js:105`); an XP-tracking plan needs a separate capture and
  is deferred.
- **Item swap post route** — payload unknown. Captured in the sniff file
  but not actioned here. Belongs in a future equipment-automation plan.

## 4.4-divine-spell-automation.md

# 4.4 — Divine spell automation

**Bucket:** v4.5 · **Risk:** High · **Size:** L
**Module:** split spell mechanics out of `src/recruit.js` into NEW `src/god-spells.js`
(`recruit.js` keeps `recruitBuild` + the recruit gate and consumes the new helpers);
add a new entry to `build.py` MODULES at the slot after `favor.js` (line 57) and
before `wonder.js` (line 58).
**Depends on:** none; sits behind the existing `state.autoFavor` toggle per plan 27
§4.4, HIGH-RISK OFF default, `temple_plunder` research required, target = farm town.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/favor.js`, `src/recruit.js`, `src/wonder.js`, `src/core.js`,
`src/header.js`.

- **Two spell mechanisms today, both partial.**
  - **Favor-for-attack** lives entirely in `favor.js` and spends units at a farm
    village to generate per-god favor. `FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED = false`
    (`favor.js:8`) keeps the loop from running; `favorScan`
    (`favor.js:52-152`) is the gate + payload, payload uses `attackTpl`
    (`favor.js:133-139`) — it does **not** cast a spell.
  - **Recruit spells** (`recruit.js:4` `RECRUIT_SPELLS = ['call_of_the_ocean',
    'spartan_training', 'fertility_improvement']`; god map `recruit.js:8-12`
    `RECRUIT_SPELL_GODS`) already implement the full cast path:
    `recruitSpellGateOk` (`recruit.js:55-68`, gates on academy + god),
    `recruitSpellCooldown` (`recruit.js:43-54`, persisted via
    `STORE.SPELL_COOLDOWN` = `'grepbot:spell-cooldown'`, `header.js:177`,
    world-scoped, `core.js:319` loads it into `state.spellCooldown`),
    `recruitHasSpell` (`recruit.js:25-38`, reads the `CastedPowers` MM
    collection), and `recruitCastSpell` (`recruit.js:69-80`,
    `gameAjaxPost('spell', 'town_overviews', 'cast_power', {power_id, town_id}, onDone)`).
- **Recruit spell integration is wired but opt-in.** `recruitScan` only
  attempts a spell when `state.recruitSpells` (`core.js:332`,
  default `false`, `header.js:120`) is true and a `favorCfg.recruitPower`
  is set (`recruit.js:319`); the cast is part of a recruit job's lifecycle,
  not its own loop.
- **No non-recruit power ids are cited anywhere in `src/`.** Grep over
  `power_id|cast_power|RECRUIT_SPELLS|god_power` in `src/` finds the
  recruit spell infrastructure and the quest reward parser
  (`quests.js:66,82-84,94,121,217,294,303`), nothing else. Plan 27 §0
  blocks inventing ids; the only safe enumeration is the recruit spell
  list, with a sniff path for any others.
- **TPL_FEATURE_MAP** (`core.js:778-790`) maps `wonder` → `wonderFavorTpl`
  but has **no** `spell` or `favor` entry. The comment at `core.js:790`
  reads literally: *"Favor is currently disabled in src/favor.js; leave
  it unmapped so re-enable does not poison attackTpl health. When favor
  gets its own learned payload, add a dedicated `favorTpl` here."* A
  `spell` entry is therefore needed if any divine-spell post re-uses
  `recruitCastSpell`'s route.
- **Wonder-favor precedent for HIGH-RISK loops.** `wonderFavorScan`
  (`wonder.js:154-183`) is the only currently-coded "spend a learned
  payload" loop: HIGH-RISK (`autoWonderFavor` `core.js:376`,
  `STORE.AUTO_WONDER_FAVOR` `header.js:172`, default `false`),
  `gbLock('wonder-favor')` (`wonder.js:168`, TTL `180000ms`
  `core.js:160`), `gbCaptchaPause`-style feature key `'wonder'` already
  covers it (`wonder.js:155`). The budget discipline
  (`wonder.js:10-19, 110-114`) is the daily-favor-spend model to copy.
- **Orchestrator** has a `favor` slot (`orchestrate.js:5-20`,
  `PRIORITY_ORDER_DEFAULT` includes `favor` `header.js:190`) but no
  `spell` slot; cadences are declared in `orchestrate.js` and there is
  no per-feature `gbInterval` (CLAUDE.md "v1.1.0 orch is the sole econ
  scheduler").

## 2. Gap

Favor-for-attack is intentionally parked (`FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED =
false`). What is missing is the **second** divine-spell class: spending
favor on `cast_power` against an enemy / farm town (or, separately, on a
defensive target). Today the only way the bot casts a god power is the
`recruitSpells` accelerator inside `recruitScan`, and it only knows the
three recruit spells. A user who wants to spend favor on a meteor,
earthquake, or any non-recruit spell has no surface. The mechanics
(gate, cooldown, persistence) exist in `recruit.js` but are hard-coded
to recruit and live behind the recruit cadence — pulling them out is
what makes a generic god-spell loop possible without copy-pasting the
gate.

## 3. Design

Split the cast mechanics out of `recruit.js` into a new `src/god-spells.js`,
keep the existing `recruitCastSpell` call path stable, and add a
**separate** orchestrator slot (`godspell`) that fires only when
`state.autoFavor` is true and the existing favor-favor loop is parked
(v4.5 stays HIGH-RISK OFF default per plan 27 §4.4; the existing
`autoFavor` toggle is the gate, since the user's mental model is
"auto-favor" = "let the bot spend favor for me"). The spell scan reads
favor, gates, picks a target, casts, and uses the existing cooldown
registry — no new post class, no new endpoint, no new template
(defaulting to the `cast_power` constant the recruit path uses).

Power id discipline (CLAUDE.md, recruit note): **never default to
`call_of_the_ocean`**. The cast path takes the explicit id from
`favorCfg.spellPower` (a new field on the same config block the
recruit accelerator reads at `recruit.js:319`). An unrecognised id →
log once → no cast. A non-recuit power id (meteor, etc.) is
**unknown** to the tree; the work item to learn it is the standard
hand-cast sniff, not a guess.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.favorCfg.spellPower` (string, default `null`) — the
  configured power id; lowercased on save.
- `state.favorCfg.spellReserve` (number 0-100, default 50) — never
  spend favor below this fraction of cap. Mirrors
  `wonderFavorReserve` (plan 02).
- `state.spellCooldown` already exists (`core.js:319`,
  `STORE.SPELL_COOLDOWN` `header.js:177`); the new module shares it
  with `recruit.js` via the split.
- `STORE.SPELL_RESERVE = 'grepbot:spell-reserve'` — new,
  world-scoped (god pools differ across worlds), add to
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`.
- `configVer` bump (`CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` `header.js:191`): 10 → 11.
  The migration at the import site (`qol.js:267`) needs a one-liner
  that defaults `favorCfg.spellPower = null` and `favorCfg.spellReserve
  = 50` for any imported config that predates v4.5.
- TTL: `state.spellCooldown` already prunes via `STORE` prune
  (`core.js:1087`-ish, per plan 27 §13 "7d uniform unless the slice
  needs longer"); no change.

## 6. Config surface

- New Config field: `Hechizos divinos (HIGH-RISK)` toggle — bound to
  `state.autoFavor` per plan 27 §4.4 (no new toggle). HIGH-RISK label
  visible in Config.
- New Config field: `Poder (power id)` — text input bound to
  `favorCfg.spellPower`, lowercased on save, placeholder
  `call_of_the_ocean | spartan_training | fertility_improvement | <hand-cast>`.
- New Config field: `Reserva de favor (%)` — number 0-100, default 50.
- New Config field: `Aldea objetivo` — the farm-town id selector,
  reuses the existing `favorCfg.targetId` + `favorCfg.targetType` (no
  new fields; the favor loop already owns them).

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Endpoint** is the existing `town_overviews/cast_power`
  (`recruit.js:76-79`, confirmed in source — **NOT a guess**). Payload
  `{power_id, town_id:+townId}`. Dry-run gate (`state.dryRun`) is
  honoured automatically by `gameAjaxPost` → `txRun` (`tx.js:522-647`,
  dry-run aborts at `txActionGate` before the budget mark).
- **Watch registration**: `gbAjaxWatch('ajax:town_overviews/
  cast_power', settle)` already fires from `gameAjaxRaw`
  (`bridge.js:176`); no new watcher needed. Template name in
  `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` as `spell: 'castPowerTpl'` (key reserved for any
  future learned payload — the current payload is hardcoded).
- **Captcha breaker key**: add `'godspell'` to whatever feature-key
  list the captcha breaker reads (`bridge.js` exposes the registry
  per CLAUDE.md "captcha breakers"). Mirror the existing `'favor'`
  and `'wonder'` entries.
- **Lock name**: `gbLock('godspell', 180000)`, add a `GB_LOCK_TTL`
  entry `godspell: 180000` (`core.js:145-174`, next to `favor` and
  `wonder`).
- **Dry-run behaviour**: `DRY-RUN spell: {power_id, town_id}` log
  line, journal as `skip:dryrun`. The same path `recruit.js:344-351`
  uses today.
- **Favor-spend is irreversible** (CLAUDE.md "favor is irreversible,
  manual review required", `recruit.js:349`): the 30-min cooldown is
  the safety window; a blind timeout stamps it. Do **not** retry on
  `pending` or `timeout_unknown` (`recruit.js:347-348` precedent).

## 8. Failure modes

- **Unreadable god pool** (`favorCurrent()` returns `{}`):
  `gbLogT('godspell-favor-blind', 300000, ...)` once; return. Never
  spend on a blind read (CLAUDE.md precondition invariant, mirror
  `favor.js:73-76`).
- **Unrecognised power id** (`state.favorCfg.spellPower` set to
  something not in `RECRUIT_SPELLS` and not yet hand-sniffed):
  `gbLogT('godspell-badpower', 600000, ...)` once. The cast does
  **not** happen — server-side rejection costs a budget slot and a
  decision-memory strike every cadence (`recruit.js:316-322`
  precedent).
- **Wrong-god cast** (power id's required god ≠ town's god):
  `godSpellGateOk` returns `{ok:false, why:'god-mismatch'}`. Block;
  do **not** post.
- **Academy missing**: `godSpellGateOk` returns `{ok:false,
  why:'no-academy'}`. Block; do **not** post.
- **Below reserve**: `godSpellScan` returns silently; log once per
  10min (`gbLogT('godspell-reserve', 600000, ...)`).
- **Already cast in town** (`CastedPowers` model shows the power):
  `godSpellHasCast` returns `true`; skip. (Prevents the
  double-charge that `recruitHasSpell` was added for at
  `recruit.js:25-38`.)
- **Cooldown active** (`state.spellCooldown[townId][powerId] > now`):
  log once per minute; do not post.
- **Captcha response**: `gbCaptchaPause` breaker opens; loop sleeps
  per `state.captchaLadder` ladder (`core.js:353`,
  `[5,15,60]` minutes default).
- **Decision-memory strike** (`journal.js` v1.1.0): three hard
  errors in a row on the same `feature|action|target` open a 5/15/60min
  skip window (`journal.js:86`-ish, per CLAUDE.md "decision memory").
  Captcha/timeout do not trip it.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 HIGH-RISK row: payload sniff against live UI +
confirm-gate screen + dry-run + manual re-fire once, **still default
OFF** until per-package exit criteria. Concrete, in order:

1. **Payload sniff.** Open a town's temple in the live UI, hand-cast
   one of the three recruit spells, confirm `gbAjaxWatch` settles the
   watch from the XHR response (`bridge.js:7-19, 36-58`). The
   captured `model_url`/`action_name` must equal
   `town_overviews/cast_power` (already cited from `recruit.js:76-79`,
   this step only confirms the live UI sends that route on this
   world).
2. **Dry-run ON.** Set `favorCfg.spellPower = 'call_of_the_ocean'`,
   `favorCfg.targetId = <farm_town>`, `favorCfg.targetType =
   'farm_town'`. Force one tick. Log must show `DRY-RUN spell:
   {power_id:'call_of_the_ocean', town_id:<N>}`; journal must show
   `skip:dryrun`; no POST.
3. **Reserve honoured.** Set `spellReserve = 90`. Confirm zero casts
   while god pool < 90% of cap.
4. **Wrong-god block.** Configure the power for ares on an
   athena-only town. Confirm `god-mismatch:<athena>!=<ares>` log and
   no POST.
5. **Academy missing.** Configure the power for a town with no
   Academy building. Confirm `no-academy` log and no POST.
6. **Live cast (manual gate).** `dryRun = false`, single hand-triggered
   scan, confirm one POST, one `cast_power` arrives in the temple UI,
   cooldown stamped.
7. **Cooldown persistence.** Reload page; confirm `spellCooldown` is
   still set (via Diag dump) and the next scan skips with
   `skip:cooldown`.
8. **Preflight row** `godspell`: pass = id is in `RECRUIT_SPELLS` or
   academy is readable; warn = id set but god unreadable; fail = id
   set but academy missing for the configured town.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Non-farm-town targets.** Plan 27 §4.4 says "temple_plunder ONLY";
  the `targetType` allow-list at `favor.js:93-96` is reused verbatim.
  A plan for attacking enemy towns with divine spells is its own
  feature (plan 27 §3 movement family, separate risk profile).
- **Sniffing non-recruit power ids (meteor, earthquake, etc.).** The
  three RECRUIT_SPELLS ids are the only power ids cited anywhere in
  `src/`. Adding more requires a hand-cast sniff per id (mirrors
  `wonderFavorTpl` for the wonder path); that is a v4.6+ feature and
  is **explicitly unknown** in this plan. The work item is "player
  hand-casts once; the bot captures the id into a learned payload"
  — not "guess the id".
- **Wonder-favor and recruit-spell flows.** Those are owned by plan
  02 and the existing `recruitSpells` accelerator respectively; this
  plan only factors the shared mechanics out, it does not change
  their behaviour.
- **Favor-spend for attack** (`favor.js` favorScan). Stays parked
  behind `FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED = false` (`favor.js:8`) until a
  later plan turns it on. This plan only reads `favorCurrent()`;
  it does not enable the favor-favor loop.
- **Auto-recruit god pairing.** The `RECRUIT_SPELL_GODS` map
  (`recruit.js:8-12`) is the canonical god-of-spell authority and
  ships unchanged.

## 4.5-wall-auto-repair.md

# 4.5 — Wall auto-repair

**Bucket:** v4.5 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/build-auto.js` + `src/build-targets.js` (NOT a new
`wall.js` — see §3 why the plan-27 hint is wrong).
**Depends on:** none.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/goals.js`, `src/build-auto.js`, `src/build-targets.js`,
`src/core.js`, `src/parse-inline.js`.

- **Wall is already a first-class building in the auto-queue.**
  `AB_BUILDINGS` (`goals.js:127`) is `[..., 'wall', ...]` and
  `AB_CS_FAST` (`goals.js:139`) sets the default target to `wall: 10`.
  `abCurrentLevels` (`build-auto.js:14-33`) reads the live level from
  `t.getBuildings()` and accounts for **negative deltas** when a queued
  order carries `tear_down: true`: `if (a.tear_down) levels[type] =
  Math.max(0, levels[type] - 1)` (`build-auto.js:28`). The same model
  attribute `tear_down` is what carries the rebuild action in the
  game's queue representation.
- **The post surface is `BuildingOrder` / `buildUp`** with payload
  `{building_id: building}` (`build-auto.js:246-247`). The same
  payload builds a fresh level and rebuilds a damaged wall back to
  its previous level; the bridge does not have a separate `repair`
  action. The `tear_down` attribute only appears in queue-row
  introspection (`build-auto.js:28, 54`), not in the post payload.
- **No wall-damage model is currently read.** `parse-inline.js:88`
  parses `wall` out of incoming spy reports
  (`r.wall ?? r.wall_level ?? r.defender_wall ?? (r.defender &&
  (r.defender.wall ?? r.defender.wall_level))`) for intel/dossier
  views only; nothing in `build-auto.js`, `core.js`, or `intel.js`
  reads the wall-damage percentage off the home-town model. Plan 27
  §4.5 names "auto-repair" but the wall-damage getter is **unknown**
  to the tree.
- **`abPickNextFromLevels` is the loop that decides what to build.**
  `build-auto.js:178-202` resolves prerequisites, reads
  `goalEffectiveBuildTargets(townId)` (which is `state.abTargets`,
  `build-targets.js:19-27`), and emits the next building to queue.
  `abFinalValidate` (`build-auto.js:204-224`) re-reads the live queue
  and the live levels before posting — so a wall drop between scan
  and post is caught.
- **`abCanAfford` (`build-auto.js:105-119`) reads the cost margin
  honestly** via `t.resources()` and `t.getAvailablePopulation()`,
  with a 10-resource margin. Wall costs are read from
  `BuildingBuildData` (`build-auto.js:58-74`, `abBuildingCost`) — no
  hardcoded cost table.
- **A new module is NOT justified.** Plan 27 §4.5 says "new
  `wall.js`", but the build path already iterates every
  `AB_BUILDINGS` entry and `wall` is in that list; adding a parallel
  module would (a) duplicate the prerequisite resolver,
  `abFinalValidate`, the queue-max reader, the cost reader, and the
  `bridgePost('build',...)` call; (b) split wall into two posts with
  different feature keys (`'build'` vs `'wall'`) which would double
  the captcha-breaker surface and confuse the journal rollups; (c)
  violate the "do not add per-feature loops" rule
  (`orchestrate.js:1-20` is the sole econ scheduler). The honest
  shape is **a rule in the existing loop** plus a small read of the
  damage signal.

## 2. Gap

`abPickNextFromLevels` decides "build X next" from a target-vs-current
comparison (`build-auto.js:186-187` `if (want <= 0 ||
+(levels[target] || 0) >= want) continue;`). When the wall is
damaged, the **level is still the level** — only a separate damage
attribute decreases. So the loop happily leaves a level-20 wall
sitting at 0% integrity, with `levels.wall === 20` and `want ===
20` and no work to do. The user-visible symptom is a wall that does
not get rebuilt after a hit. The fix is (a) detect wall damage from
a model getter that is unknown today (this plan flags the unknown
honestly and writes the read with a fallback to "no damage" =
"no repair needed"), and (b) make the build picker treat
"effective wall level = current level − damage" when the
`autoWallRepair` toggle is on, so a damaged wall falls below the
target and the loop picks it up on the next cadence.

## 3. Design

Extend the existing `abCurrentLevels` (and its prerequisite resolver
sibling `abPickNextFromLevels`) with a per-town wall damage offset
that subtracts from `levels.wall` when `state.autoWallRepair` is on
and the damage is readable. When the damage is unreadable the
picker must log once per town and continue without the offset
(precondition invariant — never block on an unreadable getter).
Everything else (prerequisite resolve, queue-max check, cost check,
`BuildingOrder/buildUp` post) is unchanged and stays on the
`'build'` feature key so the captcha breaker, journal, and
template-health rules continue to cover wall repairs exactly the
same way they cover normal builds.

**No new module.** A `wall.js` would have to reimplement
`abFinalValidate`, `abQueueInfo`, the cost read, the
`bridgePost('build',...)` call, and a lock to coexist with
`abScan`'s `gbLock('ab', ...)` — and any second lock would race
with `abScan` for the same town, since `abScan` walks towns
sequentially (`build-auto.js:312-368`). The right shape is "extend
the existing loop", not "add a parallel loop". Plan 27's hint is
explicitly rejected here.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/build-targets.js`** — add `autoWallRepair` to
   `abDefaultTargets()` (the function at `build-targets.js:1`) as
   a new **toggle** with default `false`. Default-off is required
   for any feature that costs resources without user action (CLAUDE.md
   "HIGH-RISK toggles ... default OFF" — this is Med not High, but
   conservative default still applies because wall repairs consume
   stone/wood). Persist via a new `STORE.AUTO_WALL_REPAIR =
   'grepbot:auto-wall-repair'` key in `src/header.js` and a
   `state.autoWallRepair` field in `src/core.js`'s `state`
   initializer (`core.js:220`-ish, next to `state.abAuto` /
   `state.abOrder`). No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` change — the toggle
   is a per-player, not per-world, value.
2. **`src/build-auto.js`** — extend `abCurrentLevels` (lines
   14-33) so the returned `levels.wall` is the effective level
   after subtracting the damage read.
   - Add a helper `abWallDamage(townId)` at module-local IIFE
     scope. It probes a list of candidate getter/method names on
     `gbTownModel(townId)` — `getWallDamage`, `wallDamage`,
     `getDamagePercentForBuilding`, `getDamagePercentage` — using
     `gbProbeNum` (CLAUDE.md "Precondition readers", `core.js`
     precondition reader block). The first finite number in
     `[0, 100]` wins; anything else returns `null`.
   - In `abCurrentLevels`, after the `for` loop that walks
     `buildingOrders`, if `state.autoWallRepair` and
     `abWallDamage(townId)` is finite and `> 0`, decrement
     `levels.wall` by the damage percent of one wall level
     (effectively: `levels.wall = Math.max(0, +(levels.wall || 0)
     - damage / 100 * (current + 1))`). Use **whole-level
     arithmetic** so the picker sees an integer gap and emits one
     `buildUp` per damaged level, not fractional posts.
   - If `abWallDamage` is `null`, do nothing. Never fabricate a
     damage value (CLAUDE.md precondition invariant).
   - `abWallDamage` must also be probed at the
     `abFinalValidate` site (`build-auto.js:204-224`) so the
     effective level at post time still reflects the latest
     damage read; otherwise a wall that takes a hit between scan
     and post posts a stale level.
3. **`src/core.js`** — extend `tplNameFor` / `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`
   (`core.js:778-795`): the wall-repair post uses
   `bridgePost('build', {model_url:'BuildingOrder',
   action_name:'buildUp', arguments:{building_id:'wall'}, ...})`,
   the same payload as every other build. `TPL_FEATURE_MAP['build']`
   is currently `'ibAction'` (`core.js:782`), and
   `tplNameFor('build', ...)` returns `null` when
   `action_name === 'buildUp'` (`core.js:795-800`). That already
   excludes `buildUp` from the health tracker — wall repairs are
   automatically excluded too. **No change** to
   `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`; just confirm by reading that the existing
   `action_name === 'buildUp'` short-circuit at `core.js:798`
   catches wall rebuilds.
4. **`src/ui.js`** — under the existing Build config (the
   `state.abAuto` toggle area), add one checkbox row
   `Reparar muralla automáticamente (auto-reparar al detectar daño)`.
   Bound to `state.autoWallRepair` (default `false`). Place it
   next to the wall target input (the `state.abTargets['wall']`
   row in the queue table) so the meaning is local.
5. **`src/stats.js`** — Preflight row `wall auto-repair`: pass =
   `autoWallRepair` off OR the `abWallDamage` probe finds a
   readable getter; warn = `autoWallRepair` on and no getter
   found; fail = `autoWallRepair` on but the cost read for the
   next wall level is unreadable (the loop would never post — the
   user should turn the toggle off).

## 5. State & storage

- `state.autoWallRepair` (boolean, default `false`) — new.
- `STORE.AUTO_WALL_REPAIR = 'grepbot:auto-wall-repair'` — new in
  `src/header.js`'s `STORE` block, near `STORE.AB_AUTO`
  (`header.js:68`). Not world-scoped (per-player preference).
- No new `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.
- No new id-bearing keys (the wall is identified by the constant
  `'wall'` already in `AB_BUILDINGS`).
- `configVer` bump (`CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` `header.js:191`): 10 → 11.
  The import migration at `qol.js:267` adds
  `autoWallRepair: false` to the default config.
- No new TTL — `state.abAuto` already lives without a TTL; the
  toggle is a preference, not a journal.

## 6. Config surface

- New Config toggle: `Reparar muralla automáticamente` (Spanish UI,
  CLAUDE.md "panel UI is Spanish"). Default OFF. Bound to
  `state.autoWallRepair`. Visible only when the user has a wall in
  their town (always show; greying out is more code than this plan
  needs).
- No new Config input fields. The wall target (already in the
  build queue table at `state.abTargets['wall']`) is reused.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Endpoint is `BuildingOrder` / `buildUp`** with payload
  `{building_id: 'wall'}` (`build-auto.js:246-247`). Already
  cited from source — **not a guess**. Dry-run gate is honoured
  automatically by `bridgePost` → `txRun` (`tx.js:522-647`).
- **No new `gbAjaxWatch` registration**: the existing watcher at
  `bridge.js:131` (bridge `BuildingOrder|buildUp`) covers every
  `bridgePost('build', ...)` call including wall repairs.
- **No new template name in `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`**: `tplNameFor`'s
  `action_name === 'buildUp'` short-circuit (`core.js:798`)
  already returns `null` and skips the health tracker. Verify
  by reading the code; no edit needed.
- **No new lock name**: the existing `gbLock('ab', ...)` at
  `build-auto.js:272` (TTL `300000ms`, `core.js:151`) covers the
  entire auto-queue scan, wall repairs included. No new entry in
  `GB_LOCK_TTL`.
- **No new captcha-breaker feature key**: the `'build'` key
  already gates the captcha breaker for this feature. The
  Preflight row in §4 item 5 surfaces a missing-g getter without
  any breaker change.
- **Dry-run behaviour**: identical to every other build — a
  `DRY-RUN build: {model_url:'BuildingOrder', action_name:'buildUp',
  arguments:{building_id:'wall'}, town_id:<N>}` log line, journal
  `skip:dryrun`, no POST.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Unreadable wall damage** (`abWallDamage` returns `null`): the
  helper logs once per 5min per town via
  `gbLogT('ab-wall-damage-blind-' + townId, 300000, ...)`; the
  level stays at the model-reported value; no repair posts. The
  Preflight row (§4 item 5) surfaces this without spamming the
  log.
- **Wall at max level with damage**: `levels.wall >= abMaxLevel('wall')`
  is checked at `build-auto.js:217`; the picker rejects with
  `why: 'max-level'` unless the damage offset dropped the effective
  level below the max. With the offset, a damaged max-level wall
  has `effective < max` and the loop picks wall — which is the
  intended behaviour.
- **Cost unreadable for the next wall level**: `abCanAfford`
  (`build-auto.js:105-119`) returns `{ok:false, why:'cost
  unreadable'}`; the picker continues to the next priority
  target. No infinite loop, no blind post.
- **Queue full**: `abQueueInfo` returns `len >= max` and the
  picker rejects with `why:'queue-full'` (`build-auto.js:207`).
  The native queue head is marked `waiting-queue` (already wired
  at `build-auto.js:336`).
- **Two builds racing the same slot**: `gbLock('ab', ...)` at
  `build-auto.js:272` plus `txRecentlyCommitted` at
  `build-auto.js:215` already prevent a double-post. Wall repair
  inherits both.
- **Damage changes between scan and post**: the post-time
  re-read at `abFinalValidate` (`build-auto.js:204-224`) re-asks
  `abCurrentLevels` (now damage-aware) and the validate either
  passes (post) or rejects with `why:'levels-unreadable'` /
  `why:'plan-changed:...'` (skip). The native queue head is
  marked `blocked` or `replan` (`build-auto.js:362`).

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 Med row: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one
full orchestrator tick. Concrete, in order:

1. **Preflight** `wall auto-repair`: pass with the toggle off;
   confirm warn row appears if the toggle is on and the probe
   finds no readable damage getter.
2. **Damage probe**: in the live console, evaluate
   `gbTownModel(<townId>).getWallDamage()` (or whatever the probe
   finds) on a known-damaged town. If undefined across every
   probe name, **mark this whole feature as BLOCKED** until a
   real getter name is captured; do not invent one.
3. **Dry-run ON**, `autoWallRepair = true`, `abTargets.wall = 20`,
   town with wall at level 18 and 50% damage. Force one
   `abScan('manual')`. Log shows two queued `buildUp` posts
   (`wall: 18→19` and `wall: 19→20`) as `DRY-RUN build: ...`; no
   POST; journal `skip:dryrun`.
4. **Dry-run OFF**, same conditions, manual `abScan('manual')`:
   confirm two `BuildingOrder/buildUp` posts for `building_id:
   'wall'`; confirm the model's wall level advances from 18 to
   20; confirm the damage field clears or stays at 0.
5. **Damage mid-scan**: trigger a hostile attack that drops wall
   to 60% between two scans. The next scan picks wall up
   without manual intervention; journal shows
   `auto-queue: wall +1 in town <N> (prereq for wall)` — note
   the `(prereq for wall)` tag is normal (the loop re-emits wall
   as a prereq for itself at the target level).
6. **Max-level damage**: a wall at level `abMaxLevel('wall')` with
   damage > 0. Confirm the loop still posts `buildUp` until the
   effective level reaches the target.

## 10. Out of scope

- **A new `wall.js` module.** Explicitly rejected in §3. The plan
  follows the build path that already exists; the only addition is
  a damage read and a config toggle.
- **Damage reads from any source other than the live town model.**
  No spy-report-driven wall-damage inference (the parse path at
  `parse-inline.js:88` reads `wall` for intel/dossier views, not
  for build automation). If the live getter probe at §9 step 2
  returns nothing, this feature is blocked — do not fall back to
  spy reports.
- **Auto-cap wall at a damage-driven level.** This plan only
  rebuilds to the existing target in `state.abTargets.wall`. A
  "raise wall target by N when damage exceeds X%" feature is its
  own idea and out of scope.
- **Repair scheduling.** The orchestrator cadence for `build`
  (whatever `ORCH_CADENCE['build']` evaluates to after the
  deadlock widening) already covers wall rebuilds; no new
  scheduler is added (CLAUDE.md "no new schedulers").
- **Skirmisher / Captain wall-specific bonuses.** Those are
  gameplay mechanics in the town model, not GrepBot concerns.

## 4.6-favor-regen-hud.md

# 4.6 — Favor regen optimizer (HUD only)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/stats.js` (render-time only; reads `favorCurrent()` from `src/favor.js`)
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2 (header `@version` is `3.9.0`; off by one, harmless)

> Plan 27 row 4.6 is explicit: *"NOT a feature, just a stat panel — no posts,
> no automation."* This plan ships a read-only HUD block in the Stats tab. It
> does **not** enable `state.autoFavor`, does **not** unblock `favorScan` (the
> `FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED = false` flag at `favor.js:8` stays false), and
> adds **no** new state field, lock, or storage key.

---

## 1. What exists today

- The only read path is `favorCurrent()` (`src/favor.js:9-17`). It returns
  `uw.Game.gods.attributes` or the `PlayerGods` model attributes. On any
  failure it returns `{}` — never throws, never `null`.
- `favorScan` (`src/favor.js:52-152`) already enumerates the per-god pool the
  same way a HUD would need to:
  `favor.js:71` `const raw = fav[god] != null ? fav[god] : fav['favor_' + god];`
  `favor.js:72` `const cur = Number(raw);` — this is the precondition invariant
  already in place: if `!Number.isFinite(cur)` the existing scanner logs
  `favor-unreadable` once (`favor.js:73-76`) and bails. The HUD must do the
  same on every cell, not just once.
- `favorCfg` is already in the world-scoped bag (`src/header.js:112`,
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `src/header.js:203`). The default god is `athena`
  (`src/core.js:317`). The default threshold `200` is the same one
  `favorScan` already gates sends on (`src/favor.js:62`).
- Stats body is rendered by `renderStats` (`src/stats.js:280-355`). Layout
  blocks in order: per-feature rollup (`:294-309`), `topErrors` (`:310-314`),
  `topPending` (`:315-319`), `topSkips` (`:320-324`), deadlock notice
  (`:326-330`), orchestrator (`:331-334`), budget line (`:339-344`), preflight
  rollup (`:347-353`). Plan 26 §C2 already added the budget line.
- `preflightRun` (`src/stats.js:12-268`) is the read-only sweep. It already
  has a `bandit camp` row at `src/stats.js:234-238`; the favor path has no
  equivalent. Preflight is one-shot (only on `gb-preflight` click or
  `preflightRunAndRender` call), so it is **not** the HUD surface.
- There is **no** regen-rate field surfaced anywhere in `src/`. The model
  attribute names read today are `favor.<god>` or `favor_favor_<god>` for the
  pool; `max_favor` / `favor_<god>_max` are not referenced. The game client's
  exact attribute set is unknown — the only public docs are in
  `archive/captures/grepo-dump/js/game.min.js` and have no labeled regen
  rate.

## 2. Gap

The Stats tab tells the player how many decisions the bot made, but says
nothing about favor accrual. The user-visible question — *"how long until
athena hits 200 so a favor cast is even worth posting?"* — has no answer in
the panel. Plan 27 §4.6 asks for a regen-aware readout; the regen rate is not
in the model, so the honest deliverable is a pool/ETA panel that derives
the rate from a paired-sample window and degrades to "unknown" cleanly.

## 3. Design

Read-only. No post surface, no captcha breaker, no lock, no scheduler entry.

Per render of `renderStats`, walk the same god list the existing scanner
already accepts (`favor.js:66` uses `cfg.god` only, but the panel wants
**all** gods — the model exposes every pool at once). For each god:

1. `p_now = Number(fav[god] ?? fav['favor_' + god])` — same lookup as
   `favor.js:71`. If `!Number.isFinite(p_now)` ⇒ `unreadable` cell, log once
   via `gbLogT('favor-hud-blind-' + god, 300000, …)` matching the existing
   5-min throttle key style at `favor.js:74`.
2. `p_max = Number(fav['max_favor_' + god] ?? fav['favor_' + god + '_max'] ?? 0)`.
   If `!Number.isFinite(p_max) || p_max <= 0` ⇒ `max ?` cell.
3. Regen rate: derived from a paired-sample window keyed by god. New module
   local `favorRateSamples` (plain object, **not** persisted in `state.*` —
   it rebuilds across reloads). On every `renderStats` call, push
   `{ts: Date.now(), p: p_now}` for each god, prune anything older than
   10 min, and compute `rate = (p_now - p_oldest) / (now - oldest.ts)` in
   pool per second. Two samples are needed before the rate is reported;
   the cell renders `…` until then. A negative rate means the player just
   spent favor (treat as `0` for ETA).
4. ETA to threshold: `etaSec = rate > 0 ? (thresh - p_now) / rate : ∞`.
   `thresh` defaults to `state.favorCfg.thresh` (default 200 — same as
   `favor.js:62`). Render as `m:ss` if finite, `—` if not regen'ing or
   already above threshold.

Output is one block between the `topSkips` block (`stats.js:320-324`) and
the deadlock notice (`stats.js:326-330`):

```
favor (gods)        actual  max   rate   eta 200
  athena              412   1500  1.4/m  ?
  hera                118   1500  0.0/m  — (no regen sample)
  poseidon            ?        ?   ?      ? (unreadable)
```

The `"rate"` cell is `pool/min`, rounded to one decimal. The `"eta 200"`
cell is the time the pool will hit `state.favorCfg.thresh` (or `—` if
rate is zero / negative / unreadable).

The block is **always** rendered when the player has at least one readable
god; otherwise one line `favor (gods) unreadable`. No Config toggle, no
`configVer` bump.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/stats.js` — add a module-local `const favorRateSamples = Object.create(null);`
   `(god -> [{ts, p}, …])` at the top of the file (before `preflightProbe`).
2. `src/stats.js` — add `function favorHudBlock()` returning the lines
   above. It calls `favorCurrent()` (defined in `src/favor.js` at line 9;
   `favor.js` is loaded at MODULES index 26, `stats.js` at index 36, so
   the call is safe). Inline the precondition invariant per cell.
3. `src/stats.js` — inside `renderStats`, between the `topSkips` block
   end and the deadlock guard, insert:
   ```js
   lines.push('');
   lines.push(...favorHudBlock());
   ```
4. `src/stats.js` — inside `preflightProbe`, add a `favor pool read` row
   that calls `favorCurrent()` and reports the number of god keys with
   finite numeric values. This is the one-shot mirror of the HUD; it
   belongs in Preflight by the same pattern as `bandit camp` at
   `stats.js:234-238`. **No** state field, no `STORE.*` key.

## 5. State & storage

None.

The sample window is a JS `Object.create(null)` local to `stats.js`. It is
**not** persisted (`STOR`/`save`/`load` would mean a `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
entry and a `configVer` bump — neither justified). Across reloads the
window restarts; the rate cell renders `…` until two samples accumulate
after each fresh load.

## 6. Config surface

None.

The plan 27 row carries no Config label. The HUD is gated by the render
itself: if the model's `PlayerGods` is unreadable, every cell prints `?`
and the block is a single `unreadable` line. No HIGH-RISK toggle, no
default to set.

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbDomClick`,
no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no `gbCaptchaPause`
key. The HUD reads only.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`favorCurrent()` returns `{}`** — every god cell falls through to `?`;
  the block renders the single-line `favor (gods) unreadable` and logs
  once per god via `gbLogT('favor-hud-blind-' + god, 300000, …)`. The
  precondition invariant is preserved per cell (read each value, log
  once, never block).
- **Regen rate derivation** — if the player spent favor between two
  samples the rate is negative; render as `0.0/m` and `eta —`. If the
  pool increased by less than 1 across 10 min, treat as `0.0/m`. If the
  window has fewer than 2 samples, render `…` for the rate.
- **God list source** — the model exposes a fixed set of gods per world;
  the HUD derives the list from the first `favorCurrent()` call (keys
  matching `/^favor(_|$)/` and `/^max_favor/`), instead of hard-coding
  `['athena','hera','poseidon','hades','zeus','ares','aphrodite',
  'artemis']`. A future god the client adds appears automatically.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), install, open the Stats tab. The new
  `favor (gods)` block appears between `topSkips` and the deadlock line.
- Preflight (`Comprobar sistema`) shows a new `favor pool read` row with
  `N gods readable` and no `?`s once `PlayerGods` is populated.
- Open the game's favor panel, click a god — the Stats HUD mirrors the
  pool within one render cycle (the next `renderStats` is fired by the
  15s `renderStats` interval at `src/boot.js:108-115`).
- Manually spend favor in the game; the next Stats render shows the pool
  drop and the rate column stays accurate (or reports `0.0/m` if the
  elapsed since the last sample is small).
- Switch tabs and switch back; the rate `…` shows briefly on the first
  render after a reload and resolves to a number on the next.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Auto-favor.** Plan 27 §4.4 (`favor` toggle, HIGH-RISK OFF) and 4.6 are
  related but separate. The scanner stays disabled because
  `FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED = false` at `src/favor.js:8` — flipping that is
  a different plan that needs a target contract the catalog explicitly
  defers.
- **Regen rate from the model.** If the game client exposes a regen-rate
  field on `PlayerGods`, that is a future improvement to this HUD — but
  the sniff task is *not* this plan's work. The derived rate is good
  enough; the model field is a "nice to have" tracked in `TASKS.md`.
- **Per-town favor readout.** Favor is a player-level pool, not per
  town. The HUD reads the player's pool once.
- **Wonders / `WonderFavor`.** `state.wonderFavorTpl` and
  `state.autoWonderFavor` (`src/core.js:375-376`) are a separate feature
  (plan 27 §3.1-adjacent). Not this plan.

## 5.1-resource-balancing-ai.md

# 5.1 — Resource balancing AI (greedy LP solver)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** L
**Module:** extends `src/transport.js` (adds the planner recipe + scoring; no new file). The signature contract from plan 1.3 (`transportBalanceJobs`, `transportTownETA`, `transportProjectHeadroom`) is the **dependency surface** — 5.1 imports it without modification.
**Depends on:** **1.3 (transport automation) — the `transportBalanceJobs` planner from `src/transport.js` is the inner loop.** Also reads the profile `resource: {wood, stone, iron}` bias added by sibling plan 1.2 (`gbCityProfile(townId).resource`).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Three sub-planners in `src/trade.js` already produce balanced moves;
each is rule-based, not optimisation-based:

- `tradeFillStorageJobs` (`src/trade.js:130-172`) — the global
  fill-storage rule: any town ≤ 25 % empty gets wood+stone+iron from
  any town ≥ 85 % full, capped by `state.tradeReservePct`
  (`core.js:296`, default 20) and `state.tradeMinBatch` (`core.js:297`,
  default 1000). Skips when `tgt` has no room (audit I9 ledger
  discipline).
- `tradeIslandShipJobs` (`src/trade.js:173-208`) — special-case
  fill for `t.small` towns (small-island). Limit 4 jobs / scan.
- `tradeGoalJobs` (`src/trade.js:262-330`) — deficit-driven planner
  for `party` / `unit` preset. Picks donors by per-resource surplus,
  applies deficit + cap clamp + free-space cap. Limit 6 jobs / scan.

**Plan 3.1's `tradeRouteJobs`** (sibling plan, extends `trade.js`)
adds a fourth: user-defined named routes that run before
`tradeFillStorageJobs` and claim headroom first.

**Plan 1.3's `transportBalanceJobs`** (sibling, NEW `transport.js`)
adds a fifth: profile-biased fleet-wide balance, also runs before
the global sub-planners via the same `tradeApplyJob` ledger.

**What is missing** vs. the plan 27 §5 row 5.1 description
("Resource balancing AI, greedy LP solver"):

- **No objective function.** Each existing sub-planner is a single
  heuristic ("send to emptier", "drain pinned resource"). None of
  them considers the fleet-wide balance after this batch lands —
  the system has no notion of an optimal target state.
- **No profile-aware prioritisation.** Plan 1.2 ships
  `gbCityProfile(townId).resource.{wood,stone,iron}` in
  -1..+1. None of the existing sub-planners reads it; the closest is
  `tradeGoalJobs` reading `(state.recruitTargets || {})[townId]`
  for the `unit` preset (`trade.js:242-243`).
- **No cross-resource substitution.** Grepolis has no exchange rate
  between wood and stone (cave only stores iron; build orders need
  each resource independently). A real LP would treat
  `wood + stone + iron` as three independent supply chains. The
  "LP" in plan 27's row name is therefore a **loose** LP — see §3
  for the honest model.

**Precondition readers used today:**
- `tradeTownRes(townId)` (`src/trade.js:1-22`) — per-town
  `{wood, stone, iron, cap, tradeCap, small}`.
- `townResState(townId)` (`src/bridge.js:235-273`) — `{cap, wood,
  stone, iron, full, n, fillPct}` with 3s memo; blind on unreadable.
- `ironReservedForCave(townId)` (`src/core.js:685-722`) — gates iron
  sources when `state.autoCave` is on.
- `plannerAvailable(townId, {allowSoft:false})` — read by
  `tradeValidateJob` (`src/trade.js:338`).

**Hard limits in the post pipeline that constrain any solver:**
- One `trade` post = `gameAjaxPost('trade', 'town_info', 'trade',
  {...})` (`src/trade.js:37-46`). No batched API; every move is one
  post.
- `'trade'` lock name, TTL 180000ms (`src/core.js:153`).
- `'trade'` captcha breaker key (`src/qol.js:404-408`).
- Request budget: `state.reqBudgetPerMin` ×
  `REQ_SCOPE_FRACTION.action = 1.0` (`src/core.js:608-612`), default
  40 / 60s. Each scan costs at most ~6 action slots per
  `tradeFillStorageJobs:168` (6 jobs max).
- `tradeScan` runs on `'trade'` cadence 120000ms (`qol.js:393`),
  jittered ±20 %.

**Post-mortem on a real optimization:** plan 26 §B6 already audited
`tradeScan` end-to-end and noted that the existing heuristics double-
count incoming movements correctly (`trade.js:71-83` comment). The
"I9 ledger threading" is closed; 5.1 inherits it.

## 2. Gap

Plan 27 §5 row 5.1 wants an "AI" planner. The honest reading is:

- **No real LP.** Grepolis has no exchange API between resources;
  wood, stone, iron are three independent supply chains. A linear
  program that models wood→stone substitution would have no slack to
  optimise against. A "greedy" pass that scores each (source,
  destination, resource) triple by a hand-picked objective is the
  most the data structure permits.
- **Greedy is sufficient for the actual win.** The user pain is
  *cross-town imbalance that the global fill-storage rule misses*.
  Fill-storage targets any town ≤ 25 % empty; it cannot express
  "town A is building a farm and will need 6000 wood in 8 minutes".
  A planner that reads ETA + profile bias + iron-reserve can do
  better. Greedy on `O(towns² × resources)` ≤ 64 evaluations per
  scan (8 towns × 8 towns × 3 resources) is sub-millisecond and the
  diminishing-returns ceiling for a userscript scheduler.
- **The objective function lives in the planner, not the post.** The
  post is `tradeSend`. The plan is a `transportAiJobs(towns,
  ledger)` function in `transport.js` that follows the same shape
  as `transportBalanceJobs` from sibling plan 1.3.

## 3. Design

**Objective.** Maximise a fleet-wide balance score after this batch
lands, where balance is:

```
score = Σ over towns of
        Σ over resources r in {wood,stone,iron} of
          w_r(profile[t].resource[r]) × distance_to_target_fill_pct(t, r)
```

Where `distance_to_target_fill_pct(t, r) = |fill(t, r) - target_pct(r)|`
and `target_pct(r)` is **per-resource**:
- `wood: 60%` (build + farm are wood-heavy, see CULTURE_COSTS party
  15000 wood, `src/cave.js:284`).
- `stone: 50%` (less demand than wood).
- `iron: 30%` (cave reserves most; see `caveThreshPct = 90`,
  `core.js:288`).

`w_r(profile[t].resource[r])` is the per-town profile bias from
sibling plan 1.2's `gbCityProfile(townId).resource[r]` in -1..+1,
clamped to a [0.25, 2.0] weight so an extreme ±1 does not 8× the
score of one resource.

**Algorithm.** Greedy one-move-at-a-time on
`{from, to, resource}` triples:

1. **Snapshot.** Build a working ledger `L` from `tradeLedger(towns)`
   (sibling 1.3 / `trade.js:71-83` reuses it).
2. **Score every triple.** For each (from, to, resource) where
   `from !== to` and `from.cap > 0` and `to.cap > 0`:
   - source fill >= 0.85,
   - target fill <= 0.25,
   - source `tradeCap >= transportMin`,
   - `ironReservedForCave(from)` is not reserved (or resource != iron),
   - estimate `delta_score` = `score_after - score_before` for the
     triple, sending `min(transportCap, source[res] - keep,
     target.cap - target[res])`.
3. **Pick the top-N.** Sort by `delta_score` desc; pick the top 6
   (matching `tradeFillStorageJobs:168` ceiling).
4. **Apply sequentially.** For each picked job:
   - `tradeApplyJob(L, job)` mutates the ledger.
   - The next pick sees the deduction — no double-counting.
   - Build the `{from, to, wood, stone, iron}` job object exactly
     like `tradeFillStorageJobs:159-164`; **zero the resource** that
     was not part of this triple (the planner sends one resource per
     job, not a multi-resource haul).
5. **Cap.** 6 jobs / scan. The 7th-best triple returns to the
   queue; the next tick re-scores with the actual warehouse state.

**Why greedy over a real LP.** Three honest reasons:

- **No substitution.** A linear program that has no slack to
  optimise is a single-system of equalities with a unique solution
  per demand vector. The "greedy" pass returns that solution when
  the score function is linear and the constraints are tight. There
  is no second-best world to compare against.
- **Sub-millisecond cost.** 8 × 8 × 3 = 192 triples evaluated;
  each evaluation reads `townResState` (3s memo, free after the
  first call) and `gbCfgNum` (constant-time). Wall cost is
  dominated by `tradeApplyJob`, which is a handful of integer
  arithmetic. A real LP — even a 12-variable one — would cost
  comparable time and ship no additional correctness.
- **No new dependency.** A pure-JS LP solver (`javascript-lp-
  solver`, `glpk.js`, …) is not in the repo today; adding it
  conflicts with CLAUDE.md "No linter, no test runner, no Node
  workflow — paste-only mode" because the user would have to
  validate the solver against fixtures the build pipeline does not
  ship. A greedy pass is reviewable in 30 lines.

**Sub-planner shape:**

```js
// src/transport.js (extends — no new file)
function transportAiJobs(towns, ledger) {
  if (!state.autoTransportAi) return []; // toggle, default OFF
  const L = ledger || tradeLedger(towns);
  if (!L) return [];
  // ... greedy loop as in §3 ...
  return jobs;
}
```

**Orchestrator wiring.** No new orchestrator key. 5.1 is a
sub-planner of `tradeScan` (`trade.js:350-407`), called from the
same insertion point as 1.3's `transportBalanceJobs`:

```js
// src/trade.js, after the tradePreset block (line ~360):
if (state.autoTransport) jobs = jobs.concat(transportBalanceJobs(towns, ledger));
if (state.autoTransportAi) jobs = jobs.concat(transportAiJobs(towns, ledger));
```

The order is **transportAiJobs AFTER transportBalanceJobs**, because
the AI planner is greedy-once and should not be clobbered by the
heuristic's claim first. Both run BEFORE `tradeFillStorageJobs`.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Post path is unchanged.** Same as 1.3 — every AI job runs through
  `tradeSend` (`src/trade.js:37-46`) which posts
  `gameAjaxPost('trade', 'town_info', 'trade', {id, wood, stone,
  iron, town_id, nl_init:true})`.
- **No `gbAjaxWatch` registration.** Same as 1.3 — trade is server-
  rendered.
- **No new `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry.** Same as 1.3.
- **Captcha breaker.** `'trade'` (existing), shared with global
  `tradeScan` and 1.3's `transportBalanceJobs`. Captcha on the trade
  queue pauses AI + transport + global sub-planners + 3.1 routes for
  the ladder window.
- **Lock name.** `'trade'` (existing), TTL 180000ms
  (`src/core.js:153`). Acquired once per `tradeScan` at `trade.js:381`.
- **Dry-run.** `txActionGate` (`tx.js:522-534`) returns `'dryrun'`
  when `state.dryRun` is set. Verified: every AI send inherits the
  dry-run gate (same call chain as 1.3).
- **No new scheduler.** No `gbInterval`. Cadence is `'trade'`
  120000ms (`qol.js:393`), jittered ±20 %.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`townResState` blind for any owned town.** Skip that town in the
  scoring loop; logged once via
  `gbLogT('ai-blind-' + townId, …)`. Per scan, per town.
- **`gbCityProfile` returns the seed `custom` profile.** All
  `resource[r] = 0` → neutral weights → AI behaves like
  `transportBalanceJobs` but with the per-resource target (60/50/30)
  applied. Verified: 1.2's `goalTownCfg` defensively seeds
  (`goals.js:5-12`).
- **All three `AI_TARGET_*` are equal.** Degenerate score function —
  every resource weighted equally → equivalent to global fill-storage.
  Preflight warns (`stats.js:171` work item 10).
- **`ironReservedForCave(from) === reserved:true`** on the chosen
  source and the triple's resource is iron. Skip; the AI loop
  re-scores with the next candidate. Same path as
  `tradeGoalJobs:301`.
- **Two AI picks target the same destination with the same
  resource.** `tradeApplyJob` mutates `L` after each pick, so the
  second pick sees the first's deduction and clamps itself. The
  6-job ceiling (`tradeFillStorageJobs:168` analogue) keeps the
  scan bounded.
- **Profile `resource` outside [-1, +1] range.** Clamped on read;
  `gbCfgNum` is for numbers, so this is a `Math.max(-1,
  Math.min(1, +v || 0))` guard in `aiScoreTriple`. No log spam.
- **Scan exceeds `'trade'` lock TTL (180000ms).** Same as today —
  the orchestrator's adaptive cadence widens the gap
  (`orchestrate.js:107-114`). A scan that posts more than the lock
  TTL allows gets truncated by `gbLock`; the AI loop is bounded to
  6 picks (≤ 6 posts), well under 180s at 800ms+600ms jitter per
  post (`trade.js:404`).
- **Captcha during an AI send.** `tradeScan` releases the trade
  lock on `'captcha'` callback (`trade.js:399`). AI inherits.
- **Decision-memory trip.** `trade` is a write feature in
  `TX_WRITE_FEATURES` (`planner.js:212-216`); three hard errors
  open a 5/15/60min skip window (`journal.js` plan 01, §11 of
  plan 27). The AI loop is the slowest of the sub-planners to
  recover after a bad window — that's the right behaviour
  (irreversible action, server is the authority).

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 (Med risk): **dry-run + one hand-triggered firing +
one full orchestrator tick.**

1. **Dry-run smoke.** Toggle `state.dryRun` on; toggle
   `state.autoTransportAi` on; set `state.aiTargetWood = 80`,
   `state.aiTargetStone = 80`, `state.aiTargetIron = 80` (force
   any wood/stone/iron imbalance to be acted on). Wait one trade
   tick. Expect at most 6 `DRY-RUN trade: …` lines; verify the
   per-resource target %s are reflected in the picked (from, to,
   resource) triples by counting the resource breakdown.
2. **Single-tick live.** Disable dry-run, force one scan. Expect
   ≤ 6 `trade: A→B w…/s…/i…` lines where the resource fields are
   mutually exclusive (only one of `wood`/`stone`/`iron` is
   non-zero per job — the AI ships one resource at a time).
3. **Profile bias verification.** Set town A profile
   `resource.iron = +1`; town B fill iron 90 %; town C fill iron
   10 %. The picked triple should be `(B → C, iron)` regardless of
   A. Then set town C profile `resource.iron = -1`; expect the
   triple to flip toward a different destination or be skipped
   entirely.
4. **Objective monotonicity.** Force a state where two triples
   have similar `delta_score` but one is strictly better. Log both
   `delta_score` values; confirm the better one is picked (ties
   broken by lexicographic `from+to+resource`, deterministic).
5. **Iron-reserve-for-cave interaction.** On a town with
   `state.autoCave` on and `caveThreshPct = 90`, set that town's
   profile `resource.iron = +1` (it needs iron) and another
   town's profile `resource.iron = -1` (dump it). AI should
   prefer the `-1` town as the source. Verify via
   `gbLogT('ai-iron-reserved-' + from, …)`.
6. **Six-job ceiling.** Disable `autoTrade`, `islandShip`,
   `autoTransport`. Set `autoTransportAi` on. Set up 12 valid
   (from, to, resource) triples via direct state mutation in
   the panel. Expect exactly 6 picked; the next scan picks the
   next 6.
7. **Preflight row.** Stats → Preflight shows `transport AI: ok`
   when `autoTransportAi === false`. Toggling on with ≥ 2 towns
   flips to `ok`; setting all three targets equal flips to
   `warn`; setting `autoTransportAi === true` with 1 town flips
   to `fail`.
8. **Export round-trip.** Export config; the four new fields
   (`autoTransportAi`, `aiTargetWood`, `aiTargetStone`,
   `aiTargetIron`) ship in the dump. Re-import restores them.
9. **No new scheduler.** `rg -n 'gbInterval' src/transport.js`
   returns zero hits; `rg -n 'InFlight' src/transport.js` returns
   zero hits; no new top-level `function` (IIFE only).

## 10. Out of scope

- **A real LP solver.** Plan 27 §5 row 5.1 names "greedy LP solver"
  in one phrase; this plan ships the greedy half honestly. The LP
  half is not feasible without a substitution rate between
  resources (which the game does not provide). If a future client
  releases a "convert" endpoint, 5.1 v2 swaps the inner loop for a
  single-system solver; the public surface
  (`transportAiJobs(towns, ledger)`) stays the same.
- **Cross-account balancing.** Out — GrepBot only reads towns owned
  by the logged-in player (`state.towns`).
- **Adaptive cadence per planner.** `orchAdaptive`
  (`orchestrate.js:107-114`) keys on the whole `'trade'` feature
  via `ORCH_JRN['trade']` (`qol.js:412`). Per-sub-planner adaptive
  cadence is a future optimisation; not in 5.1.
- **Auto-discovery of optimal target percentages.** A future plan
  could observe 7-day warehouse-fill curves and recommend
  `aiTarget*` values. Not in v4.2.
- **Per-resource send batching.** Grepolis' trade endpoint posts
  one job per resource triple; the AI ships one resource at a time
  for the same reason `tradeFillStorageJobs` ships wood+stone+iron
  in one go — but the AI's score function per resource makes
  one-resource jobs cleaner. A multi-resource AI batch is a future
  optimisation.
- **Sniffing `transportTpl`.** Plan 27 §1.3 hint; does not exist
  in the tree (see plan 1.3 §7 explicit unknown). The AI planner
  uses the existing `tradeSend` payload verbatim.

## 5.2-adaptive-farming.md

# 5.2 — Adaptive farming (target rotation by profit)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/farms.js` (consumes `state.farmProfit` from 2.6)
**Depends on:** **2.6** (consumes `state.farmProfit[vill_id].score`)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/farms.js`, `src/orchestrate.js`, `src/qol.js`, `src/bridge.js`.

- **Claim loop already runs through `autoClaimFarms(reason, durOverride, onBatchDone)`**
  (`farms.js:487-568`). It computes `ready = farms.filter(...)`
  (`farms.js:501-512`), acquires `gbLock('claim', …)`
  (`farms.js:525`), and walks `ready[i++]` with `claimSpacingMs`
  (`farms.js:532,561`). The order today is **insertion order from
  `farmsFromGame()`** (`farms.js:247`), which is whatever order the game
  returned the relation models in. There is no rotation, no captcha-aware
  throttling of the per-village set, and no rank input.
- **Cadence is already on the orchestrator.** `ORCH_CADENCE.farm = 60000`
  (`src/qol.js:394`); `ORCH_HANDLERS.farm` is dispatched by `orchTick`
  (`src/orchestrate.js:147-200`). Adaptive backoff (×1 → ×8 after 4 idle
  journal entries) lives in `orchIdleFactor` (`orchestrate.js:107-114`)
  and `orchNoteResult` (`orchestrate.js:120-134`). The orchestrator already
  widens the cadence when captcha is active (because every claim rejects
  fast and the journal stays empty); 5.2 makes the *which villages*
  decision adaptive, not the *when*.
- **Captcha breaker already covers `farm`.** `gbCaptchaPause` key `farm`
  is set by `autoClaimFarms` (`farms.js:450,488`) and checked at
  `farms.js:535`. `ORCH_CAPTCHA.farm = 'farm'` (`qol.js:406`). 5.2 must
  not add a second captcha key.
- **Budget pressure bus exists.** `reqBudgetOk()` gates every bridge
  write (`src/tx.js:532,646-647`); `gbServerCooldown` opens a global
  cooldown (`core.js` 429/503/Retry-After path, `bridge.js:222-231`).
  A captcha or server-pressure window means writes are already throttled
  globally; 5.2 should *prefer* that signal over inventing its own gate.
- **Decision-memory already exists.** `state.decisions`
  (`src/journal.js`), keyed `feature|action|target`, gives 3 hard
  errors in a row → 5/15/60min skip window (`decisionSkips`). Success
  clears. 5.2 does not add a new error-skip mechanism.
- **`state.farmProfit` is computed in 2.6.** `farmProfitScore(farm)`
  returns `{score, duration, distance, loyalty, headroom}`. Null
  score ⇒ rank-unknown; never an invented number.
- **Plan 27 §9 lists 15 already-shipped ideas.** None covers adaptive
  farming. 5.2 is genuinely new.
- **Risk vs HIGH:** plan 27 marks this Med. The only write is the
  existing `FarmTownPlayerRelation/claim` post (`farms.js:477-485`) — no
  new template, no new endpoint. The Med rating is for the **decision
  policy** (skipping low-profit farms under pressure), not for the
  post itself. Default OFF still holds (CLAUDE.md).

## 2. Gap

Today, when `captchaPaused('farm')` is false and the budget is open, the
claim loop will walk **every** ready village in `farmsFromGame()` order,
including villages whose profitability rank (2.6) is low. Under a tight
budget or a captcha that just tripped and is about to expire, the right
move is to skip the marginal villages for one cycle and spend the slot
on the profitable ones — fewer posts, more loot per request, less
captcha surface. Plan 26 §A1 already showed that every claim slot
counts.

## 3. Design

Re-order `ready` in `autoClaimFarms` by `state.farmProfit[vill_id].score`
descending, and apply three drop policies before the loop:

1. **Drop unknown-rank villages from the claim set when pressure is on.**
   `score == null` (read blind: missing headroom, missing x/y, missing
   loyalty) ⇒ keep if no pressure, skip if pressure. "Pressure" = one
   of: `captchaPaused('farm')` was true within the last 5min (sliding
   via `gbServerCooldown`-shaped log), OR `gbServerPaused({reason:'server'})`,
   OR `reqBudgetSoftDelayMs > 0` (per `core.js:721-728`). Tracked via a
   small `farmPressure` ring (`{at, kind}[]`, 8 entries, 30min TTL).
2. **Drop the bottom quartile when pressure is on.** Sort `ready` by
   score desc, drop the bottom 25% only when pressure is on AND
   `ready.length >= 4`. Configurable via `state.farmDropPressurePct`
   (default 25). Off-pressure ⇒ claim everything (no change from today).
3. **Cap daily claim count per village when captcha is hot.** If
   `captchaPaused('farm')` was tripped in the last hour, drop every
   village whose `state.farmClaimsToday[vill_id]` already ≥ 1 from the
   claim set. Counter lives in `state.farmClaimsToday`, dated key
   (`farmDayKey()` mirrors `farmSleepDayKey` at `farms.js:570-573`),
   reset on day rollover.

All three are **drop policies on the existing claim loop**. They do not
add a post, change a template, or open a new captcha feature key. The
`claim` lock (`farms.js:525`) and the spacing (`farms.js:532`) already
serialize everything correctly.

The pressure-skip logic also **does not run** when `state.adaptiveFarm`
is OFF — the toggle ships OFF, mirroring CLAUDE.md ("HIGH-RISK toggles
default OFF"; this is Med but the precedent holds for any new
target-rotation policy).
