- New: `state.adaptiveFarm` (bool, default **false**).
- New: `state.farmDropPressurePct` (number, default 25).
- New: `state.farmClaimsToday` (object keyed by `vill_id`, count).
- New: `state.farmClaimsDay` (string `YYYY-M-D`, last reset).
- New: `farmPressure` (module-local ring, in-memory only, not persisted
  — pressure signals are short-lived and reload-resetting is correct).
- New `STORE` entries, all in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`:
  - `STORE.ADAPTIVE_FARM: 'grepbot:adaptive-farm'`
  - `STORE.FARM_DROP_PCT: 'grepbot:farm-drop-pct'`
  - `STORE.FARM_CLAIMS_TODAY: 'grepbot:farm-claims-today'`
  - `STORE.FARM_CLAIMS_DAY: 'grepbot:farm-claims-day'`
- `configVer` bump in `qol.js qolExportConfig` for the new fields.
- Prune: `state.farmClaimsToday` self-prunes on day rollover
  (`farmDayKey()`); no need for the 7d ring.

## 6. Config surface

- Toggle `Rotación adaptativa por rentabilidad` (default **OFF**, Med
  risk per plan 27 §5; even though not HIGH, the precedent in CLAUDE.md
  holds — any new autonomous target policy ships OFF).
- Numeric `Descartar cuartil bajo bajo presión %` (default 25, range
  0-75). Hidden when toggle is OFF.

No HIGH-RISK toggles added (no new post surface).

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Reuses existing `claimTpl` post** (`farms.js:477-485`). No new
  template, no new endpoint, no new `gbAjaxWatch`, no new
  `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry, no new `tplNameFor` resolver change.
- **Reuses `gbCaptchaPause` key `farm`** (already registered for
  `autoClaimFarms` at `farms.js:450,488`). No new feature key.
- **Reuses `gbLock('claim')`** at `farms.js:525` — no new lock, no
  new `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry.
- **Cadence reuses `ORCH_HANDLERS.farm`** (`orchestrate.js:421`). No new
  scheduler (CLAUDE.md "no new schedulers"), no `gbInterval` (CLAUDE.md
  v1.1.0).
- **Dry-run gate.** `bridgePost('farm', …)` already short-circuits
  when `state.dryRun` (`bridge.js` `bridgePost` wrapper). The drop
  policies can run under dry-run to preview which villages would be
  skipped: log `farm adaptive: drop <n> villages under pressure (kept
  <k>): <ids>` once per `autoClaimFarms` call when
  `state.adaptiveFarm && state.dryRun`. Live dry-run the policy
  without firing.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`state.farmProfit` empty (2.6 not yet shipped, or all scores
  null).** `farmApplyDropPolicies` falls through to "no-op": keep
  original `ready` order. Log once: `farm adaptive: no profit scores
  yet - rotation disabled`. Precondition invariant: do not invent a
  rank.
- **Pressure ring stale on reload.** `farmPressure` is in-memory only;
  on reload it starts empty, so the first tick runs without pressure
  even if the captcha breaker is still hot. The `gbServerPaused` /
  `captchaPaused` gates still apply; 5.2 only adds a sorting /
  filtering preference, not a hard block.
- **All villages dropped.** If the drop policy empties `work`, the
  existing early-return path at `farms.js:516-524` runs (log + schedule
  wake). No post, no orphan lock.
- **Bottom-quartile drops a single low-rank village by accident.** The
  policy only fires when `ready.length >= 4`. Below that threshold,
  `farmApplyDropPolicies` returns the input unchanged.
- **`state.farmClaimsDay` drift.** Compare at the top of
  `autoClaimFarms`; on rollover, reset both `state.farmClaimsToday` and
  `state.farmClaimsDay` and `save()` both. A clock-skew on day
  boundaries is bounded to one cycle.
- **`farmSleepClaimNow` overlap.** `farmSleepClaimNow` (`farms.js:574-591`)
  shares `autoClaimFarms` with a `durOverride` (`farms.js:589`); the
  sleep path uses `farmSleepDuration` (`farms.js:410-414`), not
  `farmDurationPick`. The drop policy in §3 fires on every entry; if
  `state.adaptiveFarm && state.farmSleepAuto`, the sleep path can lose
  villages. Mitigate by skipping the drop policy when `durOverride` is
  one of `14400`/`28800` (sleep durations) — the sleep claim is a
  full-clear, not a normal cycle.
- **Orphan claim counter.** `state.farmClaimsToday` is keyed by village
  id; `refreshFarmsParsed` (`farms.js:255-268`) prunes unknown villages
  out. Persisted under `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` so a world switch resets it.

## 9. Validation gate

Med-risk (plan 27 §11: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one full
orchestrator tick).

- **Dry-run.** `state.dryRun = true; state.adaptiveFarm = true`.
  Trigger `autoClaimFarms('orch')` (the `ORCH_HANDLERS.farm` key). Log
  shows the drop policy ran; no `FarmTownPlayerRelation/claim` posts
  fired; `state.farmClaimsToday` stays empty.
- **Manual press with pressure off.** Disable adaptive; flip the
  "captcha recently tripped" sentinel (set `captchaLadder`-shaped
  timestamp) and verify the loop claims **all** ready villages in
  insertion order. Then enable adaptive + same sentinel ⇒ log shows the
  bottom quartile dropped, IDs listed.
- **Full tick.** `orchTick` runs; Stats tab `farm adaptive` row reads
  `pass`; journal entries `farm <vill_id>` are the same villages that
  would have been claimed pre-feature, minus the dropped bottom-quartile
  IDs (compare `farm <id>: ok` counts in Decisions view pre/post).
- **Quota discipline.** With `reqBudgetPerMin = 40` and 12 villages, a
  sweep under pressure-on must show fewer claim posts (per journal)
  than pressure-off, and zero `skip:budget` (the global pool already
  covers it).
- **Validation summary:** single claim-cycle delta ≤ 1 village under
  no-pressure; ≤ 25% villages dropped under pressure; sleep-claim
  path unchanged when `durOverride` is 4h/8h.

## 10. Out of scope

- Recomputing the `farmDurationPick` per village (already in
  `farms.js:426-445`; the rank from 2.6 is independent of the
  duration choice).
- Per-village post rate-limit (skip for X minutes after a captcha).
  The global breaker (`gbCaptchaPause.farm`) already covers this and
  flipping it per-village invites a hidden state machine; let the
  global gate stay.
- Cross-world village ranking. `state.farmProfit` is world-scoped via
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` and is regenerated on world switch.
- Replacing `claimFarm` outright with a graph solver. The drop policy
  is a list filter, not a rewrite of the claim path; plan 6.5's
  Quick-action toolbar is the surface for one-click full-cycle.
- Auto-teaching the loyalty research. That is plan §9 (already coded
  per `farmLoyaltyAutoTeachTick` `farms.js:935-974`).
- Captcha-aware option selection. The `option` index is world/client
  specific (CLAUDE.md "never guess a claim-option index"); 5.2 only
  rotates *which villages*, not *which option* on each.

## 5.3-threat-assessment-engine.md

# 5.3 — Threat assessment engine

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/wonder.js` (where `defenseAssessment` already lives);
expose to `src/intel.js` for display, to `src/military.js` for 5.4 consumption.
**Depends on:** none. **Consumed by:** plan 5.4 Smart dodge (planned separately,
see §10).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` is already implemented at
  **`src/wonder.js:144`** — *not* `src/intel.js` as plan 27 §5.3 hints. Plan 26
  §B2 expected exactly this kind of mismatch: the catalogued module hint says
  `intel.js` but the actual code lives where its caller
  (`defenseShouldDodge`, also `wonder.js:145`) was first needed. The live
  return shape is:

  ```
  { eta: number|null,           // seconds until landing, or null on unreadable arrival
    simultaneous: number,        // other hostile movements destined for the same town
    local: { score, count },     // defenseLocalStrength(townId) result; from wonder.js:142
    supports: [{from, travel, units}], // defenseSupportOptions(townId, eta); wonder.js:143
    safeTown: townId|null,       // dodgeSafeTown(townId, incoming); dodge.js:86
    evac: {ok, why, boats?},     // dodgeSupportValidate(...); dodge.js:157
    militia: {ok, why},          // dodgeCanRaiseMilitia(townId); dodge.js:107
    risk: number,                // 0..N additive score with embedded magic numbers
    hasCs: boolean,              // !!mov.hasCs; dodge.js:73 detector
  }
  ```

  Read by `dodgeTrySend()` (`src/dodge.js:207`), surfaced in the Intel tab at
  `src/intel.js:88-89` (the `riesgo` / `apoyo` / `esquivar` columns), and
  bound to the test hook `GB_ROOT.__grepbotTest.defenseAssessment`
  (`src/boot.js:178`).
- Caller `defenseShouldDodge(mov, incoming)` (`src/wonder.js:145`) already
  implements three modes — `notify` / `safe` / `smart` — keyed by
  `state.defenseCfg.mode` (default `'notify'`, `src/core.js:359`,
  `src/wonder.js:141`). The "smart" branch honors a separate
  `state.defenseCfg.smartAuto` flag (`src/core.js:359`, `src/ui.js:1352`) and
  decides on `a.hasCs || a.risk >= 35`. That single `risk >= 35` magic
  constant is the only place where 5.3's output is currently acted on.
- Weights are **hardcoded** in the additive score at `src/wonder.js:144`:
  `+60` if CS, `+25` if ETA < 15min, `+8…+25` per extra simultaneous hit,
  `+10` if local.score < 200, `-5…-20` for incoming supports. Changing them
  today means editing `wonder.js:144` and re-running
  `python3 build.py`.
- Hostile-movement detector (`src/dodge.js:39-52`,
  `DODGE_HOSTILE_TYPES = /^(attack|attack_sea|raid|siege|revolt|colonize|take_over|conquer|portal_attack)$/`)
  is the canonical input — never `incoming`/`started_at` alone, per CLAUDE.md
  "Dodge / militia / CS" rule.

## 2. Gap

The score has three problems 5.3 must solve cleanly:

1. The additive formula is a magic-number soup glued to one threshold; users
   cannot tune it, and 5.4 Smart dodge will need to consume a richer
   decomposition (per-factor contribution, not a single rolled-up number).
2. The output has no display-stable provenance: a future change to the
   formula quietly changes the `risk` value with no audit row, and 5.4 (smart
   dodge) would inherit those silent changes.
3. The Intel tab (`src/intel.js:75-114`) renders only three of the nine
   fields (`riesgo`, `apoyo`, `esquivar`); the rest (`simultaneous`, ETA,
   militia, supports travel times) are computed but discarded.

## 3. Design

Refactor `defenseAssessment` into a documented scoring primitive whose output
shape is **stable** and consumable by both the Intel tab and a future 5.4
consumer. Schema change is **additive only** — the existing nine fields keep
their names and meanings; new fields and a `factors` block are added.

Stable score schema (the contract 5.4 reads):

```
{
  // unchanged
  eta: number|null, simultaneous: number, local: {score, count},
  supports: [{from, travel, units}], safeTown, evac, militia, hasCs,
  // new (5.3)
  band: 'low'|'med'|'high'|'cs',   // discrete bucket for UI + 5.4
  factors: {                       // per-signal contribution; sum <= risk
    cs: number,                    // +60 if hasCs
    eta: number,                   // +25 if eta<15min
    simultaneous: number,          // +8 per extra simultaneous, capped +25
    weak: number,                  // +10 if local.score<200
    support: number,               // -5 per support, capped -20
  },
  risk: number,                    // semantically = clamped sum(factors); recomputed
  computedAt: number,              // Date.now() at the call site
  weights: {...},                  // the weight set used (see §5)
}
```

The function signature is unchanged (`(mov, incoming) -> ...`); the only
call-site adjustment is to pass `weights` via a new optional third arg
(defaults to `state.predictCfg.threatWeights`, see §5). Boot-time callers
(`src/boot.js:178`) keep working unchanged. The Intel tab gets `band` and the
factor breakdown for free; smart-dodge 5.4 gets a stable shape with
decomposed reasoning and provenance.

Display update in the Intel tab:

```
=== Entrantes ===
[CS] attack → 12345 from 67890 @1742345678 | riesgo high (60=cs,25=eta,0=sim,0=support)
  | ETA 12m30s | apoyo 2 (4-9min) | esquivar no (cannot-evacuate)
```

The `riesgo` label prints the band; the parenthetical exposes factor breakdown
in `cs=N,eta=N,sim=N,support=N` form (sign and rounding preserved). Adds at
most ~30 chars/row.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/wonder.js`** — extend `defenseAssessment` to (a) accept an optional
   `weights` arg, (b) build `factors` as it sums, (c) clamp `risk` to a
   `[0, 100]` band, (d) compute `band` from `risk` with cut points
   `cs → 'cs'`, `>=45 → 'high'`, `>=20 → 'med'`, else `'low'` (kept inside
   this file, not in `state`, so changing the band cut-points is one
   literal-line edit per plan 26 §B2). Document the new shape in a
   top-of-section comment block. **No new top-level `function`** introduced —
   the existing one grows the extra arg and returns the extra fields. Per
   build.py MODULES guard (`build.py:31-72`) this stays inside the
   `wonder.js` IIFE.
2. **`src/wonder.js`** — replace the inline magic numbers with named
   constants at module top:
   `THREAT_CS_BASE = 60`, `THREAT_ETA15_BASE = 25`,
   `THREAT_SIM_PER = 8`, `THREAT_SIM_CAP = 25`, `THREAT_WEAK_BASE = 10`,
   `THREAT_WEAK_FLOOR = 200`, `THREAT_SUPPORT_PER = 5`,
   `THREAT_SUPPORT_CAP = 20`. These remain constant; the weights in
   `state.predictCfg.threatWeights` only scale them (see §5).
3. **`src/wonder.js`** — `defenseShouldDodge` (`src/wonder.js:145`) now reads
   `assessment.band` and the factors to log a richer reason. Concretely,
   `if (a.hasCs || a.risk >= weights.smartThreshold)` reads
   `weights.smartThreshold` from `state.predictCfg.threatWeights` (default 35,
   unchanged behaviour for users who never edit the config).
4. **`src/intel.js`** — `renderIntel` (`src/intel.js:75-114`) updates the
   `=== Entrantes ===` loop to surface `band` + the `factors` summary.
   `intelDossiers` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) does **not** change.
5. **`src/ui.js`** — add four numeric Config fields (read via the existing
   `saveNum` pattern at `src/ui.js:1393-1401`):
   `threatWeightCs` (60), `threatWeightEta15` (25), `threatWeightSim` (8),
   `threatSupportReducer` (-5). Save through
   `save(STORE.PREDICT_CFG, state.predictCfg)`. Range-validate each:
   weights are non-negative integers, reducer is negative or zero.
6. **`src/boot.js`** — extend the test hook block (`src/boot.js:178-179`) to
   expose the new factor names if any test harness reuses them. No-op in
   production; this just preserves the pre-existing test surface.

## 5. State & storage

- **One new field** under the existing `state.predictCfg` (already at
  `src/core.js:358`, key `STORE.PREDICT_CFG` already in
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `src/header.js:209`):

  ```
  state.predictCfg.threatWeights = {
    cs: 60, eta15: 25, simPer: 8, simCap: 25,
    weak: 10, supportPer: 5, supportCap: 20,
    smartThreshold: 35,
  }
  ```

  Initialise on first load (no `migrateConfig` bump required — the keys
  default through `||` when missing, per `src/core.js:358` precedent).
- **No new top-level STORE key.** `PREDICT_CFG` already exists
  (`src/header.js:154`).
- **No new `*InFlight` boolean, no new scheduler.** `GB_LOCK_TTL` table
  (`src/core.js:145-173`) is unchanged — the engine is read-only and runs
  inline from `dodgeScan('loop')` (`src/boot.js:100`,
  `src/dodge.js:252`).
- **Id-bearing?** No. The shape is per-town risk, in memory only; towns are
  referenced by `mov.dest` (already in the existing flow). The CONFIG is
  world-scoped via `PREDICT_CFG` which is already there. Plan 27 §13 "world-
  scope id-bearing storage" — N/A here.
- **Prune TTL** — N/A. Derived per call.

## 6. Config surface

Four numeric fields plus a derived `smartThreshold`. The layout uses the
existing pattern at `src/ui.js:1398-1401`:

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `threatWeightCs` | number | 60 | 0..120 | `state.predictCfg.threatWeights.cs` |
| `threatWeightEta15` | number | 25 | 0..60 | `…threatWeights.eta15` |
| `threatWeightSim` | number | 8 | 0..30 | `…threatWeights.simPer` |
| `threatSupportReducer` | number | -5 | -30..0 | `…threatWeights.supportPer` |
| `smartThreshold` | number | 35 | 0..100 | `…threatWeights.smartThreshold` |

- **HIGH-RISK?** No — these tune a numeric model. Smart dodge (5.4) is HIGH-
  RISK and gated behind `state.defenseCfg.smartAuto`; that gate stays in
  place — 5.3 does not turn on auto-dodge for anyone.
- **Defaults restore** the existing magic numbers exactly so no user-visible
  behaviour changes for anyone who does not touch the config.

## 7. Post surface & safety

None. `defenseAssessment` is read-only over the in-memory game model. No
`bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbCaptchaPause`
entry. Plan 27 §7's "no post surface" applies in full — section gets one
honest line by the README §7 rule.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`dodgeIncomingMovements()` (`src/dodge.js:53`) returns `[]`** —
  `defenseAssessment` (`src/wonder.js:144`) is never called for a movement
  that wasn't already in that collection. The new factor sums all default to
  0, `band` is `'low'`, callers (`src/dodge.js:207`) short-circuit on
  `entry.state` first.
- **`dodgeEtaSec` returns `null`** (`src/dodge.js:175`) — `simultaneous` and
  `local` are still meaningful, `eta` factor stays at 0, and the `eta15`
  weight branch is skipped (per the existing `eta != null && eta < 15 * 60`
  guard at `src/wonder.js:144`). No new failure path.
- **`dodgeSafeTown` returns `null`** (everyone threatened, `src/dodge.js:99-102`)
  — `safeTown` is `null`, `evac.ok` is `false`, the consumer
  (`defenseShouldDodge`) already returns `'cannot-evacuate'` so smart-dodge
  never auto-fires. 5.3 inherits the path unchanged.
- **`unitMeta` returns `null`** — `defenseLocalStrength` (`src/wonder.js:142`)
  is unaffected (it filters `m.is_naval`); the score's `weak` branch reads the
  sum, not the metadata directly.
- **Weights misconfigured** (e.g. `cs: -60`) — `risk` can go negative. Clamp
  `risk` to `[0, 100]` after the additive pass (band still resolves
  correctly: negative → `'low'`). Document the clamp in the schema comment
  block; do not silently drop bands.

## 9. Validation gate

Plan 27 §11 risk class Low: preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

- Preflight row `intel: threat engine weights`: pass when
  `state.predictCfg.threatWeights` reads; warn on shape mismatch (out-of-
  range value from a hand-edited localStorage).
- Manual: with `state.defenseCfg.mode='notify'` and one incoming hostile in
  the Intel tab, the row should print `| riesgo low (cs=0,eta=0,sim=0,
  support=0)`. Bump `threatWeightCs` to 120 in Config, watch the next
  render: same row reads `| riesgo high (cs=120,...)`. Set back to 60.
- Failure pattern: log shows `threat engine: band=high risk=120 band=` — fix
  the clamp at the engine, not the UI.
- **Cross-feature test**: Config → smartAuto on (still `mode='smart'`),
  trigger a synthetic hostile (`dodgeIncomingMovements` returns an entry with
  `hasCs:true`), 5.4 lands later and will consume `assessment.band`; for

  when defaults are restored.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Smart dodge** (plan 27 §5.4 = `5.4-smart-dodge.md`, planned separately).
  5.3's schema is the contract 5.4 reads. 5.3 does **not** call dodge itself;

## 5.4-smart-dodge.md

# 5.4 — Smart dodge (predict attack type)

**Bucket:** v4.5 · **Risk:** High · **Size:** L
**Module:** extend `src/wonder.js` (`defenseAssessment`,
`defenseShouldDodge`) AND extend `src/dodge.js` (`dodgeTrySend`
overrides). Plan 27 names `military.js` — wrong module hint, see §1.
**Depends on:** 5.3 threat assessment engine (the per-type risk table is
the contract that 5.3 should eventually own; today it lives inline in
`wonder.js`).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

The decision plumbing is split across `wonder.js` and `dodge.js`. None
of it is in `military.js` despite the plan 27 hint.

- `wonder.js:144 defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` — per-incoming
  `{eta, simultaneous, local, supports, safeTown, evac, militia, risk,
  hasCs}`. Risk is built by literal increments (`if(mov.hasCs) risk+=60;
  if(eta!=null&&eta<15*60) risk+=25; …`) — no per-attack-type breakdown
  beyond `hasCs`.
- `wonder.js:145 defenseShouldDodge(mov, incoming)` — wraps with a
  literal `if(a.hasCs || a.risk >= 35)` threshold; returns `{yes,
  assessment, why}` consumed by `dodgeTrySend` (`dodge.js:207`).
- `wonder.js:142 defenseLocalStrength(townId)` — `dodgeTownUnits` per
  unit id, scores defense/both kinds weighted by `unitMeta.population`;
  naval units (`m.is_naval`) excluded.
- `wonder.js:143 defenseSupportOptions(dest, eta)` — own towns whose
  defense-shaped units can reach `dest` before `eta`; boat capacity and
  `isSameIsland` validated. Sorted by travel time ascending.
- `dodge.js:39 DODGE_HOSTILE_TYPES` — canonical vocabulary
  `attack|attack_sea|raid|siege|revolt|colonize|take_over|conquer|portal_attack`.
- `dodge.js:203-251 dodgeTrySend(entry, mov)` — the firing path; posts
  `bridgePost('dodge', payload)` with hardcoded `attackTpl.action_name
  || 'sendUnits'` (`dodge.js:130-138`).
- `dodge.js:252-296 dodgeScan(reason)` — main loop, scheduled on
  `gbInterval(() => dodgeScan('loop'), DODGE_CHECK_MS=5000)`
  (`boot.js:100`, `wonder.js:150`).
- `state.defenseCfg = {mode: 'notify'|'safe'|'smart', smartAuto: false,
  returnMarginSec: 120}` (`core.js:359`). UI at `ui.js:824`,
  `ui.js:1350-1353`, `ui.js:1470-1472`. `smartAuto` default false per
  HIGH-RISK (`core.js:504`), force-migrated when `dodgeMode === 'auto'`
  (`core.js:502-504`). `DEFENSE_CFG` is world-scoped (`header.js:209`).
- The literal `35` threshold is hardcoded inside `defenseShouldDodge`
  (`wonder.js:145`); it is **not** in `state.defenseCfg` today.

**Wrong-module-hint finding.** Plan 27 §5 row 5.4 says "extend
`military.js`". `military.js` has no smart-dodge logic — it owns
cancel-command (`militaryCancelCommand`), heroes, and the Attack-tab
helpers. The decision (`defenseShouldDodge`) lives in `wonder.js:140-148`
and is exported via `boot.js:178-181`. The honest split is `wonder.js`
(per-type risk table + threshold pin) + `dodge.js` (consumer).

## 2. Gap

`defenseAssessment` treats every non-CS hostile incoming as the same
risk baseline (`+25` for any eta<15min, +10 for low local, etc.). A
ten-archer scout and a 200-sword siege both score identically on the
non-CS path. The smart dodge the user actually wants:

- is **calmer** for `raid` (small, fast, often loot-only, dodge is over-
  reaction);
- is **firm** for `attack` and `attack_sea` (default posture);
- is **aggressive** for `siege` (cata damage, no milita match);
- is **forced** for `revolt|colonize|take_over|conquer|portal_attack`
  (the town is gone anyway if it lands; the units are the only salvage).

The literal threshold `35` in `defenseShouldDodge` was chosen when CS
was the only type-bump; with per-type risks, the threshold needs to
move with them. Exposing the threshold and the per-type scores as
Config is the smallest delta that gives the user agency without
introducing a new surface.

## 3. Design

A typed risk table replaces the literal `hasCs` branch. The dodge
threshold is pinned in `state.defenseCfg.riskThresholdDodge` and
defaulted to the current `35`.

```
incoming movement →
  dodgeScan (dodge.js:252) →
    dodgeTryMilitia (parallel, plan 3.6) and
    dodgeTrySend (dodge.js:203) →
      defenseShouldDodge (wonder.js:145) →
        defenseAssessment (wonder.js:144) →
          defenseAssessmentFor(mov, incoming)  ← NEW, replaces literal
            ├── typedRisk = state.defenseCfg.attackRisk[type] ||
            │               state.defenseCfg.attackRisk._default
            ├── risk = typedRisk
            │         + etaRisk(eta)               (≤15min:+25, ≤5min:+35)
            │         + simultaneousRisk(n)         (max +25, +8/stack)
            │         + weakLocalRisk(local.score)  (≤200:+10)
            │         - supportRisk(supports)       (max -20, -5/option)
            ├── alwaysCsRisk: if (mov.hasCs || type in COLONIZE_TYPES)
            │       risk += state.defenseCfg.attackRisk.csBonus (60)
            └── return {eta, simultaneous, local, supports, safeTown,
                       evac, militia, risk, hasCs, attackType:type}
        decision: yes = (mode==='safe') ||
                       (mode==='smart' &&
                        state.defenseCfg.smartAuto &&
                        a.evac.ok && (a.hasCs || a.risk >= threshold))
```

Per-type keys (default values, configurable later):
`raid:5, attack:15, attack_sea:15, siege:40, revolt:70, colonize:70,
take_over:70, conquer:70, portal_attack:70, _default:25,
csBonus:60`.

The risk formula itself is unchanged shape; the typed lookup is a
single replacement. The supporting branches (`eta`, `simultaneous`,
`local`, `supports`) stay in `defenseAssessment`.

## 4. Work items

1. In `wonder.js` (after `defenseShouldDodge`, line 145), add
   `defenseAssessmentFor(mov, incoming)` that calls
   `defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` and **replaces** the `hasCs` /
   typed branches with a single table-driven bump. Pure delta over
   `defenseAssessment`'s return value.
2. Add `function riskForAttackType(type, hasCs)` lookup helper, kept

## 8. Failure modes

- Unrecognised `mov.type` string → `riskForAttackType` falls back to
  `attackRisk._default` (25); `gbLogT('risk-type-unknown', 60000)` once
  per session. Decision path identical to today.
- Malformed `attackRisk` object from `qolImportConfig`:
  `core.js:464` migration resets to defaults; the validator at
  `qol.js:251` requires `isObj` (non-array object). `Number.isFinite`
  guard in `riskForAttackType` for any operator-typed value.
- Smart-auto ON, support in a hostile island with no boats:
  `dodgeSupportValidate` already refuses (`dodge.js:162-163`). The smart
  threshold is irrelevant; no post without green validate.
- Wave of 5 simultaneous low-risk raids on the same town:
  `simultaneous=5 → simultaneousRisk = min(25, (5-1)*8) = 25`. Combined
  with `raid=5` we land at ~30 — below threshold 35, smart-dodge does
  NOT fire (militia path may). If the operator wants simultaneous
  waves to elevate risk further, it's a per-type tuning — exposed in
  Config.
- Stats panel rendering with stale entries: the 1h TTL prune keeps the
  buffer bounded; an overnight tab is empty by morning. No leak.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 High risk: **payload sniff against live UI + confirm-gate
screen + dry-run + manual re-fire, then still default OFF**. Plus plan
27 §10 §3: only after 5.3 (threat assessment engine) passes its gate.

Steps on `es146`:

1. With `state.dryRun === true` and `state.defenseCfg.mode === 'smart'`,
   `smartAuto === true`: stage a single hostile attack. The Log MUST
   show `defense: type=<type> risk=<n> decision yes/no threshold <35>`.
2. Sniff: with the dry-run decision `no`, re-run with a CS-flagged
   attack. The Log MUST now show `decision yes` and `risk >= threshold
   + csBonus`. Hand-sniff the `sendUnits` payload via DevTools against
   the bridge post (same target) — must match.
3. Re-fire manually once with `state.dryRun === false`; verify dodge
   fires **only** when smart decided yes. Stat counter +1.
4. Per-type calibration: run `raid`, `attack`, `siege` in sequence
   against the same defender. Risk scores MUST rank
   `raid < attack < siege`. If they don't, debug per-type Config.
5. CS path: `colonize_ship`-bearing incoming — risk MUST include
   `csBonus` regardless of type lookup; smart-autododge fires
   (verifiable in journal).
6. Confirm-gate: every fire of `dodgeTrySend` runs through
   `dodgeSupportValidate` and `safeTown` (`dodge.js:215-217`). This
   plan adds **no** new human-visible confirm dialog (auto-dodge has
   never had one).
7. **Shipping default**: `mode = 'notify'`, `smartAuto = false`. Do
   **not** flip the default to `'smart'` even if validation passes.

## 10. Out of scope

- Predicting attacker composition from `mov.units` — those are the
  attacker's, not the defender's; reading them requires a counter-spy
  (plan 4.2).
- Friendly-return dodging — filtered by `dodgeIsHostileMovement`; this
  plan stays hostile-only.
- Re-evaluating decisions within the same wave. `defenseAssessment`
  re-runs every 5s tick; a wake-on-incoming optimization is a separate
  change (the wake queue is heterogeneous, `core.js:632`).
- A "force-dodge all" toggle. `defenseMode === 'safe'`
  (`wonder.js:145`) already does that. Plan 5.4 is the smart axis
  only.
- Crossing the `[10..200]` validator on the threshold. Operators
  who need extremes must use `qolImportConfig` (documented power-user
  path).

## 5.5-academy-slot-optimizer.md

# 5.5 — Academy slot optimizer, queue weighting

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/research.js`; UI/config evidence is in `src/ui.js`; cadence remains `src/orchestrate.js`
**Depends on:** 1.2 city specialization profiles; cross-reference `docs/plan-academy-queue.md` (existing academy queue plan)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today
- Academy automation already has a persisted opt-in `state.autoResearch` (`src/core.js:303`) and Config checkbox `data-cfg="auto-research"` (`src/ui.js:778`). The catalogue’s “extend research.js” hint is therefore correct for selection, not for cadence.
- `researchScan` scans towns and sorts each town’s configured targets by `order`, then chooses the first eligible unresearched, unqueued, enabled target (`src/research.js:450-489`). It does not weight targets by slot scarcity, city role, opportunity cost, or path value.
- The current queue limit is read from `GameDataConstructionQueue.getResearchOrdersQueueLength()`, with conservative fallback to curator/base values (`src/research.js:109-123`). Current orders are read through `researchOrdersFor`; unreadable non-current queues are explicitly `known:false` (`src/research.js:19-54`).
- The final precondition validates town state, researched flags, known queue, duplicate queue membership, queue full, dependencies, and affordability before post (`src/research.js:378-395`). The slot optimizer must remain advisory to this invariant, not replace it.
- The actual research post is already bridge-first through `bridgePost('research', researchPayload(...))` (`src/research.js:291-315`), with the verified `ResearchOrder` payload and top-level `town_id` (`src/research.js:295-301`). This plan adds no endpoint or payload.
- Research already receives cadence through the shared orchestrator: `research` is enabled by `state.autoResearch`/native pending state (`src/orchestrate.js:1-17`) and dispatched from `orchTick` (`src/orchestrate.js:147-195`). No `gbInterval` may be added.
- Existing `docs/plan-academy-queue.md` is not an unimplemented prerequisite: it says the queue work is coded except live validation (`docs/plan-academy-queue.md:1-9`) and records the implemented H4/H1/H3/A1 fixes (`docs/plan-academy-queue.md:300-335`). 5.5 must not duplicate those fixes.
- Plan 27’s dependency on 1.2 is real, but no `cityProfiles` implementation is present in the cited current files: `researchTownTechs` exposes academy/research/queue facts only (`src/research.js:56-107`), and `build-targets.js` contains build ordering/targets, not profile weighting (`src/build-targets.js:1-26`). Implementer must consume the 1.2 contract only after that plan lands; do not invent its field names.

## 2. Gap
Add deterministic, read-mostly ranking of candidate research jobs when multiple academy slots/towns compete. The rank should combine verified current eligibility with a city profile supplied by 1.2, target path completion/value, and queue occupancy, while preserving the configured target order as a stable fallback. It must not add a second queue, duplicate the already-coded academy queue plan, or turn Low-risk queue weighting into a new autonomous game action beyond the existing opt-in `autoResearch` path.

## 3. Design
At each existing `researchScan` invocation, gather candidates from the same town/target loop (`src/research.js:450-489`). Read `researchTownTechs` and reject only facts actually read; retain unknown queue handling (`src/research.js:454-459`). For each defined target, compute a score from: profile role weights from 1.2 (exact accessor/fields to be named by that plan), the number of missing prerequisites from the verified game model, configured order, and available queue slots. Lower cost/shorter path may be preferred only when the relevant values are readable; unreadable values are `blind` and fall back to configured order. Sort candidates deterministically by score, then town id, then configured order, and run the existing final validation immediately before `researchPost` (`src/research.js:497-516`). This optimizes selection only; it never guesses research ids or starts prerequisites.

## 4. Work items
1. `src/research.js:450-489`: refactor the current “first eligible target” loop into candidate collection, preserving explicit FIFO precedence (`src/research.js:428-447`) and the existing `nativeQueueSetJobState` behavior.
2. `src/research.js` module-local helper: define a stable `researchCandidateScore(candidate, profile, context)` with documented tie-breaks. Use only fields delivered by plan 1.2; until that contract exists, omit profile contribution rather than guessing `state.cityProfiles` shape.
3. `src/research.js`: call the research graph/path helper from 2.10 if available; otherwise use the existing live dependency verdict (`src/research.js:326-376`). Missing graph/path data must not block a server-valid candidate unless a real precondition is unreadable.
4. `src/research.js`: keep `researchValidateJob` as the final authority (`src/research.js:378-395`) and re-run it after ranking, because queue state can change while scanning.
5. `src/research.js:506-535`: retain the existing `gbLock`/unlock lifecycle and callback ambiguity handling. Do not add `researchInFlight` or another scheduler; the existing `GB_LOCK_TTL.research` is already present (`src/core.js:145-157`).
6. `src/orchestrate.js:1-17,147-195`: do not add a handler or interval. If ranking needs cadence tuning, use the existing research cadence/config mechanism, not a new timer.
7. `src/ui.js:778-779`: add a Low-risk weighting control only after 1.2 defines the profile surface. Labels remain Spanish; default must preserve current configured order. A read-only “ranking reason” line should show selected town/tech and score factors without exposing guessed ids.
8. `src/core.js:303-304` and `src/header.js:98-99,191-215`: if adding weighting config, add exact `STORE` key/state default, world-scope it because town/research ids are involved, bump config version, and add migration. Prefer a single profile-derived setting over a second target schema.
9. Cross-reference `docs/plan-academy-queue.md:260-290` in implementation notes and do not reimplement its per-town orders, points formula, endpoint, or native mount fixes.

## 5. State & storage
Existing `state.researchTargets` and `STORE.RESEARCH_TARGETS` remain the source of configured order (`src/core.js:303-304`, `src/research.js:1-7`). Prefer no new state: derive scores per scan. If a user override is required, use a new world-scoped base in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-215`), uniform 7-day prune, and `configVer` migration; do not store volatile queue scores or server model objects. No new lock state is needed.

## 6. Config surface
Existing `Auto-research` stays the only automation toggle and remains default OFF (`src/core.js:303`, `src/ui.js:778`). Add at most one Spanish selector for queue policy, default `configured order`/stable behavior, with options pinned to explicit machine values. Any automatic selection remains behind the existing opt-in and global dry-run control (`src/ui.js:785`, `src/core.js:346`). City profile controls belong to plan 1.2, not this file.

## 7. Post surface & safety
No new post surface: selected jobs still use existing `bridgePost('research', ...)` (`src/research.js:314-315`) and existing payload (`src/research.js:295-301`). Do not add `gbAjaxWatch` or a `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry. Existing research posts remain covered by the bridge’s captcha feature key and dry-run path; the optimizer must check neither by bypassing `researchPost` nor by introducing a direct XHR. Existing `gbLock('research')` is retained (`src/research.js:506-516`).

## 8. Failure modes
A candidate with unreadable town, academy, research flags, queue, cost, or profile is marked blind and falls back to configured order; it must not be treated as zero cost, zero queue occupancy, or a preferred role. The existing unknown-queue guard must continue to skip non-current towns (`src/research.js:454-459`). Every hard rejection names the value read, matching the existing `researchCanAfford`/dependency logging (`src/research.js:260-287,370-376`). A missing 1.2 profile accessor is a compatibility condition, not permission to guess a field. Final validation remains mandatory immediately before posting (`src/research.js:497-504`).

## 9. Validation gate
Low-risk gate: run Preflight, complete one in-game session with `Auto-research` OFF and inspect the ranking display/log only; no bridge research post may appear. Then enable existing automation with Dry run ON, use two towns with different 1.2 profiles and at least two eligible targets, and verify the Log explains the chosen town/target and stable tie-break. Confirm a full/unknown queue is not ranked as free (`research.js:382-391`), explicit native FIFO still wins (`research.js:428-447`), and repeated identical state produces identical order. Do not claim live correctness until academy queue validation from `docs/plan-academy-queue.md:364-365` is also complete.

## 10. Out of scope
No academy endpoint/payload changes, no native Academy mount repair, no research point or queue-reader rewrite, no prerequisite auto-enqueue, no new scheduler, no city-profile implementation (owned by 1.2), no high-risk toggle, and no duplication of `docs/plan-academy-queue.md`’s coded work. The feature cannot be fully wired until 1.2 specifies a real profile accessor/schema; plan against that dependency rather than inventing one.

## 5.6-build-queue-optimizer.md

# 5.6 — Build queue optimizer (local reorder for minimum idle)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `native-ui.js` (the native FIFO queue and its planner
adapter live there); UI in `queue-center.js`. **NOT** `build-targets.js` —
plan 27's module hint is wrong on this one; `build-targets.js` only owns
`state.abOrder` / `state.abTargets` and has no FIFO queue surface.
**Depends on:** 1.2 (city profiles) for the per-town profile read, used only
to gate the suggestion threshold; the swap itself needs no profile data.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- **The queue being optimized is `nativeQueueList(townId,'build',false)` in
  `native-ui.js:21`.** It is a stable FIFO list of `{id, building, fromLevel,
  toLevel, status, reason, …}` jobs, populated by `nativeQueueAddBuild`
  (`native-ui.js:205-269`) from the Senate window's `[+]` tile or the Queue
  Center's **+ Añadir secuencia** button (planned by 2.9). Each town has its
  own list with a `mode: 'legacy' | 'fifo'` (`native-ui.js:11`); a town in
  `fifo` mode ignores `goalEffectiveBuildTargets` entirely
  (`build-auto.js:180-181`).
- **The auto-queue already skips a blocked head.** `nativeQueueBuildPlan`
  (`native-ui.js:337-352`) returns `{hasJob:true, plan:null, why}` with
  `why ∈ {'paused','lane-review','manual-review','inflight',
  'special-conflict','max-unreadable','max-level', ...}` and the head is
  marked `waiting-resources` / `waiting-population` / `blocked` via
  `nativeQueueSetJobState` (`native-ui.js:309-317`). `abFinalValidate`
  (`build-auto.js:204-224`) re-checks the head right before posting, and
  `abPickNextFromLevels` (`build-auto.js:178-202`) only ever picks
  `list[0]`.
- **No swap.** The FIFO contract is "head posts, rest wait". When the head
  is `waiting-resources`, the rest of the list sits idle even if a later
  entry is currently affordable. `abScan` (`build-auto.js:266-369`) walks
  town-by-town and stops at `q.len >= q.max` (`build-auto.js:335-338`), so a
  town with a blocked head and a free queue slot does nothing — the next
  town is processed instead. That is the "idle gap" 5.6 targets.
- **No `abCustomQueue` / `abPin` / `abQueueStrict` in `src/`.** Plan 23's
  symbols do not exist (verified by grep; same finding as 2.9 §1 and the
  plan 26 §B2 mistake). The user's "explicit queue" here is the native
  FIFO.
- **Reorder API exists.** `nativeQueueMove(townId, lane, jobId, delta)`
  (`native-ui.js:45-50`) reorders within the list and is what the Queue
  Center ↑/↓ buttons call (`queue-center.js:150-156`). It refuses to move
  any job whose `inflight` or `manualReview` flag is set; this is the gate
  the optimizer must respect.

## 2. Gap

When the FIFO head is `waiting-resources` for more than a few minutes the
user's later entries are paying no dividend. A local swap — promote an
**affordable** successor past the blocked head — recovers the slot without
violating the user's authorship: the user said "these, in this order", not
"wait until the first is affordable even if another is ready now". The
optimizer proposes a swap, never silently performs one.

## 3. Design

Add two helpers in `native-ui.js` and one UI affordance in
`queue-center.js`. No new posts; the swap is a list mutation that goes
through the existing `nativeQueueMove` API.

**`nativeQueueHeadBlockedFor(townId, opts)`** — returns
`{townId, jobId, why, forMinutes}` where `forMinutes` is how long the head
has been in a `waiting-*` state. Backed by `job.status`, `job.reason`,
`job.reasonUpdatedAt` (set by `nativeQueueSetJobState`
`native-ui.js:309-317`). Threshold: ≥ 5min (configurable via
`state.buildSwapThresholdMin`, default 5, OFF = disabled).

**`nativeQueueSuggestSwap(townId, opts)`** — scans
`nativeQueueList(townId,'build',false)` from index 1 forward; for each job
calls `abResolvePrerequisite(townId, j.building, levels)` and
`abCanAfford(townId, j.building)` (both already in `build-auto.js`),
returning the first affordable, non-blocked entry. Returns
`{successorIndex, successor, swap: {headId, successorId, from, to}}` or
`null` if no successor is affordable in the same town. **One town at a
time** — cross-town reordering is out of scope.

**UI — Queue Center Construcción card.** When the head has been
`waiting-resources` ≥ threshold and a successor is affordable, render a
small banner under the FIFO plan card with text "Sugerencia: ascender
`<successor>` mientras se esperan recursos para `<head>`" and two buttons
**Ascender** / **Ignorar**. Click **Ascender** calls `nativeQueueMove(
townId,'build', successorId, -successorIndex)` — the existing API
(`native-ui.js:45-50`), which refuses on any inflight/manualReview so the
optimizer cannot break a frozen head. **Ignorar** stamps
`state.buildSwapIgnore[townId+headId]` (TTL 10min) so the same suggestion
does not flash again before the head recovers.

**Precedence rule.** FIFO head still wins for the auto-queue: nothing in
5.6 changes `abPickNextFromLevels` (`build-auto.js:178-202`) or
`nativeQueueBuildPlan` (`native-ui.js:337-352`). The optimizer is a UI
suggestion that mutates the list on a user click; the auto-queue then
respects the new order naturally. The user's explicit queue wins in both
the original and the swapped order — there is no case where 5.6 displaces
the head without consent.

## 4. Work items

1. `native-ui.js` — new `nativeQueueHeadBlockedFor(townId, opts)` and
   `nativeQueueSuggestSwap(townId, opts)` per §3. Both module-local (no
   new top-level `function` declarations per the `build.py:31-72` build
   gate). Wrap any shared helpers in a module-local IIFE.
2. `native-ui.js` — wire `nativeQueueSuggestSwap` into the existing
   `nativeQueueReconcileBuild` reconciliation step
   (`native-ui.js:325-335`) **only for logging**. The reconcile path
   computes `head` / `tail` already; have it call `gbLogT` once when a
   swap suggestion exists, with the suggestion in the payload (no UI side
   effect). The Queue Center does its own scan at render time.
3. `queue-center.js` — in `renderQueueCenterBuild` (`queue-center.js:116`),
   add the suggestion banner under the FIFO plan card. Reuse the
   `queueCenterButton` helper (`queue-center.js:63-73`) for both buttons.
4. `core.js` — new `state.buildSwapThresholdMin` (default 5, OFF=0/disabled)
   and `state.buildSwapIgnore = {}` (per-town+job TTL cache). Add to the
   `state` initialiser block next to the other `build*` fields.
5. `stats.js:249` — Preflight row `build swap suggestion` probing
   `nativeQueueSuggestSwap` for the open town and reporting
   `{ok, detail: 'cabeza esperando Xm · sucesora: Y'}` or
   `{ok:true, detail:'sin sugerencia'}`.
6. `qol.js` Config — expose `state.buildSwapThresholdMin` and a "Limpiar
   ignorados" button that wipes `state.buildSwapIgnore`.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.buildSwapThresholdMin` — number, default 5, OFF=0. Not
  id-bearing; no world-scope.
- `state.buildSwapIgnore = {}` — `{ [townId+':'+jobId]: untilTs }`.
  Id-bearing ⇒ **`STORE.BUILD_SWAP_IGNORE` is a new key, add to
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` in `header.js:193-214`** next to `STORE.NATIVE_QUEUE`
  (line 209).
- `configVer` bump (CLAUDE.md / plan 27 §13).
- Prune TTL: 10min (the `untilTs` is what enforces it; no 7d ring needed —
  the cache never grows beyond a few entries per town because the user can
  only ignore a head once per block cycle).

## 6. Config surface

- `state.buildSwapThresholdMin` — number input, **default 5**. Low risk,
  no HIGH-RISK rule applies (the user-confirmed swap is the consent gate;
  see §3).
- `state.buildSwapIgnore` reset button — parity with other
  reset-style rows in `qol.js`.
- No new top-level toggles.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **No new post surface.** `nativeQueueMove` (`native-ui.js:45-50`)
  mutates the list and calls `nativeQueueRebaseBuild` /
  `nativeQueueSave` — neither posts. The next `abScan('native-watch')`
  (`boot.js:91`) sees the new head and `nativeQueueBuildPlan`
  (`native-ui.js:337-352`) returns its `ready` / `waiting-resources` plan.
  The post that fires is the same `bridgePost('build', …)` from
  `abBuildUp` (`build-auto.js:246`) — already journaled, captcha-gated,
  and dry-run-aware.
- `gbCaptchaPause` — no new feature key needed.
- `gbLock` — no new lock; the swap runs between two `abScan` calls, not
  inside one, and the gate (`inflight` / `manualReview`) is enforced by
  `nativeQueueMove` itself. Adding `ab` to `GB_LOCK_TTL` is unnecessary.
- `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` — no new template.
- `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` — no change.
- **Dry-run behaviour** — with `state.dryRun = true`, the swap still
  works (it is a list mutation); the subsequent `abScan` posts become
  `DRY-RUN build: … buildUp` lines. This is the right parity — the user
  can validate "swap promotes Y, head recovers" without spending a slot.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Unreadable levels / costs** (`abCurrentLevels(townId)` returns `null`,
  `build-auto.js:14-33`) → `nativeQueueSuggestSwap` returns `null`; the
  banner does not appear; `gbLogT('build-swap-blind-'+townId, 60000, …)`
  once.
- **Unreadable planner ledger** (`plannerAvailable(townId)` returns
  `null`, `planner.js:82-86`) → swap suggestion suppressed; the banner
  reads "planificador ilegible" and **Ascender** is disabled.
- **`nativeQueueMove` refuses** on `inflight` / `manualReview`
  (`native-ui.js:47`) → flash the same reason the Queue Center × button
  uses (`queue-center.js:103-114`); the banner stays visible so the user
  can retry once the head recovers.
- **Cycle in prerequisite walk** (`abResolvePrerequisite` returns
  `{error:'dependency-cycle'}`, `build-auto.js:162`) → `nativeQueueSuggestSwap`
  skips that successor and tries the next; no log spam (`gbLogT` keyed on
  the successor id+townId, 60s throttle).
- **The user has zero FIFO entries** (`nativeQueueList(townId,'build',
  false).length === 0`) → no banner; this is also the legacy-mode path
  where `goalEffectiveBuildTargets` already drives picks and the head is
  never "blocked on resources for 5min" in the same way.
- **Cross-town ambiguity** — the suggestion is always intra-town. If the
  user has a blocked head in town A and an affordable build queued in
  town B, the banner does not appear and the swap does not happen.
  Cross-town rebalancing is plan 5.1 territory and depends on
  transport automation (1.3); out of scope here.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class: Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure.

1. **Preflight** — `build swap suggestion` row reports
   `cabeza esperando Xm · sucesora: Y` for a town whose head has been
   `waiting-resources` for ≥ 5min and whose second FIFO entry is currently
   affordable. With threshold = 0 the row reads `desactivado`.
2. **Queue Center Construcción** — open the Build tab on a town with a
   blocked head and an affordable second entry; the banner appears with the
   correct suggestion. Click **Ascender**; the FIFO card repaints with the
   two jobs swapped (head now affordable, second now head). `abScan` fires
   within ~80ms (`native-ui.js:268`); the first build lands.
3. **Head recovery** — when the resources for the original head arrive, the
   FIFO order remains swapped (we are not auto-reverting). `abScan` will
   build the now-affordable head and reconcile the rest naturally via
   `nativeQueueReconcileBuild` (`native-ui.js:325-335`).
4. **Ignore path** — click **Ignorar**; the banner hides. Within 10min the
   suggestion does not re-appear even if the head is still blocked. After
   10min it can appear again.
5. **Precedence preserved** — with `state.abAuto` ON and the FIFO head
   swapped, `abPickNextFromLevels` picks the new head (the now-affordable
   successor), never the original head. The original head, now in slot 2,
   gets built when resources arrive.
6. **Dry-run parity** — `state.dryRun = true`; perform the swap; verify
   the post line `DRY-RUN build: BuildingOrder/buildUp …` fires for the
   new head, not the old one.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Auto-swap without user click.** Plan 27 §5.6 says "local reorder for
  minimum idle", which reads as user-confirmed; an auto-swap variant
  would need a HIGH-RISK toggle (default OFF per CLAUDE.md) and is
  deferred. The current plan's contract is "suggest, never silently do".
- **Cross-town reorder.** See §8; cross-town balancing belongs with 5.1
  resource balancing AI.
- **Reorder to minimise *gold* idle, not just resource idle.** Grepolis
  has no gold cost on `buildUp`; the planner ledger covers wood/stone/
  iron/population/tradeCap only (`planner.js:1`). No further dimension
  to optimise without inventing a new cost.
- **A general "auto-promote to head" rule for the legacy (non-FIFO) lane.**
  The legacy lane picks targets one at a time from
  `goalEffectiveBuildTargets` and skips past `waiting-resources` via
  `afford` (`build-auto.js:197-198`). The skip is already correct for the
  legacy case; 5.6 only addresses the FIFO lane.
- **Implementing plan 23's `abCustomQueue` / `abQueueStrict` knobs.**
  Those are owned by plan 23's eventual rewrite; 5.6 reuses the native
  FIFO surface they were meant to wrap.

## 5.8-booty-camp-optimizer.md

# 5.8 — Booty camp optimizer (bandit ranker)

**Bucket:** v4.2 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/bandit.js` (unit-picker heuristic) + add a read-only
  rollup row in `src/stats.js` (cycle deltas)
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2 (header `@version` is `3.9.0`; off by one, harmless)

> The Grepolis booty camp is per-player (one `PlayerAttackSpot` model per
> account, `src/bandit.js:186`), so the "ranker" this plan ships is a **unit
> picker**, not a camp picker. It changes *which* units are payload, not
> *which* camp is attacked. The catalog's "ranker" intent is satisfied:
> the bandit `attack` payload now carries a ranked, capped subset of the
> current town's offense units, and the Stats tab shows the per-cycle mix
> so the player can see why.

---

## 1. What exists today

- `banditAttackUnits(uw, rawUnits)` (`src/bandit.js:24-37`) is the only
  caller-side unit filter. It walks `rawUnits`, deletes `militia` and
  anything whose `GameData.units[id].is_naval` is truthy, then drops
  anything `banditIsOffenseUnit` rejects. The result is the **full**
  remaining map — every eligible offense unit count is sent.
- `banditIsOffenseUnit(uw, id)` (`src/bandit.js:10-23`) is the eligibility
  test. It accepts `godsent`/`hoplite` exceptions, prefers the
  `unit_function` attribute (`off`/`def`/`both`/`none`), and falls back to
  the `BANDIT_OFFENSE_IDS` regex at `src/bandit.js:9` (`slinger|hoplite|
  rider|chariot|minotaur|manticore|cyclops?|zyklop|harpy|erinys|fury|
  centaur|griffin|satyr|giant|godsent`).
- `banditViaGame()` (`src/bandit.js:182-298`) builds the payload from the
  current town only: `t.units()` at `src/bandit.js:273`. There is no
  town-picker branch — picking a different town would require a separate
  bridge call to switch `Game.townId`, which `bandit.js` does not have.
- The "ranker" hook is `banditAttackUnits`. It already runs per cycle and
  is the only place the payload mix is decided.
- `state.banditLog` (`src/bandit.js:347-351`) is a 50-entry ring of
  `{ts, ev}` strings. It is the only bandit-related state. There is no
  cycle-by-cycle history of the payload mix.
- `logBandit('attack')` (`src/bandit.js:291`) is the only place the
  payload is journaled — and it stores the *string* `attack`, not the
  units. So after the fact, no record shows which units were sent.
- Defaults: `state.autoBandit` defaults to `false` (`src/core.js:247`),
  HIGH-RISK per CLAUDE.md. Stats surface for the bandit is one
  Preflight row at `src/stats.js:234-238` (`bandit camp`) and the
  per-feature rollup line in `renderStats` (`src/stats.js:294-309`,
  derived from `jrnStats`).
- Plan 26 §C2 added the scope-aware budget line at `src/stats.js:339-344`.
  The per-feature rollup already lists `bandit` rows under the existing
  `feature ok err tout pend cap skip rate` table (`:294-309`); the
  ranker HUD goes inside the same per-feature block, not next to it.

## 2. Gap

Today the bot sends every offense unit from the current town. Three
failure modes follow:

1. **Donate the defenses.** A balanced town that happens to be the
   current town during the bandit cycle loses its offense reserve with
   no warning. The dodge floor (`state.dodgeFloor`, `src/bandit.js:117`
   and `src/core.js:324`) is checked by the **favor** scanner but is
   **not** checked by `banditAttackUnits`.
2. **No cycle history.** The payload disappears once `bridgePost` is
   called. The player (and the validation gate) cannot tell whether the
   last 3 attacks all sent the same 80 hoplites or whether the unit
   mix shifted.
3. **No opt-out for one cap.** The catalog description is "ranker" but
   the only knob today is the binary enabled toggle. There is no way
   to say "send at most 50 of each unit type" without rewriting the
   picker.

The ranker closes those three.

## 3. Design

Two changes, both inside the existing schedule:

1. **Unit-picker with rank + cap.** New module-local IIFE
   `banditRankUnits(uw, rawUnits, cfg)` returning the post-map. The
   shape is unchanged (`{ unitName: count }`); the contents are
   different. Default `cfg` is the empty object — the picker falls back
   to today's "send all" behaviour, so the ranker is **off** by default
   (no change in v3.8.2 behavior).
2. **Stats readout.** New module-local `banditAttackHistory` (plain
   array, **not** persisted; pruned module-local to 20 entries). Each
   successful `post('attack', ...)` callback at `src/bandit.js:275`
   pushes `{ts, units}` onto the array, and `renderStats` prints the
   last 3 cycles.

Both changes are gated by `state.autoBandit === true`; with the master
toggle off (default), the code path is identical to today.

### Ranker contract

`banditRankUnits(uw, rawUnits, cfg)`:

- Apply the existing legality filter the same way `banditAttackUnits`
  does today (delete `militia`, drop naval, drop `banditIsOffenseUnit`
  rejects). After this: `map = { unit: count }` containing only offense
  units.
- If `cfg.smartCap` is not set or `cfg.smartCap <= 0`, return `map`
  unchanged. This is the v3.8.2 baseline.
- Else for each entry, compute `rank = (units[unit].cost?.iron ?? 0) +
  (units[unit].cost?.wood ?? 0) + (units[unit].cost?.stone ?? 0)` —
  i.e. the unit's total resource build cost, a proxy for "productive
  per unit" under the catalog's "ranker" rubric. The rank window is
  sorted once descending.
- For each unit in rank order, cap to `Math.min(count, cfg.smartCap)`.
  One floor: `cap = Math.max(1, Math.min(+cfg.smartCap, count))` —
  never zero out a unit the player bought (the ranker is a *cap*, not
  a *filter*).
- Optionally subtract `state.dodgeFloor` for each unit type that
  matches `dodgeFloorUnits` (default empty array — opt-in). Plan 27
  says Low risk for this cluster; the dodge floor carve-out is
  intentionally NOT active by default because it interacts with the
  `dodge.js` reserve pipeline and changing that would be Med risk.
- Return the capped map.

The picker's `cfg` is read from `state.banditCfg` (new, see §5).

### Stats readout

`renderStats` at `src/stats.js:280-355` already iterates the per-feature
rollup table. We add a sub-table after the `bandit` feature row in the
loop at `src/stats.js:297-309`:

```
  bandit        12   1   0   0   0   4   92%
    ult envio  hoplite:30  rider:12  manticore:2
    anterior  hoplite:35  rider:10  manticore:4
    -3h        hoplite:24  rider:14  manticore:1
```

The Stats row is read-only and reuses the existing `bandit` feature key
in `state.banditLog` decisions. The dedupe pattern follows
`jrnStats(...).byFeature` which already keys `bandit` (`src/stats.js:295`).

### Post volume

**Unchanged.** The send cadence is `banditScheduleNext` (`src/bandit.js:328-338`)
gated by `banditIdleUntil`, `state.autoBandit`, and `gbLocked('bandit-reward')`.
The ranker only changes the units inside the payload. The dry-run gate
already covers `bridgePost('bandit', ...)` at `src/bandit.js:190-193` per
CLAUDE.md "v1.4.0 dry run: `state.dryRun` short-circuits inside
`bridgePost` / `gameAjaxPost` only." No new dry-run gate is needed.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/header.js` — add `STORE.BANDIT_CFG = 'grepbot:bandit-cfg'` to the
   `STORE` map (near `STORE.BANDIT_LOG` at `src/header.js:37`). Do NOT
   add it to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `src/header.js:193-214` — the cfg
   is player preference, not world-specific (or, if a future need
   surfaces, it inherits the same world scoping as `AUTO_BANDIT`; for
   v4.2 keep it unscoped so the same player keeps the same cap across
   world switches). Document the choice in the comment.
2. `src/core.js` — add `banditCfg: load(STORE.BANDIT_CFG, {})` to the
   state initializer (next to `autoBandit` at `src/core.js:247`).
3. `src/core.js` — bump `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` from `10` to `11` at
   `src/header.js:191` (it lives in `header.js`). In `migrateConfig` at
   `src/core.js:394-512`, add a `ver < 11` branch that defaults
   `state.banditCfg = {}` if missing.
4. `src/bandit.js` — add `banditRankUnits(uw, rawUnits, cfg)` near the
   top of the module (right after `banditAttackUnits` at
   `src/bandit.js:24-37`). Use a module-local function — no top-level
   declaration (`build.py:76-80` `DECL_RE` rejects duplicate
   `function` names across modules).
5. `src/bandit.js` — at the call site `bandit.js:273`, change
   `const units = banditAttackUnits(uw, t.units());` to
   `const units = banditRankUnits(uw, t.units(), state.banditCfg || {});`.
   The fallback is harmless: with `cfg = {}` the ranker returns the
   map unchanged (matches v3.8.2).
6. `src/bandit.js` — at the success branch in the `post('attack', units, ...)`
   callback at `src/bandit.js:288-291`, push the payload into a new
   module-local `banditAttackHistory` array (cap 20, ring-style).
   `logBandit('attack')` at `src/bandit.js:291` continues to fire
   unchanged.
7. `src/bandit.js` — expose a reader `banditAttackHistoryGet(n)` for
   the Stats renderer. Module-local `function` declared via the same
   IIFE-style wrapping.
8. `src/stats.js` — inside `renderStats`, after the per-feature rollup
   loop at `src/stats.js:297-309`, when the current feature `f` is
   `'bandit'`, append the up-to-3-entry table using
   `banditAttackHistoryGet(3)`. The text is appended directly into the
   `lines` array (the array is `join('\n')` at `src/stats.js:354`).
9. `src/ui.js` — add a Config toggle group inside the bandit section
   of the Config tab (same block as `[data-cfg=auto-bandit]` at
   `src/ui.js:1144,1170,1210`):
   - checkbox `[data-cfg=bandit-smart-cap]` → `state.banditCfg.smartCap`
     (number, default 0 = off)
   - numeric input `[data-cfg=bandit-smart-floor]` → `state.banditCfg.dodgeFloor`
     (default 0 = off)
   Both follow the existing `setChk`/`bindToggle` pattern at
   `src/ui.js:1144-1210`.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.banditCfg` (`src/core.js:247` neighbour): an object, default
  `{}`. New `STORE.BANDIT_CFG` key (`src/header.js`).
- `configVer` bump: `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` 10 → 11 at `src/header.js:191`,
  migration branch in `migrateConfig` (`src/core.js:482`).
- `banditAttackHistory` is **module-local only** in `src/bandit.js`,
  not persisted. Reasoning: the per-cycle mix is a UI nicety; persisting
  it would mean a `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry and a 7d prune
  (`journal.js`) for cosmetic data. After a reload the Stats row
  shows the next 3 cycles from the new window.
- `STORE.BANDIT_LOG` (`src/header.js:37`) is unchanged — already
  in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `src/header.js:196`.

## 6. Config surface

Two new fields with text labels (Spanish, per CLAUDE.md):

- **Cap por unidad (0 = desactivado).** Number input, default `0`,
  stored in `state.banditCfg.smartCap`. When `0`, the ranker is a
  pass-through and v3.8.2 behavior is preserved.
- **Reservar para defensa.** Number input, default `0`, stored in
  `state.banditCfg.dodgeFloor`. When `0`, the dodge floor carve-out is
  skipped. (Distinct from `state.dodgeFloor` for favors: that one is
  read by `favor.js:117` and is per-favor-unit; this one is per-bandit
  unit.)

Both fields are **OFF** by default. LOW risk — the ranker only takes
effect when the master `Banda automática` toggle is ON, and that toggle
is already HIGH-RISK OFF default per CLAUDE.md.

## 7. Post surface & safety

The post surface is unchanged. The ranker modifies the unit payload
inside `bridgePost('bandit', payload, onDone)` at `src/bandit.js:190-193`,
which is already dry-run gated inside `bridgePost` (CLAUDE.md,
v1.4.0). The capture-pause feature key `'bandit'` is already wired
(`src/bandit.js:183,302`). The reward lock `gbLocked('bandit-reward')`
at `src/bandit.js:202` already covers the reward path. This plan adds
**no** new `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, **no** new `gbCaptchaPause` key, **no**
new `gbAjaxWatch` registration (`bandit.js` uses the post-template
`PlayerAttackSpot/<playerId>` from `src/bandit.js:191`, which is set
inside the bridge via `bridgePost`, not via a learned `tplNameFor`
template). No new `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry.

The `FAVOR_AUTOMATION_ENABLED = false` flag at `src/favor.js:8` is
unrelated and stays false.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`GameData.units[id].cost` is undefined** — the ranker falls back to
  cost `0` for that unit, which puts it at the bottom of the rank
  order but never excludes it. The cap is applied on count, not on
  rank, so the unit still ships.
- **`rawUnits` is `null` or `undefined`** — the existing
  `banditAttackUnits` early-out at `src/bandit.js:25` is
  `Object.assign({}, rawUnits || {})`. The ranker inherits that.
- **`cfg.smartCap` is non-numeric** — coerced via `+cfg.smartCap` and
  `Math.max(1, Math.min(...))`. Non-numeric input becomes `NaN`,
  `Math.min(NaN, …)` is `NaN`, `Math.max(1, NaN)` is `NaN`, which
  passes through to `Math.min(count, NaN)` = `NaN`. The fix is
  `const cap = Math.max(1, Math.min(+cfg.smartCap || count, count))` —
  fall back to "no cap" if `+cfg.smartCap` is `NaN` or `0`.
- **`banditAttackHistory` overflow** — capped at 20 module-local
  entries, push-then-shift is O(n) on 20 elements, well below
  noticeable.
- **Sub-camp not present (`m.getLevel() == null`)** — the existing
  early-return at `src/bandit.js:195` runs before the ranker; no
  change.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), open the Config tab. The new bandit
  block shows two new inputs under the existing `Banda automática`
  toggle. Leave both at `0` (default).
- Open the Stats tab, click the `Banda ahora` … wait, there is no
  manual-fire button. Trigger the scheduler by waiting for the next
  bandit cycle (every ~30s when idle, per `bandit.js:251` and the
  cooldown branch). The per-feature table's `bandit` row now has 2-3
  indented sub-rows showing the last attack mix.
- Set `Cap por unidad` to `5` in Config, wait for the next attack, and
  confirm the next sub-row shows at most 5 of each unit.
- Set DRY-RUN on (`state.dryRun` in Config), trigger a cycle, and
  confirm the Log shows `DRY-RUN bandit: {...}` with the new
  capped payload (the existing dry-run gate covers this; nothing to
  add).
- Preflight (`Comprobar sistema`) — the existing `bandit camp` row at
  `src/stats.js:234-238` still passes; no new row is needed.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Town picker.** Picking the *best* town to attack from would require
  a separate `bridgePost` to switch `Game.townId`, which is not in
  `bandit.js` and would change post volume. The catalog says "Low/S"
  for this row; an inter-town ranker is a future Med-risk item.
- **Reward-rank by power id.** The reward pick at `src/bandit.js:208-209`
  uses `pid.includes('instant')` to pick `useReward` vs `stashReward`
  based on the catalog key. The full set of reward power ids is *not*
  enumerated in `src/`; extending the picker to rank by reward type is
  a separate work item.
- **Per-island group optimization.** `banditWrongIsland` at
  `src/bandit.js:160-181` is a hard skip; the ranker does not change
  it.
- **Auto-bandit v3 (different cadence).** Not this plan. The catalog
  entry is the ranker, not a redesigned cadence.

## 6.1-theme-system.md

# 6.1 — Dark mode / theme system

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/ui.js` (theme is pure CSS) — no `theme.css` file, the
existing `GM_addStyle` block in `ui.js:397-549` already ships the panel CSS.
**Depends on:** none (read-only over the panel; does not touch the game DOM,
does not register a post surface).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0 (header.js:4).

---

## 1. What exists today

- The panel is a single `#grepbot-panel` element injected into `document.body`
  by `ui.js:560-898` (the `panel.innerHTML` template). All styling is inlined
  via one `GM_addStyle` call: `ui.js:397-549` (`#grepbot-panel { background:#181a1f;
  ... }`). The Queue Center window uses a second scoped root
  `#grepbot-queue-center` defined later in the same style block
  (`ui.js:525-543`).
- Colours are **hardcoded hex** at every rule: background `#181a1f` / `#22252b`
  / `#262626`, borders `#333` / `#414650`, accent `#f5a623` (warning amber),
  text `#eef1f5`, error `#f55`, success `#8fe0a8`. ~30 rules reference them.
- No CSS custom properties (`--gb-bg`, `--gb-fg`, …) are declared today
  (`grep -n -- '--gb-' src/` returns zero matches). The panel has no
  light-mode alternative, and no theme toggle exists.
- The `Config` tab is rendered by `bindConfig()` at `ui.js:1137-1540`; toggles
  use `data-cfg="..."` selectors and `state` mutations like
  `state.foo = e.target.checked; save(STORE.X, state.foo)`. This is the
  template a new theme toggle must follow.
- The migration ladder is `migrateConfig()` at `core.js:394-511`. The current
  version is `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT = 10` (`header.js:191`); the latest migration
  block is the `ver < 10` branch at `core.js:482-505` (native queue migration).
  Any new persisted field needs a `ver < 11` block that writes its default.
- Sniffer contracts that plan 27 §0 ties to "Shadow-DOM UI hiding / variable
  rename":
  - `sniffBridgeBody` (`farms.js:1-60`) matches the bridge request **body**
    string against `/FarmTownPlayerRelation/` and `/BuildingOrder/` + `/Instant/`.
    These are URL/body regexes; CSS class names in the panel are invisible to
    them.
  - `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` and `tplNameFor` (`core.js:778-808`) key off JS symbol
    names (`claimTpl`, `attackTpl`, `ibAction`, `ibActionR`). CSS class names
    on the panel do not appear in this map and are not part of any sniffer.
  - The Queue Center template `native-ui.js:2-15` reads `state.nativeQueue` —
    pure state, not CSS. `nativeTownAction` (`native-ui.js:590`) injects
    `+` / `-` / `×` buttons into the game's own DOM via `GPWindowMgr`; CSS
    on `#grepbot-panel` cannot affect those nodes.
- **Conclusion:** changing panel colours is safe. Renaming panel CSS classes or
  ids, hiding the panel inside Shadow DOM, or restructuring the
  `panel.innerHTML` template would be unsafe — plan 27 §0 already bans that.

## 2. Gap

There is one fixed dark theme. Players who want a light panel either live
with it or hand-edit CSS. The plan delivers a small, scoped theme toggle
(dark/light/system) backed by CSS variables, with zero impact on the
sniffers, the game DOM, or the build queue / Queue Center contracts.

## 3. Design

Convert every literal colour in `GM_addStyle` (`ui.js:397-549`) to a CSS
custom property on the panel root, then resolve those properties under three
classes (`#grepbot-panel.gb-theme-dark`, `#grepbot-panel.gb-theme-light`,
`#grepbot-panel.gb-theme-system`). A fourth default rule (`#grepbot-panel`
without a theme class) keeps today's look, so no migration is required for
existing installs. The active class is set at boot and on Config toggle change.

Data flow:

1. `state.theme` (new, default `'dark'`) drives which class is on the panel
   element.
2. On boot, `boot.js` runs `applyTheme()` after the panel exists.
3. In Config, a new `select[data-cfg=theme]` writes the value to
   `state.theme`, calls `applyTheme()`, and `save(STORE.THEME, ...)`.
4. `applyTheme()` removes the three theme classes and adds the one
   corresponding to `state.theme`. For `'system'`, it reads
   `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches` once at apply
   time and applies `'dark'` or `'light'` accordingly (no live listener —
   this is a small toggle, not a sync engine).

CSS variable set (declared on `#grepbot-panel`, scoped so the game's own DOM
is untouched):

```
--gb-bg        #181a1f
--gb-bg-alt    #22252b
--gb-bg-row    #262626
--gb-border    #414650
--gb-border-soft #353a44
--gb-fg        #eef1f5
--gb-fg-soft   #aeb5c0
--gb-fg-mute   #888
--gb-accent    #f5a623
--gb-ok        #8fe0a8
--gb-warn      #ffd27a
--gb-err       #ff9aa3
--gb-link      #6cf
```

The light-theme rule overrides each variable with a near-white pair. The
dark-theme rule is a no-op (defaults already match today's palette, so it
exists only as an explicit anchor for the system-mode resolver).

The Queue Center window (`#grepbot-queue-center` at `ui.js:525-543`) and the
panel share the same variable names — both scopes declare a re-binding under
each theme class so a light theme also lights the Queue Center. No rule
outside `#grepbot-panel` and `#grepbot-queue-center` is touched.

## 5. State & storage

- New `state.theme` (`core.js:~378`, near the visual prefs cluster).
- New `STORE.THEME` (`header.js:63`).
- `configVer` bump: `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` 10 → 11 (`header.js:191`); new
  `ver < 11` migration block (`core.js:~506`) stamps the default.
- No id-bearing key, so no `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry (`header.js:193-214`
  rules).
- No prune TTL — the theme is a single short string.

## 6. Config surface

- Label: `Tema del panel` (panel theme). Three options:
  `oscuro` (dark, default), `claro` (light), `sistema` (follows OS).
- Position: top of Ajustes, just above the per-town checkboxes (around
  `ui.js:800`). Rationale: theme is the first thing a user customizes; the
  existing layout puts always-shown, safe toggles there.
- Default: `oscuro` — matches what every existing install renders today.
- No HIGH-RISK toggle involved; risk stays Low.

## 7. Post surface & safety

Read-mostly feature: **no post surface**. No `bridgePost`, no `gbXhr`, no
`bridgePost`-covered DOM click. The only DOM side effect is toggling classes
on the panel and Queue Center, which is not a write and is not under
dry-run.

- No `gbAjaxWatch` registration needed.
- No `gbCaptchaPause` feature key needed (the feature never posts).
- No `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry needed (no async work; class swap is
  synchronous).
- No dry-run gate needed.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`window.matchMedia` unavailable** (rare; covers Tampermonkey contexts
  without a `window`). `matchMediaDark()` returns `false` (treat as light);
  the user can still pick `oscuro` from the Config dropdown. No crash path.
- **User picks a theme before the panel is mounted.** `applyTheme()` is a
  no-op if `panel` is `null` (it is set at `core.js:386` and assigned during
  `panel.innerHTML = ...` at `ui.js:560`). On first boot the call from the
  boot sequence happens after `appendChild` (`ui.js:899`), so this is moot.
- **CSS variable inheritance across shadow boundaries.** The plan does not
  introduce any shadow DOM (plan 27 §0 explicitly forbids Shadow-DOM UI
  hiding). The two scoped roots (`#grepbot-panel`, `#grepbot-queue-center`)
  are both in the light DOM, so `var(--gb-...)` resolves in both.
- **Theme breaks the sniffer contracts.** Cannot happen — sniffers
  (`farms.js:1-60`, `core.js:778-808`, `native-ui.js:2-15`) key off URL/body
  regexes and JS state, not panel CSS. Plan 27 §0's "would break template-sniff
  contracts" wording targets DOM restructuring and shadow hides, not colour
  changes. This plan does neither.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk = Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Install the new `grepbot.user.js`. Confirm panel still renders dark on first
  boot — no flash of unstyled content, no missing glyphs (font fallback at
  `ui.js:399-401` is intact).
- Config → Tema → `claro`. Panel background goes light; text stays dark; the
  amber accent at `ui.js:403-404` remains. Queue Center window (open it via
  the `Colas` button at `ui.js:561`) also lights up.
- Config → Tema → `sistema`. With OS in dark mode, panel is dark; switch OS
  to light mode and click the dropdown again — panel goes light (no live
  listener, so the toggle is re-applied on each user action, which matches
  the rest of the panel).
- Log tab shows zero new entries (theme emits no log).
- `python3 build.py` passes; install via paste into Tampermonkey.
- Preflight (Stats → Comprobar sistema) reports no new warn rows.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-theme font choice.** Theme only swaps colour tokens. Font stack is
  declared at `ui.js:399-401` and stays.
- **Per-theme icon set.** All icons are unicode glyphs (`_`, `[]`, `↑`,
  `×`, …) declared inline; no asset swap.
- **Auto-switch on time-of-day.** Some games have a day/night theme. Out of
  scope — plan 27 §6 lists only a static toggle.
- **Game-window theming.** The plan only touches the GrepBot panel and Queue
  Center. The Grepolis game UI itself is not restyled (ToS-adjacent and out
  of scope per CLAUDE.md "no Shadow-DOM UI hiding").
- **Theme picker UI** beyond the Config dropdown. No draggable swatch palette
  (that belongs to 6.2 Draggable widget system, planned separately).
