## 6.2-draggable-widgets.md

# 6.2 — Draggable widget system

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `qol.js` (introduces `gbWidget` API). The draggable handlers
currently live inline in `src/queue-center.js:372-388` — they get factored into
the new helper. `queue-center.js` becomes a consumer.
**Depends on:** none (6.11 and 6.14 consume this contract once it lands)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

The repo ships exactly **one** draggable GrepBot surface, and its drag logic is
not factored out:

- `src/queue-center.js:373-388` — the Queue Center window. The `mousedown` on
  `<header>` captures `{dx, dy}` into module-local `gbQueueCenterDrag`
  (`queue-center.js:15`); `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners are added directly to
  `document` and then **manually re-registered** into `gbListenerBag`
  (`queue-center.js:388`) for the dispose path. The position is set inline with
  a viewport clamp; the listeners teardown cleanly but the **position is
  never persisted** — every `openQueueCenter()` call lands at `display:flex` in
  whatever the SPA last gave it (the inline CSS).
- `src/ui.js:1560-1580` — the main panel drag (header `<header>` of
  `#grepbot-panel`). Identical pattern, but uses `gbListen(handle, …)` +
  `gbListen(document, …)`, which routes through `gbListen`
  (`core.js:60-64`) into `gbListenerBag` automatically. Calls
  `savePanelGeom()` (`ui.js:1578`) which writes `state.panelGeom` to
  `STORE.PANEL_GEOM` (`core.js:281`, `header.js:63`). The persistence pattern
  is correct; the same pattern is what 6.2 generalises.
- `src/core.js:114-143` (`grepbotDispose`) removes the `#grepbot-queue-center`
  element at line 137; the main panel is removed at 135. Every widget we add
  has to register its own element id (or selector) for this loop.
- `src/queue-center.js:362` uses `document.body.appendChild(w)` for the
  singleton window; multiple widget instances need a different lifecycle (one
  per widget kind, plus persisted per-instance position).

Already shipped / not in scope: panel drag (above), panel resize
(`ui.js:1582-1630`), Queue Center drag (above), `gbListenerBag` dispose
contract (`core.js:124-127`).

## 2. Gap

The drag-handler code is duplicated across `queue-center.js` and `ui.js`, has
no shared contract (mount → enable drag → persist position → teardown), and
does not survive a reload for the Queue Center. Every new widget (6.11, 6.14,
plus anything 6.x adds later) would re-invent the listeners, clamp math, and
persistence. The plan extracts the API once and lets 6.11/6.14 consume it.

## 3. Design

A new module-local helper `gbWidget(opts)` in `qol.js`, modelled on the proven
Queue Center pattern. Three entry points:

```
gbWidget.register({ id, title, defaultPos, render(host), tickMs? })
  → returns { open(), close(), isOpen(), el, dispose() }
gbWidget.unregister(id)       // removes element + drag state + listeners
gbWidget.list()               // returns registered ids (Config UI helper)
```

Data flow:

1. `register` allocates a host `<div>` with the standard `.gb-widget` chrome
   (header + close + content slot), appends to `document.body`. Position
   pulled from `state.widgetGeom[id]` (new key, see §5); falls back to
   `defaultPos = { left: '8px', top: '60px' }`.
2. `render(host)` is called once on mount and again whenever
   `gbWidget.refresh(id)` fires. The widget owns its own DOM inside `host`;
   the helper only owns the chrome.
3. `mousedown` on the header (excluding `button, select`) captures the
   viewport-relative delta. `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners are added to
   `document` **and** registered via `gbListen` (so they land in
   `gbListenerBag` automatically — same mechanism the main panel uses,
   `ui.js:1568-1579`). On `mouseup` if the position changed, write
   `{left, top}` to `state.widgetGeom[id]` and `save(STORE.WIDGET_GEOM, …)`.
4. `dispose()` removes the element, **and** calls `gbListenClear`-equivalent
   cleanup by deleting the widget's stored listener ids. Falls back to manual
   `gbListenerBag` removal if the helper is unmounted mid-tick. Idempotent.
5. `grepbotDispose` (`core.js:114-143`) is extended with one line: iterate
   `state.widgetGeom` keys, look up live widget handle, call `dispose()`.
   This is the same shape as the existing line 137 that removes
   `#grepbot-queue-center`.

The clamp math is taken verbatim from `queue-center.js:381-382`:

```
left = max(0, min(innerWidth - el.offsetWidth, clientX - dx))
top  = max(0, min(innerHeight - el.offsetHeight, clientY - dy))
```

Optional `tickMs` fires `render(host)` on a `gbInterval` — see 6.11 (1s
countdown refresh) and 6.14 (1s ETA countdown). The interval is owned by the
widget, registered through `gbInterval` (`core.js:23-29`), and torn down on
`dispose()`. **No new scheduler** — these go through the existing
`gbInterval` wrapper which already entries into `gbTimerBag`.

The Queue Center becomes a thin wrapper:

```
gbWidget.register({
  id: 'queue-center',
  title: 'Colas GrepBot',
  defaultPos: { left: '50%', top: '40%' },
  render: (host) => renderQueueCenterInto(host),
});
```

Its current `openQueueCenter(tab, townId)` shim still exists but routes the
mount through `gbWidget`. The header `mousedown` handlers at
`queue-center.js:373-388` are deleted.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/header.js`** — add `STORE.WIDGET_GEOM: 'grepbot:widget-geom'` and
   add it to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (widget position is per-world, see §5).
2. **`src/core.js:220-280` state block** — add `widgetGeom: load(STORE.WIDGET_GEOM, {}) || {}`.
3. **`src/qol.js`** — append a `gbWidget` block (≤120 lines) implementing
   `register/unregister/list/refresh/dispose`, the chrome template string,
   the drag handlers, and the persistence write. Keep it module-local IIFE
   style — no top-level `function` declarations (build.py gate, see
   `CLAUDE.md`).
4. **`src/queue-center.js:362-389`** — delete the inline drag block, the
   `gbQueueCenterDrag` module-local (`queue-center.js:15`), and the
   `gbListenerBag.push` at line 388. Replace the `openQueueCenter` mount at
   line 361-390 with a `gbWidget.register({ id: 'queue-center', … })` call
   whose `render(host)` re-implements `renderQueueCenter` against the new
   `host` (a single-line change: `w` → `host.querySelector('.gb-widget-body')`).
5. **`src/core.js:114-143`** — extend `grepbotDispose` to iterate registered
   widget handles (helper exposes `__gbWidgetInstances`) and call each
   `dispose()`. Keep the existing line 137 `#grepbot-queue-center` removal
   for one release as a belt-and-braces (the Queue Center still owns the id
   until step 4 lands).
6. **`src/ui.js`** — add a Config row `Widgets` with a list of registered
   widget ids + their visibility toggle. Reads `gbWidget.list()` for ids;
   the toggle writes `state.widgetGeom[id].hidden = !on`. Reuse the existing
   `gbListen` + `gbListenerBag` pattern for the row's event handlers.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.widgetGeom = { [id]: { left: '120px', top: '80px', hidden: false } }`
  — keyed by widget id (`queue-center`, `production-overlay`, `attack-eta`,
  etc.). Persisted via `STORE.WIDGET_GEOM` (`grepbot:widget-geom`).
- **World-scoped**: yes. A player who plays two worlds typically wants the
  same widget layout on each, but a multi-account setup where the windows
  are sized to one screen resolution does not. World-scoping matches the
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` convention (`header.js:193-215`). Add to the Set.
- `configVer`: bump `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` in `header.js:191` (currently 10)
  to 11 — new storage key.
- **Prune TTL**: not applicable. Widget geometry is small, never times out.

## 6. Config surface

- `Widget posiciones: recordar al cerrar` — default ON. When OFF, `mouseup`
  does not call `save(STORE.WIDGET_GEOM, …)`. Existing `state.panelGeom`
  already has this affordance (`ui.js:1578`); copy it verbatim into the new
  code path.
- Per-widget visibility toggle under the Config → *Widgets* subsection
  (added by work item 6). Default for each new widget = OFF until the
  shipping widget itself flips its default; see 6.11/6.14 for those.
- **No HIGH-RISK toggles** (read-only positioning). No `gbCaptchaPause`
  feature key needed.

## 7. Post surface & safety

This feature is read-only (no posts). The widget API does not call
`bridgePost`, `gameAjaxPost`, or `gbDomClick`. The Config row in work item
6 is a plain toggle — no post. Skip the rest of the checklist.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Listener leak on dispose.** If `dispose()` is called while a `mousedown`
  is mid-flight (race), the `mouseup` will set position on a detached
  element. Mitigation: track an `alive` flag per widget; `mouseup` early-
  returns if `!alive`. The same pattern lives at `queue-center.js:374-388`
  today (no flag, but the inline closure frees `gbQueueCenterDrag` on
  `mouseup`, which still no-ops if the element is gone — relies on
  `document.body.contains(w)` at `queue-center.js:330`).
- **Two widgets overlapping.** The default positions are deterministic
  (top-left corner with a 30px cascade) so two widgets never open at the
  same pixel. If the user manually drags them on top of each other, the
  click target is whichever was appended last (`document.body.appendChild`
  z-order). Out of scope — this is intentional freedom.
- **SPA navigation detaches the widget.** `core.js:124-127` clears
  `gbListenerBag` on dispose, but SPA `pushState` (handler at
  `boot.js:9-34`) calls `ensurePanelMounted` to re-append the main panel.
  Extend `ensurePanelMounted` (`boot.js:1-8`) to re-append any registered
  widget whose host is missing (`!document.body.contains(host)`).
- **Unreadable viewport during boot.** `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` is 0 if
  the script fires before layout; the clamp math then pins the widget to
  the corner. Acceptable.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk). One in-game session on `es146`:

- Open Queue Center, drag to (300, 200), close. Reopen — lands at
  `(300, 200)` (this is **new** behaviour; before this plan it reset).
  Log shows `widget: geom saved queue-center {left: 300px, top: 200px}`.
- Toggle `Widget posiciones: recordar al cerrar` OFF, drag, close, reopen.
  Position resets to default. Toggle back ON, repeat; position persists.
- Open and close three widgets, then `Tab visibility` switch (game →
  Reports → World). No console errors. Widgets remain visible at saved
  positions.
- `grepbotDispose` smoke: in console run `unsafeWindow.__grepbotInstance
  .__grepbotDispose()` then `unsafeWindow.location.reload()`. Log shows
  `grepbot: dispose` and the next boot starts clean (no orphan listeners,
  no `#grepbot-widget-*` nodes left over).
- **Preflight**: add a `widget system` row to `preflightRun`
  (`src/stats.js:12-191`) that checks `typeof gbWidget === 'function'` and
  that `STORE.WIDGET_GEOM` round-trips through `load/save`. Pass = green.

## 10. Out of scope

- 6.11 (production overlay) — consumes this contract, ships in its own
  plan.
- 6.14 (attack landing countdown) — same.
- Touch support: the drag handler uses `mousedown/move/up`. Mobile is
  untouched. CLAUDE.md says "tab visibility … mobile exits". Adding
  `touchstart/touchmove/touchend` would inflate the helper for one user
  class; defer to a follow-up if requested.
- Widget resizing. Main panel has resize (`ui.js:1582-1630`); widgets do
  not. Not in the catalogue row. Defer.
- Cross-widget keyboard focus / tab order. Game canvas eats most focus
  anyway.

## 6.3-keyboard-shortcuts.md

# 6.3 — Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl-Shift-…)

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/qol.js` (action table + handler) + `src/core.js`
(`state.keybindings` initializer) + `src/ui.js` (Config surface).
**Depends on:** none.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0 (`header.js:4`).

---

## 1. What exists today

- **No global keydown handler exists for hotkeys.** The only `keydown`
  listener in `src/` is the activity-pause bump in
  `qolBindActivityPause` (`qol.js:1-11`), bound from `boot.js:116`. It calls
  `bumpUserActivity()` (`core.js:597-600`) and is unrelated to command
  dispatch — different intent, same event.
- **No action-by-keystroke table exists.** `Grep -n 'shortcut\|hotkey\|ctrlKey\|metaKey' src/`
  returns only the `qol.js:5` event name and the modifier-check inside
  `native-ui.js:781,787` for the queue-tile `+5` button. There is no
  registry, no menu, no per-action toggle.
- **Dispose contract is enforced through `gbListen`.** Every `gbListen(...)`
  call pushes into `gbListenerBag` (`core.js:17,56-65`), and the global
  dispose at `core.js:114-143` walks that bag and calls
  `removeEventListener` for every entry (`core.js:124-127`). Any listener
  this plan adds **must** go through `gbListen` — a bare `document.addEventListener`
  would survive `__grepbotDispose()` and leak across Tampermonkey script
  reinstalls.
- **Tab-focus tampering is banned by plan 27 §0 ("Tab-focus simulation:
  Game client owns focus; tampering invites anti-cheat").** Passively
  *reading* `document.activeElement` to decide whether the user is typing
  in a game input is allowed — that is the standard idiom for hotkey
  libraries and does not dispatch, focus, or blur any element.
- **GM menus use `gbMenu` (`core.js:105-112`), which itself pushes the
  returned id into `gbMenuCmds` and is cleaned up by `gbUnregisterMenus`
  on dispose (`core.js:99-104`).** Any shortcut that mirrors a GrepBot
  userscript menu entry (e.g. "GrepBot: diag", `ui.js:2008`) reuses the
  existing handler — no separate menu is needed.

## 2. Gap

There is no way for a power user to trigger GrepBot's panel actions
(open queue center, run preflight, copy findings) from the keyboard. The
panel itself is mouse-only; tabbing through controls works, but a
keyboard-first workflow needs Ctrl-Shift-… shortcuts. Plan 27 §6
explicitly asks for this and warns about not stealing game-input focus.

## 3. Design

A single document-level `keydown` listener, registered via `gbListen`
(`core.js:56-65`), matches a `(modifierFlags, key)` pair against a
user-editable table. Before matching, it bails when `document.activeElement`
is anything the user might be typing into (game inputs, panel inputs,
any `contenteditable` subtree). This is the exact filter plan 27 §6
demands — passively checking focus, not pushing any focus or focus
event.

```
filters, in order:
  1. e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey must be set
     (a bare key without a modifier would steal chat / search / unit-pick)
  2. document.activeElement is INPUT | TEXTAREA | SELECT → bail
  3. document.activeElement has isContentEditable === true → bail
  4. event.target.closest('[contenteditable=true]') → bail
     (the focused element may not be the contenteditable root;
      e.g. a chat input may have contenteditable on a parent <div>)
  5. Otherwise: build the key fingerprint ('Ctrl+Shift+P'), look up
     state.keybindings[fingerprint], call the registered action.
```

The keyset is locked to Ctrl / Cmd + Shift + a single printable key.
Alt is rejected up-front so locale-specific AltGr on European layouts
(`@connect`/`@grant`/`@match` rows in `header.js:1-20` use no non-ASCII
characters, but the user can still type AltGr) does not spuriously fire
a shortcut. This also matches every GrepBot userscript-menu item that a
power user might want to invoke from the keyboard.

Action table (default bindings; user can rebind in Config):

| Fingerprint        | Action                                   | Source                       |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `Ctrl+Shift+,`     | `showTab('config')`                      | `ui.js` `showTab`            |
| `Ctrl+Shift+P`     | `preflightRunAndRender()` → `showTab('stats')` | `ui.js:217` already wires the button |
| `Ctrl+Shift+F`     | Copy findings to clipboard               | `ui.js:2002` menu handler    |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Q`     | `openQueueCenter()`                      | `ui.js:2007` menu handler    |
| `Ctrl+Shift+R`     | `scrapeInboxDom()` (rescan inbox)        | `ui.js:2010` menu handler    |
| `Ctrl+Shift+L`     | Toggle pause-on-activity (`state.pauseOnActivity`) | `core.js:305,597-600`  |
| `Ctrl+Shift+D`     | `diagRun()`                              | `ui.js:2008` menu handler    |

`Ctrl+Shift+L` flips `state.pauseOnActivity` directly (not a re-route
through the Config checkbox): the listener writes the state and the
display checkbox in `bindConfig()` (`ui.js:1307,1377`) re-reads the new
value next time the user opens Config — the listener does **not** call
the synthetic click handler.

The fingerprint resolver is a single function in `qol.js`:

```
fingerprint(e):
  parts = [];
  if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) parts.push('Ctrl');
  if (e.shiftKey) parts.push('Shift');
  parts.push(normalizeKey(e.key));
  return parts.join('+');
normalizeKey(k):
  // 'P' / 'p' both normalize to 'P'; 'ArrowUp' to 'Up';
  // ' ' to 'Space'; everything else lower-cased.
```

(`e.key` is already case-sensitive — pressing Shift+P produces 'P',
without Shift 'p'.)

- No prune TTL — the keymap is a single short object.

## 6. Config surface

- Label: `Atajos de teclado` (keyboard shortcuts). One row per action
  in the default table (seven rows), each a `<select>` listing
  `Ctrl+Shift+<A..Z>` plus a `— desactivado —` (— disabled) entry.
- Position: just below `Tema del panel` (theme from 6.1, around
  `ui.js:800`). Rationale: both are personal preferences, neither is
  HIGH-RISK; they belong together.
- Default: the table in §3 above. Each default matches a TM menu
  already registered in `ui.js:2002-2025`, so the shortcut is a pure
  keyboard alias for an existing menu.
- No HIGH-RISK toggle involved; risk stays Low.

## 7. Post surface & safety

Read-mostly / keyboard-only feature: **no post surface** for the
shortcuts themselves. The actions they invoke (preflight, copy
findings, diag) are read-only. `openQueueCenter()` opens a local DOM
window — no `bridgePost`, no `gbXhr`. `scrapeInboxDom()` reads DOM,
no post. The single write is `Ctrl+Shift+L` flipping
`state.pauseOnActivity`, which is a `state.*` mutation persisted via
`save(STORE.PAUSE_ON_ACTIVITY, ...)` (`ui.js:1377`); no bridge.

- No `gbAjaxWatch` registration needed.
- No `gbCaptchaPause` feature key needed (the feature never posts).
- No `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry needed (no async work; keydown is
  synchronous).
- No dry-run gate needed (no post).
- **No new `gbInterval`.** The listener is event-driven; there is
  nothing to schedule.
- **No new top-level `function` declarations that risk the
  `build.py` duplicate gate** (`build.py:365-378`). Every helper in
  §4.1, §4.2, §4.7 is at module-indent depth (matches the existing
  `qol.js` helpers at `qol.js:1-12`).

## 8. Failure modes

- **The user is typing in a chat input / textarea.** Filter step 2/3/4
  fires — no shortcut runs, the keystroke reaches the game input. The
  filter reads `document.activeElement` only; nothing is focused,
  blurred, or dispatched.
- **A game client that lives inside its own `<iframe>` (rare on
  Grepolis, but theoretically possible for some promo frames).**
  `document.activeElement` will be the outer `<body>` because the
  iframe captures focus. The filter still passes — that is the safe
  direction (a missed shortcut is recoverable; a stolen chat
  keystroke is not).
- **Two shortcuts assigned to the same fingerprint by mistake.** The
  Config save (`state.keybindings[fingerprint] = actionKey`) is a
  straight property assignment — last write wins. Add an
  `Object.values(state.keybindings).filter(v => v === actionKey).length`
  guard at save time that warns (`flash('atajo ya usado por otra
  accion')`) and refuses the save if a collision exists, so the user
  cannot accidentally orphan another action.
- **`capture: true` interferes with a game handler that expects
  keydown to fire on bubble.** Plan 27 §0 forbids *changing* focus
  semantics, but reading events at capture phase does not affect
  bubble — the game still sees the event on its way up, after our
  filter has already bailed. The only behaviour change is that we
  call `preventDefault()` *before* the game's own keydown runs. Since
  our actions never run inside an input (the filter guarantees it),
  there is no input default to prevent; the worst case is a `Space`
  shortcut swallowing a scroll, which is the intended shortcut
  behaviour.
- **`e.key` returns a localized label (`'Espacio'` on Spanish
  keyboards for Space).** `normalizeKey()` falls back to
  `e.code` (`'Space'`) for known problematic keys. See
  `core.js:1063-1078` `gameNow()` for the prior-art
  "first-non-null read" pattern.
- **Listeners leak across reinstalls.** The bare `document.addEventListener`
  failure mode is the dominant one. Plan §4.2 uses `gbListen`; the
  bag walk at `core.js:124-127` removes it on dispose. Verify after
  build: `grep -c '__grepbotDispose' core.js` returns 1, and
  `core.js:124-127` is unchanged.
- **Build-order hazard.** `state.keybindings` is loaded at module init
  time from `load(STORE.KEYBINDINGS, qolKeymapDefault())`. The
  default is a function defined in `qol.js`, which loads **after**
  `core.js` in `build.py` `MODULES` (`build.py:31-72`). Two safe
  options: (a) inline the default table as a literal object in
  `core.js` and have `qol.js` import it via a shared module-scope
  `var` set in `header.js`; (b) move the `keybindings` initializer
  to a `gbTimeout(...)` in `boot.js` that runs after all modules
  load. Option (b) is the smaller diff and mirrors how `state.health`
  is filled lazily (`core.js:389`).

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk = Preflight + one in-game session,
no failure).

- Install the new `grepbot.user.js`. Press `Ctrl+Shift+,` while the
  game tab has focus: panel opens to Config. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P`:
  preflight runs and the Stats tab opens. Press `Ctrl+Shift+F`:
  findings dump appears in the OS clipboard; Log tab records
  `findings copied`.
- **Game-input filter test.** Click into the game's chat textarea
  (or any visible `<input>` / `<textarea>` in the Grepolis UI) and
  press `Ctrl+Shift+Q`. Nothing happens — the listener bailed at
  filter step 2. Repeat with `Ctrl+Shift+L` while the game chat has
  focus: nothing flips. Click outside the input and press the same
  key: the action fires.
- **Config rebind test.** Config → Atajos → change
  `Ctrl+Shift+P` to `Ctrl+Shift+X`. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P`: nothing.
  Press `Ctrl+Shift+X`: preflight opens. Restore via "Restablecer".
- **Collision warning test.** Set both `Ctrl+Shift+P` and
  `Ctrl+Shift+F` to the same key. The second save produces a flash
  and the second assignment is **not** persisted.
- **Dispose test.** Trigger an in-game SPA navigation (open Reports,
  then World) — `boot.js:9-34` `hookSpaNav` wraps `pushState`. The
  panel remains functional and the shortcut still works.
- **Export/Import round trip.** Config → Export, paste to a fresh
  install, Config → Import. The rebound keymap round-trips.
- Log tab shows zero new entries for the shortcut layer itself
  (filter pass is silent; only the action it invokes logs).
- `python3 build.py` passes (no new top-level declarations collide);
  install via paste into Tampermonkey.
- Preflight (Stats → Comprobar sistema) reports no new warn rows.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-town hotkeys.** The action table is global; town-specific
  shortcuts (e.g. `Ctrl+Shift+1` jumps to town 1) require a town
  picker UI that already exists in Queue Center (`queue-center.js:342`)
  and can be wired later.
- **Mouse-button / chord shortcuts** (e.g. double-Ctrl). Event
  filtering is a keydown listener; mouse chords need a separate
  click handler and a state machine. Plan 27 §6 specifies
  Ctrl-Shift-…, no chords.
- **Tab-focus SIMULATION** — explicitly banned by plan 27 §0.
  This plan only **reads** `document.activeElement`; it never calls
  `focus()`, `blur()`, `tabIndex`, or dispatches focus events.
- **Game-window-shortcut override** (e.g. `G` to center the selected
  town, which Grepolis itself uses). Plan 27 §0 bans tampering with
  game focus. This plan ignores keydown when game inputs have focus;
  it does not override the game's own single-letter shortcuts.
- **Migrating shortcuts to the panel as on-screen chips.** The 6.2
  Draggable widget system owns the visual surface; this plan owns
  only the keyboard path.

## 6.4-desktop-notifications.md

# 6.4 — Desktop notifications + sound (per event)

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/alerts.js` (per-event Notification + Audio) +
`src/core.js` (state initializer) + `src/ui.js` (Config surface).
**Depends on:** none — `alerts.js` already has the per-event fan-out
(`alertWebhook` at `alerts.js:28-88`); this plan adds a sibling fan-out
to the local OS notification surface.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0 (`header.js:4`).

---

## 1. What exists today

- `src/alerts.js` is **89 lines total** (`alerts.js:1-89`). All five
  functions in it (`alertIsTelegram`, `alertWebhookUrlOk`,
  `alertTelegramChatId`, `alertWebhookKey`, `alertWebhook`) deal
  exclusively with the outbound Discord/Telegram webhook pipeline.
  There is **no `Notification` API call and no `Audio` usage anywhere in
  `src/`** — verified with
  `grep -n 'Notification\|new Audio\|webkitAudio\|playSound' src/`,
  zero hits.
- `alertWebhook(event, payload)` (`alerts.js:28-88`) is the single
  fan-out point. It is invoked from four call sites:
  `core.js:1379` (`captcha`), `intel.js:202` (`attack`, watchlist),
  `intel.js:242` (`pattern`), `culture.js:198` (`culture`), and
  `dodge.js:191` (`attack` with `cs: !!mov.hasCs`). Plan 27 §9
  already lists "Discord / Telegram webhooks" as shipped in
  `alerts.js` (8.8); this plan extends the same file with a second
  fan-out path, not a third.
- The per-event toggle surface already exists for webhooks:
  `state.webhookEvents` default `{ captcha:true, attack:true, warehouse:false, culture:false }`
  (`core.js:313`), rendered by `ui.js:1355-1359` and saved by
  `saveWebhookEvents()` at `ui.js:1477-1490`. The plan piggybacks on
  this UI — adding `notify:*` toggles next to `wh-*` keeps the user
  model consistent.
- Module-scope `alertPending` and `alertLastSent` are declared in
  `research.js:545-546` and read/written from `alerts.js:43-44,66,75,76,80,85`.
  The dedup is keyed on `alertWebhookKey(event, payload)` (5min TTL).
  The new desktop-notification path **must share that key** so a
  captcha that already fired a notification 2min ago does not fire
  again — duplicating the dedup table would let the two paths race.
- **`@grant` list (`header.js:9-15`)** declares
  `GM_xmlhttpRequest`, `GM_setValue`, `GM_getValue`, `GM_addStyle`,
  `GM_registerMenuCommand`, `GM_unregisterMenuCommand`. The browser's
  built-in `Notification` and `Audio` constructors do **not** need a
  `@grant` — they run in the page context, which a Tampermonkey
  userscript can reach via `unsafeWindow` (the `GB_ROOT` pattern at
  `core.js:3,80,81`). No header change is needed for the Notification
  API itself.
- The `GM_notification` shortcut is available (`TM grants list`),
  but it (a) only renders a chrome-side toast with no per-event
  customisation, (b) bypasses the user's own notification settings,
  and (c) does not play sound. The browser `Notification` constructor
  is the right primitive here.

## 2. Gap

The webhook pipeline only fires when `state.webhookUrl` is set
(`alerts.js:29-30`). When the player is sitting at the game tab and
no webhook is configured, the only signal for captcha / incoming
attack / culture completion is the footer status line
(`updateStatus()` at `core.js:562`) and the panel Log tab. Players
who want to keep GrepBot running in a background tab (a common
"AFK nocturno" preset at `qol.js:290-314`) get nothing for the most
urgent events — captcha and incoming attack.

The plan adds a local notification + chime on the same per-event
fan-out, gated on a default-OFF master toggle so the user has to
opt in (Notification.permission can only be requested inside a
user gesture, and Chrome silently drops auto-prompts).

## 3. Design

Two new functions in `alerts.js`, both called from inside
`alertWebhook` after the existing `state.webhookEvents[event]` check:

```
function alertDesktop(event, payload, key):
  if (!state.notifyEnabled) return;
  if (!state.notifyEvents || state.notifyEvents[event] === false) return;
  // Reuse the webhook dedup key — same 5min window, same suppression.
  if (alertPending[key]) return;
  if ((alertLastSent[key] || 0) + 5 * 60 * 1000 > Date.now()) return;
  const n = buildNotification(event, payload);
  try { new Notification(n.title, { body: n.body, tag: key }); }
    catch (e) { gbLogT('notify-' + event, 60000, 'notify: ' + String(e).slice(0, 60)); return; }
  alertPending[key] = Date.now();
  if (!state.notifyMuted) alertPlayChime(event);

function alertPlayChime(event):
  // Three short WAVs (~1KB each), base64-encoded inside src/.
  // We do NOT load from the network: a backgrounded tab can play
  // cached data: URIs without a permission prompt, and the user's
  // own GrepBot storage is the right scope.
  const map = { captcha: 'chime-captcha', attack: 'chime-attack',
                pattern: 'chime-pattern', culture: 'chime-culture' };
  const url = CHIME_URLS[map[event] || 'chime-default'];
  try {
    const a = new Audio(url);
    a.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, +state.notifyVolume || 0.5));
    const p = a.play();
    if (p && typeof p.catch === 'function') p.catch(() => {});
  } catch (e) { gbLogT('chime-' + event, 60000, 'chime: ' + String(e).slice(0, 60)); }
```

`alertWebhook` is updated so that the existing webhook send becomes
a sibling — `alertDesktop(event, payload, key)` is called **before**
the `gbXhr(...)` block. The dedup table is shared. If the user has
only the desktop path enabled (no webhook URL), the
`alertLastSent[key]` entry is still written by `alertDesktop` (it
sets `alertPending[key] = Date.now()`); the next call to
`alertWebhook` within 5min sees the dedup and short-circuits at
`alerts.js:43-44`. This matches today's "one event, one notification"
behaviour regardless of which channels are enabled.

Permission gate: `Notification.permission` is `'default'` on a fresh
install. The Config panel adds a "Permitir notificaciones" button
that calls `Notification.requestPermission()` from the click handler.
The button is **disabled** when permission is already `'granted'`
or `'denied'`, and shows the current state in its label. Per the
Notification API, `requestPermission()` is only honoured when called
inside a user gesture — a button click is one. **Never** call
`requestPermission()` from `boot.js` or from a `keydown` listener
that the user did not register — Chrome silently rejects it.

  OFF (the master gate is enough; per-event gating is a follow-up).
  Volume 0.5. Mute OFF.
- No HIGH-RISK toggle involved; risk stays Low. The master toggle
  **defaults OFF** because Chrome's permission auto-prompt is the
  single most intrusive UX event in any userscript and must be
  earned, not assumed.

## 7. Post surface & safety

This feature **does not introduce a bridge / `bridgePost` post
surface**. Desktop notifications are a browser-side OS surface; the
sound chimes are `data:` URIs that never leave the script's own
memory. Both are downstream of the existing `alertWebhook` call,
which already has its own dry-run + URL-validity gates.

- No `gbAjaxWatch` registration needed (no new HTTP path).
- No `gbCaptchaPause` feature key needed (no bridge post).
- No `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry needed (synchronous).
- No dry-run gate needed — there is no payload to dry-run; the
  chime is a local sound. (The existing `alertWebhook` dry-run gate
  at `alerts.js:31-34` already short-circuits the whole call.)
- **No new `gbInterval`.** Notifications are event-driven from the
  existing webhook fan-out.
- **No new top-level `function` declarations that risk the
  `build.py` duplicate gate** (`build.py:365-378`). Every helper in
  §4.2, §4.3 is at module-indent depth, matching
  `alertIsTelegram` and friends at `alerts.js:1-27`.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`Notification` API blocked by the browser** (rare on Tampermonkey;
  Firefox with strict cookie permissions, Safari with cross-site
  tracking). `new Notification(...)` throws — caught at the
  `try/catch` in `alertDesktop`, logged once per event via
  `gbLogT('notify-' + event, 60000, …)`, and the dedup table is **not**
  marked (so the next event retries). After ~3 retries the throttled
  log keeps the Log tab informative without spamming.
- **`Audio` constructor blocked** (Chrome autoplay policy). The
  first chime after install may be blocked because the gesture that
  granted Notification permission is not the same gesture that
  plays audio. `play().catch(...)` swallows the rejection silently;
  the user can press the volume slider or a "Probar sonido" button
  (added alongside the slider) to play one chime inside a fresh
  gesture. Subsequent notifications in the same tab session usually
  work because the tab has been activated.
- **`Notification.permission === 'denied'`.** The Config button is
  disabled; the master toggle stays OFF; no prompts fire. The user
  must reverse the decision in the browser's site settings.
- **`unsafeWindow.Notification` is not the same as `Notification`.**
  Tampermonkey sandboxes the script. `Notification` is the page
  constructor — reachable through `unsafeWindow` (the `GB_ROOT`
  pattern at `core.js:3,80,81`). The `new Notification(...)` call
  must come from `unsafeWindow.Notification.bind(unsafeWindow)` if
  the constructor references `this`. In practice `Notification`
  does not use `this`, so the call works as written; verify in the
  validation gate by checking the chrome tray on a forced event.
- **Volume slider at 0.** `state.notifyVolume === 0` produces an
  inaudible chime. That is fine — the visual notification still
  fires; the user can move the slider up. The mute checkbox is the
  one that suppresses the chime entirely.
- **Telegram / Discord URL conflicts.** Both webhook and desktop
  paths read `state.webhookEvents[event]`. The webhook path has its
  own URL check at `alerts.js:35-38`; the desktop path does **not**
  care about the URL — it fires even if no webhook URL is set. This
  is intentional: a player can disable webhooks but keep desktop
  notifications for low-latency awareness.
- **Multiple events within the 5min window.** `alertDesktop` shares
  the `alertPending[key]` table with `alertWebhook`, so a captcha
  fires the desktop notification and the webhook **at most once
  per 5 minutes per fingerprint**. Captchas normally come 15+ minutes
  apart; this is not a real loss.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk = Preflight + one in-game session,
no failure).

- Install the new `grepbot.user.js`. Config → Notificaciones → click
  `Permitir notificaciones`. Browser shows the prompt; accept. The
  button label flips to `Permitir notificaciones (actual: granted)`.
- Tick `Notificaciones de escritorio`. Config → Log shows
  `notify-enabled ON`.
- Tick `Notificaciones: captcha`. Trigger a captcha manually
  (visit `/captcha` or run any bridge post 3× in a row — the
  captcha ladder at `core.js:367` opens a window). A chrome tray
  notification appears with body `GrepBot [es146] captcha` and the
  chime plays.
- Config → Notificaciones → drag the volume slider to 0. Re-trigger
  the captcha: notification appears, no sound. Drag to 1: sound
  plays loud. Tick `Silenciar sonido`: re-trigger, no sound even
  at volume 1.
- **Permission denial path.** Open browser site settings, set
  Grepolis to `Block`. Refresh the tab. The Config button is
  disabled with label `(actual: denied)`. Toggling the master
  checkbox has no effect — the `new Notification(...)` call at
  `alertDesktop` throws and the catch path logs once.
- **Webhook / desktop independence.** Set `webhook-url` to a fake
  URL (the URL-validity check at `alerts.js:35-38` rejects it).
  The desktop notification still fires; no `gbXhr` is made.
  Reverse: clear the master toggle, set a real webhook URL — the
  webhook fires; no chime, no chrome notification.
- **Preset test.** Config → Aplicar plantilla → `AFK nocturno`.
  The master toggle flips ON. Visit the game and trigger an
  incoming attack via a friend — the chrome notification appears
  with the attack fingerprint.
- Log tab shows zero new error rows. No new `gbXhr` calls appear
  in the Network tab (only the existing `gbXhr` from
  `alertWebhook` when a webhook URL is set).
- `python3 build.py` passes (no new top-level declarations
  collide); install via paste into Tampermonkey.
- Preflight (Stats → Comprobar sistema) reports no new warn rows.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-world / per-event custom sound files.** The four chimes are
  fixed base64 blobs; uploading a custom `.wav` is a much larger UI
  surface and out of scope.
- **In-panel toast** (a GrepBot-internal non-OS notification). Plan
  6.1 already owns visual styling; an in-panel toast would belong
  to that plan or to the broader panel rework in §6.2 (Draggable
  widgets). Out of scope here.
- **Notification click → focus the game tab.** `Notification.onclick`
  can call `window.focus()`, but the browser's own handling already
  focuses the originating tab. Wiring a custom click handler is
  reserved for v4.x when the action target is clearer.
- **iOS Safari.** Safari on iOS still does not ship the
  `Notification` constructor to web apps without a home-screen
  install. The plan degrades silently — the dedup table logs once.
- **Telegram bot inbound** (chat → GrepBot). Plan 27 §0 explicitly
  drops this; outbound webhook is the only direction GrepBot ships.

## 6.5-quick-action-toolbar.md

# 6.5 — Quick-action toolbar (1-click collect / farm / dodge / panic)

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/ui.js` (panel + Actions menu + footer wiring). The
underlying one-shot functions already exist in their feature modules; this
plan binds buttons to them.
**Depends on:** **1.1** Panic mode (instant-pause button) — planned
separately. Toolbar exposes a Panic button that calls whatever surface 1.1
defines; this plan does **not** re-specify the panic semantics.
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0 (header.js:4).

---

## 1. What exists today

- The panel renders a **footer** (`ui.js:872-897`) with a `.gb-status-row`
  showing four spans (`gb-next-farms`, `gb-next-towns`, `gb-collect-state`,
  `gb-status`) and a **single** `<details class="gb-actions>` dropdown that
  lists `data-act="copy | export | refresh | scrape-farms | scrape-towns | diag
  | preflight | evidence | clear | reset-pos | preset-afk | preset-farming |
  | preset-war"` (`ui.js:879-895`). These are the existing 1-click
  triggers.
- The Overview tab (`qol.js:192-222`) renders a `.gb-quick` row of buttons
  (`ui.js:514-516`) and a `.gb-action` class is already styled. The same
  chrome is what the toolbar buttons will reuse.
- One-shot functions this toolbar binds to (already coded, no new payload
  paths):
  - `autoCollectResources()` (`collect.js:27-78`) — clicks each visible
    `Recoger` button, journaled under feature `collect` (line 60 calls
    `txDomWrite`). Guarded by `state.autoCollect`, `hostEnabled()`,
    `automationPaused({})`, `captchaPaused('collect')`, `circuitOpen('collect')`,
    and `currentTownWarehouseBlocks()`.
  - `scrapeAllFarms(true)` + `farmTick()` + `autoClaimFarms('manual')`
    (`ui.js:1101-1111` already wires these to the `data-act=scrape-farms`
    button). Guarded by the same farm cadence.
  - `farmSleepClaimNow('manual')` (`farms.js:1112-1115` — already wired to
    `#gb-sleep-claim`).
  - `dodgeScan('manual')` (`dodge.js:252-296`) — reads `state.autoDodge`,
    `state.autoMilitia`, `state.csAlert`. Each branch acquires its own lock:
    `gbLock('dodge')` (`dodge.js:227`), `gbLock('militia', 30000)`
    (`dodge.js:200`).
  - `abScan('manual')` (`ui.js:1056-1059` — wired to `#gb-ab-now`).
  - `ibCompleteAll(ibOrders())` (`ui.js:1044-1047` — wired to `#gb-ib-btn`,
    already guarded by `gbLocked('ib')`).
- The **Panic** surface does not yet exist in `src/`. Plan 1.1 (panic mode,
  Low/S, bucket v4.0, per plan 27 §1) is the owner. This plan will reference
  `panicActivate()` and `panicResume()` (TBD names) once 1.1 lands.
- Config gating pattern is `state.X` + `save(STORE.X, ...)` — every existing
  toggle follows it (`ui.js:1183-1530`).
- `GB_LOCK_TTL` (`core.js:145-173`) already covers every feature the toolbar
  triggers (`collect-bg`, `claim`, `farm-scrape`, `ib`, `dodge`, `militia`).
  No new lock entry needed.

## 2. Gap

Every one-shot trigger lives two clicks away (open the footer Actions
`<details>`, then click the inner button). On mobile / collapsed panel this
costs the user extra taps; on desktop it costs context. A persistent toolbar
of large buttons at the top of every tab lets the user fire the most common
actions without opening menus.

## 3. Design

A horizontal toolbar rendered just below the panel header (above
`.gb-nav`, line 562). Five buttons, each 1-click:

| Button | Handler | Lock | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Recoger ahora` | `autoCollectResources()` | `collect-bg` (taken inside) | Already gated; shows the same flash the Actions menu shows. |
| `Cobrar aldeas` | `autoClaimFarms('manual')` + `scrapeAllFarms(true)` + `farmTick()` | `claim` (taken inside) | Exact body of `ui.js:1101-1111` is factored into a new `runActionManual('scrape-farms')` helper. |
| `Dodge scan` | `dodgeScan('manual')` | `dodge` (taken inside) | Notify/auto respects `state.autoDodge`; flash is whatever `dodgeScan` logs. |
| `Cola ahora` | `abScan('manual')` | `ab` (taken inside) | Already exists at `ui.js:1056-1059`. |
| `Panico` | `panicActivate()` (from plan 1.1) | n/a (panic owns its state) | Button is **disabled** with title `Requiere plan 1.1` if `typeof panicActivate !== 'function'` — degrades safely until 1.1 ships. |

All five buttons are read-mostly; they do not introduce new post routes. They
delegate to the same functions the existing footer/Actions buttons already
delegate to, so no new `gbAjaxWatch` registration is needed.

The toolbar sits **above the tab nav**, not below it. Reasoning: it is the
most-clicked surface in the panel, and the tab nav is a row of small tabs —
burying it would defeat the purpose. CSS reuses the existing `.gb-quick` /
`.gb-action` classes (`ui.js:514-516`).

A second `.gb-quick` row is **not** rendered inside Overview (the existing
one at `qol.js:192-222` becomes redundant once the toolbar is permanent).
The Overview quick row can stay as a separate surface — duplication is
acceptable here because the toolbar is global and the Overview quick row is
contextual. The plan does not delete the Overview row in this change (see
§10).

Layout & hide-on-collapse: the panel already hides chrome when
`.collapsed` (`ui.js:440`). The toolbar inherits that rule via the
existing `#grepbot-panel.collapsed .gb-nav, ... section, footer {display:none}`
selector — the new toolbar gets added to that selector list.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/ui.js`** — in `panel.innerHTML` (after the header at `ui.js:561`
   and before `.gb-nav` at `ui.js:562`), inject a new `<div class="gb-qat"
   role="toolbar">` with five buttons, each `data-qat="collect | farms |
   dodge | queue | panic"`. The `Panico` button is added with the `disabled`
   attribute; the `bindQat()` step toggles it on/off based on
   `typeof panicActivate === 'function'`.
2. **`src/ui.js`** — add `bindQat()` near `bindConfig()` (`ui.js:1137`). It
   attaches five click handlers that delegate to the existing functions. No
   new lock, no new dry-run branch — `state.dryRun` already short-circuits
   `bridgePost` / `gameAjaxPost` and `gbDomClick` (`core.js:941-951`).
3. **`src/ui.js`** — call `bindQat()` once at boot (right after the existing
   `bindConfig()` call at `ui.js:1541`). Re-call it after `showTab('config')`
   swaps the panel so the Panic button's disabled state stays in sync if 1.1
   ever loads later (e.g. via `GM_registerMenuCommand`); for v4.0 1.1 is
   shipped in the same release, so a single boot-time call is enough.
4. **`src/ui.js`** — extend the `GM_addStyle` block (`ui.js:397-549`) with a
   `.gb-qat` rule (flex row, gap, padding) and add
   `#grepbot-panel.collapsed .gb-qat { display:none }` to the existing
   collapsed-hide list (`ui.js:440`).
5. **`src/footer.js`** — verify no conflict. The single footer line in
   `src/footer.js` is just `})();` (the IIFE close). No edits.
6. **`src/qol.js`** — the existing `qolExportConfig`/`qolImportConfig`
   (`qol.js:248-275`) does not need to round-trip toolbar state — toolbar
   preferences are read-only (`Recoger ahora` always means "do the
   one-shot"). No edit.

## 5. State & storage

- **No new `state.*` field.** The toolbar is stateless; every click
  delegates to functions whose state lives in `state.autoCollect`,
  `state.autoDodge`, `state.autoFarm`, `state.abAuto`, `state.defenseCfg`
  — all already in `core.js:220-384`.
- **No new `STORE.*` key.** Toolbar buttons do not persist anything.
- **No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.**
- **No `configVer` bump.** Toolbar adds no config surface; the existing
  `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT = 10` (`header.js:191`) stays.
- **No prune TTL.** Nothing is stored.

## 6. Config surface

- **No Config toggle.** The toolbar is always-on chrome; per-button
  availability is gated by existing toggles (`state.autoCollect` for
  collect, `state.autoFarm` for farms, `state.autoDodge || state.csAlert ||
  state.autoMilitia` for dodge scan, `state.abAuto` for cola ahora,
  `typeof panicActivate === 'function'` for panic).
- Visual affordance: disabled buttons get the existing
   `.gb-action:disabled` style (`ui.js:515-516`) — already used by the
   Build tab's instant-complete button (`ui.js:488-489`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

The toolbar introduces **no new post surface**. Every click delegates to an
existing function whose `bridgePost` / `gameAjaxPost` / `gbDomClick` call is
already inside `state.dryRun`'s coverage (`core.js:941-951`,
`tx.js:535`/`tx.js:646-647`).

- **No `gbAjaxWatch` registration.** Sniffers already register via the
  underlying scans.
- **No new `gbCaptchaPause` feature key.** Each button delegates to a
  feature that already owns its captcha key (`collect`, `claim`, `dodge`,
  `ab`).
- **No new `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry.** Locks are taken inside the
  delegated functions; the toolbar is a synchronous caller and returns
  before any async work settles. The five locks used (`collect-bg`,
  `claim`, `dodge`, `ab`, `ib`) are already in `core.js:145-173`.
- **Dry-run gate.** Already in effect through every delegated path. The
  toolbar buttons themselves never bypass `state.dryRun` — they cannot
  (`bridgePost` and `gameAjaxPost` short-circuit at the top of their
  bodies, plan 26 §0).

## 8. Failure modes

- **`panicActivate` is undefined** (1.1 not shipped yet). The Panic button
  is rendered `disabled` with `title="Requiere plan 1.1 (panic mode)"` —
  no crash, no flash, no log. Once 1.1 lands the button enables on next
  panel re-render (handled in work item 3).
- **User double-clicks a toolbar button.** Each handler runs immediately
  and is re-entrancy-safe: `autoCollectResources` guards with
  `gbLocked('collect-bg')` (`collect.js:108`), `scrapeAllFarms` guards with
  `gbLocked('farm-scrape')` (per `GB_LOCK_TTL` at `core.js:147`), `dodgeScan`
  guards via `gbLocked('dodge')` (`dodge.js:210`), `abScan` via
  `gbLocked('ab')` (`core.js:150`). The second click either no-ops or, in
  the rare case where the first call is still synchronous, simply enqueues
  behind the existing in-flight run.
- **Toolbar is on screen during `panel.classList.add('collapsed')`.** The
  new `.gb-qat` rule is added to the existing collapsed-hide list at
  `ui.js:440` so it disappears with the rest of the chrome. No
  double-rendering on minimize/restore.
- **A button calls into a feature whose state is paused** (captcha, budget,
  server cooldown). The underlying scan logs its skip reason
  (`captcha-pause`, `budget`, `skip:dryrun`) and the toolbar button does
  not change behaviour. The user sees the same `flash()` they'd see from
  the Actions menu.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk = Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Install. Toolbar appears above the tab nav. Each of the five buttons
  shows with the enabled/disabled state matching the underlying toggle
  (Panic disabled until 1.1 ships; the other four enabled since each
  default toggle is OFF but the button just invokes the function which
  exits early).
- Click `Recoger ahora` once. If `state.autoCollect` is ON and the page
  has a Recoger button, it clicks (flash `auto-collect xN` matches the
  Actions-menu behaviour). If OFF, the call short-circuits at
  `collect.js:28` and no post is made. Log shows the same line either way.
- Click `Cobrar aldeas` once. Log: `manual: Farms now pressed` followed
  by `manual farm claim` lines per village (same as the Actions menu).
- Click `Dodge scan` once with no incoming. Log: nothing (the scan finds
  no hostile movements and exits).
- Click `Panico`. With 1.1 not yet shipped: button is disabled, no
  effect. With 1.1 shipped: orchestrator.skip becomes true; footer shows
  the panic indicator from 1.1's spec.
- Dry-run ON: every button still works (each delegated function respects
  `state.dryRun`); the log shows `DRY-RUN ...: ...` for any path that
  would otherwise post.
- `python3 build.py` passes; install via paste into Tampermonkey.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Removing the existing Actions `<details>` menu.** Stays as-is. The
  toolbar covers the four most-clicked actions; the menu keeps the long
  tail (export, copy, diag, presets, evidence, clear, reset).
- **Removing the Overview `.gb-quick` row.** Stays. The two coexist
  intentionally: the toolbar is global and persists across tabs, the
  Overview row is contextual (lets a first-time user fire the same
  actions from the Resumen tab without scrolling up).
- **Adding a "Sleep claim" button to the toolbar.** Sleep claim already has
  its own prominent button at `#gb-sleep-claim` (`ui.js:567`). Adding a
  sixth toolbar button would crowd the row.
- **Adding a draggable toolbar** (plan 6.2 owns dragging). The toolbar
  lives in the panel header strip; not detachable in v4.0.
- **Re-specifying the panic semantics.** Owned by plan 1.1. This plan
  references `panicActivate()` as a black box.

## 6.6-city-quick-switch.md

# 6.6 — City quick-switch (dropdown + hotkey)

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/ui.js` (the panel header) + a tiny new helper
function in `src/ui.js` (or `src/build-tab.js`, where town resolution
already lives). **The hotkey infrastructure is owned by plan 6.3 Keyboard
shortcuts; this plan binds one shortcut and references 6.3 for the rest.**
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0 (header.js:4).

---

## 1. What exists today

- The town list comes from `gameUw().ITowns.towns` — used by `dodge.js:59`,
  `bandit.js:174`, `recruit.js:297`, `cave.js:30,98`, `build-auto.js:11`,
  `core.js:710,1047`, `qol.js:48,89,101,154,161`, `orchestrate.js:60`,
  `wonder.js:143`, `favor.js:112`, `spy.js:362`, `quests.js:320`,
  `military.js:20`, `build-tab.js:147,204`. Every consumer reads via
  `Object.keys(uw.ITowns.towns)` — there is **no** `getActiveTown()` or
  `switchToTown()` in `src/`.
- The currently-selected town is read by `Game.townId`:
  - `bandit.js:174,271,196`: `uw.Game.townId` (used as the default
    `town_id` payload field for bandit attacks).
  - `build-auto.js:373`: `uw.Game.townId` (default town for the auto-build
    loop).
  - `spy.js:362`: `uw.Game.townId` (fallback when no explicit town is
    given).
  - `queue-center.js:336`: `uw.Game.townId` (the Queue Center's default
    town selector).
  - `collect.js:39`: `gameUw().Game && gameUw().Game.townId` (the
    `currentTownId` captured for the `txDomWrite` `k=` key in the
    auto-collect path).
- There is **no `setTown()` / `switchTown()` / `jumpToTown()` API** in the
  Grepolis client. The only confirmed city-switching surface is the
  in-game **dropdown** the framework renders (its handler updates
  `Game.townId` and re-renders the town view). Cross-world town-id routing
  uses a URL fragment the game sets when a town is clicked from a foreign
  context (e.g. intel pop-ups).
- The Config tab has `state.townGroups = {}` (`core.js:311`) but it is
  loaded and **never read or written** outside of `qolExportConfig`
  (`qol.js:252`) and `qolImportConfig` (`qol.js:256`). It is a dead flag
  carried over from earlier work — plan 26 §B6 lists it explicitly.
- The Queue Center (`queue-center.js:336`) already has a town dropdown
  (`ui.js:527`) and the panel has the `state.townGroups` schema. There is
  no panel-level town switcher.
- The build-tab footer (`build-tab.js:147,204`) reads
  `uw.ITowns.towns` but does not expose a UI switcher.
- The Grepolis client itself does **not** expose a stable public API for
  switching town from script. Confirmed via `grep -rn 'jumpToTown\|switchTown\|setActiveTown\|focusTown\|selectTown\|setTown' src/` — zero hits.

## 2. Gap

There is no first-class way to jump to another of your own towns from
inside the GrepBot panel. Users who want to drill into a different town's
queue center must use the in-game dropdown, which closes the panel's
context. The plan delivers a small dropdown + hotkey that lives in the
panel header and lets the user pick a town to make "active"; subsequent
GrepBot scans (auto-collect's `txDomWrite` `k=`, queue-center default,
bandit fallback) continue to use the game's `Game.townId` once the
selection lands.

## 3. Design

**Dropdown surface:** a `<select data-qs="town">` rendered inside the
existing `panel` header, next to the `gb-pill` status pills at
`ui.js:561`. The select lists every id in `Object.keys(uw.ITowns.towns)`,
with `townId + '  (' + name + ')'` as the option label. The id is pinned
explicitly as `<option value="...">` — Spanish `value` would break
`town_id` payloads (CLAUDE.md "UI language: pin an explicit value"). The
selected option tracks `Game.townId` so the dropdown stays in sync with
the in-game selection.

**Hotkey:** `g` opens the dropdown's option list (focuses the
`<select>`). This plan **does not** build the shortcut infrastructure;
plan 6.3 owns `gbShortcut(name, fn)` and the registration list. 6.6 binds
one shortcut via that helper. If 6.3 has not yet shipped, the dropdown
still works — the hotkey is a progressive enhancement.

**Selection handler:** on `change`, call `jumpToTown(newId)`. The
implementation is the smallest surface that works without inventing a
public API:

```
function jumpToTown(id) {
  // The game's own dropdown updates Game.townId when the user picks one.
  // We mirror that by simulating a click on the in-game town's link, which
  // is the only confirmed way to switch town without a framework API.
  const uw = gameUw();
  if (!uw || !id) return;
  try {
    // The in-game selector renders <a href="?action=town&id=X&town=X"> or
    // sets the same on a button click. The exact selector is intentionally
    // not guessed: see §8 ("Unknown: in-game town-switch selector").
  } catch (_) {}
}
```

This is **deliberately not implemented as a hardcoded DOM click** — the
selector is unknown without a live sample. The plan §8 carries the
unknown explicitly and proposes the sniff path.

**No new post surface.** Switching town is a navigation event, not a
write. The framework handles it (URL change, model reload).

**No new lock / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry** — switching town is a synchronous
DOM click, not an async post.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/ui.js`** — in `panel.innerHTML` (insert inside the existing
   `<header>` at `ui.js:561`, before the `Colas` button at `ui.js:561`),
   inject a new `<select data-qs="town" title="Saltar a una ciudad">`
   with a single placeholder `<option value="">ciudades</option>`. Populated
   at boot via the helper in step 2.
2. **`src/ui.js`** — add `populateTownSwitcher()` near `applyPanelGeom`
   (`ui.js:278`). It reads `Object.keys(uw.ITowns.towns)`, builds an
   `<option value="<id>"><id>  (<name>)</option>` for each, prepends the
   placeholder, and sets `select.value = String(uw.Game.townId)` if the
   active town is in the list.
3. **`src/ui.js`** — add the `change` handler. On change, call
   `jumpToTown(newId)` (step 4). If `typeof jumpToTown !== 'function'`
   (the selector path is unimplemented — see §8), fall back to a
   `gbLogT('townswitch', 60000, 'town switch: in-game selector not yet
   learned')` so the user sees a clear "not yet" message rather than a
   silent no-op.
4. **`src/ui.js`** — add `jumpToTown(id)` as a stub that calls
   `gbLogT('townswitch-fallback', 60000, 'town switch: use the in-game
   dropdown until the selector is sniffed')`. The real implementation is
   §8 ("unknown"), to be filled by a follow-up sniff commit. Until then,
   the dropdown selection is recorded in `state.lastTownSwitchPick` (see
   §5) so the **intent** is durable; the actual navigation still uses the
   in-game dropdown.
5. **`src/ui.js`** — wire the hotkey. **Reference plan 6.3** for
   `gbShortcut('qs-town', () => focusTownSwitcher())`. The
   `focusTownSwitcher()` helper is local: `select.focus();
   select.size = Math.min(select.options.length, 12); select.click();` —
   the standard `<select>`-open trick. If 6.3 is not yet shipped, this
   step is gated behind `typeof gbShortcut === 'function'`.
6. **`src/ui.js`** — call `populateTownSwitcher()` from the boot sequence
   (right after `applyPanelGeom(state.panelGeom)` at `ui.js:907`). Re-call
   it on `visibilitychange` / `pageshow` (`boot.js` already calls
   `hookFetch` / `hookXhr`; the re-populate can hook into the same
   handler if town ids change between sessions).
7. **`src/ui.js`** — add a `.gb-qs-town` CSS rule to the existing
   `GM_addStyle` block (`ui.js:397-549`) reusing the header pill style
   (`#grepbot-panel .gb-pill` at `ui.js:505-508`). The select must
   inherit the panel theme variables (6.1) without breaking anything in
   the header.

## 5. State & storage

- **New `state.lastTownSwitchPick`** (`core.js:~380`, near visual prefs).
  Holds the last id the user picked in the dropdown so the panel restores
  it across reloads even if the actual navigation still goes through the
  in-game dropdown.
- **New `STORE.TOWN_SWITCH_PICK`** (`header.js:64`, next to `PANEL_GEOM`).
  Non-id-bearing (it is the user's *own* active town, which is the same
  scope as the rest of `state.towns`), but it is still per-user-not-per-
  town so it does **not** go in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
  (`header.js:193-214`).
- **No `configVer` bump** if we treat `lastTownSwitchPick` as a UI-only
  affordance (it does not change feature behaviour). If a future version
  starts using the pick to drive an actual `bridgePost`, bump then. v4.0
  ships read-only.
- **No prune TTL.**

## 6. Config surface

- **No Config toggle.** The dropdown is always shown; the placeholder
  `<option value="">ciudades</option>` is what users see when the panel
  loads before towns are populated.
- The `gbShortcut('qs-town', ...)` registration is silent (no Config
  surface) — keyboard-shortcut UI is owned by plan 6.3.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**Read-mostly feature: no post surface.** Town navigation is a framework
event (URL change, model reload); GrepBot does not POST to switch town.

- **No `gbAjaxWatch` registration.** Town switches do not produce a
  bridge payload.
- **No `gbCaptchaPause` feature key.** No writes means no captcha.
- **No `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry.** Synchronous DOM click; the
  in-game framework handles any async re-render.
- **No dry-run gate.** Nothing posts.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Unknown: in-game town-switch selector.** The plan §3 deliberately
  leaves `jumpToTown(id)` as a stub because the Grepolis client's town-
  switch DOM is **not** in `src/` and is not a stable, documented
  contract. Three paths to fill it (work item 8 in v4.0 is to do this
  sniff; see also §11 below):
  1. Open the game's town dropdown in a live session, inspect the
     rendered `<a>` or `<button>` per town, capture the selector and the
     payload it carries.
  2. Register `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` over the framework's town-
     switch XHR (the URL pattern is `action=town&id=X` per
     `bandit.js:192`-style framing — but the URL itself is not
     confirmed; record the raw signature once observed).
  3. Capture the response template into `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` only if the
     switch produces a bridge-style payload. Most town switches are
     pure navigation; nothing to capture.
  Until this work item is closed, the dropdown records the user's pick
  and the Log says `town switch: use the in-game dropdown until the
  selector is sniffed`. No crash, no half-broken UX.
- **Town list stale across world switches.** `populateTownSwitcher()`
  reads `uw.ITowns.towns` at boot; a `worldId` change between sessions
  rebuilds the option set because `wkey()` keys the persisted pick
  (`STORE.TOWN_SWITCH_PICK` is not world-scoped on purpose — the active
  town is per-user, not per-world). If a town id from world A is
  selected while the user is on world B, `select.value` does not match
  any option and the placeholder is shown — silent degrade, no error.
- **Precondition invariant.** The dropdown reads `Object.keys(...)` and
  `uw.Game.townId` directly; both calls are wrapped in `try { ... } catch
  (_) {}` per the existing pattern at `dodge.js:82-84`,
  `orchestrate.js:60`. If `ITowns.towns` is unreadable, the dropdown
  shows only the placeholder. **No silent dead guard** — `gbLogT` fires
  once via `townswitch-itowns-unreadable` key in the catch, matching the
  plan 26 §A1 pattern.
- **Hotkey conflicts.** Plan 6.3 owns the registration; if `g` is
  already taken (e.g. by the game itself for "select all in chat"), the
  helper returns false and the dropdown still works without a hotkey.
  Plan 6.3's lockable key list will own this conflict.
- **Theme integration (6.1).** The select uses CSS variables; the theme
  plan's `--gb-link`/`--gb-fg` tokens carry over. The `option` element is
  styled by the browser, not the panel — that is acceptable (CLAUDE.md
  treats in-game markup as out-of-scope).

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk = Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Install. Header shows the new dropdown to the left of the `Colas`
  button.
- Open the panel on a 5-town world. Dropdown lists all 5 ids with names.
  The active town is pre-selected.
- Pick a different town from the dropdown. Log shows the
  `town switch: use the in-game dropdown until the selector is sniffed`
  line (one-time per pick via `gbLogT`). The in-game dropdown in the
  game's chrome is **not** auto-clicked by GrepBot in v4.0 (per §8
  "unknown").
- Press `g`. The dropdown opens (focuses + size-expands). Pick a town,
  same log line. Press `g` again — same.
- Reload the page. The last pick is restored as the dropdown's selected
  option (or the placeholder if the pick was for a different world).
- `python3 build.py` passes; install via paste into Tampermonkey.
- Preflight: no new warn rows.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Building the in-game town-switch selector** (work item 8 in §8).
  This plan ships the read-only dropdown + hotkey; the actual click is a
  follow-up that requires a live in-game sniff (§8 step 1).
- **Cross-town "compare" panel.** Show two towns side by side. Out of
  scope; belongs to a different feature.
- **Filtering the dropdown by town groups.** `state.townGroups`
  (`core.js:311`) is a dead field today (plan 26 §B6); wiring it into the
  dropdown would unblock a second dead-flag cleanup but is its own work
  item.
- **Town groups + template hotkeys.** Owned by plans 1.2 / 6.8.
- **Re-specifying the keyboard-shortcut framework.** Plan 6.3 owns it;
  this plan binds one shortcut via that helper and degrades silently if
  6.3 has not landed.
- **Switching to a farm village or to a target town from intel.** Town
  switcher is for **own** towns only; farm villages (`FarmTownPlayerRelation`)
  and enemy towns are not navigable the same way and have their own UI
  (intel pop-up).
