## 6.7-map-context-menus.md

# 6.7 — Context menus on the map (right-click)

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** new `src/context-menu.js`; **MODULES** slot in `build.py` is **after `ui.js`, before `boot.js`** (panel data shape + tab visibility assumed already loaded; reads `renderAttack`, `applyAttackTarget`, `sendAttackViaBridge`, `fetchReport` from later modules in the IIFE — those names resolve at runtime, not load time, so a slot between `attack.js` and `boot.js` is safe).
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/native-ui.js`, `src/core.js`, `src/boot.js`, `src/attack.js`, `src/spy.js`, `src/intel.js`, `src/header.js`.

- **No right-click handler anywhere in `src/`.** A targeted `rtk grep` for
  `contextmenu|context-menu|onContextMenu|right.click|map\.|map_mini|map_main|popup`
  across `src/` returns zero hits (the only matches are the phrase
  "stacking context" in the `gb-native-qctl` stylesheet, `native-ui.js:543,721`).
  The closest analogue is `nativeUiScan` (`native-ui.js:836-876`) which mounts
  small controls inside server-rendered town windows. It does **not** touch
  the in-game map surface at all.
- **The map surface is canvas, not DOM.** Grepolis renders the world map on a
  `<canvas>` overlay with absolute-positioned info-popup tiles for selected
  towns. Verified by `nativeUiScan` (`native-ui.js:838`) querying
  `.window_content,.gpwindow_content,#unit_order` — town *windows*, never map
  tiles. There is no `data-town-id` attribute on the map and no DOM hit-test
  hook for a tile. The `nativeWindowTownId` walker (`native-ui.js:562-589`)
  reads town ids off `data-town-id`/`data-town_id`/`data-townid` attributes
  on focusable windows — none of those exist on the map.
- **Action entry points the menu would call already exist.**
  `sendAttackViaBridge(target, srcTownId, units, mission, onDone)`
  (`attack.js:502-578`); `applyAttackTarget(t)` (`attack.js:272-284`) which
  is the canonical "set the attack plan target" path; `attackRememberTarget`
  (`attack.js:233-242`); `fetchReport(id, hintUrl)` (`spy.js:266-297`); the
  report-driven `ingestReport` → `parseReport` → `state.findings` flow
  (`parse-inline.js:33-93`); the attack planner tab's `renderAttack`
  (`ui.js:370, 388, 392, 237` — exposed via `__grepbotTest` in `boot.js:237`).
- **`gbDomClick(el, feature)` is the only DOM-click path that respects
  `state.dryRun`** (`core.js:941-951`). Any new DOM side effect from a
  context menu item must route through it or `state.dryRun` silently stops
  covering that path (CLAUDE.md "dry-run (v1.4.0)"; `docs/plans/README.md`
  "Conventions every plan follows" line 130).
- **Game context menus on the map are server-rendered.** Grepolis opens a
  popup when a town is right-clicked on the map (e.g. "Atacar / Espiar /
  Vista"). The popup lives outside the panel tree; `nativeUiScan` excludes
  `#grepbot-panel` (`native-ui.js:838`) but the game's own popup is
  positioned at the click coordinates, not inside any selectable window.
  The plan 27 caveat — "respect game context menus; only override GrepBot
  areas" (plan 27 §6) — applies.
- **Lock registry pattern is the only inflight signal.** `gbLock` / `gbUnlock`
  / `gbLocked` + `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry (`core.js:145-215`). Already used by
  every post path (`attack.js`, `spy.js`, `build-auto.js`, etc.). No new
  `*InFlight` booleans (CLAUDE.md "v1.4.0 lock registry: never reintroduce").
- **Disposal hook is `__grepbotDispose`** (`core.js:114-141`). It tears down
  `gbListenerBag`, the panel, the queue center, every `.gb-native-qctl` and
  `.gb-native-panel`. Any new listener registered with `gbListen`
  (`core.js:56-72`) is dropped on dispose automatically.
- **`TPL_FEATURE_MAP`** (`core.js:778-790`) holds the post surface map for
  the `attack` feature: `attack: 'attackTpl'`. `tplNameFor('attack', payload)`
  (`core.js:795-801`) returns `'attackTpl'` for an `attackTpl`-shaped
  payload and `null` for hardcoded `buildUp`/research posts. A new
  `attack-via-context` feature key would be a config-only label unless it
  goes through the same `sendAttackViaBridge` — which is the right choice
  (no new template).
- **Plan 27 §9 lists 15 already-shipped ideas.** None cover a map context
  menu. The "Cancel / recall" row points at `military.js + cancelTpl (10.5)`,
  not a right-click surface. 6.7 is genuinely new.

## 2. Gap

The map is the one game surface the bot currently treats as untouchable.
Every GrepBot action that targets a town — attack send, spy, dossier lookup,
note edit, watchlist add, support/recall (the v0.6.0 cancel path) — currently
requires the player to first navigate to the Attack tab, paste a target id,
or open a separate UI. The player has to leave the map to do anything.

A right-click surface on the map that lists the actions GrepBot can do
*for the town under the cursor* would unify that flow. But the map is
canvas + DOM-popup, and the game's own context menu is also a popup — so
the work is not "intercept the click", it is "render our own popup next to
theirs, only on tiles we can identify, only on hosts we own".

The "Med" risk class is correct: the menu is read-mostly and a single
right-click is cheap, but the *target id* must be resolved without guessing
(map tiles carry no `data-town-id`; only the popup that opens on click does,
and the popup's id source is the same canvas hit-test the game itself runs).

## 3. Design

The new `src/context-menu.js` does **not** intercept any game DOM event.
It runs a 750ms self-rescheduling `gbTimeout` chain (mirrors the 8.2
snapshot pattern — README Hard rule #4 forbids new `gbInterval` /
`setInterval`; only `gbTimeout`/`setTimeout` chains are allowed for new
per-feature polling) that polls `document.body` for the game's own
town-info popup (which is the only piece of map UI that DOM-renders a
town id) and mounts a sibling GrepBot menu next to it. The menu items are
pure links into existing entry points — nothing new gets posted without
going through `sendAttackViaBridge` / `fetchReport` /
`applyAttackTarget` / `intelSetNote` etc.

```
game town popup (canvas + DOM popup, id in popup body)
       │
       │  750ms poll
       ▼
contextMenuScan()
  ├─ find popup by class match (server-rendered, not under #grepbot-panel)
  ├─ read town id from popup's data-id / .town_id / href fragments
  ├─ if popup missing  OR  popup still on the same town as last scan  → return
  └─ otherwise: dispose old menu, build a new one at popup position
                items:
                  • Atacar (engages attack planner: applyAttackTarget + flash)
                  • Espiar (opens a report-fetch for this town)
                  • Añadir a lista de vigilancia
                  • Nota jugador (prompt) → intelSetNote
                  • Nota alianza (prompt) → intelSetAllianceNote
                  • Abrir pestaña Ataque
```

**Hit-test (the decision that decides ours vs. theirs):**

- A GrepBot menu only renders when a *game-rendered* town-info popup is
  present in `document.body` and its tree is **not** a descendant of
  `#grepbot-panel` (mirrors `nativeUiScan:838`). The popup is identified
  by a class match: the standard Grepolis info popup carries
  `.ui-dialog-content` or `.town_name` + a `[data-townid]` (or
  `[data-town-id]`) attribute on the title bar; a class match **or** the
  data-attribute match qualifies. If neither is present, we do nothing.
- A second scan: the popup's anchor in the topmost 1/4 of the viewport
  means the player is mid-click; render the menu. The game's own popup
  continues to be the click target for the GAME's items — we never call
  `e.preventDefault()` on anything. The GrepBot menu is a SIBLING
  `<div class="gb-ctx-menu">` positioned with `style.left/top` matching
  the popup's bounding rect (offset +12px right, +0px down so the menus
  do not overlap the cursor).
- A *defensive* hit-test runs once on mount and every 750ms:
  `document.elementFromPoint(rect.left + 4, rect.top + 4)` MUST be the
  GrepBot menu's first item (the same pattern `nativeQctlHitCheck` uses
  at `native-ui.js:724-734`). If not, `gbLogT('ctx-covered', 300000, …)`
  once and abort. This is the same "stacking context buried us" trap
  `nativeQctlHitCheck` was written to catch (comment at
  `native-ui.js:721-723`). The hit-test fires only while the menu is
  mounted; the chain re-arms the next `gbTimeout(contextMenuScan, 750)`
  only when the previous scan settled, so the chain self-throttles under
  a slow `elementFromPoint`.
- The menu is removed in two cases: (a) the scan finds no game popup, or
  (b) the scan finds a popup for a different town id (menu was stale,
  town changed). Both cases call `contextMenuDispose()` which removes
  the menu, removes its `document`-level click-outside listener
  (registered via `gbListen` so it is dropped on dispose), and clears
  the menu's `dataset.grepbotOn` so the next scan does not double-render.

**The "Atacar" / "Espiar" items route through existing entry points only:**

- Atacar: `applyAttackTarget({ id: <town id>, name: <town name>, x, y, src: 'map' })`
  (`attack.js:272-284`) → which itself only writes to `state.attackPlan` and
  calls `renderAttack`. The actual post is still gated by the
  ATTACK_ROLE_OFFENSE plan, the confirm-gate, and the dry-run path that
  `bridgePost` already provides (CLAUDE.md "Attack planner v2 (v0.6.0)").
  No new template, no new lock, no new post surface.
- Espiar: `fetchReport(id, hintUrl)` (`spy.js:266`) with the town id as
  the report id. The XHR spy (`spy.js:8-112`) will queue the report
  through `parseReport`; the player gets the same flow as a hand-click.
  Already locked by `gbLocked('report-catchup')` when burst-mode is on;
  no new lock entry needed.
- Nota jugador / Nota alianza: `intelSetNote(player, note)` (`intel.js:115-120`)
  and `intelSetAllianceNote(alliance, note)` (`intel.js:124-132`). Setters
  already exist (plan 26 §B2 closed the "no setter" gap).
- Lista de vigilancia: `state.watchlist.push({ id, townId, src: 'map' })`
  plus `save(STORE.WATCHLIST, state.watchlist)`. Read path at
  `watchMatch` (`intel.js:145-185`).

**The menu is a SIBLING, not a parent, of the game popup.** This is the
non-negotiable of plan 27 §6's caveat. We never attach to the popup
itself, never override its `oncontextmenu`, never bubble-cancel any click.
If the game's popup is closed by clicking elsewhere, our menu disposes in
the next scan tick.

## 4. Work items

1. `build.py`: add `'context-menu.js'` to `MODULES` between `'ui.js'` and
   `'boot.js'` (line 70-71). The plan 27 hint ("new `context-menu.js`") is
   correct. Slot is after `ui.js` so `renderAttack` is defined; before
   `boot.js` so the periodic scan starts in the standard place.
2. New `src/context-menu.js`: open the existing IIFE (every module is at
   two-space indent per `DECL_RE` at `build.py:76-80`); declare a
   module-local `let contextMenuState = { el: null, townId: null, at: 0 }`
   wrapped in an IIFE so no top-level `let` collides with another module
   (Hard rule #4: "module-local IIFE wrapping when adding helpers").
3. `src/context-menu.js`: `contextMenuFindPopup()` returns
   `{ el, id, name, x, y }` or `null`. Class match is loose by design
   (server markup drifts across client versions): any element that
   (a) is not inside `#grepbot-panel`, (b) carries a `[data-townid]`,
   `[data-town-id]`, `[data-townid]`, or `[data-town_id]` attribute with a
   numeric value, OR has a `.town_name` descendant whose first child is a
   `<a href*="town_id=">`, qualifies. Returning `null` is the no-menu
   case.
4. `src/context-menu.js`: `contextMenuScan()` is the 750ms poller. If the
   popup is `null` and the menu is mounted → call `contextMenuDispose()`.
   If the popup's id matches `contextMenuState.townId` → return (nothing
   changed). Otherwise call `contextMenuMount(popup)`.
5. `src/context-menu.js`: `contextMenuMount(popup)` builds the menu
   `<div class="gb-ctx-menu">` with `position: fixed; z-index: 2147482000`
   (mirrors `native-ui.js:544`); appends the five item buttons
   (Atacar, Espiar, Lista de vigilancia, Nota jugador, Nota alianza);
   positions it at `popup.getBoundingClientRect()` with `+12px, +0`.
   Each button is a plain `<button>` with `textContent` set in Spanish
   (per CLAUDE.md "UI language: panel UI is Spanish"); each click
   handler routes through `gbDomClick` (so dry-run covers it), then
   into the existing entry points listed in §3.
6. `src/context-menu.js`: register the click-outside handler with
   `gbListen(document, 'mousedown', contextMenuOnClickOutside)` (so it
   is dropped automatically by `__grepbotDispose` at `core.js:124-127`).
   The handler disposes the menu when the click target is not inside
   `gb-ctx-menu` and not inside the game popup.
7. `src/context-menu.js`: schedule the scan from inside the module as a
   self-rescheduling `gbTimeout` chain (Hard rule #4 — no new
   `gbInterval`; **no new** `*InFlight` booleans either). Concretely:

   ```js
   function contextMenuLoop() {
     try { contextMenuScan(); } catch (_) {}
     gbTimeout(contextMenuLoop, 750);
   }
   gbTimeout(contextMenuLoop, 750);   // first kick
   ```

   `gbTimeout` schedules one tick — never an interval. The chain is
   stored in the module-local `contextMenuState` so `__grepbotDispose`
   (`core.js:114-143`) can clear the pending handle on teardown.
   This matches the 8.2 snapshot pattern, which carries the same rule.
8. `src/header.js`: add `STORE.CTX_MENU_ENABLED: 'grepbot:ctx-menu-enabled'`
   and put it in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:193-214`) so the
   toggle survives a world switch without a stale UI flag. Add
   `state.ctxMenuEnabled: load(STORE.CTX_MENU_ENABLED, true)` in the
   state block at `core.js:220` (next to the other feature flags). The
   default is `true` because the menu is read-mostly and a misfire only
   adds a floating div for ≤750ms before the next scan disposes it.
9. `src/stats.js`: add a Preflight row `map context menu` that probes
   `state.ctxMenuEnabled` + that the game popup class is matched by the
   same `contextMenuFindPopup` predicate. The preflight call is
   `preflightProbe('map context menu', () => ({ ok: !!state.ctxMenuEnabled, warn: false, detail: state.ctxMenuEnabled ? 'scan running, listens to game town popup' : 'disabled in Config' }))`.
   This follows the `preflightProbe` signature at `stats.js:3-11`.
10. `src/core.js`: no new `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry needed. The menu is
    read-mostly; the actions it triggers (`sendAttackViaBridge`,
    `fetchReport`) already use their own locks (`attack.js:540`, the
    report-catchup lock at `spy.js:118`). The menu's only inflight
    signal is "is there a popup on screen?" — a single boolean that
    flips on every 750ms scan, never a `*InFlight`.

## 5. State & storage

- New: `state.ctxMenuEnabled: boolean` (default `true`, world-scoped).
  Stored under `STORE.CTX_MENU_ENABLED` (new key in `header.js`), value
  survives a world switch. Config-gated.
- No id-bearing per-target state. The menu reads from existing
  `state.attackPlan`, `state.watchlist`, `state.playerNotes`,
  `state.allianceNotes`; all of those already live in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
  (`header.js:200-206`).
- No new `STORE.*` keys beyond the toggle. The menu does not journal
  (`journal.js` is the only writer; nothing here adds a `skip:*` row).
- `configVer` bump in `qol.js qolExportConfig` if a new Config field is
  added (the toggle is hidden behind a single checkbox; no schema bump
  is required unless we expose per-feature sub-toggles).
- Prune: none. The menu element is removed on every scan tick when the
  popup disappears; no persistent DOM survives the page.

## 6. Config surface

- Toggle: `Menú contextual en el mapa` (default ON, `state.ctxMenuEnabled`).
  Lives in the Intel / Config group. Off ⇒ the 750ms `gbTimeout` chain
  still re-arms (cheap) but `contextMenuMount` is gated on
  `state.ctxMenuEnabled`. No HIGH-RISK marker — the menu is read-mostly;
  every action it launches is gated by its own module's confirm-gate
  (attack), dry-run (CLAUDE.md v1.4.0), or post-payload validation (spy).
- Per-action sub-toggles: not in v4.1. A future iteration can hide
  individual items by adding `{enabled:bool}` rows; v4.1 ships a single
  switch.

## 7. Post surface & safety

The menu itself posts **nothing**. The five items route into existing
post paths:

- **Atacar → `applyAttackTarget`** (`attack.js:272-284`): no post.
  Writes `state.attackPlan.targetId/targetType/targetX/targetY` and
  calls `renderAttack`. The actual post (`sendAttackViaBridge` at
  `attack.js:502-578`) is reached only via the Attack tab's
  "Send" button, which still runs the v0.6.0 confirm gate
  (CLAUDE.md "Attack planner v2 (v0.6.0): planner dialog has Copy + **Send
  attack** (confirm gate, payload logged)").
- **Espiar → `fetchReport`** (`spy.js:266-297`): post is `gameAjaxPost`
  with `controller: 'report', action: 'view'`. Already registered with
  `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` by the bridge's auto-settle path
  (`bridge.js:7-12, 23-50`). Template: `TPL_FEATURE_MAP.report` —
  not in the table at `core.js:778-790`, so `tplNameFor` returns
  `undefined`; `tplHealthNote` short-circuits on `!name`
  (`core.js:837`). **No template health charge for spy.** Already
  locked by `gbLocked('report-catchup')` when in batch mode.
  Dry-run: `state.dryRun` flows through `txRun` → `bridgeRaw` /
  `gameAjaxRaw` and logs the payload without sending. Captcha breaker
  uses the **existing** `'report'` feature key (`spy.js:268`,
  `state.captchaBreakers.report`); no new key needed.
- **Lista de vigilancia → `state.watchlist.push`** + `save`: no post.
- **Nota jugador / Nota alianza → `intelSetNote` / `intelSetAllianceNote`**
  (`intel.js:115-120, 124-132`): no post. `intelSetAllianceNote` was
  added in v3.x per plan 26 §B2.
- **Abrir pestaña Ataque → tab switch** (no post): routes through the
  existing tab-render switch (`ui.js:370, 388, 392`).

Therefore: no `gbAjaxWatch` registration from this module, no new
`TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry, no new `gbCaptchaPause` feature key, no new
`gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no dry-run gate on the menu itself
(`gbDomClick` already covers the menu's DOM side effects; the post
paths have their own gates).

`state.dryRun` coverage: a player with dry-run ON who right-clicks a
town and picks "Atacar" will see `DRY-RUN ctx-menu: click blocked` in
the Log (per `gbDomClick:946`) and a `skip:dryrun` journal entry
(deferred to the post path, where `txRun` logs it). The `applyAttackTarget`
write itself is **not** gated by dry-run — that is consistent with
the existing Attack tab (dry-run gates posts, not plan edits).

## 8. Failure modes

- **Game popup class drifts across client versions.** The
  `contextMenuFindPopup` predicate has two branches (data-attribute,
  class match); if both miss, the menu silently does not render. The
  750ms scan wastes a single `querySelectorAll` (cheap). Symptom
  logged once via `gbLogT('ctx-popup-miss', 600000, …)`.
- **GrepBot menu is covered by a stacking-context ancestor.**
  Hit-test per `nativeQctlHitCheck` (`native-ui.js:724-734`). Symptom
  logged once via `gbLogT('ctx-covered', 300000, …)`. The menu
  remains mounted but a click on it does not reach its handler.
  Defensive: the player can still use the Attack tab.
- **Town id is unreadable from the popup.** `contextMenuFindPopup`
  returns `null`. The menu does not mount. This is the precondition
  invariant: a read that did not return a finite value is unknown,
  the menu does not invent one. `gbLogT('ctx-id-blind', 600000, …)`
  fires once per unknown popup class.
- **Tab leader not held.** `gbTabLeader === false` (`core.js:11, 51-55`):
  every menu action calls a `flash('GrepBot está activo en otra pestaña')`
  guard, mirroring `nativeTownAction` (`native-ui.js:590-592`).
  Inherited from the existing tab-leader contract; the menu does not
  need its own implementation.
- **Stale menu on popup close.** The 750ms scan disposes the menu in
  one tick. Worst-case UX: the menu lingers for 750ms after the
  popup closes; clicking it does nothing because every handler
  re-checks `contextMenuState.townId` against the current popup.
- **SPA navigation re-renders the popup tree.** The scan rebuilds
  the menu from scratch. No `MutationObserver` is needed — the
  750ms poll already covers this (`native-ui.js:555-557` uses the
  same 80ms debounce pattern; we do not need sub-second latency
  for a context menu).
- **Modal window open (report, attack planner, etc.).** The
  game town popup cannot coexist with another full-window
  popup, so the scan returns `null` and the menu does not
  mount. The native queue controls handle the window case
  (`native-ui.js:736+`); no overlap.

## 9. Validation gate

Med-risk (plan 27 §11: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one full
orchestrator tick).

- Open a world with ≥1 own town. Open the map. Right-click a town.
  Log: `ctx-menu: mounted for town <id>`. Right-click again on the
  same town ⇒ no second mount. Right-click a different town ⇒
  rebuild + `ctx-menu: rebuilt for town <id>`.
- Pick "Atacar" with the panel on the Attack tab. The plan's target
  field populates with the town id; no `bridgePost` is sent. Clicking
  "Send" still requires the v0.6.0 confirm gate; the menu did not
  bypass it.
- Pick "Espiar". A report fetch is enqueued; the report appears in
  the Intel/Fichaje tab (existing path). No new `gbCaptchaPause`
  key was registered; captcha still trips the `report` breaker.
- Pick "Lista de vigilancia". A row is added to the watchlist
  (`state.watchlist`); a future report that touches the town
  triggers `intelWatchlistScan` (`intel.js:186-205`).
- Pick "Nota jugador" / "Nota alianza". A `prompt()` opens; the
  entered text lands in `state.playerNotes` / `state.allianceNotes`
  and is persisted by the existing setters (`intel.js:115-132`).
- Right-click on the open world, then move the mouse far enough
  for the game's popup to close. The GrepBot menu disposes within
  one 750ms tick.
- Run a session with `state.dryRun === true`. Every menu item
  click logs `DRY-RUN ctx-menu: …` (per `gbDomClick:946`). The
  items that touch state (`Atacar`, watchlist, notes) still write
  to state because the bot's dry-run contract gates **posts**,
  not plan edits (mirrors Attack tab).
- Preflight row `map context menu`: pass when `state.ctxMenuEnabled`
  and the scan can find a town popup at least once during the
  Stats refresh; warn when enabled but no popup ever seen (the
  player may be in a non-map view); never fail.
- `__grepbotDispose` smoke: toggle the panel off (re-enable with
  a hot reload) ⇒ `contextMenuState` is reset; no `gbListenerBag`
  leak (verified via `core.js:124-127`).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Selecting a source town from the map.** The map's "from" side of an
  attack (which of your own cities sends) is not a map right-click
  surface — that is the Attack tab's source selector. Plan 7.1
  (shared attack planner v2) is the right place if a map source-pick
  ever lands.
- **Map tile tinting.** The map is canvas; there is no DOM tile to
  tint, and modifying game canvas bytes is out per plan 27 §0
  ("Shadow-DOM UI hide / variable rename in artifact — would break
  template-sniff contracts"). 6.7 ships right-click only.
- **Touch / long-press context menu.** The Grepolis client is mouse-
  driven; long-press would need a separate gesture path. v4.1 is
  desktop only.
- **Custom user-defined menu items.** The five built-in items are
  the contract for v4.1. A "user item list" belongs in 6.8
  (profile auto-switching) or a future UX feature.
- **Auto-opening the menu on left-click.** The game already
  left-clicks a town to recenter the map; overriding that would
  violate the "respect game context menus" caveat (plan 27 §6).
- **Hotkey trigger (Shift-R to open the menu).** That is 6.3
  (keyboard shortcuts). 6.7 only handles the right-click surface.

## 6.8-profile-auto-switching.md

# 6.8 — Profile auto-switching

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** `src/qol.js` (profile-rule engine) + `src/ui.js` (Config controls); call the existing `src/orchestrate.js` tick, with no new `build.py` MODULES slot
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `qol.js` already has three named profiles: `afk`, `farming`, and `war`, with Spanish labels and allowlisted values (`src/qol.js:272-358`). The AFK and farming profiles enable write-capable economy loops such as `autoFarm`, `autoCave`, `abAuto`, `autoTrade`, and `autoResearch` (`src/qol.js:290-336`); the war profile enables a different subset (`src/qol.js:338-356`).
- The existing safety table forces `autoFavor`, `autoRecruit`, `autoDodge`, premium culture, merchant, wonder, wonder-favor, Phoenician trade, and village recruit OFF when a preset is applied (`src/qol.js:277-288`, `src/qol.js:359-371`). It deliberately does not change `dryRun` (`src/qol.js:272-276`).
- Applying a preset is currently a direct synchronous mutation: `qolApplyPreset` assigns `state[key]`, calls `save`, forces the high-risk table, and logs one summary (`src/qol.js:359-381`). It is not routed through `qolImportConfig`, despite the design in plan 16 (`docs/plans/16-config-presets.md:31-48`).
- The only current preset controls are footer buttons wired in `ui.js`; the handler applies immediately, rebinds Config, updates status, and flashes a message (`src/ui.js:1632-1642`). There is no time/condition rule editor or auto-switch toggle in the Config markup (`src/ui.js:706-843`).
- No profile-auto state or storage key exists in the shared key table or state initializer (`src/header.js:24-187`, `src/core.js:220-384`).
- The existing orchestrator is the sole cadence for economy work: `orchTick` checks host and pause state, selects due features, and dispatches up to three per tick (`src/orchestrate.js:147-199`); boot calls it once and then every `ORCH_MS` (`src/boot.js:103-107`). A new `gbInterval` would violate the repository scheduler rule (`src/boot.js:103-107`).
- Existing pause conditions already read local time, activity timeout, captcha, and server cooldown (`src/core.js:572-600`); `gameNow` provides a server-time fallback but the night-pause implementation uses `new Date().getHours()` (`src/core.js:585-590`, `src/core.js:1063-1078`). Hostile incoming movements have a real read path in `dodgeIncomingMovements` (`src/dodge.js:53-83`), and town capacity/fill is centralized in `townResState` (`src/bridge.js:235-235`).

## 2. Gap

There is no persisted rule that selects an existing profile from a time window plus live conditions, and therefore no unattended profile transition. The delta is a default-OFF declarative evaluator that applies only the already-coded preset allow-list, records the active rule and a hold-down period, and runs from the existing orchestrator cadence without inventing a game action or post route.

## 3. Design

1. Store a bounded rule list, not JavaScript. The shape is `{enabled, minHoldMin, rules:[{id, enabled, priority, profile, days, startMin, endMin, when}]}`. `profile` is one of `afk|farming|war`; `days` contains local `Date#getDay()` values `0..6`; `startMin` and `endMin` are minutes `0..1439`; `when` is an AND map with exactly `activity: any|active|idle`, `incoming: any|yes|no`, and `warehouse: any|full|not-full`. No `eval`, arbitrary expression, endpoint, or user-event simulation is allowed.
2. Evaluate rules in ascending `priority`, then `id`, on the local wall clock. A time window with `startMin <= endMin` is half-open `[startMin,endMin)`; one with `startMin > endMin` crosses midnight. An empty `days` list never matches. This mirrors the existing explicit overnight interval logic rather than guessing server time (`src/core.js:585-590`).
3. Read `activity` from `state.pauseOnActivity` and the existing `userPausedUntil`; `active` means the timeout is currently live and `idle` means it is not. Read `incoming` through `dodgeIncomingMovements` (`src/dodge.js:53-83`). Read `warehouse` by enumerating the same owned-town models used by the existing overview (`src/qol.js:97-101`) and calling `townResState(townId)`; `full` means at least one readable town is at or above 97% of capacity, while `not-full` requires every enumerated town to be readable and below 97%.
4. If the first matching rule names the same profile as `profileAutoLast.profile`, do nothing. If it names another profile, require `Date.now() - profileAutoLast.switchedAt >= minHoldMin * 60000` (minimum 15 minutes, maximum 24 hours). If no rule matches, keep the current profile; do not bounce to a default profile.
5. On a transition, call `qolApplyPreset(profile)` once, save `{profile, ruleId, switchedAt}`, refresh the Config controls/status, and emit exactly `profile-auto: switched <old> -> <new> (rule <id>; activity=<...>; incoming=<...>; warehouse=<...>)`. The preset's existing high-risk-off and dry-run-preservation behavior remains authoritative (`src/qol.js:272-288`).
6. Call `QOL_PROFILE_AUTO.tick()` from the start of `orchTick` after the host check and before its pause return (`src/orchestrate.js:147-150`). This lets a scheduled profile change the next dispatch's pause behavior, while retaining the single 20-second cadence and no parallel scheduler.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/header.js` — `STORE`, `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`, and `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT`.** Add `PROFILE_AUTO_CFG` and `PROFILE_AUTO_LAST`; include both in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` because the rules select presets that mutate world-specific targets and must not leak across worlds (`src/header.js:193-215`). Bump the config version from 10 (`src/header.js:189-191`) to 11.
2. **`src/core.js` — `state` initializer and `migrateConfig`.** Load `profileAutoCfg` with `{enabled:false,minHoldMin:15,rules:[]}` and `profileAutoLast` with `{profile:null,ruleId:null,switchedAt:0}` (`src/core.js:220-384`). Add a `<11` migration that validates object/array shape, clamps the hold period and drops malformed rules, saves both world-scoped keys, and leaves all existing settings unchanged; retain the final `configVer` save/log path (`src/core.js:394-510`).
3. **`src/qol.js` — `QOL_PROFILE_AUTO`.** Add a module-local IIFE (not new top-level `function` declarations) exposing `tick`, `normalise`, and `ruleSummary`. Implement the exact rule grammar, bounded validation, local time/day matching, the three live condition readers, hold-down comparison, preset application, persistence, and the exact switch log. Unknown condition reads must return `blind` and be throttled with `gbLogT`, not treated as false.
4. **`src/qol.js` — export/import delta.** Add `profileAutoCfg` to the existing config export and validated import allow-list (`src/qol.js:248-267`), with schema 4 and the same rule normalizer. Importing a malformed rule must ignore that rule and never enable auto-switching implicitly.
5. **`src/ui.js` — Config markup and `bindConfig`.** Add `Cambio automático de perfiles` (unchecked by default), `Permanencia mínima (min)` (15), and a bounded rule editor with explicit Spanish labels for profile, days, start, end, activity, incoming, warehouse, enabled, priority, plus Add/Delete controls. Wire changes through `save(STORE.PROFILE_AUTO_CFG, ...)`, render persisted values on every rebind (`src/ui.js:1137-1162`, `src/ui.js:1317-1383`), and call `updateStatus` after a switch. Do not use free-form condition text.
6. **`src/orchestrate.js` — `orchTick`.** Invoke the QoL evaluator only after `hostEnabled()` succeeds (`src/orchestrate.js:147-150`); do not add `gbInterval`, a wake queue entry, an economy handler, or a `*InFlight` flag.

## 5. State & storage

- Add `state.profileAutoCfg` and `state.profileAutoLast`; both use `STORE.PROFILE_AUTO_CFG` / `STORE.PROFILE_AUTO_LAST` and are world-scoped intentionally (`src/header.js:193-215`). The rule list is capped at 20 entries; each rule has a stable bounded `id` and no town/player identifiers.
- Bump `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT` 10→11 (`src/header.js:189-191`). Migration must run through the existing ordered `<version` blocks and finish through the existing `configVer` save (`src/core.js:394-510`).
- `profileAutoLast` is one record, not a history ring, so it needs no TTL prune. Delete malformed rules on load/import; never delete learned templates, journal entries, or findings.

## 6. Config surface

- `Cambio automático de perfiles`: checkbox, default **OFF**.
- `Permanencia mínima (min)`: number `15..1440`, default `15`.
- Rule rows: `Activa`, `Prioridad`, `Perfil`, `Días`, `Desde`, `Hasta`, `Actividad`, `Incoming`, `Almacén`; defaults for a new row are disabled, priority 100, profile `afk`, all days, `00:00–00:00` (must be edited), and all conditions `any`.
- Existing `Perfil: AFK nocturno`, `Perfil: recoleccion activa`, and `Perfil: guerra` remain manual actions (`src/ui.js:892-894`, `src/ui.js:1632-1642`). Auto-switching never turns a high-risk loop ON because the existing safety map only writes those keys as `false` (`src/qol.js:277-288`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface, route, payload, `gbAjaxWatch`, `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`, captcha feature key, or lock is introduced: this feature only mutates local config by calling `qolApplyPreset` (`src/qol.js:359-381`). It can indirectly enable existing economy loops, so the feature is default OFF, preserves `state.dryRun`, and leaves all resulting posts behind the existing dry-run gate (`src/core.js:940-946`, `src/tx.js:531-555`). No new lock is needed because the tick is synchronous; do not add an in-flight boolean.

## 8. Failure modes

- Invalid rule/profile/time/day is dropped at normalization and logged as `profile-auto: invalid rule <id>`; it never activates the feature. A missing/unknown condition getter is `blind`, logged once through `gbLogT`, and the rule is not selected; no blind value is allowed to trigger a configuration change (`src/core.js:298-309`).
- Missing `ITowns`, `MovementsUnits`, or capacity data produces a throttled `profile-auto: condition blind` entry and leaves the previous profile untouched. `dodgeIncomingMovements` already filters to canonical hostile types (`src/dodge.js:39-83`); do not infer hostility from an unknown field.
- A dropped SPA callback cannot strand this feature because it has no asynchronous callback or lock; the existing orchestrator catches handler exceptions (`src/qol.js:420-435`) and the evaluator must catch its own reads.
- A profile switch never bypasses `automationPaused`; it only occurs before the existing pause return, and every subsequent write still uses existing precondition readers. Every new write guard must name the value it read; unreadable getter ⇒ `blind` ⇒ `gbLogT` once ⇒ let the server decide (`src/core.js:298-309`).
- Overlapping rules are deterministic by priority/id, and the minimum hold plus no-match no-op prevents time-boundary thrash. A switch failure leaves `profileAutoLast` unchanged and logs `profile-auto: apply failed`.

## 9. Validation gate

Med risk requires dry-run, one hand-triggered firing, and one full orchestrator tick (plan 27 §11.1). With `dryRun` ON (`src/ui.js:1384-1389`), enable auto-switching, create a rule for the current minute with `incoming=any`, and wait for one `orchTick`; the Log must show the exact `profile-auto: switched ...` line and subsequent would-be posts must be `DRY-RUN`, never live requests. Turn dry-run OFF only after comparing one manual preset application against its resulting Config values; then allow one full tick and confirm one switch only, no second switch for 15 minutes, and no high-risk toggle becomes ON. Test an overlapping rule, a midnight interval, an unreadable condition (Log `condition blind` once), reload persistence, and a world change; the other world must not inherit the active rule or last-switch record (`src/core.js:1088-1107`).

## 10. Out of scope

No new profile semantics beyond the three shipped presets, per-town profile balancing, city specialization, activity I/O, user-event simulation, or server sync. City specialization belongs to 1.2; keyboard/widget UX belongs to 6.2/6.3. This plan does not invent an endpoint or change any preset payload; it only schedules the existing local preset mutation (`src/qol.js:359-381`).

## 6.9-config-wizard.md

# 6.9 — Config import/export wizard

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** `src/qol.js` (pure prepare/validate/export helpers) + `src/ui.js` (wizard UI); both are existing MODULES slots in `build.py:61-70`
**Depends on:** 6.8 (so profile-auto rules are included as an optional section), 6.10 (import is one undoable config transaction)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- Config JSON export already exists: `qolExportConfig` returns schema, config version, host, selected planner/queue/target/profile/template data, notes, and watchlist (`src/qol.js:223-252`). Plan 27 §9 therefore correctly marks the JSON mechanism CODED (`docs/plans/27-v4-wishlist-2026-08-10.md:239-263`).
- The current GUI is only two buttons in the Overview backup section (`src/ui.js:673-691`). Export serializes `qolRedactConfigDump(qolExportConfig())` to the clipboard (`src/ui.js:985-987`); import prompts for raw pasted JSON, parses it, and immediately mutates state (`src/ui.js:989-996`). There is no preview, field-selection, validation report, or cancel step.
- The redaction path is real and defaults to protecting player/alliance notes and watchlist values: `qolRedactConfigDump` leaves raw output only when `state.exportRedact === false`, otherwise replaces note keys/values and sets `redacted` (`src/qol.js:223-246`). The Config checkbox reflects that default (`src/core.js:339-347`, `src/ui.js:1311-1314`).
- `qolImportConfig` already refuses a different host and a newer schema, validates each known section, normalizes priority/build order/targets/queues, writes accepted sections, sets the current config version, disables legacy `autoFavor`, and logs a count (`src/qol.js:254-267`). It is an apply path, not a pure validator.
- The export allow-list does not include the webhook URL, Telegram chat id, CSRF, captcha state, learned bridge templates, or other transport state (`src/qol.js:248-252`; the corresponding sensitive keys exist separately in `src/header.js:54-65`, `src/header.js:61-62`, and `src/header.js:107-108`). This omission is part of the safety boundary and must remain true.
- The current Config tab is a large set of direct controls (`src/ui.js:706-843`) whose handlers mutate `state` and call `save` directly (`src/ui.js:1193-1291`, `src/ui.js:1364-1533`). The wizard must not pretend those controls are already covered by an import/export UI.

## 2. Gap

Replace the prompt-and-immediate-apply path with a local GUI wizard that produces a sanitized export, parses pasted JSON into a previewable candidate, reports host/schema/section errors before mutation, lets the user cancel or apply, and routes the final apply through the existing validated importer. It must not add cloud sync, a server, a download endpoint, or any secret-bearing export field.

## 3. Design

1. Add `qolPrepareConfigImport(rawOrObject)` as a pure helper in `qol.js`. Parse JSON if given text; require a plain object; enforce the existing host and schema ceilings (`src/qol.js:254-256`); run the existing per-section validators/normalizers without assigning `state`; return `{ok, sections, ignored, errors, candidate, sourceHost, schema, ver}`. Unknown keys are listed as ignored, never copied.
2. Keep the existing allow-list as the source of truth. Extend it only for the optional `profileAutoCfg` section from 6.8; do not add `webhookUrl`, `webhookEvents.telegramChatId`, CSRF, captcha breakers, learned templates, findings, decisions, or alert transport state. The raw export object remains internal until redaction has run (`src/qol.js:248-252`).
3. Add `qolExportConfigForUi()` that clones `qolExportConfig()`, passes it through the existing `qolRedactConfigDump`, and returns the sanitized object. Every copy/export button must use this helper; no UI code may stringify `qolExportConfig()` directly. The redaction OFF warning remains the existing throttled machine-log path (`src/qol.js:225-228`).
4. The wizard is a modal `<dialog>`-style panel built with the repository's existing DOM creation/string markup in `ui.js`; it has `Exportar`, `Importar`, `Copiar JSON`, `Pegar JSON`, `Validar`, `Aplicar`, and `Cancelar`. Export shows read-only sanitized JSON. Import shows section statuses (`válida`, `ignorada`, `inválida`) and a compact before→after diff based on the canonical config snapshot used by 6.10.
5. `Aplicar` requires a second confirmation and calls `qolImportConfig(prepared.candidate, {source:'wizard'})`; 6.10 records the pre-apply snapshot and supplies Undo. On success close the wizard, call `bindConfig`, `renderCaveTowns`, `renderDashboard`, and `updateStatus`; on failure keep the modal open with the exact error list.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/qol.js` — split `qolImportConfig` (`src/qol.js:254-267`).** Extract parsing, host/schema checks, validators, priority/build/queue normalizers, and section writes into pure prepare plus apply functions. Preserve the current host refusal, newer-schema refusal, invalid-section ignore, `configVer` assignment, `autoFavor` safety reset, `goalPlanAll`, and applied-count log.
2. **`src/qol.js` — export wrapper.** Implement `qolExportConfigForUi` as clone → existing redaction path → return. Add `profileAutoCfg` only if its 6.8 normalizer accepts it; bump `CONFIG_EXPORT_SCHEMA` from 3 (`src/qol.js:223`) only when the payload shape changes, and retain refusal of schema values above the supported number.
3. **`src/ui.js` — backup controls.** Replace the direct prompt/copy listeners (`src/ui.js:976-996`) with one wizard opener and modal renderer. Keep the existing Overview location (`src/ui.js:673-691`) and Spanish UI convention; do not use raw `innerHTML` for pasted JSON or preview values.
4. **`src/ui.js` — preview/apply lifecycle.** On `Validar`, call the pure prepare helper and render only counts/field names/diff values that are safe to display. On `Aplicar`, require the confirmation text, call the validated import with `{source:'wizard'}`, then refresh all affected views. `Cancelar` must not call `qolImportConfig` or `save`.
5. **`src/qol.js` + `src/ui.js` — compatibility.** Keep the existing `boot.js` test-mode exports (`src/boot.js:191-193`) pointing at the public export/import contract, and add the UI-safe export helper only if the test hook needs a sanitized fixture; do not add a test harness.

## 5. State & storage

- No new persistent wizard state or id-bearing key is needed. The modal is transient DOM state; accepted config continues to use the existing `STORE.*` keys through `qolImportConfig` (`src/qol.js:256-267`).
- Do not add a new migration solely for the wizard. If 6.8 adds `profileAutoCfg`, its key and `configVer` migration remain owned by 6.8; the wizard accepts a missing optional section as “not supplied.”
- Do not persist pasted raw JSON, preview text, clipboard data, webhook URLs, Telegram chat ids, CSRF, or learned templates. Storage scope and versioning remain those of the existing keys (`src/header.js:193-215`).

## 6. Config surface

- Existing buttons keep their Spanish labels: `Exportar configuración` and `Importar configuración` (`src/ui.js:690`). Add the wizard labels `Copiar JSON seguro`, `Pegar JSON`, `Validar`, `Aplicar configuración`, and `Cancelar`.
- The existing `Redact names/ids in Copy + Export` checkbox remains default ON (`src/core.js:339-347`, `src/ui.js:788`); the wizard must visibly warn `Redacción desactivada: el JSON puede contener nombres` when it is OFF, but must never add secrets to the export.
- No new automation toggle is introduced here; no `configVer` bump is required unless the export schema is changed for the 6.8 section. A schema bump is separate from `configVer` and must be documented in the helper constant (`src/qol.js:223`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface: import/export is local clipboard/DOM work and has no route, payload, `gbAjaxWatch`, `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`, `gbCaptchaPause` feature key, or lock. The wizard must not use `gbDomClick`, `bridgePost`, `gameAjaxPost`, or any network API; this preserves the paste-only/no-server boundary (`CLAUDE.md:40-49`, `CLAUDE.md:252-255`). An imported setting may enable an existing loop, but the validated import preserves the existing `dryRun` value unless the accepted config explicitly contains it, and all resulting writes remain behind existing transaction gates (`src/qol.js:254-267`, `src/tx.js:531-555`).

## 8. Failure modes

- Invalid JSON, arrays, non-object roots, a different host, or a schema newer than supported stops at `Validar`/`Aplicar`; no `state` or storage mutation occurs (`src/qol.js:254-256`).
- Invalid sections are shown as `ignorada: <key>` and omitted exactly as the current importer does (`src/qol.js:256-267`). A valid file with zero accepted sections cannot be applied.
- A malicious or accidental secret field is unknown and ignored. Export safety is enforced by the allow-list plus `qolRedactConfigDump`, not by hiding a field in the modal (`src/qol.js:223-252`). Never display a raw webhook/Telegram value in the diff.
- A quota failure is handled by the existing `save` prune/retry path (`src/core.js:1130-1213`); the wizard reports apply failure and does not claim success. The precondition invariant still applies to any existing write-capable setting: every guard names the value read; unreadable getter ⇒ `blind` ⇒ `gbLogT` once ⇒ let the server decide (`src/core.js:298-309`).
- A dropped callback is irrelevant because there is no asynchronous game request. Clipboard rejection is a UI error only; leave the sanitized JSON visible for manual copy.

## 9. Validation gate

Low risk requires Preflight plus one in-game session with no failure (plan 27 §11). Open Overview → `Exportar configuración`, confirm the displayed/copyable JSON contains `redacted:true` and no webhook URL, Telegram chat id, CSRF, learned template, or raw player/alliance names (`src/qol.js:223-252`). Paste a valid same-host JSON, click `Validar`, verify section statuses and diff, then click `Cancelar` and confirm exported config is byte-equivalent. Reopen, `Aplicar configuración`, verify the Log `config imported: ... validated section(s)`, controls persist after reload, and Undo from 6.10 restores the prior snapshot. Paste malformed JSON, a different `host`, a future `schema`, and an invalid section; each must show an error, send no request, and leave state unchanged. Run Stats → Preflight once after applying; no new post or `UNREADABLE` error may appear.

## 10. Out of scope

No cloud sync, REST/WebSocket endpoint, webhook export, credentials, automatic import, arbitrary JavaScript conditions, plugin system, or test harness. Existing JSON validation/redaction is not rewritten into a new transport; this is a GUI delta over `qolExportConfig`/`qolImportConfig` (`src/qol.js:248-267`). Profile rule semantics belong to 6.8; undo/redo transaction/history belongs to 6.10.

## 6.10-config-undo-redo.md

# 6.10 — Undo/redo for config changes

**Bucket:** v4.0 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** `src/qol.js` (snapshot/history/apply contract) + `src/ui.js` (buttons and event boundaries); existing `build.py` MODULES slots `qol.js`/`ui.js` (`build.py:61-70`)
**Depends on:** none; 6.9 should call this transaction boundary when it lands
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- There is no `undo`, `redo`, `configUndo`, or config-history symbol in `src/`; the only existing history-like state is operational decision memory (`state.decisions`/`state.decisionSkips`, `src/core.js:343-345`) and queue/history data for other features (`src/core.js:263-285`).
- The existing config export is a partial allow-list of targets, planner/queue data, profiles/templates, and notes/watchlist (`src/qol.js:248-252`). It is redacted only by the UI export caller (`src/ui.js:985-987`), not by `qolExportConfig` itself.
- Config controls mutate `state` and persist directly in many handlers: early toggles use direct assignments (`src/ui.js:1193-1291`), later toggles use `bindToggle` (`src/ui.js:1364-1392`), and numeric/select/object fields use `saveNum` and direct listeners (`src/ui.js:1393-1533`). No common before/after checkpoint exists.
- Presets also mutate directly through `qolApplyPreset` (`src/qol.js:359-381`), and template application writes targets directly (`src/qol.js:25-44`). Plan 16 proposed snapshot/undo (`docs/plans/16-config-presets.md:45-48`, `docs/plans/16-config-presets.md:65-80`), but that behavior is not present in the shipped functions.
- `configVer` is loaded as world-scoped state (`src/core.js:339-347`, `src/header.js:193-215`), migration is ordered through v10 and ends by saving/logging the new version (`src/core.js:394-510`), and `migrateConfig()` runs during UI startup (`src/ui.js:1992-1997`). An undo implementation that simply writes an old version backward would violate this one-way migration model.

## 2. Gap

Add bounded, local undo and redo for user-facing configuration mutations without treating runtime telemetry, learned templates, journal rows, or credentials as configuration. Every checkpoint must restore a validated current-schema snapshot, preserve the migration version, and handle an old snapshot across a `configVer` boundary without replaying obsolete storage formats or silently disabling dry-run safety.

## 3. Design

1. Define `QOL_CONFIG_HISTORY` as a module-local IIFE in `qol.js`, exposing `snapshot`, `commit`, `undo`, `redo`, `canUndo`, and `canRedo`. A snapshot is `{schema, ver, at, reason, data}`. `data` is a cloned, validated configuration allow-list; it excludes `webhookUrl`, `webhookEvents.telegramChatId`, CSRF, captcha breakers, learned templates, findings, decisions, transport state, and host consent. The existing redaction path remains the export privacy boundary (`src/qol.js:223-246`).
2. Expand the canonical config snapshot/export allow-list to cover every Config-tab field that can alter automation, including the toggles and values rendered at `src/ui.js:1302-1363` and persisted at `src/ui.js:1371-1533`, while keeping sensitive/operational exclusions explicit. Do not infer keys from a deny-list: new config keys remain untouched until deliberately added to the allow-list.
3. `commit(reason, mutate)` clones the canonical `before`, runs the existing mutation synchronously, clones `after`, and pushes `before` only when the canonical JSON differs. It clears redo, caps each ring at 20 entries, stores a 7-day timestamp, and saves one world-scoped undo key. Nested apply calls use a `record:false` guard so import/preset/undo does not create recursive entries.
4. Wrap user-generated Config-tab `change` events at the section capture phase in `ui.js`, before existing handlers mutate state, then compare after the synchronous handler. The event filter is limited to `[data-cfg]` controls plus the existing preset/template/import actions; it must not capture panel navigation, Stats simulation, journal clear, scrape buttons, or runtime callbacks. Explicit `commit` calls remain required for public `qolImportConfig`, `qolApplyPreset`, and `qolApplyTemplate` so non-DOM callers are covered.
5. Undo pops the latest valid undo entry, first commits the current state to redo, then applies the popped data through the same validators/normalizers as `qolImportConfig` (`src/qol.js:254-267`). Redo does the symmetric operation. Refresh Config, Overview, and status after either action; log `config undo: <reason>` / `config redo: <reason>` with stack counts, never raw sensitive data.
6. Migration boundary rule: `ver < state.configVer` is normalized forward into the current schema and applied without lowering `state.configVer`; `STORE.CONFIG_VER` remains the current value. The apply log must say `config undo: normalized v<old> -> v<current>` and the result is not advertised as byte-identical. `ver > state.configVer` is refused and remains on its stack. This is necessary because startup migration can rewrite state and persist v10 (`src/core.js:394-510`) before the UI is available (`src/ui.js:1992-1997`).

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/header.js` — storage constants and scope.** Add `CONFIG_UNDO` and `CONFIG_REDO` keys beside `CONFIG_VER` (`src/header.js:125-140`), and add both to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-215`) so undo data from one world cannot alter another world’s config. No id-bearing key may bypass that set.
2. **`src/core.js` — state initialization.** Load `configUndo` and `configRedo` as bounded arrays in the `state` object (`src/core.js:220-384`). Do not put history into `DECISIONS`; that ring has separate TTL/duplicate semantics (`CLAUDE.md:352-365`).
3. **`src/qol.js` — canonical snapshot and history IIFE.** Implement deep cloning with the repository’s JSON style (`src/qol.js:254-257`), allow-list normalization, ring pruning, save/load, stack operations, and a non-recording apply option. Reuse import validators rather than a second unchecked setter. Preserve the existing preset high-risk-off policy (`src/qol.js:272-381`).
4. **`src/qol.js` — mutation boundaries.** Add `history:false`/`source` options to `qolImportConfig`, wrap `qolApplyPreset`, and wrap `qolApplyTemplate` (`src/qol.js:25-44`, `src/qol.js:254-267`, `src/qol.js:359-381`). A failed/zero-section import must not create an undo entry; a successful preset/template/import creates exactly one.
5. **`src/ui.js` — event capture and controls.** Register one capture listener on `section[data-tab=config]` after the existing controls are bound (`src/ui.js:1137-1540`), identify only config mutations, and close the checkpoint after the target handler returns. Add `Deshacer` and `Rehacer` buttons plus disabled-state/count rendering near the existing profile/config controls (`src/ui.js:883-894`). Clicks call the public history methods, then `bindConfig`/`updateStatus`.
6. **`src/ui.js` — no accidental captures.** Ensure the listener does not checkpoint `clear-captcha`, `research-csfast`, `pt-now`, `pt-copy`, panel navigation, or `gb-sim-run`; those controls are visible in the existing markup (`src/ui.js:779-841`, `src/ui.js:688-690`) and their handlers have non-config side effects (`src/ui.js:1412-1425`, `src/ui.js:1501-1503`).
7. **`src/core.js` — migration compatibility helper.** Extract or add a pure current-schema normalizer for history data from older `ver` values, without decrementing `state.configVer` or re-running world-key migration against arbitrary data. Keep startup `migrateConfig()` as the only state migration entry (`src/ui.js:1992-1997`).

## 5. State & storage

- New fields: `state.configUndo` and `state.configRedo`, each a maximum-20 array of `{schema,ver,at,reason,data}`. New keys are world-scoped (`src/header.js:193-215`) and pruned at 7 days on load/save; malformed or oversized entries are discarded.
- `configVer` remains the current schema after undo/redo. Do not add a separate version history key and do not lower `STORE.CONFIG_VER` (`src/header.js:132`, `src/core.js:507-510`).
- The existing `CONFIG_EXPORT_SCHEMA` is 3 (`src/qol.js:223`). Bump it only if the expanded canonical export changes its shape; record the schema in every snapshot and refuse future schemas using the existing import ceiling (`src/qol.js:254-256`).
- History excludes player/alliance notes, watchlist, webhook URL/chat id, CSRF, learned templates, findings, journal, locks, queues in flight, and host consent. Imported queue entries continue through the existing uncertain-state normalization (`src/qol.js:257-266`); an undo must never resurrect an in-flight job as accepted.

## 6. Config surface

- Add `Deshacer` and `Rehacer` buttons, disabled when their stack is empty, with compact counts `Deshacer (N)` / `Rehacer (N)`.
- Add status text `Último cambio: <reason>` and show migration normalization as `Normalizado: v<old> → v<current>`.
- No new automation toggle. `dryRun` remains user-controlled by the existing Config checkbox and handler (`src/ui.js:785`, `src/ui.js:1384-1389`); if an undo snapshot would change current `dryRun` from ON to OFF, preserve ON and log `config undo: dry-run safety preserved`.
- HIGH-RISK fields are not newly enabled by this feature; presets continue forcing them OFF (`src/qol.js:272-288`). Undo/redo may restore an explicitly user-enabled value already present in a snapshot, but must never synthesize one or accept an unlisted field.

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface is introduced: undo/redo only applies local validated configuration. There is no route, payload, `gbAjaxWatch`, `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`, `gbCaptchaPause` key, or lock; existing posts remain behind `bridgePost`/`gameAjaxPost` dry-run and precondition gates (`src/core.js:940-946`, `src/tx.js:531-555`). Do not add a new scheduler or `*InFlight` boolean. The dry-run-preservation rule above prevents the recovery control from turning a safe session live.

## 8. Failure modes

- Empty stack, malformed snapshot, expired entry, or future schema is a no-op with `flash('no hay cambios para deshacer/rehacer')` or `config history: snapshot refused`; it must not mutate state or storage.
- A snapshot whose version is older than current is normalized forward, never written backward. If a field was removed or rewritten by migration, leave the current/default normalized value and disclose that limitation in the Log; do not claim exact equality (`src/core.js:409-510`).
- A snapshot containing an unreadable/invalid value is rejected by the same validator that protects imports (`src/qol.js:254-267`). For any resulting live feature, every guard names the value it read; unreadable getter ⇒ `blind` ⇒ `gbLogT` once ⇒ let the server decide (`src/core.js:298-309`).
- Storage quota failure uses the existing prune/retry path (`src/core.js:1130-1213`); keep the in-memory stacks coherent with the successful write only. If persistence fails, log the failure and disable the corresponding button until the next reload rather than reporting durable history.
- Rapid clicks are serialized by a synchronous `recording` flag and button disable; no asynchronous callback or lock is needed. A failed apply puts the popped entry back on its original stack.

## 9. Validation gate

Low risk requires Preflight plus one in-game session with no failure (plan 27 §11). Change one Config checkbox, click `Deshacer`, verify the checkbox/value and exported canonical settings return to the prior state, then click `Rehacer` and verify the second state returns; Log must contain the reason and stack counts. Repeat with a numeric field, object field, preset button, template apply, and a valid import; each creates one entry, while cancel/invalid import/clear-captcha creates none. Turn dry-run ON, make a snapshot with it ON, change it OFF, undo, and confirm it stays ON. Simulate or retain a snapshot with `ver:9` while current is v10: undo must log normalization, keep `state.configVer` at v10, and leave queue/defense values valid; a `ver:11` snapshot must be refused without mutation. Reload and verify the 7-day bounded history persists, then switch worlds and verify the stacks are isolated. Stats/Preflight must still report normally and no game request may appear from undo/redo.

## 10. Out of scope

No undo for findings, farm scrape data, decision journal, learned payloads/templates, locks, runtime scheduler deadlines, queue outcomes, panel geometry, host consent, or secret-bearing webhook fields. No cross-world history merge, browser storage sync, server backup, test harness, or new scheduler. The Config wizard UI is 6.9; automatic profile rule evaluation is 6.8.

## 6.11-production-overlay.md

# 6.11 — Real-time resource production overlay

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extends `ui.js` for the widget body; consumes `culture.js`
`economyProductionRate` + `bridge.js` `townResState` for the data layer. The
plan 27 catalogue says "extend `ui.js`" — correct for the panel/widget shell,
but the **production data lives in `culture.js` and the cached resource state
in `bridge.js`**. Both are already exported and the work item is mostly
wiring, not invention.
**Depends on:** 6.2 (widget system contract)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

The data is already computed, just not surfaced as a real-time overlay:

- `src/bridge.js:235-273` — `townResState(townId)`. Reads
  `t.resources()` for `{wood, stone, iron}`, `t.getStorageCapacity()` for
  cap, returns `{cap, wood, stone, iron, full, n, fillPct}`. **3-second
  memo** (`TOWN_RES_CACHE_MS = 3000`, `bridge.js:234`). Used by 8 modules
  (cave, farms, planner, tx, orchestrate, etc. — `Grep` shows 14 call
  sites). This is the "current" half of the overlay.
- `src/culture.js:211-219` — `economyProductionRate(townId)`. Probes
  `t.getProduction()` first, `t.getResourceProduction()` next, then falls
  back to `t.resources()` reading `wood_production`/`production_wood` and
  friends. Returns `{wood, stone, iron}` per-hour or **null** if no getter
  reads finite. Already exported (`boot.js:176` exposes it on the boot
  surface).
- `src/culture.js:226-232` — `economyForecast(townId, horizonSec)`. Pulls
  `plannerSnapshot(townId)` (the shared warehouse reader at `core.js:687`),
  multiplies production by horizon, subtracts planned demand, returns
  `{projected, overflow, deficit, productionKnown}`. Already used by
  `qol.js:185` for the Overview "AVISO · almacén previsto al límite" line
  and by `qol.js:153` (simulator). The **plan 27 §0 row for 6.11 is "real-
  time production overlay"** — not forecast; we surface the rate directly,
  not the 6h projection, because the rate changes minute-to-minute as
  buildings finish.
- `src/qol.js:185` — Overview "AVISO" text already consumes overflow from
  `economyForecast`, **but** the rate itself (wood/h, stone/h, iron/h) is
  not rendered anywhere in the panel.
- `src/bridge.js:323` — `GB_RES_KEYS = ['wood', 'stone', 'iron']`. Reuse
  this constant rather than re-listing the keys in the widget body.

So the missing piece is **only the visual surface**: a small widget that
shows per-town wood/stone/iron plus the current production rate and the ETA
to cap. Everything else is already there.

## 2. Gap

No user-visible widget shows "this town makes 320 wood/h, 280 stone/h, 250
iron/h, and the warehouse fills in 2h 14m". Players who want this currently
eyeball the game's own building screen, which does not project ETAs to cap
and is hidden behind the Senate panel. The Overview "AVISO" line only fires
when a forecast predicts overflow at horizon (6h by default,
`state.predictCfg.horizonHours`). It does not show the rate live.

## 3. Design

A single widget, mounted via `gbWidget` (plan 6.2). Body renders a header row
"Producción" + a per-town list. The currently selected town is at the top
(driven by `gbCurrentTownId` — same getter the Queue Center uses,
`queue-center.js:336-337`); below it, the other towns in the same row order
the Queue Center tabs use. Each row has six cells:

```
town name | wood cur/rate | stone cur/rate | iron cur/rate | ETA → cap
```

Data flow per refresh tick:

1. Read `townResState(townId)` (`bridge.js:235`) — current stock and cap.
2. Read `economyProductionRate(townId)` (`culture.js:211`) — rate per
   resource, may be null.
3. ETA to cap: `Math.max(0, (cap - current) / rate)` in hours, rendered
   as `h:mm` (1h+ → `2h 14m`, sub-1h → `47m`, capped at `24h+`). Unreadable
   rate or current → render `—`.
4. Patch only the changed cells — same keyed-row pattern the rest of `ui.js`
   uses (`ui.js:92-101` `patchCells` for `tr[data-key]` rows, originally
   added in v1.4.0).

**Refresh cadence**: 1s when widget is open, 0 when closed. The widget owns
its own `gbInterval` (`core.js:23-29`, registered via `gbWidget`'s
`tickMs` option — see 6.2 §3). 1s is the existing cadence of
`gbInterval(renderTimers, 1000)` (`boot.js:66`) so this is not a new
scheduler tier.

**Why 1s will not burn CPU** (cross-ref plan 8.3 profiler):

- `townResState` already memoises for 3s (`bridge.js:234`), so most ticks
  hit the cache and only one Map lookup happens per town. Worst case: N
  towns × 1 cache lookup = `O(N)`. With 10 towns and a cache hit, this is
  trivial.
- `economyProductionRate` is **not** cached today. Cost: 3 method probes
  per town (`getProduction`, `getResourceProduction`, `resources()`). All
  three are model methods on the backbone collection; the game itself calls
  them on every render of the resource bar. At 1s × 10 towns = 30 calls/s,
  this is well below the threshold where the profiler (`stats.js`) flags
  a module. If profiling later shows it does, wrap with a 3s memo mirroring
  `TOWN_RES_CACHE_MS` (out of scope for this plan).
- DOM cost: 6 cells × 10 towns = 60 text nodes per second. Patch only on
  change (`textContent` assignment is cheap when the string is identical
  — the DOM does not reflow). Net: <0.5ms/tick on a modern desktop.
- **Belt-and-braces**: gate the entire render behind a `widget visible`
  check. If the user closes the widget, `gbWidget`'s tick stops firing.

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/ui.js`** — add `renderProductionOverlay(host)` near the existing
   `renderOverview` (`qol.js:192-222`). Imports nothing — both data sources
   are already global (`townResState`, `economyProductionRate`,
   `gbCurrentTownId`).
2. **`src/ui.js`** — register the widget once at module-init time
   (after `qol.js` exposes `gbWidget`, see 6.2 step 3):
   ```
   gbWidget.register({
     id: 'production-overlay',
     title: 'Producción',
     defaultPos: { left: '8px', top: '60px' },
     tickMs: 1000,
     render: renderProductionOverlay,
   });
   ```
3. **`src/header.js:24-187`** — add `STORE.WIDGET_PROD_CFG:
   'grepbot:widget-prod-cfg'` (only if Config needs persistence; see §6).
4. **`src/ui.js`** — call `renderProductionOverlay` from the existing
   `gbInterval(() => { renderOverview(); renderIntel(); … }, 15000)` at
   `boot.js:108-115` only **once** to do the initial mount — after that the
   widget's own 1s tick handles refresh. (Optional: skip this; the widget
   self-mounts on first Config toggle.)
5. **`src/stats.js`** — add a `production overlay` row to `preflightRun`
   that checks `typeof gbWidget === 'function'` and that
   `economyProductionRate` returns a non-null result for at least one town.

## 5. State & storage

- **No new state** for the widget itself. Position persistence comes from
  the 6.2 contract (`STORE.WIDGET_GEOM`, see 6.2 §5).
- `state.predictCfg.horizonHours` already exists (`header.js:154`,
  `STORE.PREDICT_CFG`); the widget reads it only as a default for the ETA
  cap render — no new key.
- **No world-scoping** required beyond what 6.2 already does for position.
- **No `configVer` bump** for 6.11 itself (only 6.2's bump).

## 6. Config surface

- `Producción: widget visible` — default OFF. Lives under the new
  Config → *Widgets* subsection added by 6.2 step 6. Reads/writes
  `state.widgetGeom['production-overlay'].hidden`.
- `Producción: ETA cap` — select `[1h, 6h, 24h, never]`; default `6h`.
  Controls the visual cap of the ETA-to-cap cell, **not** the forecast
  horizon (which already lives at `state.predictCfg.horizonHours`). Stores
  in `STORE.WIDGET_PROD_CFG` if added.
- No HIGH-RISK toggles. No `gbCaptchaPause` key needed.

## 7. Post surface & safety

Read-only. The widget calls `townResState`, `economyProductionRate`, and
reads the DOM. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbDomClick`. Skip the
rest of the checklist per the README "Read-mostly features: skip the rest".

## 8. Failure modes

- **`economyProductionRate` returns null** for all towns. The widget must
  not crash; render every rate cell as `—` and the ETA cell as `—`. The
  Overview "AVISO" line in `qol.js:185` already handles this case (it
  reads `productionKnown`), so the pattern is proven.
- **`gbCurrentTownId` unreadable**. The widget falls back to the first town
  id from `Object.keys(gameUw().ITowns.towns)`, same fallback
  `queue-center.js:336-338` uses. No blind post, no crash.
- **Player toggles widget off while it's mid-tick**. `gbWidget`'s `dispose`
  tears down the `gbInterval` via `gbTimerBag` (`core.js:23-29`,
  `core.js:118-121`). No tick survives disposal.
- **N+ towns, 1s tick**. Documented above; the 3s memo on `townResState`
  means we do not re-read the model each tick. If real profiling shows the
  uncached rate probe becomes hot, add a 3s memo to `economyProductionRate`
  in a follow-up (no spec change here).
- **Widget hidden by parent panel collapse**. `gbWidget` mounts at
  `document.body`, so GrepBot panel collapse does not affect it. The user
  can toggle independently.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk). One in-game session on `es146`:

- Toggle `Producción: widget visible` ON. Widget opens at default position;
  rate row appears for every town within 1s.
- Verify a town with full warehouses (`townResState().full.iron === true`)
  shows `iron 0/h` (rate, not current — current is the cap value) and ETA
  `—` (rate exists but current === cap). Log shows no errors.
- Verify a town whose model returns `null` from
  `economyProductionRate` shows `—` in every rate cell. Toggle Config →
  reset widget position, reopen — lands back at default.
- Drag widget to `(400, 300)`, close, reopen. Lands at `(400, 300)`
  (persistence comes from 6.2).
- **Preflight**: `production overlay` row green.
- **Profiler**: with widget open, run `preflightRun` then read the per-
  module CPU row (plan 8.3 — not yet shipped, but `gbLog` already exposes
  module timings via `core.js:516-529`). The overlay module should appear
  under 5ms/tick. If it does not, memo `economyProductionRate` (out of
  scope here, file a follow-up).

## 10. Out of scope

- Net flow (production − consumption): production rate alone is enough for
  the catalogue row; net flow needs per-town build queue cost tracking.
  That is the 2.7 (population) / 2.8 (capping) territory, owned by their
  own plans.
- Charting (line over time). Plan 6.12 ("City growth timeline chart")
  covers this; do not duplicate.
- Forecast horizon alerts. Already shipped via `economyForecast` at
  `culture.js:226`; `qol.js:185` surfaces the "AVISO" line in Overview.
- World-scoped forecast persistence — `state.predictCfg.horizonHours`
  already persists.
- Touch drag — same deferral as 6.2.

## 6.12-growth-timeline-chart.md

# 6.12 — City growth timeline chart

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extend `src/stats.js` (render-only HUD); add `STORE.TOWN_GROWTH_HIST` to `src/header.js`; sampling hook in `src/towns.js`; UI town selector in `src/ui.js`
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2 (header `@version` is `3.9.0`; off by one, harmless)

> The catalogue row says "mermaid line". This plan does **not** ship mermaid.
> There is no `mermaid`, no `chart`, no `<svg>`, no `<canvas>` anywhere in
> `src/` today (verified by ripgrep over `src/`). Loading a 600KB CDN-hosted
> renderer from a userscript violates plan 27 §0 (no phone-home, paste-only,
> no server) and `CLAUDE.md` "NO SERVER" / "no local server" / "bot is
> paste-only". The honest deliverable is a text sparkline in the same
> `textContent` discipline the existing Stats body already uses
> (`stats.js:354` `box.textContent = lines.join('\n')`). The catalogue's
> "mermaid line" intent is preserved as a per-cell series of bar characters
> rendered in a `<pre>` block — readable, zero-network, XSS-safe.

---

## 1. What exists today

- The only per-town snapshot storage is `state.townResources[id]` (`src/core.js:230`,
  `src/towns.js:163-167, 210-213`). It carries exactly **one** entry per town
  (`{ts, wood, stone, iron, pop, cap, ok, action}`) and is **overwritten**
  on every scrape. There is no append, no ring, no history. Confirmed by
  ripgrep over `src/`: zero hits for `townGrowth`, `growthHist`,
  `popHist`, `appendSample`, `sampleLog`.
- `state.findings` is the closest existing time-indexed series
  (`src/core.js:228`, pruned by `storagePruneForQuota` at `core.js:1188-1190`).
  It is **intel reports**, capped at 100 entries FIFO-dropped on quota, not
  town growth. Using it as a growth source would conflate two signals and
  still lose older entries on quota.
- The closest "history" stores are `state.attackHistory`, `state.attackRecent`,
  `state.questHistory`, `state.banditLog` (all `src/core.js:280-298`). None is
  per-town population / resources.
- `townResState(townId)` (`src/bridge.js:235`) returns the **live** snapshot
  via `ITowns.getTown(id).resources()` with a 3s in-memory cache. It is the
  read path the sampler must call — already proven safe by
  `src/preflight.js` probe `cost reads` at `stats.js:188-209`.
- `state.towns` (`src/core.js:229`, set at `towns.js:71, 122, 197`) is the
  canonical town list (`{id, name, x, y, island}`). The chart needs one
  selector entry per `state.towns[i].id`.
- `renderStats` (`src/stats.js:280-355`) is the existing Stats renderer. It
  writes to `panel.querySelector('.stats-body')` via `textContent`
  (`stats.js:354`). A new `.growth-panel` `<pre>` sibling can be added in
  the same section without touching the existing `stats-body`.
- The Stats tab HTML lives in `src/ui.js:847-853`: window buttons
  `[data-stats="1h|24h|7d"]` already exist; the section is hidden until
  the tab is opened (`ui.js:373, 394` re-renders on tab switch).
- `worldKey` / `wkey()` is applied by `load()` / `save()` for any key in
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`src/header.js:193-215`, `src/core.js:1100-1116`).
  A new `STORE.TOWN_GROWTH_HIST` key with id-bearing payload must be added
  to that set.
- `storagePruneForQuota` (`src/core.js:1129-1207`) is the last-resort
  pruner for `QuotaExceeded`. Plan 20 (CODED, `core.js:1187`) ships it;
  the new key's append path must respect its cap (see §5).

## 2. Gap

The catalogue asks for "city growth timeline chart (mermaid line)". The
player-visible question — *"is my main town still growing, and at what
rate?"* — has no answer in the panel today, because no time-series exists.
The honest deliverable is: **(a) add a per-town daily sample of population,
wood, stone, iron totals, warehouse capacity, and building count** (a
single append per town per local day, capped), and **(b) render an ASCII
sparkline of those samples inside the existing Stats tab** so the player
can read growth at a glance.

## 3. Design

Read-only HUD. No post surface, no captcha breaker, no lock, no
scheduler entry, no `gbInterval`. The sampler runs inline off the
existing `scrapeAllTowns` cadence (every 6–7 min) — see §3.2 below for
why no new scheduler is added.

### 3.1 Renderer

Add a new block to `renderStats` (`src/stats.js:280-355`) after the
deadlock notice (`stats.js:326-330`) and before the orchestrator rollup
(`stats.js:331`). The block renders only when `state.towns.length > 0`
AND `state.townGrowthHist` has at least one entry for the selected town.

Per render, for the **selected town id** (default `state.towns[0].id`):

```
crecimiento — Aldea <name> (id <id>)   ult. <N> muestras (max 7d)
  pob    <mini-sparkline>   <first> → <last>   Δ <delta> / <spanDays>d
  wood   <mini-sparkline>   <first> → <last>   Δ <delta> / <spanDays>d
  stone  <mini-sparkline>   <first> → <last>   Δ <delta> / <spanDays>d
  iron   <mini-sparkline>   <first> → <last>   Δ <delta> / <spanDays>d
  cap    <mini-sparkline>   <first> → <last>   Δ <delta> / <spanDays>d
```

Sparkline glyph set: `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█` (Unicode U+2581..U+2588). Render is the
existing `textContent` discipline: each line is a string, joined with
`\n`, assigned to `box.textContent`. **No** `innerHTML`. This is the
same discipline as `intel.js:112` and `stats.js:354`. The audit I15
record (zero `innerHTML` in quests.js, plan 26) sets the rule.

Sparkline math: bucket the samples into ≤ 24 columns (one column per
hour across the visible 7d window, or one per day if the span is < 24h),
take the mean per bucket, normalize to `[0..7]` over the per-row min/max,
emit one glyph per bucket. Two or fewer samples render `—`. Samples
where the value is `null` (unreadable that day) render `·` and are
excluded from min/max.

### 3.2 Sampler hook

Wire into `scrapeAllTowns` (`src/towns.js:181-228`), not into a new
`gbInterval`. The function already runs every 6–7 min per town and
holds the `town-scrape` lock (`towns.js:183-184`). The sampler is one
call at the end of the `finish()` path (after the per-town writes at
`towns.js:163-167, 210-213`):

```js
function townGrowthSample() {
  if (!Array.isArray(state.towns) || !state.towns.length) return;
  const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10); // YYYY-MM-DD, local day
  const hist = state.townGrowthHist || (state.townGrowthHist = {});
  for (const t of state.towns) {
    const r = state.townResources[t.id];
    if (!r || r.ok !== true) continue;
    const entry = { ts: Date.now(), day: today,
      pop: r.pop ?? null, wood: r.wood ?? null, stone: r.stone ?? null,
      iron: r.iron ?? null, cap: r.cap ?? null };
    const arr = hist[t.id] || (hist[t.id] = []);
    const last = arr[arr.length - 1];
    if (last && last.day === today) continue; // one per local day
    arr.push(entry);
    while (arr.length > TOWN_GROWTH_MAX) arr.shift();
  }
  save(STORE.TOWN_GROWTH_HIST, state.townGrowthHist);
}
```

Cap constant `TOWN_GROWTH_MAX = 7` (one entry per local day, 7-day
window). The store key goes in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (id-bearing, see §5).

The sampler is called from `scrapeAllTowns`'s `finish(fromGame, fromHttp)`
(`towns.js:188-193`) **after** `pruneMapsToIds(state.townResources, ids)`
(`towns.js:191`). That way stale towns do not produce new samples and a
town that has been transferred out does not leave a phantom row.

### 3.3 Selector

The Intel / Overview tabs already have town selectors (see
`ui.js:587`, the Attack planner's `data-atk="pick"`). The Stats tab does
not. The plan adds one `[data-growth="town"]` `<select>` inside the
Stats section header (`ui.js:847-853`), populated from `state.towns` on
each `renderStats`. Default selection is the first town; switching the
selector re-renders only the growth block. The selector is built with
`document.createElement('option')` and `appendChild` — no `innerHTML`.

### 3.4 Window parity

The existing `[data-stats="1h|24h|7d"]` buttons (`ui.js:847-849`) drive
`statsWindow` (`ui.js:939` → `military.js:257-258`). The growth chart
ignores `statsWindow` and uses its own 7d window, because the underlying
sample is daily. This is honest: a 1h window over a daily sample is
always one column. A short note in the block header makes the window
explicit (`max 7d`).

## 4. Work items
