## 5. State & storage

- New `state.townGrowthHist` (`{}`, id-keyed), `STORE.TOWN_GROWTH_HIST`
  in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (id-bearing payload ⇒ yes, per CLAUDE.md
  "World-scope id-bearing storage").
- Per-town array `{ts, day, pop, wood, stone, iron, cap}`, capped at
  `TOWN_GROWTH_MAX = 7` entries; ring shift in `townGrowthSample`
  (`while (arr.length > TOWN_GROWTH_MAX) arr.shift()`).
- **Size estimate.** Worst case: 12 towns × 7 entries × ~80 bytes
  (serialized JSON with `day` + 6 numbers) ≈ **6.7 KB** world-scoped.
  Cross-ref plan 20 (CODED, `core.js:1187` storage quota alarm): a new
  ~7 KB key is < 0.1% of the typical `GM_setValue` quota headroom and
  is the right size for plan 20's alarm to ignore without false
  positives. The 7d cap matches plan 27 §13 ("Storage prune TTL: 7d
  uniform unless the slice needs longer").
- `configVer` bump to 11 (see §4.1) so existing users pick up the new
  field without a state-shaped migration.
- No `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry. The sampler is inline in an
  already-locked path (`towns.js:184` `gbLock('town-scrape', 300000)`).

## 6. Config surface

No toggle. The growth block is **always** rendered when the panel has
the Stats tab active, the town selector is populated, and at least one
town has ≥ 2 samples. No HIGH-RISK toggle to set OFF (Low risk; read-only).

The only Config interaction is the new `[data-growth="town"]` selector
inside the Stats section. It is render-time, not Config, and persists
nothing beyond `growthSelectedTownId` (a session-local in `stats.js` —
**not** persisted, like `statsWindow` at `military.js:257-258`).

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbDomClick`,
no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no `gbCaptchaPause`
key. The chart reads only. The sampler appends to local storage only.

The renderer uses `box.textContent = …` (`stats.js:354`-style). The
selector uses `createElement('option')` + `appendChild` (per `CLAUDE.md`
"DOM fallback" hygiene). This matches the audit-I15 XSS discipline
recorded in plan 26 — chart markup goes through `textContent`, never
`innerHTML`.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`townResState(id)` unreadable** — `townGrowthSample` skips towns
  where `state.townResources[id].ok !== true` (§3.2). Sparkline cells
  with `null` samples render `·` and are excluded from min/max; the row
  still renders the other numeric columns. No silent dead row.
- **Selector on a town with no samples** — `growthBlock` returns `[]`
  and the chart emits one line `crecimiento — sin muestras para <name>`
  instead of a partial sparkline. The precondition invariant: every
  block guard reads the value it gates on.
- **Quota pressure** — `townGrowthHist` is small (~7 KB worst case, §5)
  but `storagePruneForQuota` (`core.js:1129-1207`) trims it implicitly
  via `SAVE` retry on `QuotaExceeded`. The cap at 7 entries per town
  already matches the journal/decision pattern (`journal.js` 7-day TTL
  per plan 27 §13).
- **Sampler race** — the sampler is called from inside the held
  `town-scrape` lock (`towns.js:184`), so a second `scrapeAllTowns`
  cannot double-append. If `hostEnabled()` is false the sampler is
  a no-op.
- **Day rollover at the seam** — `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`
  is UTC. The bot's local-day rollover differs from UTC at most by a
  few hours; if the user cares, they can flip to a local-day string.
  The off-by-one is documented; it does not lose data (the `day !==
  today` guard would just delay the next append by up to 24h on the
  seam, which is invisible at the daily cadence).
- **Time-zone change** — same as above; the `day` field is a string,
  the chart sorts by `ts` for display.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), install, open the Stats tab.
- The new `[data-growth="town"]` selector lists every town from
  `state.towns`.
- After one in-game day with `scrapeAllTowns` running, the selected
  town's `crecimiento — <name>` block shows at least one sparkline
  glyph per row. Empty state: `crecimiento — sin muestras para <name>`.
- After seven in-game days, each sparkline is ≤ 24 columns and the
  block header reports `max 7d`.
- Manually click `state.dryRun = true` (`DRY-RUN` toggle in Config);
  the chart still renders (no post surface was added). Log has no new
  post-related entries.
- Run Preflight (`Comprobar sistema`); the existing `towns` row
  (`stats.js:24-27`) still passes. The chart is not gated by Preflight.
- Open a fresh world with no `state.townGrowthHist` — selector is
  populated, chart block emits the `sin muestras` line, no errors.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Per-building growth.** Building levels would need a separate
  sampler keyed by `ITowns.town(id).buildings()`; that is a future plan
  (cross-ref plan 27 §6.11 "real-time production overlay" — its data
  layer is the same `ITowns` model, but the read paths differ).
- **Mermaid / SVG / canvas.** Rejected by §3.1. If a future plan needs
  pixel rendering, it ships its own bundled renderer in `src/` and
  pays the size cost itself; the build's ASCII-escape gate
  (`ascii_escape_artifact`, CLAUDE.md) makes it tractable.
- **Alliance / cross-city view.** Cross-ref plan 6.13
  (`6.13-alliance-intel-heatmap.md`); the data sources do not overlap.
- **Trade-route / transport growth.** Plan 27 §1.3 owns transport
  automation. Once 1.3 ships, an extra sparkline row for transport
  events can be added without a separate plan.
- **Real-time per-tick update.** The current cadence is the daily
  append; a per-tick append would cost a write per town per 6–7 min,
  i.e. ~100 KB/day for the same chart. Not justified at the current
  sample size.
- **Auto-export of growth as webhook / Discord attachment.** Out of
  plan 27 §0; webhooks are for events, not bulk data dumps.

## 6.13-alliance-intel-heatmap.md

# 6.13 — Alliance intel heatmap

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js` (read-only aggregator + renderer); add `data-alliance` selector in `src/ui.js`; no `src/header.js` change (no new key)
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2 (header `@version` is `3.9.0`; off by one, harmless)

> "Heatmap" is rendered as a text grid in the existing
> `box.textContent = html` discipline (`src/intel.js:112`). Same
> justification as plan 6.12 §3.1: there is no `<svg>`, `<canvas>`,
> `mermaid`, or `chart` renderer in `src/` today (verified by ripgrep),
> and shipping one would violate plan 27 §0 (no phone-home, paste-only)
> plus `CLAUDE.md` "NO SERVER". An ASCII grid where each cell is a
> density glyph ` .,:;|+*#@` matches the existing `textContent`
> discipline and the audit-I15 XSS rule.

---

## 1. What exists today

- `intelDossiers()` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) is the only per-player
  aggregator in the tree. It walks `state.findings`, picks the
  "other side" via `intelActorIsMe`, and groups by `intelPlayerKey`.
  It reads `f.alliance` (string) on each finding at
  `intel.js:66-67` for `state.allianceNotes[alliance]` lookup. **It
  does not aggregate by alliance** — there is no `byAlliance` reducer.
- `intelPatternScan()` (`src/intel.js:206-245`) aggregates by **player**
  over a 24h window (`windowMs = 24 * 3600000` at `intel.js:208`). The
  same shape can be lifted to alliance-level with no new state.
- `intelSetAllianceNote(alliance, note)` (`src/intel.js:124-132`) exists
  and is wired at `src/ui.js:1002-1007`. Plan 26 §B2 named a missing
  setter; it was added between plan-of-record v2.9.1 and the current
  v3.8.2 (the row in plan 27 §9 also notes this — it is "Coded").
- `state.findings` (`src/core.js:228`) is the only alliance-indexed
  store. It carries one row per parsed intel report
  (`parseReport` at `src/parse-inline.js:36-86`) with `alliance`
  (`parse-inline.js:89`) — the attacker (or defender, if the attacker
  is me) alliance string. **Cap: 100 entries** (`storagePruneForQuota`
  at `core.js:1188-1190`); the array is FIFO-dropped on quota. There
  is **no `MM` Alliance collection** referenced anywhere in `src/`
  (verified by ripgrep — zero hits for `getCollectionByName('Alliance')`,
  `getAlliances()`, `alliancesCollection`). Alliance keys in this
  codebase are **opaque strings seen in report payloads**, not model
  objects.
- `state.allianceNotes` (`src/core.js:341`) is the player's free-text
  notes per alliance (`intel.js:124-132`). Keys are the same opaque
  strings as `f.alliance`. It is already exported with redaction in
  `qol.js:238`.
- `state.watchlist` (`src/core.js:338`, `intel.js:148-181`) can match
  by `entry.alliance` (`intel.js:171-173`) — the heatmap is the natural
  reader of the same key.
- `renderIntel()` (`src/intel.js:75-114`) writes the intel panel via
  `box.textContent = html` (`intel.js:112`). The same function calls
  `intelPatternScan()` at the end (`intel.js:113`). A new alliance
  block slots in before the existing `state.watchlist` block at
  `intel.js:98-102` without changing the existing order.
- The intel tab HTML (`src/ui.js:693-704`) is a single `<pre
  class="intel-panel">` plus two note-save inputs. The plan adds a
  selector inside that section to choose between two views: existing
  `intel-panel` (default) and the new heatmap view. No structural
  change to the panel chrome.
- `redactNotes` (`src/qol.js:230`) already handles `allianceNotes`
  export redaction (`qol.js:238`). The heatmap is read-only so redaction
  is a non-concern.

## 2. Gap

The catalogue asks for an "alliance intel heatmap". Today the only
alliance-aware read is `state.allianceNotes[f.alliance]` on the dossier
line (`intel.js:66-67`), and the alliance-notes dump at
`intel.js:103-108`. The player-visible question — *"which alliances are
spiking, and against which of my towns?"* — has no aggregated answer in
the panel. The honest deliverable is an ASCII grid keyed by (alliance,
my-town-id) where each cell counts reports in the rolling 7-day window
(the same 7-day window the journal TTL enforces, plan 27 §13).

## 3. Design

Read-only. No post surface, no captcha breaker, no lock, no scheduler
entry. The aggregator runs inside `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`),
mirroring the existing `intelPatternScan()` call (`intel.js:113`).

### 3.1 Aggregator

Add `intelAllianceMatrix(windowMs)` to `src/intel.js`, returning:

```js
{
  alliances: ['<name>', …],         // sorted by total desc
  towns: ['<myTownId>', …],         // sorted by id
  totalForAlliance: { name: n },    // row totals
  totalForTown: { myTownId: n },    // column totals
  cells: { '<name>::<myTownId>': n },
  windowMs, cutoffTs,
}
```

Inputs and rules:

- Walk `state.findings` once. For each finding with a string
  `f.alliance` and a `f.town.id` (the defender's town), pick
  `f.town.id` as the column if the town is **mine**, else pick
  `f.town.id` if the attacker is from `f.alliance` and the defender
  is mine. The "is mine" check reuses the existing `intelActorIsMe`
  helper (`intel.js:28-33`).
- Skip findings older than `windowMs` (default 7d). The same
  `windowMs = 24 * 3600000` shape at `intel.js:208` works — just bump
  the default to `7 * 86400000` for this aggregator only.
- Skip findings where `f.alliance` is `null`, `''`, `'?'`, or otherwise
  not a string of length 1–40. The cap is to keep the row labels
  readable and to drop game-client placeholders.
- Sort alliances by `totalForAlliance[name]` desc, then by name asc.
  Cap at 12 rows in the rendered grid (top-12). Smaller alliances
  collapse into one `(+N alianzas)` footer row with its own total.
- The "my town" list comes from `state.towns` (`src/core.js:229`,
  `src/towns.js:71, 122, 197`) filtered to **towns that appear as
  defender in at least one finding with an alliance-attributed
  attacker** — i.e. only the towns that are actually under intel
  pressure, not every own town. Cap at 8 columns; remainder collapses
  into a `(+M ciudades)` footer column with its own total.

### 3.2 Renderer

In `renderIntel` (`src/intel.js:75-114`), insert before the watchlist
block (`intel.js:98-102`):

```
=== Heatmap de alianzas (7d) ===
              Col1  Col2  Col3  …  +M   total
AllyA           3     1     -    …   1     5
AllyB           -     -     2    …   -     2
…
(+N alianzas)    -     -     -    …   1     1
total           3     1     2    …   2     8
```

Each cell renders one density glyph from ` .,:;|+*#@` keyed off
`cells[name::myTownId]`. Mapping: 0 → ` `, 1 → `.`, 2 → `,`, 3 → `:`,
4 → `;`, 5 → `|`, 6 → `+`, 7 → `*`, 8+ → `#`, 20+ → `@` (the upper
band). The exact binning does not matter; what matters is that the
glyph ordering is monotone. Alliance and town labels are truncated to
the first 12 characters with `…` if longer — same shape as the
existing dossier line at `intel.js:93-97`. All output is concatenated
with `\n` and appended to `html` (the `box.textContent = html`
discipline at `intel.js:112`). **No** `innerHTML`.

### 3.3 View toggle

The Intel tab already has two note inputs and one big `<pre>`. Add one
more control: a `[data-intel="view"]` `<select>` with options
`Resumen` (default, today's behaviour) and `Heatmap 7d`. The selector
goes immediately under the section title (`ui.js:693` `<div
style="font-size:11px;color:#f5a623;margin-bottom:4px">Intel /
amenazas</div>`). The renderer checks `state.intelView` (a new field,
**session-local**, see §5) and emits either the existing dump
(`intel.js:83-111`) or the new heatmap block. Switching the selector
calls `renderIntel()` — same call site as the existing watchlist
refresh at `ui.js:1002`.

`state.intelView` is **session-local** (a plain `let intelView = …` in
`intel.js` next to `let questMo = null` at `intel.js:249`). It does
**not** persist. Justification: it is a UI mode, not a configuration;
persisting it would force a `configVer` bump and a new `STORE.*` key
for no observable benefit across reloads. The selector's default is
always the existing dump.

### 3.4 Existing watchlist + notes

The existing watchlist match (`intel.js:171-173`) already keys by
`entry.alliance`. The heatmap surfaces the **same** string, so the two
features compose: a user who adds an alliance to `state.watchlist` as
`{alliance: 'AllyA'}` will see the `AllyA` row of the heatmap light up
in real time (next `renderIntel` cycle). The existing pattern-scan
webhook at `intel.js:241-242` continues to fire on the player-level
threshold (`n >= 3`); the heatmap adds nothing new there.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelAllianceMatrix(windowMs)` per §3.1,
   placed next to `intelPatternScan` (`intel.js:206-245`). Default
   `windowMs = 7 * 86400000`. Reuse the `intelActorIsMe` check
   (`intel.js:28-33`); do **not** duplicate the helper. The function
   must be defensive: empty `state.findings` ⇒ return the empty shape
   (all keys missing), not throw.
2. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) with a
   `if (intelView === 'heatmap')` branch that emits **only** the
   heatmap block and `return`s early (skip the existing dump blocks at
   `intel.js:82-111`). The early return is to keep the panel readable;
   the existing dump is verbose (`:83-97, 99-101, 103-108, 109-111`).
   Keep `try { intelPatternScan(); } catch (_) {}` at the bottom of
   either branch (`intel.js:113`) — the pattern scan is orthogonal.
3. `src/intel.js` — add `let intelView = 'summary';` at module scope
   next to `let questMo = null;` (`intel.js:249`). It is plain
   session-local state; no `state.*`, no `save()`.
4. `src/ui.js` — in the Intel section header (`ui.js:693-704`), add a
   `<select data-intel="view">` with two `<option>`s (`Resumen`,
   `Heatmap 7d`). Use `createElement('option')` and `appendChild`; no
   `innerHTML`. Wire its `change` handler in the same block that
   already wires the `gb-note-save` and `gb-anote-save` handlers
   (`ui.js:1002-1007`): on change, set `intelView = value;
   renderIntel();`.
5. `src/stats.js` — extend `preflightRun` (`src/stats.js:12-268`) with
   a new `intel alliance matrix` row that calls `intelAllianceMatrix(7 *
   86400000)` and reports `{alliances: N, towns: M, total: T}`. The
   row is pass / warn based on whether any alliance rows were
   non-empty (an "all-warm" heatmap with all zero cells is useless —
   warn the user). One-line addition; no new state, no new key.
6. **No `src/header.js` change.** No new `STORE.*` key — `state.findings`
   already carries the data. No `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry. No
   `configVer` bump (this is a UI-mode toggle, not a config schema
   change; see §3.3).

## 5. State & storage

None new. The aggregator reads only `state.findings`, `state.towns`,
`state.allianceNotes`, `state.watchlist`, `state.playerNotes`, and
the existing `intelActorIsMe` / `intelPlayerKey` helpers.

The session-local `intelView` is a plain `let` inside `intel.js` (§4.3).
It is **not** persisted, **not** in `state.*`, **not** in
`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`. Across reloads the selector defaults back to
`Resumen`. This matches the existing `statsWindow` pattern at
`src/military.js:257-258` (also session-local, also a UI mode).

## 6. Config surface

No toggle. The heatmap is gated by the new `[data-intel="view"]`
selector (§3.3) inside the Intel section. No HIGH-RISK toggle to set
OFF (Low risk; read-only).

The existing Config fields — `autoDodge` (`core.js:329`), `csAlert`
(`core.js:337`), watchlist (`core.js:338`), `playerNotes`
(`core.js:336`), `allianceNotes` (`core.js:341`) — are **unaffected**.
The heatmap is a render layer on top of `state.findings`, not a
configuration change.

## 7. Post surface & safety

No post surface. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbDomClick`,
no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry, no
`gbCaptchaPause` key. The aggregator reads only.

The renderer uses `box.textContent = html` (the same call as today at
`intel.js:112`). The selector uses `createElement('option')` +
`appendChild`. Audit-I15 XSS discipline (plan 26): zero `innerHTML`
where a player-controlled string is rendered. The alliance name is
player-controlled (it comes from `f.alliance`, which is parsed from
report JSON by `parse-inline.js:89`). The label truncation to 12
characters (§3.2) is a defense-in-depth; the primary defense is
`textContent`, which never parses the string as markup.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`state.findings` empty** — every row/column total is 0; the heatmap
  renders the header + one `0 totales` line. No `null`s, no crashes.
- **`f.alliance` missing on most findings** — many cells render ` `,
  the row totals are 0; the `+N alianzas` footer row collapses the
  empty ones. The block is still rendered so the user sees "no signal".
- **Top-12 / Top-8 caps clip the user's most-interesting alliance** —
  the footer shows `(+N alianzas)` and a total so the user can spot
  the cutoff. The default cap is generous (12 rows × 8 columns = 96
  cells); a future plan can lift the cap if `state.findings` grows
  past 100 entries.
- **Quota prune drops the oldest findings** — `storagePruneForQuota`
  (`core.js:1188-1190`) caps `state.findings` at 100 FIFO entries.
  The 7-day window in the heatmap header can be a lie if the user's
  reports are old enough that the cap clipped more than 7 days.
  Mitigation: include `cutoffTs` in the block header (`ventana
  2026-08-03 → 2026-08-10, N=87 informes`); if `cutoffTs > 7d ago` and
  the count is at the cap, warn "findings al limite de quota: el
  historial de 7d puede estar incompleto". One line; no separate
  probe.
- **Alliance string drift across parses** — `f.alliance` is a raw
  string from report JSON (`parse-inline.js:89`). Two clients could
  spell the same alliance differently ("AllyA" vs "Ally A"); the
  heatmap would render them as separate rows. This is the existing
  dossier-line behavior (`intel.js:66-67`) — fixing it is a
  string-normalization plan, not this one. Documented.
- **`intelView` survives a reload** — explicitly does **not** survive
  reload (§3.3, §5). The selector defaults to `Resumen` on every page
  load. Documented in the selector's `title` attribute ("se reinicia
  al recargar").

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), install, open the Intel tab. The
  selector shows `Resumen` (default) and `Heatmap 7d`.
- With `state.findings` empty (fresh world, no reports parsed): the
  heatmap emits one line `sin informes en 7d` and exits cleanly.
- After parsing 3 reports spanning 2 alliances and 2 of my towns: the
  heatmap renders a 2 × 2 grid with one density glyph per cell and
  matching row/column totals.
- Add `state.allianceNotes = { 'AllyA': 'spike' }` via the existing
  alliance-note UI (`ui.js:1002`); reopen the heatmap — the
  `AllyA` row gains the note ` — spike` after the alliance name. The
  truncation rule (12 chars + `…`) applies only to the matrix label,
  not to the note.
- Add a watchlist entry `{alliance: 'AllyA'}` and reload — the
  `AllyA` row still renders in the heatmap, the existing watchlist
  block at `intel.js:98-102` still matches on the next report.
- Preflight (`Comprobar sistema`) — new `intel alliance matrix` row
  appears; passes when `state.findings.length > 0`, warns when the
  matrix renders but every cell is zero.
- `state.dryRun = true` — heatmap still renders; no new posts in the
  Log tab. Confirm by reading the journal (Decisions sub-view, `mem`).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Alliance-member activity.** Cross-ref plan 27 §7.6 ("Alliance
  member activity dashboard"). Its data layer is `MM.getCollection
  ('Alliance')`/`Player`-by-alliance, which is **not** read today.
  Adding that would require the missing `Alliance` collection probe;
  out of scope here.
- **Alliance resource pool.** Cross-ref plan 27 §7.3. Same shape —
  needs an `Alliance` model read path; out of scope here.
- **NAP / war tracking.** Cross-ref plan 27 §7.5. The heatmap is the
  *passive observation* view; a `NAP` toggle would be a separate
  state field. The heatmap surfaces what is in `state.findings`; it
  does not infer relationships.
- **Per-day bucketing in the heatmap.** The current design shows the
  *total* across the window. A future plan can break it into 7 daily
  columns (one per day) at the cost of column count and density —
  not worth the read-path complexity yet.
- **Mermaid / SVG / pixel rendering.** Rejected by §3.2. Same
  justification as 6.12.
- **Cross-alliance attack-pattern detection.** `intelPatternScan`
  (`intel.js:206-245`) already runs a player-level pattern scan and
  fires the `pattern` webhook (`intel.js:241-242`). Lifting that to
  alliance-level is a separate plan; the heatmap is the read-side
  companion, not a writer.
- **Auto-export of the matrix.** Out of plan 27 §0. Webhooks are for
  events; bulk data dumps cross the line.

## 6.14-attack-landing-countdown.md

# 6.14 — Attack landing timeline visual countdown

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** S
**Module:** extends `ui.js` (widget body) + `intel.js` (sort/filter helper).
The plan 27 catalogue says "extend `ui.js` + `military.js`", but on read the
only military-side function we need is `dodgeEtaSec` which already lives in
`src/dodge.js:175-180`. `src/military.js` does not contribute new logic for
this feature. **No code change to `military.js`** — the catalogue row's
second module hint is wrong; the data is in `dodge.js`.
**Depends on:** 6.2 (widget system contract)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- `src/dodge.js:53-84` — `dodgeIncomingMovements()`. Returns one row per
  hostile inbound movement: `{id, dest, origin, type, hasCs, arrival,
  units, model}`. The hostile-only filter is the v1.5.3 audit rule
  (`DODGE_HOSTILE_TYPES` regex at `dodge.js:39`, `dodgeIsHostileMovement`
  at `dodge.js:41-52` — never trust `incoming`/`started_at` alone, see
  CLAUDE.md "dodge hostile-only").
- `src/dodge.js:175-180` — `dodgeEtaSec(mov)`. Returns `Math.max(0,
  arrival - gameNow())` in seconds. Handles the >1e12 ms-vs-seconds
  heuristic. **This is the function the widget renders against.**
- `src/intel.js:72-74` — `intelThreatBoard()` already calls
  `dodgeIncomingMovements()`. `renderIntel` at `src/intel.js:75-114` prints
  a text-only line per incoming attack with `riesgo`, `ETA`, `apoyo`,
  `esquivar` columns. The data is **already** in the Intel tab — but it
  is text, sorted by arrival order only by accident (the underlying
  collection returns in arbitrary order), and there is no visual
  countdown ticking down each second.
- `src/qol.js:162` — `dodgeIncomingMovements()` is also called from
  `renderDashboard` for the Overview "Amenazas" card.
- `src/dodge.js:175-180` already exists; the function is exported and
  reachable.

Plan 27 §9's 15-item "already shipped" list does **not** contain 6.14. The
nearest neighbours are "Support ETA, attack pattern, watchlist why"
(plan 27 §9 line 249 — `intel.js:89, 109-111, 133-193`) but those are
threat-board heuristics, not a visual countdown widget. **This is a
genuinely missing surface.**

## 2. Gap

A player under attack has to:
1. Switch to the Intel tab.
2. Read the text line.
3. Mentally subtract `gameNow()` from the displayed `arrival` epoch.

The Intel tab is one click + one mental subtraction away from "is this
attack landing in 30s or 30m?". Plan 6.14 closes that gap with a small
floating widget that ticks the ETA down each second, sorted by arrival
(soonest first), with a colour escalation (green → yellow → red) as the
landing window approaches.

## 3. Design

Single widget, mounted via `gbWidget` (plan 6.2). Body renders one row per
incoming hostile movement, sorted by arrival ascending. Each row has:

```
[ETA mm:ss ticking] type → dest from origin [CS] [units summary]
```

Cells:

- **ETA cell** — `dodgeEtaSec(mov)` formatted `m:ss` (≥1h shows `1h 02m`,
  per `queueCenterFmt` pattern at `queue-center.js:55-60`, reuse it). Updates
  every tick.
- **type** — `mov.type || 'atk'` (lowercased canonical form already from
  `dodge.js:71`).
- **dest / origin** — `townNameById` (already a global helper used by
  `military.js:176`). Falls back to the raw id if the model is unreadable.
- **CS badge** — only when `mov.hasCs` (the existing flag from
  `dodge.js:73`). Colour: red `#c44` regardless of ETA, since CS is its own
  alarm.
- **units** — sum of `Object.values(mov.units).reduce(+)` for a quick
  "180" badge. Do **not** enumerate unit types in this widget — that is
  the Intel tab's job and the panel already shows it.

**Colour escalation** by ETA (CSS only, no logic changes to `intel.js`):

- `> 30 min` — `#6cf` (cyan, calm)
- `5–30 min` — `#fc6` (amber)
- `< 5 min` — `#f66` (red, pulses via CSS animation)
- `0` (landed) — row gets `.gb-widget-eta-landed` class, dimmed text,
  removed after 30s of absence (when `dodgeIncomingMovements` no longer
  returns it — the collection itself drops landed movements).

**Refresh cadence**: 1s, owned by the widget's `tickMs` (same as 6.11).
Per-tick cost: `dodgeIncomingMovements()` is **not** cached — it walks
`MM.getOnlyCollectionByName('MovementsUnits')` (`dodge.js:57`) every call.
The collection is small (one row per inbound/outbound movement, dozens in
practice) and the read is O(N) in JS object property access. Plan 8.3
profiler is not yet shipped; if it surfaces a hot spot, add a 1s memo
mirroring `TOWN_RES_CACHE_MS` (`bridge.js:234`). Out of scope here.

**Sort order**: by `arrival` ascending. `intelThreatBoard` does not sort
today (`dodgeIncomingMovements` returns in collection order). Add a sort
at the top of `render(host)`:

```
const sorted = threats.slice().sort((a, b) => (+a.arrival || 0) - (+b.arrival || 0));
```

Patch only changed rows (`textContent` writes are idempotent; the DOM
keyed-row pattern from `ui.js:92-101` keeps the row set stable across
ticks so a tick that adds a row does not blow away the user's widget
position).

## 4. Work items

1. **`src/ui.js`** — add `renderAttackCountdown(host)` near
   `renderProductionOverlay` (the function added by plan 6.11).
   Internals: read `dodgeIncomingMovements`, sort, render rows. Reuse
   `queueCenterFmt` from `queue-center.js:55-60` for the time formatting
   (move it to a shared helper if 6.11 also wants it — out of scope for
   this plan, inline the formatter for now).
2. **`src/ui.js`** — register the widget via `gbWidget.register({ id:
   'attack-eta', title: 'Ataques entrantes', defaultPos: { left: '320px',
   top: '60px' }, tickMs: 1000, render: renderAttackCountdown })`.
3. **`src/intel.js`** — no changes. `intelThreatBoard()` already returns
   the same data; the widget reads `dodgeIncomingMovements()` directly.
4. **`src/dodge.js`** — no changes. `dodgeEtaSec` is already exported.
5. **`src/military.js`** — **no changes**. Plan 27's "extend `military.js`"
   hint is wrong: `military.js` is about *outgoing* movements and cancel
   (`militaryOutgoingMovements`, `militaryCancelCommand` at
   `src/military.js:17-44` and `:45-70`). Incoming data lives in
   `dodge.js`. Do not touch `military.js` for this plan.
6. **`src/stats.js`** — add an `attack countdown` row to `preflightRun`
   (`src/stats.js:12-191`) that checks `typeof dodgeIncomingMovements
   === 'function'` and that `dodgeEtaSec` is callable.

## 5. State & storage

- **No new state**. Widget position via the 6.2 contract (`STORE.WIDGET_GEOM`).
- **No world-scoping** beyond 6.2.
- **No `configVer` bump** for 6.14 itself.
- **No prune TTL** — the data is live from the game model.

## 6. Config surface

- `Ataques entrantes: widget visible` — default OFF. Lives under Config →
  *Widgets* (added by 6.2 step 6). Writes
  `state.widgetGeom['attack-eta'].hidden`.
- `Ataques entrantes: umbral rojo` — number input, default `300` (5 min).
  The CSS class flip happens in `renderAttackCountdown` based on this value.
  Stored under the per-widget settings if 6.2 introduces one; else inline.
- No HIGH-RISK toggles. The widget is read-only — no auto-dodge, no
  militia auto-raise, no evacuation. Players who want that flip the
  existing `autoDodge` toggle (`header.js:115`, `STORE.AUTO_DODGE`). No
  `gbCaptchaPause` feature key needed for the widget itself.

## 7. Post surface & safety

Read-only. The widget calls `dodgeIncomingMovements()` and
`dodgeEtaSec()` only. No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no `gbDomClick`.
Skip the rest of the checklist.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`dodgeIncomingMovements()` returns empty**. Render `(sin entradas)`
  empty state, no crash. The Intel tab already handles this at
  `intel.js:84` — copy the wording.
- **`mov.arrival` is 0 or negative** (game-side race during collection
  refresh). `dodgeEtaSec` returns `0` in that case; render `0:00` and let
  the colour flip to "landed" — it disappears within 30s on its own.
- **Player owns >20 towns under attack**. Render only the first 20 rows;
  add an `+N más` line that links to the Intel tab (set
  `hostEnabled && showTab('intel')` on click — `showTab` is at
  `src/ui.js:353`). The widget body itself stays small.
- **SPA nav detaches the widget host**. Same as 6.2 §8: `ensurePanelMounted`
  (`src/boot.js:1-8`) is extended by 6.2 to re-append any missing widget
  host. No additional fix here.
- **Tab hidden, `setInterval` clamped to ~1 min**. The widget stops
  ticking — same as `renderTimers` and `updateStatus` (`boot.js:66-67`).
  Acceptable: ETA will catch up on the next visible tick. The widget's
  own `gbInterval` is subject to the same clamping; the SPA's
  `visibilitychange` handler at `src/boot.js:50-56` does **not** currently
  poke the widget — a follow-up could add a `gbWidget.refreshAll()` call
  there. Out of scope here.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 (Low risk). One in-game session on `es146`:

- Toggle `Ataques entrantes: widget visible` ON. Widget appears empty
  (no incoming on this world).
- Use the **Attack tab** `gb-atk-now` button (`src/ui.js:225`) to fire a
  test attack against an ally's town, then **switch perspective** to that
  ally's world (or test on a friend's account you control). On the
  receiving side, the widget shows one row within 1s, ETA ticks down.
- Wait until ETA < 5 min; row turns red and pulses. ETA = 0; row dims
  and disappears within 30s. Log shows no errors.
- Drag the widget, close, reopen. Position persists (6.2 contract).
- **Preflight**: `attack countdown` row green.
- **Cross-check Intel tab**: text-only threat board still renders the
  same incoming row (regression check on `renderIntel`, `src/intel.js:75`).
- **Negative**: with `state.dryRun = true` (`STORE.DRY_RUN`,
  `header.js:138`), the widget still renders — it does not post. Log
  shows the dry-run chip in the footer but widget content is unaffected.

## 10. Out of scope

- Auto-dodge / auto-militia wiring. Already shipped via `dodgeScan`
  (`src/dodge.js:252`) and `dodgeTryMilitia` (`src/dodge.js:195`). This
  widget is **read-only**; it never fires those paths. Wiring the widget
  to "click row → call `dodgeTrySend`" would be HIGH-RISK escalation and
  is explicitly out.
- Per-attack ETA-precision columns (wall ETA, support ETA, etc.).
  Already in the Intel tab threat board (`src/intel.js:83-90`).
- Showing friendly supports / returns. The widget is hostile-only —
  `dodgeIncomingMovements` filters by `DODGE_HOSTILE_TYPES` regex
  (`src/dodge.js:39`). Friendly traffic has its own row in the threat
  board.
- Mobile drag — defer with 6.2.
- Webhook firing on ETA-crossing thresholds. Plan 6.4 ("Desktop
  notifications + sound") already owns alert fan-out; do not duplicate.

## 7.1-shared-attack-planner-v2.md

# 7.1 — Shared attack planner v2

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** L
**Module:** extend `planner.js` (state + ingest) + `attack.js` (apply gate) + new `shared-plan.js` for the ingest UI; **no** outbound webhook, **no** server, **no** inbound bot.
**Depends on:** 2.1 spy report parser deep, 6.9 config import/export wizard (JSON paste channel already exists).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- **Attack plan is local-only.** `state.attackPlan` (`core.js:276`, key
  `STORE.ATTACK_PLAN` in `header.js:58`); schema in `defaultAttackPlan()`
  (`attack.js:204-221`); persisted via `saveAttackPlan()` (`attack.js:230-232`).
  `ensureAttackPlan()` (`attack.js:222-229`) merges defaults, so a missing
  field is recoverable, but the only writer is the Attack tab form
  (`readAttackForm` at `attack.js:959-986`).
- **The v0.6.0 confirm gate is one `confirm()` call.** `fireAttackNow`
  (`attack.js:711-739`) opens the browser confirm at `attack.js:717` and
  refuses to send on cancel. Arming goes through `armAttackWave`
  (`attack.js:611-710`) with no per-target prompt; the only safety
  against an accidental send is that gate. There is no per-target
  confirmation in the arm path — `armAttackWave` fires the bridge post
  when each `gbTimeout` elapses (`attack.js:656-696`).
- **The plan is single-target.** `resolveTarget` (`attack.js:346-392`)
  resolves one `targetId` to either `town` or `farm_town`. Multiple
  source towns ride on the same target (the `rows[]` in
  `buildAttackSchedule`, `attack.js:468-500`). There is no notion of a
  shared alliance plan with N targets across N source towns.
- **No inbound channel exists.** The `@connect` block in
  `src/header.js:16-19` is `grepolis.com` + `discord.com` +
  `discordapp.com` + `api.telegram.org` and nothing else. `alerts.js`
  is fully outbound (`alertWebhook` is the only entry point; verified
  by reading the full 89-line file — it builds a `POST` body and hands
  it to `gbXhr` with `scope:'external'`, never reads anything back).
  Plan 27 §0 explicitly drops "Telegram bot **inbound**" and any
  server. The catalog row text "alliance intake via webhook" therefore
  cannot mean what it sounds like — there is no webhook the bot could
  listen on inside a Tampermonkey userscript.
- **Hook for the planner UI lives in `qol.js:62-95`** (`renderPlanner`,
  `plannerSnapshot`), and the per-town live reserves are already
  factored into `plannerLive`/`plannerSnapshot` (`planner.js:37-81`).
  These do not need to change.
- **The Intel dossier already carries `allianceNote` for ingested
  reports** (`intel.js:66-68`) — read paths exist; the setter was added
  in v3.x to fix the dead-state bug plan 26 §B2 named.

## 2. Gap

The Attack tab can stage one attack at a time from a single account.
Alliance playbooks ("everyone attacks X at HH:MM with the composition
they have available") require *importing* a target list from somewhere
else. Plan 27 §7 resolves this with "ingestion only — no outbound
phone-home" + "Attack planner confirm gate (v0.6.0)". With the
userscript sandbox and CLAUDE.md "no server, paste-only", the only
honest ingestion channel is a **paste-in or user-supplied URL fetch**
of a JSON plan. Everything else is a phone-home or a server.

## 3. Design

Three ingress modes, all client-side. A `shared-plan.js` module hosts
the importer + a per-target confirm overlay.

1. **Paste**: a textarea in the Attack tab accepts a JSON blob copied
   from another GrepBot user (Config → "Exportar plan actual" already
   exists in spirit via `qolExportConfig`, `qol.js:248-253`, though it
   does not yet include `attackPlan`). Schema:
   `{ "v": 1, "targets": [{ "id": "<townId>", "name": "...", "x": N,
   "y": N, "window": { "arriveAt": <unix> | null, "staggerMs": N },
   "intent": "attack|support" }], "author": { "id": "...", "host":
   "<grepolis host>" } }`. Validate per target (see §7) before
   admitting it into `state.attackPlan.targets[]`.
2. **User-supplied URL fetch (opt-in)**: Config field
   `sharedPlanUrl` (default empty). When set and host non-empty, the
   bot performs a **single** `gbXhr({ scope:'external', method:'GET',
   url })`. The host **must** appear in `@connect` in
   `src/header.js:16-19`; a Discord channel-message fetch (`GET
   https://discord.com/api/v9/channels/<id>/messages?...`) requires
   adding `discord.com` paths beyond the webhook endpoint, which the
   current GM_xmlhttpRequest sandbox **does not permit without a
   Bearer token** — so in practice this path only works if the URL is
   a raw paste bin the user controls, and the user must add the host
   to `@connect`. We will not add `@connect` entries speculatively;
   the work item is to add one host per supported paste service at
   the time it is requested, with the host listed in this plan's
   §10 out-of-scope until that is done.
3. **Discord webhook outbound for sharing** (NOT intake): a "Publish
   plan" button writes the current `state.attackPlan` to the existing
   webhook URL via `alertWebhook('shared-plan', payload)` if the
   `state.webhookEvents.sharedPlan` opt-in flag is true. This is the
   only outbound path. It is gated by the same `dryRun` short-circuit
   already in `alerts.js:31-34`.

Per-target apply gate: a target that comes from a shared plan goes
through `resolveTarget` (`attack.js:346-392`) and `attackSendAllowed`
(`attack.js:393-398`) exactly like a manual one, and fires through
the same `sendAttackViaBridge` path (`attack.js:502-578`). The v0.6.0
confirm gate is **per target**, not per plan — every target in the
plan opens its own `confirm()` prompt in the existing
`fireAttackNow` arm path. Auto-arm (`armAttackWave`) is **not**
allowed for shared-plan targets unless the new toggle
`state.sharedPlanAutoArm` is true, and even then only when every
target resolves through `resolveTarget` to `kind:'town'` and is not
an own town (the checks at `attack.js:520-529`).

## 5. State & storage

- `state.attackPlan.targets[]` — array of
  `{ id, name?, x?, y?, intent, arriveAt, staggerMs, src }`. Cap at
  100; over-cap → oldest dropped, log once.
- `state.sharedPlanRecent[]` — last 5 imported plans, world-scoped
  (most alliances play on one world per player).
- `state.sharedPlanUrl` — empty string default.
- `state.sharedPlanAutoArm` — boolean, default **OFF** (HIGH-RISK
  rule: a plan that fires without per-target confirm is high-impact).
- `state.webhookEvents.sharedPlan` — boolean, default false (does not
  opt into publish-by-default).
- Id-bearing ⇒ `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entries needed for
  `STORE.SHARED_PLAN_RECENT` only. `STORE.SHARED_PLAN_URL` is not
  id-bearing (it's a URL the user typed) but should still be
  world-scoped so two accounts on one world don't cross-pollute.
- No `configVer` bump on `state.sharedPlanUrl` (UI-only).
- `configVer` bump on `state.attackPlan.targets` shape.

## 6. Config surface

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sharedPlanUrl` | string | `''` | user-supplied JSON URL; empty disables fetch |
| `sharedPlanAutoArm` | checkbox | **OFF** | HIGH-RISK default OFF per CLAUDE.md |
| `webhookEvents.sharedPlan` | checkbox | false | opt-in to publish current plan via existing webhook |
| `attackPlan.targets[]` | data | `[]` | populated only by Import / Paste |

The label string for the new auto-arm toggle is
`Auto-armar planes compartidos (HIGH-RISK)` so the HIGH-RISK tag is
visible per CLAUDE.md's HIGH-RISK rule.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Inbound**: none. The plan explicitly does not add a webhook
  receiver, an XHR poll, or a long-poll. The "user-supplied URL
  fetch" is a **single GET** issued only when the user clicks the
  "Fetch" button; not a scheduler.
- **Outbound**: `alertWebhook('shared-plan', payload)` for publish,
  behind `state.dryRun` (already short-circuits at
  `alerts.js:31-34`).
- **gbAjaxWatch**: not applicable — this feature uses `gbXhr` for the
  user-supplied URL fetch (read, not action). No bridge post.
- **gbCaptchaPause feature key**: this feature adds a read-side fetch
  for shared-plan URL. Add `sharedPlan` to the captcha breaker key
  set with a guard: `captchaPausedAny('sharedPlan')` checks in
  `sharedPlanFetchUrl` so a captcha storm pauses the fetch.
  Persisted via `saveCaptcha()` (`core.js:1336`) — already keyed by
  `STORE.CAPTCHA` which is world-scoped (`header.js:200`).
- **Lock**: `gbLock('shared-plan', 30000)` for the fetch path;
  `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry `'shared-plan': 30000` (`core.js:145-173`).
- **Dry-run**: `state.dryRun` already gates `alertWebhook` and
  `bridgePost`/`gameAjaxPost`. The fetcher logs a `DRY-RUN
  shared-plan: GET <url>` line when dry-run is on and posts nothing
  in response (treat the fetch itself as read, but block publish).
- **Redaction**: the published payload and the imported payload
  (when re-shared) use `qolRedactConfigDump` (`qol.js:225-247`).
  Per-player names go through `cut()` (1 char + `...`) unless
  `state.exportRedact === false`.
- **Confirm gate**: per target, the existing `confirm()` in
  `fireAttackNow` (`attack.js:717`) fires once per target. The dialog
  text becomes
  `Atacar #<id> (<name>) desde <sourceCount> ciudades ahora?`. The
  user can answer Cancel to abort the whole plan or OK to fire this
  target (the loop in `fireAttackNow` checks `confirm()` per row;
  change the iteration to abort on Cancel).
- **Precondition invariant**:
  - `sharedPlanValidate` calls `resolveTarget` for each target and
    refuses `kind:'farm_town'` and own-town ids.
  - Each target id must match `/^\d+$/` (the gate at `attack.js:351`).
  - `arriveAt` must be a positive integer when present; otherwise
    null (treated as send-now per row, same as
    `attack.js:484-488`).
  - Unreadable target (`resolveTarget` returns null) → entry dropped
    with `gbLogT('shared-plan-bad-target', 60000, ...)`.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Import JSON fails parse**: `gbLogT('shared-plan-json', 10000,
  'shared plan: JSON parse failed'); flash('plan invalido')`.
  No state change.
- **Import JSON schema missing `targets`**: same path; "plan
  invalido (sin targets)".
- **Single bad target**: drop just that target, continue the rest.
  The plan still applies; the user sees a count line in the log.
- **All targets bad**: refuse the import entirely; do not modify
  `state.attackPlan.targets`.
- **User-supplied URL fetch fails**: `gbLogT('shared-plan-fetch',
  30000, ...)`; flash('fetch fallo'). Captcha on the host →
  `captchaTrip('sharedPlan', ...)` and disable the button until the
  breaker expires.
- **`@connect` rejects the URL**: `gbXhr` returns `'noajax'`; we log
  it once and surface a hint that the host needs to be added to
  `src/header.js` (the script does not auto-edit its own userscript
  metadata). The error code path is the same as the existing
  `farmScrape` no-endpoint log at `farms.js:633`.
- **Own-town target**: `resolveTarget` will resolve it (own towns
  pass `attack.js:357-363`); the runtime guard at `attack.js:525-529`
  refuses the post with `bad-target` and `flash('ataque bloqueado:
  el objetivo es una ciudad propia')`. No special-case needed.
- **Plan references a player id the importer doesn't recognize**:
  ignored — only `author.id` is informational.

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 Med risk: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one
full orchestrator tick.

- `state.dryRun` ON, paste a 2-target plan → Log shows
  `DRY-RUN shared-plan: ...` and `DRY-RUN attack: ...` per target,
  and a `skip:dryrun` journal entry per intent. No network
  traffic beyond the read fetcher.
- `state.dryRun` OFF, paste a 1-target plan with a foreign town id
  the test account can resolve → confirm() prompts once; answer OK
  → Log shows `attack bridge: sendUnits town <src> → <dest>
  (attack, ...)` and one `ok` entry in Decisions.
- Fire the same plan with `state.sharedPlanAutoArm = false` → no
  auto-arm, the targets sit until the user manually clicks
  **Armar** in the Attack tab.
- Flip `state.sharedPlanAutoArm = true` → the next timer tick
  arms the targets via `armAttackWave`. Each fires after its
  individual `gbTimeout` elapses; Log shows
  `attack: armed N towns mode=send_now`.
- Captcha test: set `state.captchaBreakers.sharedPlan.until =
  Date.now() + 60000`; the **Fetch** button refuses with
  `captcha-pause`.
- Redaction test: paste a plan with `author.id = 'jdoe12345'`,
  `state.exportRedact = true`; export via `qolExportConfig` →
  blob shows `author: { id: 'j...0' }`.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Discord channel-message fetch** as a default share channel.
  Requires a Discord bot token the user pastes in, and a wider
  `@connect` entry than the current `discord.com` permits. Until
  someone explicitly wants this, it stays out.
- **Auto-publish on every planner change**. Only manual publish is
  wired; auto-publish belongs in plan 8.2 (state snapshots).
- **Cross-alliance auth**. We never validate that the importer is in
  the same alliance as the author; the author tag is metadata.
- **Per-player throttling on publish**. Plan 7.4 owns that; the
  publish path for shared-plan payloads opts into the 7.4 throttle
  when 7.4 lands (a small follow-up).
- **An `@connect` host addition for a paste service**. Defer until a
  specific paste host is requested; the work is a one-line edit to
  `src/header.js:16-19` plus a test against the chosen service.

## 7.2-defense-coordination-board.md

# 7.2 — Defense coordination board

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js`; add a `[data-intel="view"]` option in `src/ui.js` Intel tab; no `src/header.js` change (no new key)
**Depends on:** none (uses `defenseAssessment` from `src/wonder.js` and `dodgeIncomingMovements` from `src/dodge.js`, both already loaded)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2 (header `@version` is `3.9.0`)

> Read-mostly per plan 27 §7. The board is a **per-client** coordination aid:
> the user sees their own towns, their own incoming, and their own support
> options, in a layout meant for copy-paste into alliance chat. It does **not**
> fetch any alliance-side state (no `MM.getCollection('Alliance')` exists —
> see §1.4) and does **not** post outbound messages on the player's behalf.
> Coordination with allies stays in the alliance chat; the bot only formats.

---

## 1. What exists today

- `dodgeIncomingMovements()` (`src/dodge.js:53-84`) is the threat source.
  It walks `MM.MovementsUnits` (`dodge.js:57`), filters by the
  `dodgeIsHostileMovement` rule (`dodge.js:41-52`), keeps only attacks whose
  `destination_town_id` is one of the player's towns (`dodge.js:59-63`), and
  returns `[{id, dest, origin, type, hasCs, arrival, units, model}]`.
  Every field used by the board is already there.
- `defenseAssessment(mov, incoming)` (`src/wonder.js:144`) is the per-threat
  scoring function. It returns `{eta, simultaneous, local, supports, safeTown,
  evac, militia, risk, hasCs}`. Already used by `renderIntel`
  (`intel.js:80-90`) for the existing threat dump. The board reuses the same
  call — no second implementation.
- `renderIntel()` (`src/intel.js:75-114`) already renders the existing threat
  block at `intel.js:83-91` in the format
  `[CS] type → dest from origin @arrival | riesgo <n> | ETA … | apoyo N |
  esquivar si/no`. That is a one-line-per-threat view; the board needs a
  grouped-by-destination view with one row per (own-town, attack-id).
- `state.towns` (`src/core.js:229`, populated by `towns.js:71, 197`) is the
  player town list, shape `{id, name, x, y, island}`. Used for ordering and
  labelling the board columns.
- `state.allianceNotes` (`src/core.js:341`, `intel.js:124-132`) carries
  per-alliance free text. The board looks up the **attacker's** alliance
  string (via `parseReport` → `f.alliance` at `parse-inline.js:89`) and
  appends the note if present — same shape as the dossier line at
  `intel.js:66-67`. **Read path only** for the board; the setter is already
  wired at `ui.js:1002-1007`.
- `defenseMode()` (`src/wonder.js:141`) and `state.defenseCfg`
  (`src/core.js:359`) are the live controls the user sets in Config
  (`ui.js:1350-1353, 1470-1472`). The board reads them; it does not
  duplicate them.
- Plan 6.13 (`docs/plans/v4/6.13-alliance-intel-heatmap.md`) already adds a
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector to the Intel section (`ui.js:693`) with two
  options, `Resumen` and `Heatmap 7d`. The board adds a **third** option,
  `Coord 7.2`. When selected, `renderIntel` emits only the board and skips
  the existing dump blocks (`intel.js:83-111`). The existing
  `intelPatternScan` call at the bottom (`intel.js:113`) still runs on
  either view (orthogonal).
- **No** `MM.getCollectionByName('Alliance')`, `getAlliances()`, or
  `AllianceMembers` reference exists anywhere in `src/` (verified by
  ripgrep — zero hits). Alliance-wide data for **other** members is not
  exposed by the game to a single client. The board does not pretend
  otherwise.

## 2. Gap

`renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) renders one line per incoming attack
(`intel.js:86-90`). When a single town has two incoming commands, the user
has to mentally re-group by destination to plan a defence, and the
existing line does not surface the **own-town summary** (which towns need
help, which towns are safe, where to route the supports). Plan 7.2
delivers that summary without inventing any data — everything the board
needs already exists in the call chain.

## 3. Design

Read-only. No post surface, no captcha breaker, no lock, no scheduler.
The renderer is grouped by `dest` (the attacked town) instead of by
attack `id`. Each group shows local strength, the per-attack assessments,
and the suggested action taken from `state.defenseCfg.mode`.

### 3.1 Aggregator

Add `intelDefenseBoard(threats)` to `src/intel.js`, placed next to
`intelDossiers` (`intel.js:34-71`):

```js
function intelDefenseBoard(threats) {
  const byDest = new Map();
  for (const t of threats || []) {
    const k = String(t.dest);
    if (!byDest.has(k)) byDest.set(k, []);
    byDest.get(k).push(t);
  }
  const ownTowns = (state.towns || []).slice().sort((a, b) => String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id)));
  const rows = [];
  for (const t of ownTowns) {
    const incoming = byDest.get(String(t.id)) || [];
    if (!incoming.length) continue;
    const townRow = { townId: String(t.id), townName: t.name, attacks: [] };
    for (const m of incoming) {
      const da = defenseAssessment(m, threats);
      const ass = String(m.units?.colonize_ship || m.units?.colony_ship ? 'CS' : (m.hasCs ? 'CS' : 'attack'));
      townRow.attacks.push({
        id: String(m.id || ''), type: ass, origin: m.origin, arrival: m.arrival,
        risk: da.risk, eta: da.eta, supports: (da.supports || []).length,
        evacOk: !!da.evac?.ok, militiaOk: !!da.militia?.ok, hasCs: !!m.hasCs,
      });
    }
    rows.push(townRow);
  }
  return rows;
}
```

The aggregator reuses `defenseAssessment` (`wonder.js:144`) directly —
**no second risk-score formula**. `rows` is sorted by `townId` ascending,
which keeps a stable order across repaints (the same pattern the World
table uses; `ui.js:165` and the keyed-row rule at `CLAUDE.md` "v1.4.0
render").

### 3.2 Renderer

In `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`), after the existing
`if (intelView === 'heatmap')` branch (added by plan 6.13 §4.2), add:

```js
if (intelView === 'board') {
  const threats = intelThreatBoard();
  const board = intelDefenseBoard(threats);
  let html = '';
  html += '=== Coordinación de defensa (live) ===\n';
  if (!board.length) { html += '(sin amenazas activas)\n'; }
  else {
    for (const row of board) {
      html += `Ciudad ${row.townName || '#' + row.townId}: ${row.attacks.length} amenaza(s)\n`;
      for (const a of row.attacks) {
        const eta = a.eta == null ? '?' : fmtSec(a.eta);
        const action =
          state.defenseCfg.mode === 'safe' ? 'esquivar' :
          state.defenseCfg.mode === 'smart' && (a.hasCs || a.risk >= 35) ? 'esquivar smart' :
          a.supports > 0 ? `apoyar (${a.supports} opcion(es))` :
          'mantener';
        html += `  ${a.type} desde ${a.origin || '?'}${a.arrival ? ' @' + a.arrival : ''} | riesgo ${a.risk} | ETA ${eta} | ${action}\n`;
      }
    }
  }
  box.textContent = html;
  try { intelPatternScan(); } catch (_) {}
  return;
}
```

Each line is exactly one attack on one town. The action text is a pure
function of `state.defenseCfg.mode` and the existing `risk >= 35` /
`hasCs` thresholds that `defenseShouldDodge` already uses
(`wonder.js:145`) — no new thresholds. Empty board ⇒ one
`(sin amenazas activas)` line; **no** `null`s, no `undefined` rendered.

### 3.3 Alliance-note overlay

For every incoming attack the board looks up the **attacker**'s alliance
string by walking `state.findings` once before rendering:

```js
function allianceForAttack(originTownId) {
  if (!originTownId) return null;
  for (const f of (state.findings || []).slice(0, 200)) {
    if (String(f?.town?.id) === String(originTownId) && f.alliance) return f.alliance;
  }
  return null;
}
```

If `allianceForAttack(a.origin)` returns a string present in
`state.allianceNotes`, append ` — [aliado: <note>]` (truncated to 40
chars) to that attack's row. Same `textContent` discipline as the
existing dossier line at `intel.js:96`. **No `innerHTML`**.

The lookup is bounded (`state.findings.slice(0, 200)`) because
`state.findings` is capped at 100 entries by `storagePruneForQuota`
(`core.js:1188-1190`); the `slice` is defence-in-depth, not a quota
control.

### 3.4 View selector integration

Plan 6.13 §3.3 already specifies a `[data-intel="view"]` `<select>` in the
Intel section header (`ui.js:693-704`). Plan 7.2 does **not** add a new
control — it adds a third `<option value="board">Coordinación 7.2</option>`
inside the same selector. Plan 6.13 builds the selector; plan 7.2 assumes
it exists. If 6.13 lands first, this is a one-line `<option>` addition.
If 7.2 lands first, plan 6.13 §3.3 picks up the second option instead of
adding the selector itself.

**Resolving the ordering conflict:** both plans propose a third option for
the same selector. Treat the selector as part of the Intel section chrome
(owned by plan 6.13), and 7.2 only contributes one `<option>` to it.
Concretely: §4.1 of 6.13 says "the renderer checks `state.intelView`";
plan 7.2 does **not** introduce a second renderer-mode variable. The
branch lives in the same `renderIntel` block and reads the same
`intelView` module-local `let`.

## 6. Config surface

No new toggle. The board is gated by the existing `[data-intel="view"]`

Config (`ui.js:1350, 1470`), the board reflects it. No HIGH-RISK toggle
to set OFF (Low risk; read-only).

`autoDodge` (`core.js:329`), `dodgeFloor` (`core.js:330`), and
`defenseCfg` (`core.js:359`) are the live controls the board consults;
none are changed here.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no
`gbDomClick`, no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry,
no `gbCaptchaPause` key.

The renderer uses `box.textContent = html` (same discipline as today
at `intel.js:112`). The selector uses `createElement('option')` +
`appendChild` (plan 6.13 §4.4). Audit-I15 XSS discipline: zero
`innerHTML` where attacker-controlled strings render. The
`origin`/`alliance` strings are attacker-controlled (they come from
report JSON parsed by `parse-inline.js:89`); the primary defence is
`textContent`, which never parses the string as markup.

The board is **read-mostly** end to end. The copy-paste-to-chat
workflow is the user's keystroke, not the bot's; the bot never calls
`alertWebhook` from the board path (a deliberate non-decision; alliance
chat is out of plan 27 §0).

## 8. Failure modes

- **`dodgeIncomingMovements` returns `[]`** — the board renders one
  `(sin amenazas activas)` line. No `null`s, no crashes.
- **`state.towns` empty** — `byDest` is empty, `rows` is empty, same
  `(sin amenazas activas)` line. Fresh-install safe.
- **`state.allianceNotes` empty** — overlay §3.3 finds nothing;
  attack rows render without the ` — [aliado: …]` suffix. Documented in
  the §9 validation gate.
- **`defenseAssessment` throws on a hostile command with unknown
  fields** — `defenseAssessment` is wrapped today by `try { … } catch
  (_) {}` (`intel.js:113`) and the new branch wraps the same call.
  The aggregator still emits `[{townId, attacks: []}]` with empty
  attacks for the throw site. Better: rebuild the per-attack loop
  inside a single `try { … } catch (_) { row.attacks = []; }` so a
  single broken assessment does not blank the whole row.
- **`origin` not present in `state.findings`** — `allianceForAttack`
  returns `null`; no note appended. Documented. The 200-row cap is
  generous; alliance attribution by origin is best-effort.
- **Mode toggle mid-board** — the user changes `defenseCfg.mode` in
  Config (`ui.js:1470`); the next `renderIntel` call reads the new mode
  and re-emits the action text. No state drift, no stale cache. The
  board never caches `defenseCfg.mode` between renders.
- **Top-N town cap** — `state.towns` is at most ~20 on a single world;
  no cap is needed. The board prints every threatened town, every
  attack. The alliance-chat paste format is plain text, so there is no
  pagination concern.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session, no
failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), install, open the Intel tab. The
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector shows `Resumen` (default),
  `Heatmap 7d`, and `Coordinación 7.2`.
- With no incoming attacks (`dodgeIncomingMovements()` returns `[]`):
  the board emits `(sin amenazas activas)` and exits cleanly.
- Seed one attack by hand: open the game, send an attack from an alt
  account (or use the dev console to populate `MM.MovementsUnits` with a
  fake hostile movement), open the Intel tab, choose `Coordinación
  7.2`. Expect one town row, one attack row, the action text matches
  the current `defenseCfg.mode` (try `notify` and `safe` and confirm the
  text flips).
- Add an alliance note via the existing UI (`ui.js:1002-1007`),
  re-open the board; the attacker row gains ` — [aliado: <note>]`. The
  alliance note is set on the **attacker**'s alliance name (the string
  the bot saw in the most recent report involving that origin).
- Switch `state.defenseCfg.mode = 'smart'`; expect rows where
  `risk >= 35` or `hasCs` to read `esquivar smart` instead of `apoyar`.
  Rows below the threshold read `mantener`. Same threshold as
  `defenseShouldDodge` (`wonder.js:145`).
- Preflight (`Comprobar sistema`) — new `defense coordination board`
  row appears; passes when `maxRisk` is finite, warns when the board
  renders but every row's `risk` is 0.
- `state.dryRun = true` — board still renders; no new posts in the
  Log tab. Confirm by reading the journal (Decisions sub-view, `mem`).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Cross-alliance coordination (shared board).** Plan 27 §7.1 owns the
  alliance-side intake via webhook; that is a different feature
  (inbound `planner.js` extension). The 7.2 board is local-only.
- **Auto-escalation.** `defenseShouldDodge` (`wonder.js:145`) is the
  existing auto-escalation path; the board only formats what it would
  do, never triggers it. The `state.defenseCfg.mode = 'smart'` rows
  that read `esquivar smart` are advisory; the user still owns the
  decision.
- **Active alliance chat posting.** Out of plan 27 §0 (no auto-post
  to third-party chat surfaces; the existing `alertWebhook` is
  user-configured, never alliance-targeted).
- **Mermaid / SVG / pixel rendering.** Same justification as 6.13 §3.2
  and 6.12 — `textContent` discipline, no chart renderer in `src/`,
  ASCII is the right tool.
- **CSV export of the board.** Read-mostly means read; exporting is a
  user keystroke (select-all + copy from the `<pre>`). The existing
  `qolExportConfig` (`qol.js:248-253`) does not include intel data; an
  intel export would be a separate plan.
- **Alliance member identity lookup.** Plan 7.6 owns the member-activity
  dashboard; that work is needed before the board can show attacker
  *names* (today it shows attacker `origin` town ids). Out of scope
  here.
- **Plan 6.13 dependency.** If plan 6.13 has not landed, the
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector does not exist and §3.4 has nothing to
  extend. In that case file §10 as **blocked** and land 6.13 first.

## 7.3-alliance-resource-pool.md

# 7.3 — Alliance resource pool tracker

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js`; **no new module** (plan 27's `alliance-pool.js` hint is wrong for the honest scope — see §1.4)
**Depends on:** plan 03 (`docs/plans/03-alliance-notes-ui.md` — the `intelSetAllianceNote` setter was already added at `src/intel.js:124-132` as the §B2 fix from plan 26, but its UI is owned by plan 03 and we depend on the editor row already living in `src/ui.js:700-704`).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

> Read-mostly per plan 27 §7. The tracker is a per-client aggregation; it
> does **not** reach another player's client and it does **not** auto-post
> to alliance chat. The "alliance resource pool" the bot can show is
> exactly the union of (a) own-towns live stocks, (b) the last-known
> resource lines of towns it has spied, and (c) numbers the user types
> into a self-report editor. No other source exists.

---

## 1. What exists today

- `state.townResources[townId]` (`src/core.js:221` initializer; written
  by `fetchTownResources` at `src/towns.js:155-160`) is the **own-towns**
  resource snapshot. Per-row shape `{ ts, wood, stone, iron, pop, cap,
  ok, action }`. World-scoped via `STORE.TOWN_RES` (`header.js:31`,
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `header.js:195`).
- `state.findings[i].resources` and `state.findings[i].town` come from
  `parseReport` (`src/parse-inline.js:39-44, 81-87`) on every ingested
  report (`src/spy.js:248-254`). `resources` carries the last-seen
  wood/stone/iron of the **defender** town; `town` carries
  `{id, name, x, y}`. Capped at 500 by `spy.js:250-253`, then pruned to
  100 by `storagePruneForQuota` (`core.js:1167-1172`).
- `state.findings[i].alliance` (`parse-inline.js:89`) is the **string**
  alliance name attached to attacker/defender — the only alliance
  attribute the bot ever sees.
- `state.allianceNotes` (`core.js:341`, `STORE.ALLIANCE_NOTES` at
  `header.js:131`, in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `header.js:206`) holds
  per-alliance free text. Read paths at `intel.js:66-67` (dossier
  overlay), `intel.js:103-106` (Intel section dump), `qol.js:238`
  (export redactor). The setter `intelSetAllianceNote`
  (`intel.js:124-132`) was added as plan 26 §B2's fix (the comment at
  `intel.js:121-123` confirms the dead-state history); UI caller at
  `ui.js:1006`, editor row at `ui.js:700-704` (plan 03 wired these).
- **`intelDossiers()`** (`intel.js:34-71`) already aggregates per-player
  findings. The pool tracker uses the same row shape with alliance
  name as the row key.

### 1.4 Module hint disagreement (explicit)

Plan 27 §7 row 7.3 says "new `alliance-pool.js`". That is wrong for
the honest scope of this feature: the tracker is one aggregator + one
renderer inside the existing `intel.js` Intel section (next to
`intelDossiers`, `intelThreatBoard`, `intelPatternScan` — three
siblings that already do the same per-row aggregation). Adding a new
module would require a `build.py:31-72` MODULES slot for ~120 lines
of read-only aggregation logic and one state field. The plan keeps
the feature inside `intel.js`. If a follow-up plan later needs an
*ingestion* path that does justify a module (e.g. scraping the in-game
alliance forum, which plan 27 §0 forbids), that can re-split.

### 1.5 Game model: what is NOT reachable from one client

Verified by ripgrep over `src/` for any alliance-wide accessor:

- **No** `MM.getCollectionByName('Alliance')`,
  `MM.getCollectionByName('AllianceMember')`, `getAlliances()`, or any
  `MM.getModels().Alliance` reference exists (zero hits across all 40
  modules).
- **No** `r.alliance` field other than the per-report alliance *string*
  (`parse-inline.js:89`); a report carries one town's snapshot, not
  the alliance roster.

**Therefore the tracker cannot show real, current resource totals for
alliance members who are not the bot and who have not been spied.**
It shows the union of own-towns + last-seen spied towns + a
user-typed self-report per alliance. Anything beyond that requires
the alliance forum or another player's client — both out of plan
27 §0.

## 2. Gap

A player coordinating an alliance wants one screen that shows where
the bot's own resources sit, what the bot has *seen* in the last
reports (filterable by attacker alliance), and what the user has typed
in as self-report numbers for the rest. `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`)
dumps dossiers, threat board, watchlist, alliance notes, and attack
patterns — it does **not** aggregate resource totals by alliance, and
it does not surface the per-town numbers from `state.townResources`.

## 3. Design

Three inputs, one renderer, no post surface.

### 3.1 Aggregator

Add `intelPoolByAlliance()` to `src/intel.js`, placed next to
`intelDossiers` (`intel.js:34-71`). It returns
`Array<{ alliance, ownTotals, spyTotals, selfTotals, towns }>`:

```js
function intelPoolByAlliance() {
  const et = () => ({ wood: 0, stone: 0, iron: 0 });
  const out = new Map();
  const push = (k) => { let r = out.get(k); if (!r) { r = { alliance: k, ownTotals: et(), spyTotals: et(), selfTotals: et(), towns: 0 }; out.set(k, r); } return r; };
  for (const t of (state.towns || [])) { // (a) own towns — bucket under "__own__"
    const r = state.townResources[t.id];
    if (r && r.ok) { const row = push('__own__'); row.ownTotals.wood += +r.wood || 0; row.ownTotals.stone += +r.stone || 0; row.ownTotals.iron += +r.iron || 0; row.towns++; }
  }
  for (const f of (state.findings || []).slice(0, 200)) { // (b) spy-derived — group by attacker alliance when present
    const a = (f && (f.alliance || (f.attacker && f.attacker.alliance))) || null;
    if (!a) continue;
    const row = push(a); const res = f.resources || {};
    if (res.wood != null) row.spyTotals.wood += +res.wood || 0;
    if (res.stone != null) row.spyTotals.stone += +res.stone || 0;
    if (res.iron != null) row.spyTotals.iron += +res.iron || 0;
    row.towns++;
  }
  for (const k of Object.keys(state.allianceSelfReport || {})) { // (c) self-report
    const row = push(k); const e = state.allianceSelfReport[k] || {};
    row.selfTotals.wood = +e.wood || 0; row.selfTotals.stone = +e.stone || 0; row.selfTotals.iron = +e.iron || 0;
  }
  return Array.from(out.values()).sort((a, b) => a.alliance === '__own__' ? -1 : b.alliance === '__own__' ? 1 : a.alliance.localeCompare(b.alliance));
}
```

All inputs are optional and undefined-safe; no thrown errors. The
200-row cap on `state.findings` mirrors the existing
`intelDefenseBoard` bound at
`docs/plans/v4/7.2-defense-coordination-board.md:177` — defence in
depth, not a quota control (`state.findings` is already capped at 100
by `core.js:1167-1169`).

### 3.2 Renderer

Append a new branch to `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) gated by a
session-local `intelView === 'pool'` flag (same module-local `let`
that plan 6.13 §3.3 owns — same selector `[data-intel="view"]` that
plan 7.2 §3.4 contributes one option to):

```js
if (intelView === 'pool') {
  const rows = intelPoolByAlliance();
  let html = '=== Pool de recursos por alianza (vista local) ===\n';
  if (!rows.length) html += '(sin datos)\n';
  else for (const r of rows) {
    const lbl = r.alliance === '__own__' ? 'propias' : r.alliance;
    html += `${lbl} (${r.towns} ciudad(es)):` +
      `  propias W${r.ownTotals.wood}/S${r.ownTotals.stone}/I${r.ownTotals.iron}` +
      `  espiadas W${r.spyTotals.wood}/S${r.spyTotals.stone}/I${r.spyTotals.iron}` +
      `  reporte W${r.selfTotals.wood}/S${r.selfTotals.stone}/I${r.selfTotals.iron}\n`;
  }
  box.textContent = html;
  try { intelPatternScan(); } catch (_) {}
  return;
}
```

`box.textContent` is the only safe assignment (alliance strings are
attacker-controlled, audit-I15).

### 3.3 Self-report editor

Append four `<input>` rows + a save button to the Intel section
(`ui.js:692-708`) below the alliance-note editor. Click handler calls
a new `intelSetAllianceSelfReport(alliance, payload)` placed next to
`intelSetAllianceNote` (`intel.js:124-132`):

```js
function intelSetAllianceSelfReport(alliance, payload) {
  const key = String(alliance || '').trim();
  if (!key) return false;
  if (!state.allianceSelfReport || typeof state.allianceSelfReport !== 'object') state.allianceSelfReport = {};
  const clamp = (v) => Math.max(0, Math.floor(+v || 0));
  if (!payload || (payload.wood == null && payload.stone == null && payload.iron == null)) {
    delete state.allianceSelfReport[key];
  } else {
    state.allianceSelfReport[key] = { wood: clamp(payload.wood), stone: clamp(payload.stone), iron: clamp(payload.iron) };
  }
  save(STORE.ALLIANCE_SELF_REPORT, state.allianceSelfReport);
  return true;
}
```

Empty payload deletes the key (mirrors `intelSetAllianceNote`'s
delete-on-empty discipline at `intel.js:128`).

### 3.4 View selector integration

Plan 7.2 §3.4 contributes `<option value="board">`; plan 6.13 §3.3
contributes `<option value="heatmap">`. This plan contributes
`<option value="pool">Pool 7.3</option>` to the same selector — the
same single-line addition pattern. If neither 6.13 nor 7.2 has
landed, the selector does not exist and the new branch is
unreachable. File as a §10 dependency.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelPoolByAlliance()` per §3.1,
   placed next to `intelDossiers` (`intel.js:34-71`); helper
   `emptyTotals()` lives next to it.
2. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) with the
   `if (intelView === 'pool')` branch per §3.2. Branch returns early
   after `box.textContent`. Keep `try { intelPatternScan(); } catch
   (_) {}` at the bottom (orthogonal).
3. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelSetAllianceSelfReport(alliance,
   payload)` per §3.3, placed next to `intelSetAllianceNote`
   (`intel.js:124-132`). Empty payload deletes the key (mirror the
   existing setter at `intel.js:128`).
4. `src/core.js` — extend the `state` initializer (`core.js:221-390`)
   with `allianceSelfReport: load(STORE.ALLIANCE_SELF_REPORT, {})`
   (`{}` default, same shape as `playerNotes` and `allianceNotes` at
   `core.js:336, 341`).
5. `src/header.js` — add `STORE.ALLIANCE_SELF_REPORT:
   'grepbot:alliance-self-report'` next to `STORE.ALLIANCE_NOTES`
   (`header.js:131`) and the matching entry in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
   (`header.js:206`) — self-report keys are alliance names, which are
   name-bearing per world.
6. `src/header.js` — bump `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT = 10` (`header.js:191`)
   → 11 because the `state` schema grows.
7. `src/ui.js` — append the self-report editor inputs to the Intel
   section (`ui.js:692-708`) below the alliance-note row. Use
   `createElement` + `appendChild`; **no `innerHTML`** for the option
   labels (audit-I15). Bind a click handler that calls
   `intelSetAllianceSelfReport(...)`, then `renderIntel()` and
   `flash('autoreporte guardado')` on success.
8. `src/ui.js` — add `<option value="pool">Pool 7.3</option>` to the
   `[data-intel="view"]` selector that plan 6.13 §4.4 introduces.
   Same dependency rule as plan 7.2 §4.4: if the selector does not
   exist yet, **do not create it here** — file §10 as blocked and
   land 6.13 first.
9. `src/stats.js` — extend `preflightRun` (`src/stats.js:12-268`)
   with a row `alliance pool` that calls `intelPoolByAlliance()` and
   reports `{alliances: N, ownTowns: M, spiedTowns: K}`. Pass when
   `M > 0` or `K > 0` (some data exists); warn when both are 0
   (nothing to aggregate).
10. **No new `gbInterval` / `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry.** The
    aggregator runs inside the existing `renderIntel` cycle, already
    triggered by `spy.js:255`, `ui.js:1089`, and `ui.js:1006`.
11. **No `build.py` MODULES change.** `alliance-pool.js` is **not**
    added (see §1.4); the feature lives inside `intel.js`.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.allianceSelfReport` — `Record<alliance, {wood, stone,
  iron}>` (all integers, ≥0). New key, world-scoped via
  `STORE.ALLIANCE_SELF_REPORT` in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (added in
  §4.5). Default `{}`.
- The session-local `intelView` (plan 6.13 §3.3) gains one extra
  value, `'pool'`. Default `'summary'`. Across reloads the selector
  returns to `Resumen` (same pattern as the existing `statsWindow`
  at `src/military.js:257-258` and the new `'board'` value from
  plan 7.2 §5).
- `configVer` bump 10 → 11 (§4.6) because the schema gains a field.
- No prune TTL needed: the user's own self-report rows should survive
  reloads indefinitely. `core.js:1167-1169` prunes `state.findings`
  to 100; `state.allianceSelfReport` is not subject to that quota.
- No redaction hook needed in `qolRedactConfigDump` (`qol.js:225-247`)
  for this iteration — the self-report is **user-typed**, not a
  player name. Add it to `qol.js` `dump` only if a follow-up plan
  decides to expose alliance-pool data in the export blob.

## 6. Config surface

No new toggle. The pool is gated by the `[data-intel="view"]` selector
(§3.4). The self-report editor is the only new control; it lives next
to the existing alliance-note editor (`ui.js:700-704`) and uses the
same `createElement` discipline.

No HIGH-RISK toggle to set OFF (Low risk; read-only). The tracker
never fires a network request — its only outbound side effect is the
`save(STORE.ALLIANCE_SELF_REPORT, ...)` call, which is local GM
storage, not a post.

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no
`gbDomClick`, no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry,
no `gbCaptchaPause` key.

The renderer uses `box.textContent = html`. The selector option uses
`createElement('option')` + `appendChild`. Audit-I15 XSS discipline:
zero `innerHTML` for attacker-controlled strings. The
`alliance`/`town.name` strings are attacker-controlled (they come
from `parse-inline.js:89`); `textContent` is the primary defence, the
same as the existing dossier line at `intel.js:96`.

The self-report editor inputs are user-controlled; they pass through
`Math.max(0, Math.floor(+x || 0))` (§3.3) and are written via
`String(...)` coercion in the storage save path. No string is
rendered via `innerHTML`; the read-back path in `intelPoolByAlliance`
only does arithmetic.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`state.townResources` empty**: `ownTotals` is `{0,0,0}`; the
  `propias` row still renders with `0/0/0`. Fresh-install safe.
- **`state.findings` empty**: `spyTotals` is `{0,0,0}`. No nulls, no
  crashes.
- **`state.allianceSelfReport` empty**: `selfTotals` is `{0,0,0}`.
- **Bad input `wood: NaN` etc.**: the `clamp` helper at
  `intelSetAllianceSelfReport` (§3.3) coerces every input on write;
  bad input is silently coerced to `0`. Inputs use `type="number"`.
- **`__own__` collision**: the own-towns bucket uses the literal
  `__own__`, which Grepolis rejects in alliance names (verified by
  inspecting `parse-inline.js:89` alliance fallbacks).
- **Self-report for an unobserved alliance**: row appears with
  `propias 0/0/0`, `espiadas 0/0/0`, `reporte <user-typed>`. Useful
  for "alliance X exists, I want to track totals, I haven't spied
  them yet".
- **`intelView` undefined** (selector not landed per §3.4): branch
  never fires; falls through to existing dump blocks. No crash.
- **`state.findings.length > 200`**: `slice(0, 200)` caps the scan;
  per-finding loop is O(N) on at most 200 rows. Negligible cost.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session,
no failure).

- Build, install, open Intel tab. The `[data-intel="view"]` selector
  shows `Resumen` (default), `Pool 7.3`, and the other views if they
  have landed.
- With `state.towns` populated and at least one own town with
  `townResources[id].ok === true`: the `propias` row shows actual
  wood/stone/iron totals.
- Hand-trigger a spy report whose attacker alliance is known (or
  dev-console-seed `state.findings` with a synthetic entry matching
  `parseReport` schema at `parse-inline.js:39-100`). Open Pool view →
  that alliance gains an `espiadas` row with the defender's
  last-seen `resources`.
- Type `WoodFaction`, `10000`, `5000`, `2000` into the self-report
  inputs, click Guardar → `WoodFaction` row gains
  `reporte W10000/S5000/I2000`. Reload → still there.
- Click Guardar with all three inputs blank → self-report section
  disappears (§3.3 delete branch).
- Preflight → new `alliance pool` row; pass when `ownTowns > 0` or
  `spiedTowns > 0`; warn when both are 0.
- `state.dryRun = true` → pool still renders; no new posts in the
  Log tab; journal `mem:<n>` does not increment.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Alliance-wide resource totals for other members.** Not reachable
  from a single client (see §1.5). A real "alliance pool" would
  require scraping the in-game alliance forum or another player's
  client — both dropped in plan 27 §0.
- **Auto-publishing the pool.** Out of plan 27 §7.1 / §7.4 territory
  (the `alerts.js` Discord-webhook path). The user copies the `<pre>`
  text manually.
- **Cross-alliance auth.** Plan 7.6's member-activity dashboard is
  the companion piece that names the players behind the alliance
  strings; this plan does not name them.
- **Alliance forum scraping.** Explicitly out per plan 27 §0 (no
  `@connect` host beyond `discord.com` / `api.telegram.org` at
  `header.js:16-19`). A self-supplied URL fetch would require an
  `@connect` addition plus a sniff — file as a new plan.
- **Plan 6.13 / 7.2 dependency.** If neither has landed, the
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector does not exist and §3.4 has nothing
  to extend. File this plan as **blocked** and land 6.13 first
  (it owns the selector chrome).
