## 7.4-mass-intel-autopost.md

# 7.4 — Mass intel auto-post (Discord digest per spy)

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Med · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `alerts.js` (no new module) — add `intelDigest` event +
post surface; spool logic in a new IIFE-wrapped section at the bottom of
`alerts.js` (`build.py:54` slot, between `research.js` and `merchant.js`).
**Depends on:** none (2.1 spy report parser deep is the producer; if 2.1 is
absent, the feature still buffers raw `state.findings` ingestions — see §3).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

- **`alerts.js` is 89 lines, all outbound.** Reads: `state.webhookUrl`
  (`alerts.js:29`), `state.webhookEvents[event]` (`alerts.js:39`,
  `ev[event] === false`), `state.dryRun` (`alerts.js:31-34`). Writes
  the key-throttle maps `alertPending` and `alertLastSent` (definitions
  exist but are **not in the 89 lines of `alerts.js`** — grep confirms
  no `let alertPending` / `const alertLastSent` line is reached by the
  Read, so they must be declared in the closure of a sibling module —
  but they are referenced at `alerts.js:43-44`, `alerts.js:66`,
  `alerts.js:75-77`, `alerts.js:80`. The 5-minute per-key dedup
  (`alertLastSent[key] + 5*60*1000 > now`, `alerts.js:44`) only blocks
  the **same key** for 5 minutes; it does **not** enforce a per-day
  limit. This is the gap.
- **The Discord payload cap is at the `slice(0, 1800)` calls**
  (`alerts.js:46,60`). Discord's actual limit is 4096 chars per
  embed description and 6000 per embed (10 embeds/msg, body cap 2000
  chars). The existing 1800-char trim is comfortably below Discord's
  per-embed cap but is silent on oversize — payload gets `slice(0,1800)`
  mid-token and the JSON is corrupted. For digest payloads this matters
  more than for one-liner `attack` events.
- **The Telegram payload cap is `text.slice(0, 3900)`** (`alerts.js:54`)
  and is fine for digests. Telegram path uses `chat_id` resolved by
  `alertTelegramChatId` (`alerts.js:9-18`), `@connect` permits
  `api.telegram.org` (`header.js:19`).
- **Webhook event subscription is configurable but the keys are
  hard-coded.** `state.webhookEvents` default is
  `{ captcha:true, attack:true, warehouse:false, culture:false }`
  (`core.js:313`). The UI renders checkboxes for those four
  (`ui.js:1356-1359`) and `saveWebhookEvents` whitelists those names
  on save (`ui.js:1478-1484`). Adding a fifth event requires UI work,
  not state work. (The assignment cites the read at `ui.js:1168` and
  the save at `ui.js:1246-1253`; the actual locations are `ui.js:1354-1360`
  for the read and `ui.js:1477-1490` for the save — the older lines
  are the generic `setChk` / `bindToggle` plumbing that runs before
  the webhook block. Plan 26 §B2 caught this same drift when the
  `intelSetAllianceNote` line was off by 40 lines.)
- **One outbound webhook, no fan-out.** `alertWebhook` issues exactly
  one `gbXhr({ scope:'external', method:'POST', url, … })`
  (`alerts.js:67-83`) per deduped key. There is no multi-channel
  bridge — Discord + Telegram share one URL slot (`state.webhookUrl`).
- **No inbound side.** `@connect` `header.js:16-19` is
  `grepolis.com + discord.com + discordapp.com + api.telegram.org`;
  no other host is permitted (CLAUDE.md sandbox rule).
- **Findings buffer is `state.findings[]`**, capped at 500 entries
  (`spy.js:250-253`, with a 100-entry tighter cap in
  `core.js:1167-1172` under storage pressure). Each finding has
  `player` / `town` / `alliance` / `attacker` / `defender` /
  `vill_id` / `units` / `wall` / `note` / `allianceNote` / `ts`
  — verified by grepping `f.player`, `f.town.id`, `f.alliance`,
  `f.units` and reading `intelDossiers` (`intel.js:37-70`) and
  `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`). `intel.js:1-10`
  `intelPlayerKey(p)` is the canonical "player identifier" used by
  every existing dossier/intel read; the digest MUST reuse it so the
  throttle keyspace agrees with what the dossier shows.
- **Redaction convention is already in place.** `qolRedactConfigDump`
  (`qol.js:225-247`) is the export-side convention for dumps;
  outbound intel pattern-scans (`intel.js:235-238`) use the inline
  `String(h.name).slice(0, 2) + '***'` form when
  `state.exportRedact !== false`. The digest MUST apply the same
  per-name inline redact so a Discord channel does not become a
  player-name leak.

## 2. Gap

The current `alertWebhook(event, payload)` path will fire an alert
when something dramatic happens (attack arrival, watchlist match,
captcha) but nothing aggregates intel *outward* on a regular
cadence — so an alliance-mate playing on Discord never sees your
spies unless they read the GrepBot panel. Plan 27 §7 closes this by
"Discord digest per spy", throttled to once per player per day,
HIGH-RISK toggle default OFF, since the threat model is **data
exfiltration** (a leaked webhook URL, a leaked player name, a
Discord channel flooded with 500 digests overnight), not game
state mutation.

## 3. Design

A pure **outbound** feature. Reuses `alertWebhook`
(`alerts.js:28-88`) and the existing webhook URL/secret
(`state.webhookUrl`); adds nothing new to `gbXhr`'s transport, no
new `@connect` entry (Discord + Telegram are already
`header.js:16-19`), no new post scheduler.

A new IIFE-local section at the bottom of `alerts.js`
(`build.py:54`, between `research.js` and `merchant.js` in the
concat order — `alertWebhook` is already defined by the time the
new code runs, since the entire file is one IIFE body) adds five
module-local symbols:

```js
const intelDigestState = { queue: [], lastFlushAt: 0 };
const intelDigestPostedToday = {}; // playerKey -> utcDay
function intelDigestKeyFor(f) { return intelPlayerKey(f.player || f.attacker || f.defender) || 'unknown'; }
function intelDigestRedactName(name) { return state.exportRedact === false ? String(name) : String(name).slice(0, 2) + '***'; }
function intelDigestBuildPayload(playerKey, items) { /* see §7 */ }
function intelDigestTick() { /* see §7 */ }
```

The spool is `intelDigestState.queue[]`. Each item is
`{ ts, playerKey, summary }`. Per-spy enqueue happens inside a
small hook appended to `ingestReport` (which lives in
`spy.js:236-257`); the digest runs on:

1. **Burst trigger** — `intelDigestState.queue.length >= 12` (cap per
   digest, see Discord size discipline §7), OR
2. **Time trigger** — `Date.now() - intelDigestState.lastFlushAt >= 30 * 60 * 1000`,
   whichever comes first. The 30-min cadence piggybacks on
   `reportCatchUpRun`'s wake entry (`spy.js:120`,
   `gbWake('reportCatchUp', …, { priority: 80 })`): extend the
   existing done step (after `release()` at `spy.js:174`) to enqueue
   `gbWake('intelDigest', intelDigestTick, { priority: 90 })` so
   this feature has no scheduler of its own. No `gbInterval`.

Per-player-per-day throttle: before calling
`alertWebhook('intel-digest', payload)`, check
`intelDigestPostedToday[playerKey] === utcDay` (where
`utcDay = Math.floor(Date.now() / 86400000)`); if already true,
skip and drop the queued items with a one-line `gbLogT` on
`intel-digest-skip-<playerKey>` (TTL 24h). Mark only after the
underlying `alertWebhook` reaches the `gbXhr` POST (skipping
`pending`/`lastSent` 5-min dedup at `alerts.js:43-44` is *not* a
valid skip reason — a fresh key passes the per-key dedup every
day, so the `utcDay` stamp is the only thing that throttles across
days). The stamp is **not** flipped when `state.dryRun` short-circuits
the webhook at `alerts.js:31-34` (same-day replay against a non-empty
queue is the user's "log the dry run payload" path — see §9).

Storage of the stamp: `wkey(STORE.INTEL_DIGEST_POSTED)` (a new key
defined in `header.js:24-187`, added to `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`
`header.js:193-215` because it bears player keys). Loaded on
startup as `Object.create(null)`, written only on a state flip.

## 5. State & storage

- `state.intelDigestCfg.autoPost` — boolean, **default OFF**
  (HIGH-RISK rule + the silent-leak risk is real).
- `state.intelDigestCfg.batchMaxFindings` — number, default **12**
  (the Discord embed description cap; the existing
  `slice(0, 1800)` at `alerts.js:60` will trim further if a 12-line
  description overflows).
- `state.intelDigestCfg.batchMaxMinutes` — number, default **30**.
- `state.intelDigestPosted` — `{ [playerKey]: utcDayNumber }`,
  id-bearing ⇒ `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry needed for
  `STORE.INTEL_DIGEST_POSTED`. Loaded via
  `load(STORE.INTEL_DIGEST_POSTED, {})`; written via
  `save(wkey(STORE.INTEL_DIGEST_POSTED), state.intelDigestPosted)`
  inside `intelDigestTick` only when the per-day stamp flips.
- `state.intelDigestState` — in-memory only (not persisted).
  The queue survives no reload, by design — a fresh-day reload
  starts with an empty spool and the next report catches up.
- Prune TTL: 7 days, uniform. After 7d of no flips the map is
  bounded by the number of distinct intel'd players the user has
  seen (commonly <200); no periodic prune is required, but a
  defensive one-shot prune inside `intelDigestTick` drops keys
  whose `utcDay` is `< currentUtcDay - 7` to keep the map tidy.
- `configVer` bump: yes (work item 1).

## 6. Config surface

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state.intelDigestCfg.autoPost` | checkbox | **OFF** | HIGH-RISK default OFF per CLAUDE.md |
| `state.intelDigestCfg.batchMaxFindings` | number | `12` | min 4, max 50 |
| `state.intelDigestCfg.batchMaxMinutes` | number | `30` | min 5, max 240 |
| `state.webhookEvents['intel-digest']` | checkbox | `true` | opt-in to event firing (must be true to send even when `autoPost` is true) |
| `state.hostIntelDigest` | per-host flag | `false` | mirrors `state.enabledHosts[location.host]` (`core.js` per-host gate pattern); refuses to enqueue on a host the user hasn't enabled |

Two toggles are needed (and are *not* the same): the
**autoPost** (does the spool exist at all) and the
**webhookEvents['intel-digest']** (is this event name allowed to
fire through `alertWebhook`). Both default OFF-ish. A user who
wants digests must turn both on, mirroring the
`autoBandit + state.webhookEvents.attack` two-step.

## 7. Post surface & safety

- **Outbound only.** No `gbDomClick`, no `bridgePost`, no
  `gameAjaxPost`. The whole feature is a thin wrapper around
  `alertWebhook` — `gbXhr({ scope:'external', method:'POST', url,
  headers, data })` is the only network path, and that is already
  gated by `state.dryRun` at `alerts.js:31-34`.
- **`alertWebhook` event name**: `'intel-digest'`. The key under
  `state.webhookEvents` matches (`alerts.js:40`).
- **`alertWebhookKey`** (`alerts.js:19-27`) computes
  `event:cs:id` — `id` is the finding's `report_id` (or
  `report_id` fallback). The 5-min per-key dedup means two
  *different* spy findings on the same player will both pass the
  dedup; the per-day stamp at `state.intelDigestPosted[playerKey]`
  is the only thing that throttles across days.
- **Discord payload shape**:
  ```js
  { content: null,
    embeds: [{
      title: `GrepBot: intel-digest <playerRedacted>`,
      description: lines.join('\n').slice(0, 3500),
      footer: { text: location.host },
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    }] }
  ```
  The 3500-char pre-trim keeps the existing
  `slice(0, 1800)` (`alerts.js:60`) safely inside Discord's
  4096-char embed description cap. Telegram path uses
  `text.slice(0, 3900)` (`alerts.js:54`) — a long digest will
  trim further there.
- **Discord size discipline**:
  - On overflow, `intelDigestBuildPayload` truncates to the
    first 12 items and appends `(+N more today)`. There is **no
    fan-out** to multiple embeds — the existing single-embed
    shape is reused (no Discord `split` to a second message).
  - If a single finding summary exceeds 200 chars, the summary
    is trimmed to 197 chars + `…`. Player and town names get
    `intelDigestRedactName` regardless.
- **Redaction** (the main failure mode for this feature):
  - `intelDigestRedactName` is called on every player name in
    `alertWebhook`'s payload at composition time (`qol.js:230`).
    When `state.exportRedact === false` the raw name is sent
    (this is the user's explicit "I know what I'm doing"
    override; `qol.js:226-229` warns once).
  - The webhook URL **must never** appear in any log line. The
    `gbLogT` keys used (`intel-digest-*`) carry no URL fragment.
  - `state.captchaBreakers['intel-digest']` (see work item in
    §4) is the only breaker code that *could* land a Discord
    response into the log, and `captchaTrip` already wraps the
    body in `JSON.stringify(data).slice(0, 120)`
    (`spy.js:332`) — that trim is what stops a webhook URL leak
    via captcha detail.
- **`gbCaptchaPause` feature key**: `intelDigest`. Added to the
  captcha breaker registry the same way `'report'` is
  (`spy.js:126`, `spy.js:224`). When `captchaTrip('intelDigest',
  detail)` fires (status >= 400 from the Discord endpoint),
  `captchaPaused('intelDigest')` returns true and
  `intelDigestTick` short-circuits silently for the rest of the
  backoff (`state.captchaLadder`, `core.js:353,367`, default
  `[5, 15, 60]` minutes). Persisted via the existing
  `saveCaptcha` (`core.js:1336`) keyed by `STORE.CAPTCHA`
  (`header.js:200`).
- **Lock**: `gbLock('intel-digest', 60000)` during the flush
  (`GB_LOCK_TTL['intel-digest'] = 60000`, new entry in
  `core.js:145-173`). No new `*InFlight` boolean.
- **Dry-run**: `state.dryRun` already short-circuits
  `alertWebhook` (`alerts.js:31-34`) — the payload is logged as
  `DRY-RUN webhook intel-digest: <pretty JSON>` and nothing is
  sent. The per-day stamp is **not** flipped during dry run
  (work item 3's `state.intelDigestPosted` writer is gated on
  the actual POST reaching `gbXhr`, not on `alertWebhook`'s
  return value).
- **`@connect`**: no change. The `header.js:16-19` allowlist of
  `discord.com + discordapp.com + api.telegram.org` covers
  every destination this feature can post to. If a future
  iteration wants a custom Discord channel-message fetch (as
  the catalog row's literal phrasing tempts), that would need a
  wider allowlist and a Bearer token — out of scope per §10
  and consistent with sibling plan 7.1's
  "Discord channel-message fetch" out-of-scope line.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Webhook URL is empty**: `alertWebhook` returns at
  `alerts.js:30`. The per-day stamp **does** flip on success —
  but for an empty URL, "success" never arrives and we keep
  retrying every 30 min. We log once per session:
  `gbLogT('intel-digest-no-url', 86400000, …)` to keep
  stamp-table noise out of the log.
- **Webhook host is not in `@connect`**: `gbXhr` returns
  `'noajax'` (`core.js:1180-1188`); we never reach
  `alertWebhook` because `intelDigestTick` skips when
  `captchaPaused('intelDigest')`. The breaker opens
  immediately on the first attempt and stays open until
  `state.captchaLadder` (default `[5,15,60]`) decays.
- **`@connect` rejects a URL** because the user pasted a
  Discord channel-message URL (not a webhook endpoint):
  `alertWebhookUrlOk` (`alerts.js:4-8`) rejects the regex; log
  `webhook-url` once per 120s (`alerts.js:36`).
- **Per-day limit fires inside the flush**: `gbLogT`
  (`intel-digest-skip-<playerKey>`, TTL 24h) is the *only*
  log; the spool stays empty afterwards (we drop the
  player's queued items, not the whole queue). A subsequent
  flush for a different player can still fire.
- **Storage prune** during quota alarm
  (`core.js:1087-1140`, `state.findings` cap 100 under pressure):
  `state.findings` drops oldest; the digest spool is in-memory
  and unaffected. If `state.findings` was already pruned before
  the spool saw the entry, we just never get the digest line.
- **Reload in the middle of a flush**: `gbLock` (`core.js:189`)
  holds a foreign-token-aware handle; the foreign instance
  keeps the lock across reload (verified by
  `pagehide`/`beforeunload` both calling `gbUnlockAll()` per
  CLAUDE.md v1.4.0 lock registry).
- **Precondition invariant**:
  - The hook in `ingestReport` checks `state.intelDigestCfg.autoPost`
    *and* `state.enabledHosts[location.host] === true`; if either
    is false, no enqueue (read-from-state, no invented truth).
  - `intelDigestKeyFor` calls `intelPlayerKey` (`intel.js:1-10`),
    which returns `null` for `unknown`; the `|| 'unknown'`
    fallback groups unknown-actor findings under a single
    playerKey — they share the per-day stamp, by design (no
    player-name → no per-player cadence), and the daily
    cadence collapses 12 unknown-keyed items into one message.
  - `utcDay = Math.floor(Date.now() / 86400000)` is local-time
    agnostic (UTC days); the user-visible cadence lands
    whenever their clock rolls past UTC midnight. This is
    deliberate (no tz data in the state; plan 27 §13 says
    world-scoping is per-world not per-tz).

## 9. Validation gate

Per plan 27 §11 Med risk: dry-run + one hand-triggered firing + one
full wake-drain.

- **`state.dryRun` ON, ingest one fake spy finding** (`Log` →
  manual `forceIngestReport({...})` if shipped, or hand-visit
  inbox to make `reportCatchUpRun` actually queue a real one):
  Log shows `DRY-RUN webhook intel-digest: {…}` with the
  redacted payload; per-day stamp is **not** flipped
  (`state.intelDigestPosted === {}`).
- **Toggle `state.intelDigestCfg.autoPost = true`**,
  `state.webhookEvents['intel-digest'] = true`,
  `state.dryRun = false`: ingest 3 findings on player A and 2
  on player B in sequence. After 30 min (or after firing
  `intelDigestTick` from the DevTools console), Log shows
  `webhook: intel-digest` twice — once for player A, once for
  player B. Decisions subview shows two `ok` rows with
  `feature:'alert'`, `action:'webhook'`.
- **Ingest one more finding on player A** within the same UTC
  day: Log shows `intel-digest-skip-<playerA>` once and
  Decisions shows no new entry.
- **Ingest one finding on player C** (new player) right after:
  Log shows another `webhook: intel-digest` line. The
  per-player stamp map now has three keys.
- **Set `state.intelDigestPosted.<playerA> =
  Math.floor(Date.now()/86400000)` (today) and reload**:
  storage round-trips via `wkey()`; the stamp survives.
  On the next ingest of a player-A finding,
  `intelDigestTick` skips again with `intel-digest-skip-<playerA>`.
- **Wait past UTC midnight (or set system clock forward)**:
  `utcDay` increments; `intelDigestTick` fires the next time
  the spool reaches 12 or 30 min elapses.
- **Captcha test**: set
  `state.captchaBreakers['intelDigest'].until = Date.now() + 60000`:
  `intelDigestTick` short-circuits silently via
  `captchaPaused('intelDigest')`. Captcha breaker key works
  because the webhook response path (alerts.js:74) is what
  `captchaTrip` would extend; since the spec is
  "external-only" we mirror the captcha-on-DND pattern by
  detecting the `gbXhr` 429/503 path during `intelDigestTick`'s
  caller (`spy.js:120`'s wake) and calling `captchaTrip`
  directly when the `gbXhr` returns a 429 from the webhook
  — implementation detail belongs in work item 4.
- **Redaction test** with `state.exportRedact === true` and a
  payload with `playerName = 'loremipsum123'`: payload sent to
  Discord shows `lo***`. Flip
  `state.exportRedact = false`; same payload shows the raw
  name (and `qol.js:227`'s one-shot warning fires).

## 10. Out of scope

- **Inbound telegram/discord** (chat → GrepBot). Plan 27 §0 drops
  this; CLAUDE.md "no phone-home" and the lack of a webhook
  receiver in the userscript sandbox make it impossible without
  a server.
- **Fan-out to per-alliance channels.** Each `state.webhookUrl`
  is one destination; multi-channel support would require a
  destination map in `state.intelDigestCfg`. Defer until
  specifically requested (consistent with sibling plan 7.1's
  "cross-alliance auth" out-of-scope).
- **Alliance-digest cadence** (one digest per alliance, not per
  player). Plan 7.6 ("Alliance member activity dashboard")
  owns the read-side; cross-reference, do not duplicate.
- **Cross-alliance auth** on the digest payload. The author of
  the digest is the player who ingested the finding; we redact
  author identity (no payload has an `author` field). Anyone
  reading the Discord channel can correlate `worldKey = X,
  intelPostedBy = null`; that's the threat model.
- **Discord channel-message fetch** (catalog row's "alliance
  intake via webhook" phrasing). Same reasoning as sibling
  plan 7.1's §10. Out.
- **Player notes and `allianceNotes` inclusion in the digest
  payload.** `intelDossiers` already attaches these
  (`intel.js:65-68`), but they are user-private; a digest sent
  to a Discord channel must never carry them. `intelDigestBuildPayload`
  composes the payload from `state.findings` only; the notes
  live in `intel.js`'s render path, never in this payload.
- **A `@connect` host addition for a paste service** that
  might carry the digest to a wider audience. Defer per
  CLAUDE.md sandbox rule; not requested.

---

## 7.5-nap-war-tracking.md

# 7.5 — NAP / war tracking (player + alliance + status overlay)

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js` (state + render + setters) and `src/ui.js` (Intel panel editor rows). No new module. No edit to `qol.js` (see §1).
**Depends on:** none (read paths use existing `state.findings`, `state.playerNotes`, `state.allianceNotes`; setters already exist per plan 26 §B2).
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

## 1. What exists today

Verified against `src/intel.js`, `src/qol.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/native-ui.js`, `src/core.js`, `src/header.js`, `build.py`.

- **Player notes path is complete.** `intelSetNote(player, note)` (`intel.js:115-120`) writes `state.playerNotes[player]`, persisted by `save(STORE.PLAYER_NOTES, …)`. `STORE.PLAYER_NOTES` is in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:206`). Read paths: dossiers (`intel.js:65`), watchlist rule (`intel.js:148-150`), Intel dump (`intel.js:103-108` analogue for alliance notes). The Input row exists in the Intel tab (`ui.js:696-698`) and the click handler is at `ui.js:997-1001`.
- **Alliance notes path is now complete.** `intelSetAllianceNote(alliance, note)` was added in v3.x per plan 26 §B2 and lives at `intel.js:124-132`. The Input row is at `ui.js:701-703`, click handler at `ui.js:1002-1007`. `STORE.ALLIANCE_NOTES` is at `header.js:131` and in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:206`).
- **Plan 27's "qol.js (autocomplete)" hint is wrong.** `qol.js` is 436 lines and contains activity pause (`qol.js:1-11`), city templates (`qol.js:12-44`), goals/planner/dashboard/health (`qol.js:46-189`), overview (`qol.js:192-222`), config export/import (`qol.js:223-268`), config presets (`qol.js:272-382`), and the orchestrator config tables (`qol.js:384-436`). **Zero `autocomplete|datalist|typeahead|suggest|combo` hits anywhere in `src/`** (verified with `rtk grep -i "autocomplete\|typeahead\|datalist\|suggest\|combo" src/*.js` returning only the placeholder `<input id="gb-note-player">` in `ui.js:696`). The current player/alliance name inputs are bare `<input>` elements with `placeholder="player"` / `placeholder="alianza"` (`ui.js:696,701`) — no `list=`, no `datalist` child, no JavaScript helper. Plan 27 §6's hint is a phantom; the autocomplete lives nowhere. v4.4 ships a small inline `<datalist>` in the new editor rows, not a qol.js helper.
- **No NAP / war / diplomatic data is read from the game.** `rtk grep -i "nap\|diplom"` over `src/` returns 0 hits. Grepolis exposes a diplomacy model in the client (`ITowns`/`MM` provides `Player`, `Alliance`, `AllianceDiplomacyRelation` collections in the modern client), but it is **not** consumed by GrepBot today. The store in 7.5 is **player-managed** (the user types "Treaty of foo with bar"), not driven by a game endpoint. Plan 27 §13's "never invent a game endpoint" rule means a live `AllianceDiplomacyRelation` / `MEMBER_PROFILE` route is **not** in this plan; the work item below §4.1 explicitly opts to keep the store user-managed in v4.4 and lists the bridge endpoint as an unknown for a future sniff.
- **The map is canvas, not DOM.** Verified by sibling 6.7 §1: `nativeUiScan` (`native-ui.js:838`) reads `.window_content,.gpwindow_content,#unit_order` — town *windows*, never map tiles. There is no `data-town-id` on the map. The only DOM town-id surface on the map is the game's own **canvas + town-info popup** that opens on click (the same popup 6.7's context menu mounts next to). Map "tinting" by direct canvas paint is out per plan 27 §0 (canvas/WebGL/fingerprint noise needs WebExtension privileges the userscript context does not have — plan 27 §0 "Conditional / gray-area") and per sibling 6.7 §10 ("Map tile tinting. The map is canvas; there is no DOM tile to tint"). The "map tint" half of 7.5 is therefore re-anchored as a **status overlay on the Intel panel dossier rows** (the only DOM surface where towns are listed and tagged by their player/alliance). The colour is a CSS rule on the existing `<pre class="intel-panel">` lines plus a thin legend — no game DOM mutation, no canvas read, no Shadow-DOM hide.
- **Dry-run and DOM-fallback contract is the same as 6.7.** `gbDomClick` (`core.js:941-951`) is the only DOM click that respects `state.dryRun`. No new post surface is added (the store is local + persist-only); nothing routes through `bridgePost`/`gameAjaxPost`.
- **Disposal hook is `__grepbotDispose`** (`core.js:114-143`). It clears `gbListenerBag`, `gbTimerBag`, `gbXhrBag`, restores `gbHookOrig` (lines 78-98), removes the panel + queue center + every `.gb-native-qctl` and `.gb-native-panel`. Any new DOM listener registered with `gbListen` (`core.js:56-65`) is dropped on dispose automatically.
- **Plan 27 §9 lists 15 already-shipped ideas.** None of them is a NAP/war store. The "Alliance notes" line in the wishlist is the only neighbouring feature, and it is already shipped (plan 26 §B2 + `intel.js:124-132`). 7.5 is genuinely new work.

## 2. Gap

GrepBot's Intel tab shows player notes (`ui.js:696-700`) and alliance notes (`ui.js:701-704`) as free-text fields with no semantic meaning. Two natural extensions are missing:

1. A **typed** diplomatic status store (NAP / war / neutral / ally) keyed by player id and by alliance name, with values that mean something to the player and that the bot can read back to colour its own intel view.
2. A **status overlay** rendering that status back to the player in the most visible place: the dossier rows in the Intel panel, which is the only DOM surface where player + alliance names are already listed by their map presence.

There is no way to add a map-canvas tint (sibling 6.7 §1 + plan 27 §0 already closed that path). The 6.7 context menu already lets the player right-click a town and call `intelSetNote` / `intelSetAllianceNote` — 7.5 reuses the same entry points and adds a **status dropdown** in the same editor row so the player can mark "Bob is at war with me" instead of typing free text.

## 3. Design

Two halves, sharing the same in-memory store. No new post surface, no new `*InFlight` boolean, no new `gbInterval`, no new module.

**Half 1 — store + editor (extend `intel.js` + `ui.js`).**

```
state.napStatus = {
  players: { [playerKey]: 'nap' | 'war' | 'neutral' | 'ally' },
  alliances: { [allianceName]: 'nap' | 'war' | 'neutral' | 'ally' },
}
// playerKey is the same key the dossiers already use:
//   intelPlayerKey(p) at intel.js:1-10 — id:<id> for object players, raw name for strings.
//   This is the rule intelDossiers/intelPatternScan already key by, so the lookup
//   is a single Map-style hit per dossier row.
```

- Three new setters in `intel.js`: `intelSetPlayerStatus(player, status)`, `intelSetAllianceStatus(alliance, status)`, `intelClearStatus(...)`. Status is one of `'nap' | 'war' | 'neutral' | 'ally'`; null/undefined/empty string deletes the entry. Same 200-char note ceiling does not apply — status is a 4-value enum, not free text. Persisted via two new `STORE.*` keys (see §5).
- A new `intelStatusFor(player, alliance)` resolution in `intel.js` — given a player and (optionally) the alliance that owns them, returns the stronger of the two statuses. Strength order for rendering: `war > ally > nap > neutral > unknown`. The function reads `state.allianceNotes` (player-side note does not affect diplomatic status; the new store is the only source of truth for the four enum values).
- A new `intelApplyStatusToDossier(d)` decorator (called from `intelDossiers` at `intel.js:46-72`) sets `d.status = intelStatusFor(...)` and `d.statusSource = 'player' | 'alliance' | null`. Dossier render (`intel.js:92-97`) appends `[WAR]/[NAP]/[ALLY]/[NEUTRAL]` to the row.

**Half 2 — status overlay in the Intel panel (extend `ui.js` + small CSS).**

- `renderIntel` already calls `box.textContent = html` (`intel.js:112`). The current rendering is a `<pre>` with plain text. v4.4 wraps that in a CSS-styled structure so rows can be tinted without breaking the existing `<pre>` contract. **Concretely:** replace the `textContent` write with a DOM-construction loop that builds each row via `document.createElement('div')`, sets its text via `row.textContent = lineText` (so attacker-controlled player / alliance strings from `f.attacker.name` / `f.alliance` / `f.defender.name` / `state.playerNotes[…]` / `state.allianceNotes[…]` are escaped by the browser, never serialized into HTML — same XSS discipline as sibling plans 7.2 / 7.3 / 7.6), and toggles `row.classList.add('gb-intel-row', 'status-' + status, …)` for the accent. No `box.innerHTML = …`. The `<pre>` outer wrapper stays — only the children change. CSS (added inline in `intel.js` via `GM_addStyle` so no `theme.css` regen is needed) is **four** rules: `.gb-intel-row.status-war { background: rgba(255,80,80,0.18) }` and the three analogous rules for `nap`/`ally`/`neutral`. Player Spanish labels live in the row text: `[GUERRA]`, `[PAZ]`, `[ALIADO]`, `[NEUTRAL]`. Theme.css is untouched.
- The status colour comes from the dossier's `d.status` (resolved in the store decorator). Rows with no status set retain today's plain rendering. The legend is a single header line at the top of the panel: `Leyenda: [GUERRA] rojo · [PAZ] verde · [ALIADO] azul · [NEUTRAL] amarillo`. The legend itself is a status-free row.
- The editor row in `ui.js` (next to the existing text-note rows, `ui.js:696-704`) gains two more input groups: a player dropdown + status `<select>` and an alliance dropdown + status `<select>`. The "dropdown" is a `<datalist>` attached to the existing text input so the player can type a partial name and the bot offers the names already seen in `state.findings` (server-rendered, no post). When the player picks a `<option>` from the datalist, the click handler at `ui.js:997-1007` is supplemented with a sibling handler that calls `intelSetPlayerStatus` / `intelSetAllianceStatus`. The existing `intelSetNote` / `intelSetAllianceNote` paths stay — the new editor does not replace them; the player can keep free-text notes.

**Hit-test and teardown (sharing 6.7 + `native-ui.js` patterns):**

- 7.5 does **not** add a sibling popup on the map. The map is canvas (6.7 §1). The 6.7 context menu (if and when it ships) already calls `intelSetNote` / `intelSetAllianceNote` from a right-click; 7.5 adds a new "Diplomacia" item that calls `intelSetPlayerStatus` / `intelSetAllianceStatus` with a 4-button prompt (NAP / WAR / ALLY / NEUTRAL / Cancel). That prompt is a `gameUw().confirm(...)` ring, not a custom DOM popup — no map mutation, no overlay div, no canvas read.
- 7.5 adds **no new DOM mutation** outside the Intel panel. `__grepbotDispose` (`core.js:114-143`) tears the panel down on dispose; the rows are children of the panel `<pre>` and die with it. No `gbListenerBag` entry is added by 7.5 outside the existing `'#gb-note-save'` + `'#gb-anote-save'` handlers, which are already wired by `ui.js:997-1007`.

Preflight sends nothing; it only confirms the states are loadable.

## 5. State & storage

- New: `state.napPlayers: { [playerKey: string]: 'nap'|'war'|'neutral'|'ally' }`. Defaults to `{}`. Persisted via `STORE.NAP_PLAYERS` (new key in `header.js:131`). Id-bearing ⇒ `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:206`).
- New: `state.napAlliances: { [allianceName: string]: 'nap'|'war'|'neutral'|'ally' }`. Defaults to `{}`. Persisted via `STORE.NAP_ALLIANCES` (new key). Id-bearing ⇒ `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`.
- No new `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry beyond the two above (the existing `state.allianceNotes`/`state.playerNotes` keep their `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` placement — no rename).
- `configVer` bump is **not** required because the new keys are pure state, not Config (the editor exposes them as a row in the Intel tab, not as a field in the Config tab; `qolExportConfig` at `qol.js:248-253` does not include `napPlayers`/`napAlliances` and that is intentional — diplomatic status is per-player knowledge, not a Config preset).
- Prune: none. A diplomatic status is long-lived and never auto-expires. The watchlist (`state.watchlist`) and alliance notes (`state.allianceNotes`) follow the same policy — both stay forever.

## 6. Config surface

- **No Config tab toggle.** 7.5 is a feature the player either uses (it is always on) or does not. A "Diplomatic status" toggle in Config would be misleading: turning it off would still leave the persistent store and the datalist suggestions saying "NAP / WAR / ALLY" on the player row. The store itself is the toggle.
- The editor rows in the Intel panel (`ui.js:696-704`) carry a Spanish label: `Diplomacia jugador` / `Diplomacia alianza`. They live in the same scroll section as the existing text-note rows. The `<select>` options are `nap`/`war`/`neutral`/`ally` with Spanish labels: `Paz (NAP)`, `Guerra`, `Neutral`, `Aliado`. The `value` attributes are pinned (CLAUDE.md "UI language: when translating an option label, pin an explicit value").
- The legend row in the Intel panel (`renderIntel` first child) is unconditional: `Leyenda: [GUERRA] rojo · [PAZ] verde · [ALIADO] azul · [NEUTRAL] amarillo`. The legend is one `<div>` with no status class and is always visible.

## 7. Post surface & safety

7.5 adds **no post surface**. The store is local; the read paths (`state.findings` → dossier render) are read-only. The editor writes only to `state.napPlayers` / `state.napAlliances` via `save(STORE.NAP_PLAYERS, …)` / `save(STORE.NAP_ALLIANCES, …)`. The `save` helper is a `GM_setValue` wrapper, not a network post.

- No `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` registration. No `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry. No `gbCaptchaPause` feature key. No `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry. No `state.dryRun` gate — there is no post to gate.
- `__grepbotDispose` (`core.js:114-143`) tears the panel down on dispose; the Intel panel rows live inside the panel and die with it. The store `state.napPlayers` / `state.napAlliances` survives dispose (they are `GM_setValue`-persisted) and is reloaded on the next session — that is the intended contract.
- **Template-sniff contracts preserved.** Plan 27 §0 calls out `claimTpl`, `attackTpl`, `ibAction` as untouchable. 7.5 does not rename any artifact variable, does not touch any learned template, does not hide any UI element in Shadow DOM. The status overlay is plain CSS on the panel's own `<pre>` children; the rows are constructed in `renderIntel` and do not traverse the game DOM. Plan 27 §0 "Shadow-DOM UI hide / variable rename in artifact" is not violated.
- **Game canvas never touched.** Verified by sibling 6.7 §1: the map is canvas, the town-info popup is the only DOM town-id surface on the map. 7.5 does not query the canvas, does not read its pixel data, does not paint onto it. The status colour lives entirely inside the panel.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Editor row receives a name not in `state.findings`.** The datalist is a hint, not a validator. Typing a free-text name and clicking `Guardar` calls `intelSetPlayerStatus(name, status)` with the typed string. The setter stores `state.napPlayers[name] = status` regardless of whether the game knows that player. The dossier render at `intel.js:46-72` only colours rows whose `intelPlayerKey` matches a player in `state.findings`, so free-text names that no report ever carried are stored but never surfaced. This is acceptable: the player may know a player by a name that no report has reached the bot yet. The store stays consistent. The precondition invariant holds — every read goes through a real lookup, no invented id.
- **Player renames / alliance tag changes.** Grepolis allows players to change names; alliances can be re-tagged. The dictionary key is the **typed string** at the moment the editor accepted it, so a renamed player leaves a stale entry. This matches the existing `state.playerNotes` and `state.allianceNotes` policies (`intel.js:115-132`) — those are also typed-string keys with no rename tracking. v4.4 ships the same contract; a future plan could add a `MergedAlliances` map if rename tracking becomes a real player need.
- **Modal window opens over the Intel panel.** The `<pre>` is hidden behind the modal window; `renderIntel` early-returns when the section is hidden (`intel.js:78-79`). The status overlay is then effectively off-screen. The dossier data is intact and re-renders when the panel is shown again. No error, no leak.
- **Datalist never populates.** `state.findings` may be empty on a fresh world. The datalist is empty; the `<input>` becomes a free-text field. The editor still works. The legend is still rendered. Status values set on unknown names are persisted silently (handled above). `gbLogT('nap-datalist-empty', 600000, …)` once per scan if preflight wants to surface it.
- **Status enum drifts.** A new client shape adds a fifth diplomatic enum (e.g. `'non-aggression'`) that the bot does not model. `isNapStatus` returns false for the new value, the setter rejects it, the editor dropdown does not show it. The player cannot set a status the bot does not understand. No silent data corruption.
- **`__grepbotDispose` mid-edit.** The panel is torn down (`core.js:135-136`). The handler never fires; the in-memory state is lost (it would have been persisted to `GM_setValue` only on click). The next session loads the previously persisted state. No partial state — `save` is atomic.
- **Tab leader lost (`gbTabLeader === false`, `core.js:11`).** The editor is local UI; it does not need the tab leader. Reading `state.napPlayers` / `state.napAlliances` is local. No `flash('GrepBot está activo en otra pestaña')` guard is needed (the guard is reserved for post paths; the editor writes only to `GM_setValue`).

## 9. Validation gate

Low-risk (plan 27 §11: Preflight + one in-game session, no failure).

- Open the Intel tab. The new editor rows appear with the datalist empty. Type a player name known to `state.findings` (one the bot has seen in a report) and pick `Guerra` from the dropdown. Click `Guardar`. Log: `nap: set player <name> = war`. The Intel panel rows re-render; the dossier for that player shows `[GUERRA]` in the row text and a red background.
- Repeat for an alliance name. The dossier's player row gets `[PAZ]` (green) when the alliance is set to NAP and the player has no individual status — the dossier-level `intelStatusFor` falls back to the alliance side.
- Set a player to `war` and the underlying alliance to `nap`. The dossier row shows `[GUERRA]` (red) — the player-side entry wins per the strength order in §3. The keyboard shortcut is not exercised; the UI is mouse-driven.
- Open a new tab in the same world → the status values are still there (`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` keeps them). Open a different world (`wkey` differs) → empty store, no leak.
- Run with `state.dryRun === true` (Defence-in-depth: 7.5 has no post surface, so dry-run is a no-op). Log: no `DRY-RUN nap: …` is printed because no DOM click handler is gated by `gbDomClick` — the editor save is a direct `save()` call. The status still lands in `state.napPlayers` and the dossier still colours. Dry-run coverage is verified by the journal's silence — no `skip:dryrun` row is ever generated by 7.5.
- Preflight row `diplomatic status store`: pass when both `state.napPlayers` and `state.napAlliances` are objects. Warn when both are empty (the player has not used the feature yet; not a failure).
- `__grepbotDispose` smoke: toggle the panel off → the Intel panel rows are removed from the DOM (`core.js:135-136`). The store survives in `GM_setValue`. Re-enable the panel → the rows re-render from `state.napPlayers` / `state.napAlliances`. No `gbListenerBag` leak (the only added handlers are wired on the same panel-level delegate that already tears down cleanly).
- Manual confirmation that the **map canvas is untouched** — the world map renders identically with the feature on or off; the status colour is panel-only.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Live diplomatic state from the game.** Grepolis exposes `AllianceDiplomacyRelation` / `MEMBER_PROFILE` collections in the modern client; the bridge endpoint is **not** known to this plan and would need a `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` sniff + `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` entry. v4.4 ships the player-managed store. A future plan 7.5b can read the game-side state and reconcile, but **must not** invent the endpoint — the work item is "sniff via `gbAjaxWatch` while a player alliance page is open, capture the template into `TPL_FEATURE_MAP`", not a payload guess.
- **Map-canvas tinting.** The map is canvas. Plan 27 §0 forbids canvas/WebGL fingerprint noise (WebExtension privileges). Sibling 6.7 §10 closed the same path. 7.5 ships the panel dossier overlay only.
- **NAP / war auto-detection from incoming attacks.** `intelWatchlistScan` (`intel.js:186-205`) already fires `alertWebhook('attack', …)` on watchlist hits; that path could in principle auto-set a player to `war` after N hits. That is a separate plan (an "auto-detect" feature) and is **not** in 7.5 — auto-mutation of player-managed state would violate CLAUDE.md "HIGH-RISK toggles default OFF" and would belong in a CONFIRM-gated feature, not in a Low/M read-mostly plan.
- **Player-vs-alliance reconciliation.** Setting a player to `nap` while their alliance is `war` is a conflict the user can resolve manually. v4.4 does not auto-resolve; the strength order (player > alliance) is the only rule.
- **Export/import of diplomatic status.** `qolExportConfig` (`qol.js:248-253`) and `qolImportConfig` (`qol.js:254-268`) do not carry `state.napPlayers` / `state.napAlliances`. Diplo status is per-player knowledge, not a config preset. If a future plan wants to export it, it belongs in a separate "Intelligence transfer" plan.
- **Mobile / touch editor.** The Intel tab editor is mouse-driven (same as the existing note rows). Touch support is whatever the browser provides for native `<select>` + `<input>`.
- **Bulk-set from a treaty page.** A "click a list of N players and set them all to `nap`" UI is a future UX plan. v4.4 ships one-player / one-alliance at a time.

## 7.6-alliance-activity-dashboard.md

# 7.6 — Alliance member activity dashboard

**Bucket:** v4.4 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/intel.js`; no new module, no new state, no `build.py` MODULES change
**Depends on:** plan 6.13 (`[data-intel="view"]` selector chrome — same dependency rule as plans 7.2 §3.4 and 7.3 §3.4)
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.8.2

> Read-mostly per plan 27 §7. The dashboard is a per-client view of
> player activity the bot has *observed* — spies seen, attacks
> received, watchlist hits, pattern hits — grouped by player name
> with optional alliance filter. The bot cannot enumerate the
> alliance roster (see §1.5), so "member" here means "any player who
> has shown up in a report the bot ingested", filtered by the
> alliance string the user types.

---

## 1. What exists today

- `state.findings[]` (`src/core.js:221`, capped at 500 by
  `spy.js:250-253` then pruned to 100 by `core.js:1167-1172`) holds
  every parsed report. Per-finding shape (`parse-inline.js:39-100`):
  `{id, ts, type, attacker:{id,name,alliance,...}, defender:{...},
  town:{id,name,x,y}, units, resources, alliance, ...}` — exactly
  what the dashboard reads.
- `intelDossiers()` (`src/intel.js:34-71`) already aggregates findings
  **per-player** (`intelPlayerKey` at `intel.js:1-10`) with
  `reports, units, towns, walls, last, note, allianceNote`. The
  dashboard extends this with two extra counts: `attacksOnMe`
  (defender is me) and `attacksByMe` (attacker is me).
- `intelMyIdentity()` (`intel.js:17-27`) reads the player's id/name
  via `MM.getModelByNameAndPlayerId('Player')` with `Game.player_id`
  as fallback (`intel.js:23`). Used by `intelActorIsMe`
  (`intel.js:28-33`), the existing "who is me" gate.
- `intelPatternScan()` (`intel.js:206-245`) already groups findings
  by player (24h window) and emits `attackPatternNote`. The dashboard
  reuses the same grouping with a wider window (default 7d) and an
  alliance filter.
- `state.watchHits` (`core.js:373`, key `STORE.WATCH_HITS` at
  `header.js:170`) records watchlist-rule hits by rule string.
  Already world-scoped.
- `state.allianceNotes` (`core.js:341`, `STORE.ALLIANCE_NOTES`,
  `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `header.js:206`) is the per-alliance
  free-text map. The dashboard reads it to attach the same
  `[aliado: ...]` suffix the existing dossier line carries at
  `intel.js:96`.
- The session-local `intelView` flag (owned by plan 6.13 §3.3, with
  contributions from plans 7.2 §3.4 and 7.3 §3.4) lives in
  `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`).

### 1.5 Game model: what is NOT reachable

Same honesty boundary as plan 7.3 §1.5: the bot does not have access
to the alliance roster. The dashboard's "member" set is the union of
player strings seen in `state.findings[i].attacker.name` or
`defender.name`, filtered by the alliance string the user types into
a small filter input. A real "list every member of alliance X with
their last login" needs the alliance forum or another player's
client — both out of plan 27 §0.

## 2. Gap

`renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) emits one line per dossier
(`intel.js:93-97`), but the per-player row carries only
`reports, note, allianceNote` — no notion of *role* (attacker vs
defender vs both), no window filter, no alliance filter, no
watchlist/pattern overlay. When a player wants to answer "who in
alliance X has been most active against me in the last 7d?" they
have to mentally aggregate the raw findings tab. Plan 7.6 gives them
that view without inventing data.

## 3. Design

One aggregator, one renderer, one filter input, no post surface.

### 3.1 Aggregator

Add `intelMemberActivity(opts)` to `src/intel.js`, placed next to
`intelDossiers` (`intel.js:34-71`). It returns
`Array<{player, alliance, key, reports, attacksOnMe, attacksByMe,
spiedByMe, towns, firstTs, lastTs, allianceNote}>` sorted by
`lastTs` descending:

```js
function intelMemberActivity(opts) {
  opts = opts || {};
  const filter = String(opts.alliance || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  const cut = Date.now() - ((Number.isFinite(opts.windowHours) ? opts.windowHours : 24 * 7) * 3600000);
  const me = intelMyIdentity();
  const byPlayer = {};
  const inFilter = (s) => s && String(s).toLowerCase() === filter;
  (state.findings || []).forEach(f => {
    if (!f || !(f.ts >= cut)) return;
    const atk = f.attacker || null, def = f.defender || null;
    const atkA = (atk && (atk.alliance || atk.alliance_name)) || f.alliance || null;
    const defA = (def && (def.alliance || def.alliance_name)) || null;
    if (filter && !inFilter(atkA) && !inFilter(defA)) return;
    const add = (p, alliance) => {
      if (!p) return;
      const key = intelPlayerKey(p) || ('name:' + p);
      let r = byPlayer[key];
      if (!r) { r = { player: intelPlayerLabel(p, key), key, alliance: alliance || null, reports: 0, attacksOnMe: 0, attacksByMe: 0, spiedByMe: 0, towns: new Set(), firstTs: f.ts, lastTs: f.ts, allianceNote: null }; byPlayer[key] = r; }
      r.reports++;
      if (intelActorIsMe(def, me)) r.attacksOnMe++;
      else if (intelActorIsMe(atk, me)) r.attacksByMe++;
      else r.spiedByMe++;
      if (f.town && (f.town.id != null || f.town.name)) r.towns.add(String(f.town.id || f.town.name));
      if (f.ts < r.firstTs) r.firstTs = f.ts;
      if (f.ts > r.lastTs) r.lastTs = f.ts;
      if (state.allianceNotes && r.alliance && state.allianceNotes[r.alliance]) r.allianceNote = state.allianceNotes[r.alliance];
    };
    if (atk) add(atk, atkA);
    if (def && !intelActorIsMe(def, me) && !intelActorIsMe(atk, me)) add(def, defA);
  });
  return Object.values(byPlayer).map(r => ({ ...r, towns: r.towns.size })).sort((a, b) => b.lastTs - a.lastTs);
}
```

Notes: the aggregator never *invents* a roster — a player appears
only when at least one finding names them. The `key` is
`intelPlayerKey(...)` (same discipline as `intelDossiers` at
`intel.js:45`). Role counts come straight from `intelActorIsMe`
(`intel.js:28-33`), no second implementation. Alliance attribution
falls back to `f.alliance` (`parse-inline.js:89`) when the player
object does not carry one.

### 3.2 Renderer

Append a new branch to `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) gated by
`intelView === 'activity'` (same module-local `let` plans 6.13, 7.2,
7.3 share):

```js
if (intelView === 'activity') {
  const alliance = (document.querySelector('#gb-intel-alliance-filter') || {}).value || '';
  const rows = intelMemberActivity({ alliance, windowHours: 24 * 7 });
  let html = '=== Actividad por miembro (7d, vista local) ===\n';
  if (!rows.length) html += '(sin actividad en la ventana)\n';
  else for (const r of rows) {
    const last = new Date(r.lastTs).toLocaleString();
    html += `${r.player} (${r.alliance || '?'})${r.allianceNote ? ` [aliado: ${r.allianceNote}]` : ''}: ${r.reports} informe(s), me-ataca ${r.attacksOnMe}, yo-ataco ${r.attacksByMe}, espiado-por-mi ${r.spiedByMe}, ${r.towns} ciudad(es), ultima ${last}\n`;
  }
  box.textContent = html;
  try { intelPatternScan(); } catch (_) {}
  return;
}
```

`box.textContent` is the only safe assignment (audit-I15; player
names and alliance strings are attacker-controlled).

### 3.3 Filter input

Append a single text input to the Intel section chrome
(`ui.js:692-708`) below the alliance-note editor row:

```js
const f = document.createElement('input');
f.id = 'gb-intel-alliance-filter';
f.placeholder = 'alianza (filtro)';
f.style.cssText = 'width:160px;background:#111;color:#cfc;border:1px solid #333;padding:2px 4px;font-size:11px';
f.addEventListener('input', () => renderIntel());
```

The renderer reads the input's current value on every render
(§3.2); no state field is added. The input persists for the session
because the Intel section is rebuilt only on tab switch.

### 3.4 View selector integration

Same selector dependency as plans 7.2 §3.4 and 7.3 §3.4: this plan
contributes `<option value="activity">Actividad 7.6</option>` to the
`[data-intel="view"]` selector owned by plan 6.13 §3.3. If neither
6.13, 7.2, nor 7.3 has landed, the selector does not exist and the
new branch is unreachable. File as §10 dependency.

## 4. Work items

1. `src/intel.js` — add `function intelMemberActivity(opts)` per
   §3.1, placed next to `intelDossiers` (`intel.js:34-71`).
   All undefined inputs ⇒ empty result, never throw.
2. `src/intel.js` — extend `renderIntel` (`intel.js:75-114`) with
   the `if (intelView === 'activity')` branch per §3.2. Branch
   returns early after `box.textContent`. Keep
   `try { intelPatternScan(); } catch (_) {}` at the bottom
   (orthogonal).
3. `src/ui.js` — append the alliance filter input to the Intel
   section (`ui.js:692-708`), bound to `renderIntel()` on `input`.
   Use `createElement` + `textContent`; **no `innerHTML`** for any
   label or placeholder.
4. `src/ui.js` — add `<option value="activity">Actividad 7.6</option>`
   to the `[data-intel="view"]` selector that plan 6.13 §4.4
   introduces. Same dependency rule as plans 7.2 §4.4 and 7.3 §4.8:
   if the selector does not exist yet, **do not create it here** —
   file §10 as blocked and land 6.13 first.
5. `src/stats.js` — extend `preflightRun` (`src/stats.js:12-268`)
   with a row `alliance activity` that calls `intelMemberActivity({})`
   and reports `{members: N, withAlliance: K, attacksOnMe: A}`. Pass
   when `members > 0`; warn when 0 (no findings ingested yet).
6. **No `src/header.js` change.** No new `STORE.*` key — the
   dashboard reads `state.findings`, `state.allianceNotes`,
   `state.watchHits`, and `state.towns` (all already in
   `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` at `header.js:194-215`). No `configVer`
   bump (the `state` schema is unchanged).
7. **No new `gbInterval` / `gbLock` / `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry.** The
   aggregator runs inside the existing `renderIntel` cycle, already
   triggered by `spy.js:255`, `ui.js:1089`, and `ui.js:1006`.
8. **No `build.py` MODULES change.** Plan 27 §7 row 7.6 already
   says "extend `intel.js`" — that is the right scope; no new
   module needed.

## 5. State & storage

None new. The dashboard reads `state.findings`, `state.allianceNotes`,
`state.watchHits`, `state.towns`, and the live `intelMyIdentity()`
output — all already in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:194-215`).

The session-local `intelView` (plan 6.13 §3.3) gains one extra value,
`'activity'`. Default `'summary'`. Across reloads the selector returns
to `Resumen`.

The filter input's value is **not** persisted (it is a session-local
DOM input; reload clears it). If a follow-up plan wants the filter to
survive reload, it would add a `state.intelFilter` and a
`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry — out of scope here.

## 6. Config surface

No new toggle. The dashboard is gated by the `[data-intel="view"]`
selector (§3.4). The alliance filter is the only new control; it
lives next to the existing note editors (`ui.js:700-704`) and uses
the same `createElement` discipline.

No HIGH-RISK toggle to set OFF (Low risk; read-only).

## 7. Post surface & safety

**No post surface.** No `bridgePost`, no `gameAjaxPost`, no
`gbDomClick`, no `gbAjaxWatch`, no `gbLock`, no `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry,
no `gbCaptchaPause` key.

The renderer uses `box.textContent = html`. The filter input uses
`createElement('input')` + `placeholder` attribute (text content only).
Audit-I15 XSS discipline: zero `innerHTML` for attacker-controlled
strings. Player names (`f.attacker.name`, `f.defender.name`) and
alliance strings (`f.alliance`, `f.attacker.alliance`) come from
`parse-inline.js:39-100` and are attacker-controlled; `textContent`
is the only safe assignment.

## 8. Failure modes

- **`state.findings` empty**: `byPlayer` is `{}`, output is `[]`,
  renderer emits `(sin actividad en la ventana)`. Fresh-install safe.
- **`intelMyIdentity()` returns `{id:null, name:null}`** (`intel.js:26`):
  `intelActorIsMe(...)` returns false in both directions (`intel.js:28-33`);
  every finding falls into the `spiedByMe` bucket.
- **Window cut before earliest `ts`**: that finding is filtered out;
  widen `windowHours` to recover.
- **Alliance case mismatch**: comparison is
  `String(...).toLowerCase() === filter` on both sides — matches.
- **`f.alliance` null on a finding**: `r.alliance` stays `null`,
  label renders `?`. Player still appears if the filter is empty.
- **`state.watchHits` empty**: the dashboard does not currently
  surface a `[W]` marker for watched players; follow-up work.
- **`intelView` undefined** (selector not landed per §3.4): branch
  never fires; falls through to existing dump blocks. No crash.

## 9. Validation gate

Manual, per plan 27 §11 Low class (Preflight + one in-game session,
no failure).

- Build (`python3 build.py`), install, open the Intel tab. The
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector shows `Resumen` (default),
  `Actividad 7.6`, and the other views from plans 6.13 / 7.2 / 7.3
  if they have landed.
- With `state.findings` containing at least one enemy attack on an
  own town (a real bot has this within minutes of opening the
  inbox): the dashboard emits one row per attacker with
  `me-ataca ≥ 1`, `yo-ataco = 0`, `aliado: <note>` if
  `state.allianceNotes` has the alliance.
- Type `WoodFaction` into the alliance filter; rows collapse to only
  attackers whose `f.attacker.alliance === 'WoodFaction'`
  (case-insensitive). Clear the filter; rows return.
- Switch `intelView` between `Resumen` and `Actividad 7.6`; the
  filter input value persists in DOM. Reload → filter returns empty
  (session-local, not persisted).
- Preflight → new `alliance activity` row; pass when `members > 0`;
  warn when 0.
- `state.dryRun = true` → dashboard still renders; no new posts in
  Log tab; journal `mem:<n>` does not increment.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Alliance roster.** Not reachable from a single client (see §1.5).
  Real roster requires the alliance forum scrape, out per plan 27 §0
  (no server, no `@connect` host beyond `discord.com` /
  `api.telegram.org` at `header.js:16-19`).
- **Auto-publishing the dashboard.** Out of plan 27 §7.1 / §7.4
  territory (the `alerts.js` Discord-webhook path).
- **Filter persistence.** Session-local DOM only; a follow-up plan
  can add `state.intelFilter` with a `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` entry.
- **`watched` / `inPattern` marker display.** Aggregator computes
  both; renderer does not yet emit `[W]` / `[P]` suffixes — follow-up.
- **Cross-alliance auth.** Plan 7.3's resource-pool tracker is the
  companion piece that aggregates by alliance; this plan aggregates
  by player. Together they cover the read-mostly alliance views
  promised in plan 27 §7. Anything beyond read-mostly is out per
  plan 27 §0.
- **Plan 6.13 dependency.** If plan 6.13 has not landed, the
  `[data-intel="view"]` selector does not exist and §3.4 has nothing
  to extend. File this plan as **blocked** and land 6.13 first.

## 8.1-circuit-breaker.md

# 8.1 — Per-module circuit breaker (generalized)

**Bucket:** v4.1 · **Risk:** Low · **Size:** M
**Module:** extend `src/planner.js` (the breaker already lives here, `planner.js:172-208`); extend `src/bridge.js` for the threshold constants; surface in `src/stats.js` (already half-rendered at `stats.js:261-263`) and `src/ui.js` (Config + manual reset at `ui.js:2018` already wired).
**Depends on:** none
**Status:** PLANNED — written 2026-08-10 against `src/` @ v3.9.0

## 1. What exists today

A per-feature breaker is **already coded**, hidden in `planner.js` under the name `circuit*` and called from the write path in `tx.js`. Evidence:

- `planner.js:170` `CIRCUIT_TRIP = 3`; `:171` `CIRCUIT_STRUCTURAL_RE` (a regex that fires on `unknown.?action|invalid.?action|unknown.?model|...|endpoint.?not.?found`).
- `planner.js:172-208` `circuitSave` / `circuitState` / `circuitOpen` / `circuitNote` / `circuitSuccess` / `circuitClear`. State shape: `state.circuits[feature] = { strikes, open, openedAt, lastError, lastAt }`.
- Persisted via `STORE.CIRCUITS` (`header.js:146`), loaded as `state.circuits = load(STORE.CIRCUITS, {})` (`core.js:350`), normalised in the v3 migration (`core.js:412`), and whitelisted in `WORLD_SCOPED_BASES` (`header.js:209`).
- **Callers — only on the WRITE path.** `tx.js:528` `txActionGate`: if `write && circuitOpen(feature) → 'circuit-open'`. `tx.js:587/589` and `:661/674/686`: `circuitSuccess` on `ok`, `circuitNote` on hard err. `bandit.js:149`: explicit `circuitSuccess('bandit')` after bridge success. `build-auto.js:268` and `:231`: `circuitOpen('build')` short-circuit. `collect.js:29`: `circuitOpen('collect')` short-circuit.
- Surfaced in `stats.js:261-263` (Preflight `guards` row: `OPEN circuits: …`), `stats.js:251-266`, `ui.js:1833/1849` (footer pauseInfo carries `circuits: openCircuits`), `qol.js:146/149/164/170/177/182` (Overview health panel), and a manual `GrepBot: clear circuit breakers` menu entry at `ui.js:2018-2024`.

What is **also already there but narrower** — the farm scrape endpoint breaker from plan 26 §A1 work item 1, coded:

- `state.farmScrapeState = { dead: false, misses: 0 }` loaded at `core.js:243`, persisted via `STORE.FARM_SCRAPE_STATE` (`header.js:181`).
- `farms.js:652-689` `farmScrapeState` / `farmScrapeSaveState` / `farmScrapeEnabled` / `farmScrapeClearErrors` / `farmScrapeNoteSweep` / `farmScrapeRevive`. `FARM_SCRAPE_DEAD_SWEEPS = 2` (`farms.js:650`).
- Hooked at `farms.js:869` (`farmScrapeNoteSweep(ok)` after each sweep), at `farms.js:720` (`farmScrapeRevive` on a real `learnFarmAction`), and at `ui.js:1244-1245` (Config toggle ON → revive, OFF → clear errors). Surfaced in `stats.js:38-50` (Preflight `farm resource scrape` row).
- The two breakers do **not** overlap: `state.circuits` fires on bridge structural errors, `state.farmScrapeState` fires on the village-resource **HTTP scraper** returning 0 OK across two sweeps. Plan 26 §A1 names this distinction explicitly: "the breaker was waiting for a real action from the player's own traffic."

What is **absent**:

- **No breaker on READ paths** (`gbXhr`, scrapes). Plan 26 §A1 names one for farms; nothing generalises it to town scrapes (`towns.js:101-149`, 6-deep `TOWN_ACTION_GUESSES`), report catch-up (`spy.js:117-163`, `fetchReportHttp`), CSRF hunt (`core.js` around `huntCsrf`), or phoenician view sniff.
- **No breaker on bridge NON-structural errors** (timeout, captcha). `circuitNote` (`planner.js:184`) ignores `timeout`/`captcha`/`captcha-pause`/`timeout_unknown` — that is the right call today (own breakers own them), but a feature like `phoenician` whose endpoint silently dies without producing a structural message has no protection.
- **No Config surface.** `CIRCUIT_TRIP` is a hardcoded constant (3); the threshold cannot be tuned. There is no per-feature override, no auto-recovery probe cadence, and no max-open-time before forced half-open.
- **No half-open probe.** Once a circuit opens it stays open until `circuitSuccess(feature)` fires (`planner.js:198`) — but `circuitSuccess` only resets `strikes`, never clears `open`. The only path that closes an open circuit today is the manual `circuitClear` from `ui.js:2020`. A long-running feature can stay disabled until the user notices.
- **Stats only shows "OPEN circuits" by name** (`stats.js:263`); it does not show how long each has been open, what the last error was, or how many strikes it has accumulated.

The journal skip mechanism plan 27 cites (decision-memory at `journal.js:31-247` with `JRN_FAIL_TRIP=3` `bridge.js:450`, `JRN_BACKOFF=[5,15,60]` `bridge.js:451`) is **adjacent but separate**: it gates the **same feature+action+target** for 5/15/60 min on per-target errors, while the circuit breaker gates the **whole feature** on structural errors. The two compose: a `circuit-open` rejection in `txActionGate` (`tx.js:528`) is journaled as `skip:circuit-open` (`journal.js:16`, `JRN_SKIP_ERRS` at `bridge.js:457-466`) and short-circuits future posts.

## 2. Gap

The catalogue promises a generic per-module breaker that **extends the journal skip mechanism**. The reality is that the breaker already exists in a tighter form (per-feature, structural-error only, write-path only, manual clear only). The remaining work is (a) generalise it to **read paths and silent-endpoint failures**, (b) add **half-open probing** so a feature can recover without a manual click, (c) **expose thresholds** in Config, and (d) **show richer state** in Preflight so the user can see *why* each circuit is open.

This plan explicitly generalises plan 26 §A1's farm-specific breaker (`state.farmScrapeState`, `farms.js:652-689`) into the per-feature registry rather than replacing it: the farm scrape breaker is an HTTP-scrape specialisation, not a write structural-error breaker, and the two coexist with `farmScrapeNoteSweep` calling `circuitNote` would be a category error. The plan leaves `state.farmScrapeState` in place and adds a parallel generic mechanism for the other read paths that today lack any breaker.

## 3. Design

One shared registry (`state.circuitBreakers[feature] = { state: 'closed'|'open'|'half-open', strikes, lastError, lastAt, openedAt, halfOpenAt, probeFailures }`) backed by a new `STORE.CIRCUIT_BREAKERS` key. The existing `state.circuits` shape (closed-via-strikes, opens-on-3) is **migrated** into the new shape on first load — `state.circuits` stays as a read-cache used by the existing call sites, so nothing in `tx.js:528` / `build-auto.js:231` / `collect.js:29` / `bandit.js:149` changes.

- **State machine.** `closed` (normal) → on Nth structural error within W → `open` → after `cooldownMs` → `half-open` (next attempt becomes a probe; success → `closed`, failure → `open` with `cooldownMs *= 2`, capped at 1h).
- **Trigger.** `circuitNote(feature, err)` (already at `tx.js:589,674` and `planner.js:181`) becomes the only write path; **plus** a new `circuitNoteRead(feature, err, ok)` for read paths called from `gbXhr` failures in `core.js` (around `:1233-1236` `failEarly`) and from per-loop result handlers (`farms.js:869`, `towns.js` scrape result).
- **Recovery.** A `gbInterval`-free sweeper (`gbTimeout` chain, `setInterval` would conflict with the "no new schedulers" rule) inside `boot.js`'s existing `gbInterval(gbLockSweep, 10000)` line (`boot.js:124`) — half-opens any circuit whose `cooldownMs` has elapsed. The next post attempt then re-tries the endpoint naturally (no new probe scheduler).
- **Stats.** `stats.js:261` `OPEN circuits:` line grows to `OPEN farm:no-endpoint 12m (no data) · scrape:town 4m (404)` — name, age, lastError first 40 chars.
- **Config.** New Config section "Cortacircuitos" with `circuitTripN` (default 3), `circuitCooldownMin` (default 15), `circuitReadEnabled` (default OFF — read breakers are noisy), `circuitAutoClear` (default ON — sweep half-open after cooldown).

Data flow: `bridgePost → txRun → txActionGate` (unchanged; reads `state.circuits[feature].open` via `circuitOpen`); on err: `circuitNote` updates `state.circuits`; every save call (existing `jrnSave` at `journal.js:104` / `txSave` / per-feature saves) piggy-backs a `circuitBreakerSave()` write that goes through `save(STORE.CIRCUIT_BREAKERS, …)`. The 10s `gbLockSweep` line in `boot.js:124` also calls `circuitBreakerSweep()`.

## 5. State & storage

- New `STORE.CIRCUIT_BREAKERS` (`header.js`) — id-bearing-by-feature, world-scoped (`WORLD_SCOPED_BASES`).
- New `state.circuitBreakers = { [feature]: { state, strikes, lastError, lastAt, openedAt, halfOpenAt, probeFailures } }` (`core.js:350`).
- New `state.circuitTripN` (default 3), `state.circuitCooldownMin` (default 15), `state.circuitReadEnabled` (default OFF), `state.circuitAutoClear` (default ON) — four new fields in the state initializer block at `core.js:240-385`, each `load(STORE.…, default)` and `save(STORE.…)` on toggle.
- New `CONFIG_VER_CURRENT = 11` (`header.js:191`); new v11 migration step copies old `state.circuits` into `state.circuitBreakers`.
- `state.circuits` is **kept** as a back-compat mirror written by `circuitSave` (existing call sites keep working). Prune TTL: never (a circuit's `openedAt` lives until `circuitSuccess`/`circuitClear`).
- No prune of `state.circuitBreakers` — entries age out via `circuitSuccess` reset and `circuitClear` clear. Total size: bounded by feature count (~14 features per `PRIORITY_ORDER_DEFAULT` at `header.js:189`) × ~80 bytes ≈ <2 KB. Well under the 5 MB GM budget (`docs/plans/20-storage-quota-alarm.md`).

## 6. Config surface

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `circuitTripN` | int 1-10 | 3 | Strikes before opening. Overrides the hardcoded `CIRCUIT_TRIP=3`. |
| `circuitCooldownMin` | int 1-120 | 15 | Minutes before an open circuit becomes half-open. Doubles on probe failure, capped at 60. |
| `circuitReadEnabled` | bool | **OFF** | Read-path breakers (`towns-scrape`, `spy-catchup`, `phoenician-view`). OFF because they are noisy and the manual reset is faster than a tripped auto-breaker. |
| `circuitAutoClear` | bool | ON | The 10s sweep half-opens eligible circuits. OFF = manual `GrepBot: half-open all circuits` only. |

HIGH-RISK OFF default applies **only** to `circuitReadEnabled` (read breakers trip on benign noise); the others are tunables, not autonomy. **Do not** add a "force-open" / "force-close" toggle — that would re-introduce a phone-home remote flag (plan 27 §0 dropped that idea).

## 7. Post surface & safety

This is a **read-mostly** feature: no new bridge posts, no new `bridgePost`/`gameAjaxPost` calls, no new `gbAjaxWatch(sig, settle)` registrations, no template additions to `TPL_FEATURE_MAP` / `tplNameFor`. The breaker only **gates** existing posts; it does not create any.

- `gbCaptchaPause` feature key: not needed (no new post surface).
- `gbLock` name + `GB_LOCK_TTL` entry: not needed (no in-flight coordination).
- Dry-run: not applicable (read-only infrastructure).
- **Bridge-first**: irrelevant — no new transport.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Breaker trips on a transient blip.** A user-configured `circuitTripN=1` would open a circuit on a single error. Default 3 absorbs this; the Config input enforces min=1 to allow tuning but the default is the safe value.
- **Auto-clear (`circuitAutoClear` ON) opens a circuit that is still genuinely broken.** The half-open probe will hit the same dead endpoint; `probeFailures` doubles `cooldownMs` up to 1h. After 3 probe failures the circuit stays open until `circuitClear` (manual) or until the next `ok` arrives. This is the correct behaviour — auto-retry storms are the failure mode this plan prevents.
- **`circuitReadEnabled` OFF but a read path keeps hammering the budget.** The Preflight `guards` row (`stats.js:263`) shows the open-circuit count; if it grows, the user flips the toggle ON. Plan 26 §A1 explicitly recommends the breaker over an un-throttled scraper.
- **`state.circuitBreakers` shape diverges from `state.circuits` after a partial migration.** The migration in work item 2 is a one-shot copy in v11; after it runs the two mirrors are kept in sync by every write through `circuitSave`. A `console.warn` from `loadValueOk` (`core.js:1101`) on size >2MB catches accidental divergence (a feature that writes huge `lastError` blobs).
- **Unreadable breaker state ⇒ blind.** `circuitOpen` (`planner.js:177`) returns `false` when `state.circuitBreakers[feature]` is missing or unparseable — the safe default is "act as if closed". A log entry via `gbLogT` (`core.js`'s logger, journal.js:215 shows the pattern) once per 60s prevents log spam.
- **Precondition invariant**: the breaker checks `state.circuitBreakers[feature].state` (read value), never a derived field. The half-open flip reads `Date.now()` (read value) against `openedAt + cooldownMs` (computed from read values). No guard depends on a value that wasn't read.

## 9. Validation gate

Low risk per plan 27 §11. Per Low gate: Preflight + one in-game session, no failure.

1. **Preflight `circuit breakers` row** renders with `0 open, 0 half-open, autoClear ON, trip 3, cooldown 15m` on a fresh install.
2. **Triggered trip:** in DevTools console: `GB_ROOT.__grepbotTest` (exposed at `boot.js:147-160` test hook) — call `circuitNote('bandit', 'unknown action')` three times. Preflight re-run shows `OPEN bandit 0m (unknown action)`. Footer badge shows `⚡circ:1`.
3. **Half-open recovery:** wait 15 min (or temporarily set `circuitCooldownMin=1`). Re-run Preflight: `half-open bandit 15m`. Cause one bandit success (`bandit.js:149` calls `circuitSuccess` on success path) — circuit closes, badge clears.
4. **Read breaker disabled by default:** with `circuitReadEnabled` OFF, simulate 10 dead `towns-scrape` reads — Preflight shows no circuit. Flip ON, repeat — circuit opens after 5 misses (`CIRCUIT_READ_TRIP`), confirming the toggle works.
5. **Manual reset:** `GrepBot: clear circuit breakers` confirms the dialog (`ui.js:2020`), clears the registry, Preflight shows `clear`.
6. **Back-compat:** with a persisted `state.circuits = { build: { strikes: 3, open: true, lastError: 'unknown action' } }` from a pre-v4.1 install, the v11 migration writes an equivalent `state.circuitBreakers.build = { state: 'open', … }`; `circuitOpen('build')` still returns true; `tx.js:528` still rejects writes with `skip:circuit-open`.

## 10. Out of scope

- **Auto-recovery via captcha-bypass / server-side probe.** Plan 27 §0 dropped those. This plan only opens/closes based on observed POST results, never invents a probe.
- **Replacing `state.farmScrapeState` (`core.js:243`, `farms.js:652-689`).** Plan 26 §A1's farm-specific breaker is an HTTP-scrape specialisation (counts 0-ok sweeps, recovers on `learnFarmAction`); the generic breaker here counts structural-error strikes per feature. Work item 7 calls `circuitNoteRead` **in addition to** the existing `farmScrapeNoteSweep`, so both still fire on the same dead scrape. Migration away from the farm breaker would break the `learnFarmAction` revive hook at `farms.js:720`.
- **Decision-memory skip windows** (`journal.js:172-247`, `bridge.js:450-451`). Plan 27's "extends the journal skip mechanism" is true by composition (`circuit-open` rejections journal as `skip:circuit-open` per `JRN_SKIP_ERRS` at `bridge.js:457-466`), not by refactoring. The journal's per-target skip is the right grain for transient per-town failures; the circuit is the right grain for whole-feature structural failures.
- **A new top-level `gbInterval`.** Work item 5 piggybacks on `boot.js:124`'s existing 10s `gbInterval(gbLockSweep, …)` line. Per plan 27 §13 / `docs/plans/v4/README.md` Hard rule 4.
- **Cloud sync, REST API, plugin hooks, automation-recovery bot.** All explicitly dropped by plan 27 §0.
